How Cardinals, Seahawks Week 9 Injury Report Changed
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Seattle Seahawks both saw a handful of changes to their Week 9 injury report after Thursday's slate of practices.
Most notably, Quenton Nelson was downgraded from limited to DNP in Seattle while Earnest Jones was added today with an ankle injury. In Arizona, majority of their rest guys returned to practice (Josh Sweat, Budda Baker among others), while Max Melton was added with a knee injury.
With so many injuries in Arizona's running back room, LaFleur was down to only one running back last Sunday in Dallas.
Who would have been the emergency back? While LaFleur will have more resources this week, he pointed to wide receiver Devin Duvernay.
"I know it crossed my mind, but it was what it was. And so, if ‘TA ‘would’ve started cramping and needed to come out, we would’ve had to make a decision within 10 seconds of 'who was going to go back there," LaFleur said.
"We would’ve made it and you guys would’ve thought we were ready for it, but we weren’t. We would’ve just flown and guess what? Whoever would’ve went back there, again, I’ll just keep using (WR Devin) Duvernay because that’s who comes to the top of my head, he would’ve stepped up and done whatever he could.”
LaFleur says their Week 2 film will be especially helpful preparing for Drew Lock as Darnold has been ruled out for now a second contest against Arizona this season.
“No, it’s valuable. You can see the stuff he liked and what they had success with. Obviously, a lot has changed since Week 2. The first week is what it is. Week 2, you’re still kind of trying to find yourself and you’re not really even settled in yet as a team by any means. But yes, we can use that as a benefit for sure," he said this week.
Both teams will practice once more on Friday before revealing official game designations such as out, questionable or doubtful.

title: Projecting Jacoby Brissett's Trade Value, Potential Cardinals-Ravens Package
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is currently on his way to Baltimore, most likely to complete a medical evaluation from the Ravens to finalize a previously agreed upon trade that first broke news yesterday.
Brissett, a veteran with deep experience and a cheap expiring contract, is hoping to help rescue a Ravens team that is set to lose both Lamar Jackson and backup Snoop Huntley all in the same swoop due to injury.
The trade is expected to be finalized at some point this weekend — though an interesting nugget has been the absence of a reported compensation for Brissett.
What exactly are the Cardinals getting in return for their former starting quarterback?
An interesting note before diving into Brissett's trade value is Arizona reportedly restructured his contract to effectively turn $2.7 million of his remaining $4.5 million salary into a signing bonus. Essentially, this means the Cardinals are taking on extra money to facilitate a deal.
Brissett's value isn't seen as great. He's an aging veteran who will be a free agent this coming offseason, making him a rental. And it's not as if he was playing lights out prior to the deadline — his benching at halftime last week highlights that.
We previously discussed why the deal is a win for Arizona regardless just for the simple fact of getting something for Brissett, though at the end of the day, there is a value both sides have to agree upon, and naturally Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort would want as much as possible.
On the surface, Brissett's value would sit somewhere around a seventh or sixth-round pick. However, with the Cardinals eating roughly half of Brissett's remaining salary, that could signal the arrow is pointing towards a higher pick.
Baltimore currently has eight selections in the 2027 NFL Draft, which includes multiple fifth-round picks and original sixth/Dallas' seventh-round pick. However, their three combined fifth/sixth-round picks are compensatory picks and cannot be traded until the NFL officially awards them in March ahead of the draft.
Three years ago, the Cardinals traded quarterback Joshua Dobbs to the Minnesota Vikings near the trade deadline in a swapping of picks that saw Arizona net a sixth-round pick for a conditional seventh.
However, the Cardinals didn't take on more of Dobbs' salary like they did for Brissett. Another veteran quarterback in Andy Dalton was traded for a seventh-round pick earlier in March, where value isn't as high compared to the deadline due to urgency.
How high does Baltimore value Brissett? Do they believe he can steady their ship and potentially keep them in the playoff hunt? If so, Arizona could raise the bar in terms of asking price, and Baltimore's alleged insistence in keeping the deal hush-hush in fear of being outbid could be another indicator.
Another note: It's possible the Cardinals would get Kedon Slovis back in a deal, as Arizona currently doesn't have a third quarterback on the roster behind Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck . Slovis spent camp and preseason in the desert and has first-hand experience in LaFleur's offense, which could make him an attractive trade piece.
Is it a coincidence the Ravens signed him on Tuesday, when trade negotiations were reportedly already well underway with Arizona?
It will be fascinating to see what the final details are when the dust settles.

title: Cardinals Coach Said The Quiet Part Out Loud on Carson Beck
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' most popular quarterback option for the 2026 season hasn't even been active for a game thus far.
That's set to change this week, and perhaps shortly down the road to even greater extents.
Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck got a promotion this week after the Cardinals benched starter Jacoby Brissett , propelling backup Gardner Minshew to QB1 duties and Beck now taking the QB2 seat in the desert.
With Brissett's reported trade to the Baltimore Ravens, Beck's path to playing is crystal clear.
That's something Cardinals fans have been pounding the table for since Arizona's struggles began this season, and head coach Mike LaFleur acknowledged that.
“Obviously it’s just behind the scenes. Nothing that you guys see, but I know he’s prepared to go in there if need be. Again, just like Gardner, just like anyone that you ask that’s going to be on this team, they’re prepared as if they’re going to be the starting quarterback or they’re prepared if they have to go in," LaFleur said on Beck earlier this week.
"I know that he has (a) full grasp of this game plan (and) of this system. It’s no secret, obviously, if something were to happen, it’d be nice to know what we have right there. I feel really good about where he is with his development, so if that were to come up, then obviously he’d be the next one in.”
Beck appeared in the team's preseason opener and impressed, though a ribs injury sat him out for the remainder of exhibition play. Beck also suffered a back injury in recent weeks, though he seems to have overcome that and is now healthy.
The Cardinals, with a massive 2027 offseason ahead, will need to make a decision on the future of their quarterback position. Beck's performance, if and when he enters action, will weigh heavily on the ultimate direction Arizona chooses to go in either sticking with the third-round pick or pursuing a new quarterback option elsewhere.
Exactly when Beck plays remains unknown.
In a perfect world, the Cardinals would prefer Minshew to find his prior 2023 Pro Bowl form and lead Arizona to a magical season. However, the reality is Minshew's high level of play will likely be solved by opposing defenses within the next four weeks, propping Beck up to finish the season.

title: Jacoby Brissett Requested Cardinals Trade, Per Report
full_text:
Though still unofficial, the Arizona Cardinals' trade sending quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens made waves through the NFL world just days after he was benched by the organization in Dallas.
His replacement, Gardner Minshew, rescued the day for Arizona in Week 8 — and the rest has since been history. Brissett quickly went from a starter to not even active on gamedays in seemingly the blink of an eye, and now he's packing his bags for a new opportunity in Baltimore.
That was his choice, according to new reports.
From ESPN's Josh Weinfuss:
A video of Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur and Brissett interacting on the sideline after halftime showed the quarterback was extremely displeased with the situation, as one would expect.
The compensation for Brissett is still unknown at this point in time, though it's fair to guess the Ravens are only sending out a Day 3 pick (likely sixth or seventh round) for Arizona's former starting quarterback.
The deal is likely to be complete this weekend after Baltimore plays on Thursday Night Football.
Brissett was voted a team captain ahead of this season and negotiated a significant payraise to see more guaranteed money on the final year of his contract.
“As long as we’re where our feet are and our feet are — these guys (are) handling their own responsibilities within what we’re asking them to do in getting prepared to play a tough opponent this week," LaFleur said of losing a team captain.
"I’m not worried about any of that stuff. What the outside world would consider distractions: we don’t. We’re concerned about being right here right now and having a great practice today.”
The Cardinals move forward with Minshew in the saddle and rookie third-round pick Carson Beck waiting in the wings.
Arizona's quarterback plan the rest of the season feels pretty clear in riding Minshew until the wheels fall off — whenever that may be — and handing Beck over the keys for the rest of the way.
“Just go play each play. Let’s prepare just like we would any other week," LaFleur said of his quarterback room moving forward.
"We have a great opponent and let’s have a great Wednesday and be where our feet are. If we look too far ahead, which looking too far ahead for me is Sunday, we know what kind of challenge this is going to be. We’re going into a hostile environment against arguably the best defense in football and an offense that we know firsthand can score points, but right now we’re just focused on our prep.”

title: The Surprising Salary Cap Cost of Cardinals' Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals , though still unofficial, are trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens.
Brissett was benched this past weekend in favor for Gardner Minshew, who led the Cardinals to a comeback win over the Cowboys on Sunday and now has full control the team's starting position.
Brissett, demoted to Arizona's third emergency quarterback position, now finds himself on the way to Baltimore but likely won't play until next week, as the Ravens are on Thursday Night Football.
Things are still being finalized, though Brissett's departure opens a spot in the Cardinals' quarterback room.
Brissett's trade out of the desert comes at a cost for both this season and next.
By trading Brissett, the Cardinals will take on a dead cap hit of $9.6 million for the rest of the year while 2027 will see a $7.2 million dead cap hit according to Spotrac.
The Ravens, meanwhile, take on a mere $695,000.
Assuming the Jacoby Brissett trade is processed for Week 10, the #Ravens will be taking on a $650,000 salary for the rest of the 2026 season ($695k cap hit). The #Cardinals will take on dead cap hits of $9.6M for 2026, and another $7.2M in 2027.
For the moment, Arizona saves a total of $1.3 million for the rest of the 2026 season by trading Brissett. That places their running cap total at $11.5 million per Spotrac, which keeps them firmly at No. 11 for most cap space in the league.
This money can be rolled over into next offseason.
The Cardinals' total dead cap space does increase by $8.9 million immediately, seeing their total jump from $93.1 million to $102 million for 2026. Brissett now slots into the No. 2 spot for highest dead cap hit in Arizona, trailing No. 1 Kyler Murray ($46.5 million) and No. 3 Marvin Harrison Jr. ($8.8 million).
The Cardinals still rank No, 5 in total dead cap money for 2026, far behind the No. 1 ranked Miami Dolphins at $190 million.
For next offseason, 2027, Brissett's dead cap hit ties Murray ($7.2 million) for the highest in Arizona. After accounting for Brissett's hit, the Cardinals will be up to $20.4 million — though the number will surely increase as the organization makes more moves.
Brissett, scheduled to be a free agent next offseason, initially had a void year added by the Cardinals after he had his contract restructured at the start of training camp.
Arizona made a surprising decision to not absorb all of Brissett's salary this season, though it shouldn't have a massive impact on their total spending power in 2027.
Using OverTheCap's projections, the Cardinals have the second-most projected cap space next offseason at $104.2 million.

title: 25 Players Highlight Cardinals-Seahawks Week 9 Injury Report
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Seattle Seahawks have revealed their first injury report of Week 9, and it's a lengthy, star-studded list.
The Cardinals saw massive names such as Budda Baker and Josh Sweat — two players possibly being traded ahead of next week's trade deadline — on rest days while Walter Nolen returned to practice.
For Seattle, they're already down their starting quarterback in Sam Darnold for Week 9 while Leonard Williams, Quenton Nelson and others land on the list.
Arizona moves forward with Gardner Minshew under center for his first official start of 2026 after trading away Jacoby Brissett.
“I think he kind of showed all of us in terms of him going out there being the competitor that he is. Doesn’t shock me. The production was pretty wild in terms of the amount of points and just moving up and down the field, but he’s a competitor and he’s always prepared," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of Minshew.
"He’s preparing like he’s the starter. He’s preparing like he’s going to be in there for whatever snap. He supported Jacoby at a high level too. He’s been a great backup for him. He’s been great for the room and (I) look forward to the challenge that we have this week with him.”
The Seahawks ruled out Darnold today, propping up Drew Lock for a second start against the Cardinals.
"We know what kind of challenges it's going to be. We're going into a hostile environment against arguably the best defense in football, an offense that we know firsthand can score points," LaFleur said of facing Seattle.
The Seahawks, 4-4, are trying to find their footing after losing their last three-of-four games.
Both sides face an uphill battle in terms of health this week.
Both teams will practice twice more this week on Thursday and Friday before labeling injured players as out, questionable or doubtful after Friday's practice.
On Saturday, the Cardinals and Seahawks can make up to two practice squad elevations. Based off who is listed on Friday's injury report, this could be key in identifying who the teams believe will be healthy or not.
Final inactives are due 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday, where NFL teams must decide if any questionable players will be part of the 48-player gameday roster or not.
For Sunday's 2:25 PM MST kickoff in Seattle, that will be 12:55 PM MST.

title: 3 Cardinals Most Likely to Be Traded Next After Jacoby Brissett Move
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals , as promised, remain active ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
After dealing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans weeks ago, the Cardinals have now benched and successfully traded quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
Brissett, while still awaiting official word of completion, is heading to the Baltimore Ravens today.
While terms are unknown at this point in time, the Cardinals appear to be open for business.
With less than a week left to make moves, here are three Cardinals most likely next on the trade block:
This is the most obvious candidate, as Sweat has been rumored to be unhappy in Arizona since the early days of the offseason after the Cardinals fired Jonathan Gannon.
Sweat's production has picked up the pace in recent weeks, just in time for a potential deal to get done while maximizing his value.
The Cardinals are rumored to be in search of a second-round pick, though we'll see if the deadline can bring any desperate team looking for a playoff push to that price tag. It's likely we see a team package a third and a high Day 3 pick for Sweat, if he is traded.
Baker isn't quite knocking on the door to be traded like many believe Sweat is, though the reality is the star safety is getting another year older and he's not quite closer to winning a championship in the desert.
"I'm here. I want to win. I want to be here," he said to ESPN last week. "And I'm just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I'll still be here. If not, I mean, it's a business. I understand at the end of the day and that's it."
More than anything, this would be a move to place Baker at the forefront of competing on a playoff team, something he's only done once in his decade of service for the Cardinals.
This third spot is where things can get tricky, though after Harrison and Brissett were moved, there's not bountiful options for Arizona in terms of potential trade candidates.
We arrive to Conner, who hasn't played at all this season after being injured in Week 3 of last season with a foot/ankle injury. The veteran running back restructured his deal to remain in Arizona this past offseason, though the Cardinals' backfield (when healthy) is so crowded there's essentially no room for him.
Conner, much like Baker, is on the tail end of his career, and the organization just might do right by taking him off injured reserve and dealing him to a playoff team. He's on the final year of his contract and Arizona clearly wanted to get younger at the position this past offseason.

title: Cardinals-Ravens Trade For Jacoby Brissett is Major Win for Arizona
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are finally pulling off a trade involving quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
Brissett is reportedly being dealt to the Baltimore Ravens. While terms are not yet known, getting any sort of draft capital for Brissett is a massive win for Arizona, who recently demoted Brissett to No. 3 duties.
Trade: the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, per @RapSheet and me. Deal is expected to be completed this weekend. The Ravens lost QB Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury, and his backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley to turf toe. pic.twitter.com/sGpFSxYc5u
Brissett was benched this past weekend while Gardner Minshew replaced him in the third quarter of Arizona's Week 8 matchup in Dallas, leading four straight scoring drives and ultimately an upset victory over the Cowboys.
From there, the writing was clearly on the wall for not only a demotion for Brissett, but a trade as well.
After holding out for a new contract and leading the Cardinals to a poor start in 2026, pressure mounted for Arizona to make a move to Minshew.
“That’s not easy. It’s not a fun phone call," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of benching Brissett ahead of Week 9.
"There’s no book for that. There’s a human element to it. I have a lot of respect for Jacoby, the person. I have a lot of respect for Jacoby, the player. Like I told you guys yesterday, it was not all on him. This was collective and starting with me, but the position that those guys sign up for, we know the deal. We needed a spark and obviously Gardner gave us one.”
Brissett will not make it in time for Baltimore's Thursday Night Football matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but a deal is expected to be done in the coming days. The Ravens have lost Lamar Jackson and Snoop Huntley due to injuries, seeing their quarterback room decimated nearly overnight.
That made the Cardinals and Ravens ideal trade partners in terms of opportunity for Baltimore and value for Arizona.
What exactly the Cardinals are getting in return for Brissett remains to be seen, though Arizona is expected to get a low Day 3 pick (rounds six or seven) for the veteran passer, which sees their trade deadline draft-pick haul expand after netting a second-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. weeks ago.
While the Ravens get a veteran quarterback who has prior experience with their own quarterbacks coach in Israel Woolfork, Arizona also finds themselves as a massive winner here — clearing the path for rookie Carson Beck to earn eventual playing time while adding to their pool draft picks.
The Cardinals may not be done, either. Names such as Josh Sweat and Budda Baker have recently been involved in trade rumors.
The NFL's trade deadline is Nov. 10.

title: Cardinals-Seahawks Week 9 Battle Takes Major Twist
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals will not see Sam Darnold on Sunday.
The Seattle Seahawks are ruling Darnold out with a quad injury ahead of Week 9's meeting at Lumen Field. Drew Lock will start in his place.
Seahawks QB Sam Darnold will be out Sunday vs. Arizona due to quad injury, per HC  Mike Macdonald.
The Cardinals previously saw Lock in their Week 2 loss at State Farm Stadium, where Seattle's offense put up 381 total yards and 30+ points in a 31-7 blowout over Arizona.
Prior to that matchup, Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur gave a glowing review of Darnold.
"Sam's a great quarterback. Obviously, I'd say I know Sam a little bit better than Drew because I did have, I guess you could say, a month or so with him even though he wasn't in the building in New York. I've always really respected him dating back to USC. Understanding that he was a young quarterback going through it," said LaFleur back ahead of Week 2.
"Every situation's different by the quarterback and by the club, and he got himself in a very stable situation. I think starting in San Francisco, Minnesota, and then obviously in Seattle. It's not shocking that they got the result they did last year. They are, in my opinion, the best coached team in football. I think they have the best defense in football. In my opinion, they have a really, really good quarterback with it. Yeah, he's down this week, but again, like I just said with Drew, the moment's not too big for him. I think he's a good quarterback who's played a lot of good football."
Now, Lock is set for his third start of the season.
The Seahawks are 4-4 and are have lost their last three-of-four meetings entering Week 9. They're also playing on a short week after featuring on Monday Night Football.
When Lock started for Seattle, he orchestrated a fairly efficient game — going 19/26 passing for three touchdowns and no interceptions. He was also sacked only once by the Cardinals' defense.
Darnold has struggled in 2026, so this might not be a bad switch for the Seahawks' offense — especially if he can again take advantage of a Cardinals defense that's allowed five 30+ point outings in their last six games.
Arizona's fresh off a Week 8 upset over the Dallas Cowboys and are hoping to string together consecutive wins for the first time all regular season.
ESPN's football power index gives the Cardinals just a 17.9% chance to win against the Seahawks.

title: Jeremiyah Love Joins Troubling Cardinals Trend Among Recent Draft Picks
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals will be without Jeremiyah Love moving into the foreseeable future after the organization placed him on injured reserve, ensuring he'll miss at minimum the next four weeks.
The Cardinals feel like they can't catch a break with the recent slew of injuries to younger players, and Love is just the latest of an unfortunate trend of recent first-round draft picks to miss time in their rookie season:
Love, first eligible to come off injured reserve in Week 13, will miss at least six games minimum in his rookie season thanks to three different ankle injuries suffered since preseason.
Love was hurt on the 14th and final touch of his preseason debut, which saw him miss the final two games. However, Love would return for the regular season ready to go.
Love didn't miss any of the first five weeks, though a different ankle injury hindered him – enough to make head coach Mike LaFleur sit the third overall pick for two consecutive weeks before returning in Week 8.
Love was hurt in the first half in Dallas with a high ankle sprain and now lands on injured reserve.
Ahead of 2025's training camp, the Cardinals announced Nolen would miss significant time due to a calf injury suffered while training at the team's facility.
The defensive lineman would miss the first seven games of the season before returning on Monday Night Football against the Dallas Cowboys, putting on a show and generating buzz within Arizona's fan base.
However, Nolen would only play six games before suffering a knee injury against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 16, putting him on injured reserve with what was later revealed to be a meniscus injury.
He made a full recovery and was ready to go for this year's version of training camp.
Robinson was hurt during a preseason practice, suffering a calf injury (many speculate Robinson specifically strained or tore his achilles tendon) and placing him on injured reserve before the regular season began.
He missed all but six games during his rookie year.
It is important to note the rookie defensive lineman also lost his mother before officially returning from his injury, which surely played some part in his delayed return to the field as well.
The Cardinals' injury woes extend past the first round of their draft classes.
Recently, 2026 second-round pick Chase Bisontis is set to miss his entire rookie year due to an MCL injury after looking impressive in preseason play. 2026 fourth-round pick Kaleb Proctor is also on injured reserve for the entire year with a meniscus injury.
2025 saw second-round pick Will Johnson miss five games while he's currently on injured reserve with a neck injury. Sixth-round pick from the class, Hayden Conner, began his rookie season on injured reserve after hurting his knee and played just five games for the Cardinals last season.
And for what it's worth, 2025 seventh-round pick Kitan Crawford did play most of his rookie season but went on injured reserve after 2026's season opener with an ankle injury.
2024 third-round pick Elijah Jones missed his entire rookie campaign due to an ankle injury. He played in just ten games for the Cardinals last season and now isn't even on the roster. Fifth-round pick Christian Jones had played a total of four games through his first two seasons due to ankle and knee issues before being cut this summer.

title: Falcons Get Major Defensive Boost Ahead of Joe Burrow, Bengals Showdown
full_text:
MADRID – Atlanta Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. is finally set to make his season debut, and the timing couldn't be more important for a defense searching for answers.
One week after being gashed on the ground by the Buccaneers’ rushing attack, the Falcons will face a fundamentally different challenge with Joe Burrow and the Bengals. This unit tops the NFL in passing offense and boasts one of the league's most dangerous receiving duos in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
Slowing Cincinnati's passing attack will require pressure on Burrow, making Pearce's return especially important. The Falcons have already been busy making space for their star pass rusher, and Samson Ebukam's hamstring injury has created an immediate need for snaps.
What that impact could look like remains a lingering question.
Pearce has been around the team for the past month but was only cleared to practice earlier this week. He's spent most of his time in the weight room and meeting rooms, raising questions about how much he can handle in his first game back. Stefanski said the coaching staff has a good idea of Pearce's capabilities but declined to disclose his expected snap count.
“He’s been working his butt off, and he’s super excited to get out there and help contribute,” Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said Thursday. “I think initially, he’ll probably be more in a pass-rush capacity, whether that be second-and-longs, third downs. But we’ll see. A lot of his conditioning and ability to play more will be dependent upon what he shows us as the game goes along. Thinking as we go in with a pitch count, but you can obviously change that thinking really quickly based on how it plays.”
Pearce led the Falcons with 10.5 sacks last season, marking the first time that the franchise had a player hit double digits since 2016, and he was an instrumental piece in this unit’s franchise-record 57-sack season.
Without him, the Falcons have leaned on a four-man front to generate pressure. The unit has been effective (No. 6 in pressure rate, 40.0%) but has been less consistent at getting the quarterback on the ground (No. 14 in sacks, 18).
The pass rush has spread the wealth, with 12 players having recorded a half-sack or more this season. Veteran Za’Darius Smith (4.5) has led this group, but Pearce’s return would be an adrenaline shot.
He was expected to build on his rookie on-field performance, but an offseason incident marred the first half of his sophomore season. Pearce was arrested in February on allegations of domestic violence, but a pre-trial agreement helped him avoid possible jail time . The league later suspended him for eight games.
Since rejoining the team, Pearce has had an opportunity to rebuild trust within the organization. Ulbrich believes the young pass rusher has shown meaningful personal growth during that process. The two have been meeting once a week, and the Falcons defensive coordinator called those interactions “eye-opening.”
“I think I’ve just gained appreciation for him as a man,” Ulbrich said. “I see a guy that’s really – he’s working his butt off to right some wrongs, and he’s working his butt off to become a better version of himself. I have deep appreciation for that because that’s not easy. And not everybody has the humility and the wisdom to do that. I feel like he’s made a real concerted effort to become the best version of James.
“I’m just super hopeful that that translates to success because we all know that just that would bring that idea that I’m on the right track, and I’ve got to keep going on the right track.”
Pearce's return is unlikely to immediately solve all of Atlanta's defensive problems, particularly against a Bengals offense that can attack defenses in multiple ways, but his ability to generate pressure could give the Falcons a much-needed boost. After leading the team in sacks a year ago, Pearce will have his first opportunity to show what he can contribute to this defense in 2026.
How quickly he can make an impact remains to be seen.

title: What Happened to the Atlanta Falcons' Dominant Running Game?
full_text:
In the young NFL season, the Atlanta Falcons were flying high behind a potent rushing attack.
Led by All-Pro running back and league-leading rusher Bijan Robinson , they averaged 181 rushing yards per game and were the NFL’s No. 2 team on the ground during a 2-2 start. Since then, that number has dropped to 88.5 as Atlanta has lost three of its last four.
“Those numbers are a lot different,” Robinson said, “And it’s our job to get it back to what it needs to be.”
Altogether, the Falcons average 134.8 rushing yards per game and have barely dropped, now at No. 4 in the NFL due to their hot start.
“We have to do a better job of getting back to who we are in the run game,” said offensive coordinator Tommy Rees . “It starts with me in what we call and how we design it.”
Opponents have begun catching on.
And the solution has been simple: Stack the box.
“Teams, after those couple weeks, decided they were going to play us a certain way,” Rees admitted. “Part of our challenge is finding ways to run the ball even when those boxes are loaded. Because there are ways to do it.”
It’s led to the Falcons having their lowest yard per carry, with 2.8 in their win over the San Francisco 49ers and 3.5, which isn’t half bad, in a shutout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
“I think teams have done some things to limit some explosives,” Rees said. “I think our run efficiency has been pretty good, but we’ve lacked some of those explosive runs that really propelled us early in the season. So we got to find our opportunities for that and execute when those looks do come.”
It has forced the Falcons to play complementary football, putting the game in the hands of quarterback Michael Penix Jr.
He got on a heater for a couple of weeks, which could make defenses vulnerable. But then tossed four interceptions through a Tampa Bay monsoon last Sunday, Nov. 1.
Atlanta has been stuck at eight total rushing touchdowns since exploding for five against their Week 4 rivalry clash with the New Orleans Saints en route to scoring a season-high 45 points on Oct. 5.
Part of the reason is the absence of powerback Brian Robinson Jr. , who’s been out with a hamstring injury for the last two weeks. He returned to practice on Thursday and is listed as questionable for Sunday’s NFL Week 9 Madrid game against the Cincinnati Bengals .
His potential return could provide a boost to Atlanta’s short-yardage rushing attack and complement the wiggle of Bijan Robinson.
“For us, it’s our job as an offense to execute it and get down there so we can put the ball in the endzone,” Bijan Robinson explained how to improve. “Scoring in the red zone, outside the red zone, just making sure that we put the ball in there is important for us to win these games.”
Atlanta’s dynamic run game has a golden opportunity to return against Cincinnati. The Bengals allowed the 17th most rushing yards, at 122.3 per game.
After weeks of opposing defenses rinsing and repeating the same game plan, the Falcons know Cincy will attempt to stack the box to force them to pass.
“I want to make this run game lethal, dominate,” Robinson said.
“It doesn’t matter if teams come out playing however many in the box. That’s one of the focuses for teams to stop that. But for us, that’s what gets our teams going as a whole. When the run game is operating at a high level for this team, we’re just hard to beat.”
Falcons (3-5) versus Bengals (5-2) kicks off Sunday at 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time from Madrid, Spain’s Santiago Bernabéu Stadium. The NFL Network will televise the game.
Atlanta is the designated home team.

title: How Have Falcons Fared in International Games ahead of Date with Bengals in Spain?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are no strangers to playing football outside the United States, but their international track record has been far from perfect.
As they prepare for Sunday's matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain, the Falcons will have another opportunity to build on their international history while looking to get back on track.
Atlanta enters its matchup with Cincinnati holding a 2-3 record in regular-season games played outside the United States. The Falcons have played internationally in Toronto, London, and Berlin, with Sunday's contest marking their sixth regular season game abroad and fifth trip to Europe.
The Falcons' international history dates back to 2013, when they traveled to Toronto to face the Buffalo Bills. Atlanta came away with a 34-31 overtime victory, giving the organization a successful start to its international experience.
However, the Falcons struggled in their next two trips overseas.
In 2014, Atlanta traveled to London to face the Detroit Lions. Despite building a 21-0 halftime lead, the Falcons surrendered 22 unanswered points in the second half and suffered a heartbreaking 22-21 defeat.
Atlanta returned to London in 2021 and found a different result against the New York Jets. Behind Matt Ryan's 342 passing yards and two touchdowns, the Falcons secured a 27-20 victory. That remains their most recent international win.
The Falcons' third trip to London came in 2023, when they faced the Jacksonville Jaguars. Atlanta struggled offensively throughout the afternoon, suffering a 23-7 loss at Wembley Stadium.
Most recently, the Falcons traveled to Berlin, Germany, in 2025 to face the Indianapolis Colts. Atlanta suffered a 31-25 defeat, dropping its international record to 2-3. It was the Falcons' fourth straight defeat, dropping the team to 3-6 and helping seal the fate of former head coach Raheem Morris.
The Falcons find themselves on unfamiliar ground, but familiar territory, as the team brings a 3-5 record to Spain. Now, the Falcons have another opportunity to change that narrative in Madrid. They can return home, possibly in first place in the NFC South , or they can go 3-6 for the second consecutive year.
Although the international setting provides a unique experience for the organization, head coach Kevin Stefanski understands that the most important part of the trip is preparing his team for Sunday's matchup.
Atlanta is coming off a disappointing 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, a game in which Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions and the offense struggled to establish any consistency.
The Falcons will face a considerably different challenge against Cincinnati, particularly with quarterback Joe Burrow leading an explosive passing attack.
Speaking with reporters in Madrid on Wednesday, Stefanski discussed the challenges of preparing for the Bengals after last week's disappointing performance.
"This league is so unique in that week-to-week the challenges are different," Stefanski said. "So obviously the challenges of last week were last week and I don't expect those same challenges."
He continued by emphasizing the challenge of facing Burrow and Cincinnati's offense.
"But, listen, it's just a different deal when you go up against Joe Burrow and this offense and what they're capable of doing and how they play. It's definitely one that you have to be prepared for, and it's why we're working so hard."
The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans, with Burrow throwing for 462 yards and five touchdowns while adding a rushing score.
Stefanski also recognized the challenge presented by Cincinnati's receiving duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
"Outstanding players," Stefanski said. "Having two wide receiver playmakers like they have, I don't know if anybody in the league has guys like that."
For Atlanta, limiting explosive plays will be critical to having a chance against Cincinnati.
The Falcons also have an opportunity to give their international fans something to celebrate. Stefanski encouraged Spanish fans to support Atlanta, expressing his hope to see Madrid covered in the team's red and black colors.
Sunday's matchup at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium represents another important opportunity for the Falcons to expand their international presence while trying to improve their record abroad.
With Atlanta searching for a response following its shutout loss to Tampa Bay, a victory over Cincinnati would provide a much-needed boost and give the franchise its third international win in six attempts.

title: Why Falcons’ Nightmare in Tampa Could Help Them Against Bengals in Madrid
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are in pretty unique territory.
After playing a monsoon of a road game in a history-making 16-0 road loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Atlanta has gone abroad .
On Sunday, the Falcons (3-5) face the Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) in the NFL’s second-ever game in Madrid, Spain, for a Week 9 NFC versus AFC clash .
“The challenges week to week are so vastly different in this league,” said head coach Kevin Stefanski . “You have to be ready to adapt at any moment’s notice.”
Last Sunday, Nov. 1, Atlanta was on the receiving end of a shutout against the Bucs as a torrential downpour drenched the players in Raymond James Stadium.
The Falcons aren’t accustomed to rainy conditions. They play at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, which features a retractable roof that opens only in response to Atlanta’s weather and seasonal conditions.
Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions, and Tampa became the first NFL team to win a game without a completed pass since 1974.
Want to know how bad of a stat that is? Passing the football in wasn’t as prominent in 1974 as it is now.
What an encore for the spooky Halloween holiday that happened a day before the Falcons-Bucs game.
It brought Atlanta back down to earth just a week after knocking off the undefeated San Francisco 49ers 29-20 . Talk about a roller coaster of a season.
“You spend time on the game last week, and you have honest conversations with each other,” Stefanski reflected. “Certainly feel like that experience will serve us well moving forward.”
After struggling to adjust to the elements in Tampa, the Falcons now have another opportunity to prove they can handle unfamiliar circumstances, this time with a six-hour time difference and an unconventional travel schedule.
In Madrid, adaptability is once again the name of the game.
The Falcons took the eight-hour flight from Atlanta to Madrid on Tuesday and landed on Wednesday morning. They immediately began walkthroughs to prepare for battle against the streaking Bengals, winners of three straight games.
For normal road games, the Falcons typically leave on the day before the Sunday kickoff.
So everything on the itinerary has been moved up significantly to allow adequate rest and training.
“Going into an international game, a little bit of a different schedule,” Stefanski said. “For us as coaches and players, we see that as a positive.”
Falcons-Bengals kicks off at 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time, which is 3:30 p.m. Madrid time. Atlanta is the designated home team.
Light showers are expected, but the game is at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, which has a retractable roof. NFL Network is set to televise the game.

title: Where the Atlanta Falcons Stand in the NFC South Following Week 8
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are entering a critical stretch of their 2026 season, and their latest loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers has made the NFC South even tighter.
Atlanta suffered a 16-0 shutout against Tampa Bay on Sunday, November 1, missing an opportunity to claim first place in the division. With the regular season approaching its halfway point, the Falcons have limited room for error as they attempt to overtake not one, but two division rivals.
Despite the disappointing result, Atlanta remains within striking distance of the division lead. Here is where each team stands following Week 8.
Carolina currently holds the top spot in the division despite having a losing record. The Panthers suffered a loss to the Green Bay Packers, allowing Tampa Bay and Atlanta to remain within reach.
The Buccaneers currently hold the tiebreaker over Atlanta thanks to their 2-0 divisional record. The Falcons, meanwhile, are 1-2 against NFC South opponents, making their remaining divisional matchups increasingly important.
New Orleans sits at the bottom of the standings at 2-5, one game behind Atlanta and Tampa Bay.
The good news for Atlanta is that the NFC South remains wide open. The Falcons are just half a game behind Carolina and have plenty of opportunities to improve their position over the remaining weeks.
However, their latest loss exposed some concerns that need to be addressed. Atlanta struggled offensively against Tampa Bay, failing to score a single point while allowing the Buccaneers to control the game on the ground.
The Falcons cannot afford many more performances like that, particularly against divisional opponents.
Their divisional record will also be something to monitor. With Tampa Bay already owning a head-to-head victory, Atlanta needs to find a way to even the playing field when these teams meet again.
The Falcons will turn their attention to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 9. Atlanta will travel to Madrid, Spain, for an international matchup that presents an opportunity to get back into the win column.
A victory would move Atlanta to 4-5 and keep the team firmly in the NFC South conversation. The Panthers are 2.5-point underdogs at home to the Denver Broncos, who are coming off an emotional win against the Kansas City Chiefs.  The Buccaneers are six-point underdogs at Chicago on Sunday. Night.
There's a very real scenario where a 3-5 team leads the division. However, there's also a very real scenario where the Falcons are in first place next week. And as ridiculous as it sounds, if the Saints beat the Browns, as the only team favored in the NFC South this week, and the rest lose, New Orleans moves into a tie for first place.
For Atlanta, the formula is simple. The Falcons need to start stacking wins, improve their divisional record and take advantage of the opportunities ahead.
The NFC South is still within reach, but after Sunday's shutout, Atlanta needs to respond quickly if it wants to make a serious push for the division title.

full_text:

title: Should the Falcons Trade Tua Tagovailoa? The Case For and Against Moving QB
full_text:
As the trade deadline approaches in less than a week on Nov. 10, names have begun swirling about who will be on the move across the NFL.
From top stars like Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor to depth pieces for contenders, it’s always a fun part of the season.
One name that has ascended in trade talks is Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa . The seventh-year quarterback and former Pro Bowler has backed up Michael Penix Jr. this season after returning from an early-season oblique injury soon after being named the Week 1 starter.
He’s appeared in just one game for Atlanta, its 31-23 Week 5 loss to the Baltimore Ravens , where he threw the game-sealing overtime interception after Penix suffered a rib injury late in regulation. Tagovailoa has completed 2 of 3 pass attempts for 34 yards all year.
Tagovailoa arrived in Atlanta on a one-year deal worth $1.2 million after being released by the Miami Dolphins as a potential candidate to lead the Falcons’ (3-5) offense. Instead, he’s holding the clipboard on the sideline as the NFL reaches the halfway point of the season.
The question remains: Should Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham explore trade opportunities to move Tua?
Here’s the case for and against.
There’s a quarterback desperation in the NFL, especially in Baltimore. Wouldn’t it be wild to see Tagovailoa suit up for the team he recently gifted a win to, right?
But the Ravens are in quarterback purgatory right now. Two-time MVP Lamar Jackson has battled an ankle injury just about all season, and then injured his throwing-hand thumb while returning last week against the Buffalo Bills. Backup Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley suffered turf toe in the same game and is out for the season.
Now the Ravens turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to start moving forward. Sound familiar, Jack Strand fans?
The Ravens are currently last in the AFC North with a 4-4 record, but are two games behind No. 1 Pittsburgh Steelers. The division crown is very much still in play despite the quarterback injuries, and they're just one game behind for the seventh playoff spot.
Another team to watch is the Philadelphia Eagles after the debacle of handling Jalen Hurts’ blood clot situation. But they may actually mail it in on the season and become sellers at the deadline, outside of running back Saquon Barkley.
But regardless, if any team wants Tagovailoa, he’ll be easily absorbed on a cheap contract.
After a season that started with a Rolodex of quarterbacks – Cooper Rush, Jack Strand – maybe the Falcons shouldn’t trade Tagovailoa.
Andy Dalton is now the Falcons’ emergency third-string quarterback.
Atlanta needs the depth under center.
As much as fans don’t want to speak it out loud – knock on wood before reading further – Michael Penix Jr. does have durability issues with three torn ACL injuries. The Falcons also held their breath when he hurt his ribs against Baltimore.
Love him or hate him, but Tagovailoa is the only other quarterback currently on the roster outside of Penix that would give Atlanta a shot to win games. Let’s not conveniently forget it wasn’t long ago he was leading the NFL in passer rating, yardage, and completion percentage. His passer rating last season in Miami was better than both Penix and Kirk Cousins' passer rating for the Falcons last season.
If the Falcons had benched Penix for tossing four interceptions , Tagovailoa may have come in to throw a couple more, but he’s the best option.
Plus, is the return that the team would get on the trade even worth it? Moving a quarterback getting paid for a little over a million probably won’t move the needle much. We’re talking like Day 3 NFL Draft picks here.
That’s not going to help the Falcons right now, in a year when they’ve been on a roller-coaster ride but are still in play for the NFC South division title.
Hear out offers and inquiries if they come.
But if it’s not a bona fide move or a heist that’ll upgrade the Falcons, like the Gervon Dexter Sr. trade , stand pat.
For those pro-Tua, he adds some insurance to a quarterback room that Atlanta could still very well be in the NFL Draft market for in 2027.
For the anti-Tuas, just wait on it. He’ll be off the team in a matter of months and searching for a new home.

title: Falcons Place Samson Ebukam on Injured Reserve, Make Additional Roster Move
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are making multiple roster moves as they prepare for Sunday’s matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain.
Atlanta has placed edge rusher Samson Ebukam on injured reserve following a hamstring injury suffered during Sunday’s 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The move means Ebukam will miss at least the next four games before becoming eligible to return.
The veteran defensive end was already expected to miss the Bengals matchup after head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed Monday that Ebukam was dealing with a hamstring injury . The decision to place him on injured reserve indicates the Falcons will be without one of their key defensive contributors for an extended period.
Through seven appearances this season, Ebukam recorded 2.5 sacks, 11 combined tackles, two tackles for loss, and nine quarterback hits. His presence has been valuable to Atlanta’s defensive front, particularly as a pass rusher.
The Falcons will now have to find ways to replace his production while he recovers.
Atlanta also made a corresponding series of roster moves, signing defensive end Drake Jackson back to the practice squad after releasing him from the active roster Monday.
Jackson’s return provides the Falcons with additional defensive line depth as they navigate Ebukam’s absence. The former second-round pick has experience as an edge defender and gives Atlanta another option within its practice squad.
To make room for Jackson, the Falcons released offensive lineman Colby Sorsdal from the practice squad.
The moves came one day after the Falcons released Jackson and defensive lineman Jared Ivey from their active roster as the team prepared for the return of James Pearce Jr. from his league suspension.
Pearce’s reinstatement gives the Falcons another option along the defensive front, but losing Ebukam creates a significant hole in the rotation.
The Falcons enter Week 9 at 3-5, looking to turn things around after a disappointing shutout loss to Tampa Bay.
Atlanta travels to Madrid to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, with its defensive front facing another test as the team works through its latest personnel changes.
Ebukam’s absence will put additional pressure on the remaining defensive ends to generate consistent quarterback pressure and help Atlanta get back on track.
Darius has a Master's in Communications from Georgia State and has previous experience covering the Atlanta Falcons with 3 Point Conversion and covering the NFL with On SI.

title: Updated Atlanta Falcons Draft Position, Top 3 Needs, and Mock Draft Selections
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons had a chance to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South on Sunday and put a stake in the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' chances of winning the division for the fifth time in six seasons.
Instead of becoming the only team with a .500 record and dropping Tampa Bay to 2-6, the Falcons find themselves sitting at 3-5 and looking up in the standings at both the Buccaneers (3-5) and the Carolina Panthers (3-4). Both teams have the tiebreaker over the Falcons via head-to-head record.
If there's a silver lining to this year's struggles, it's that the Falcons have a full allotment of draft picks after not having a first-round pick in 2026. New general manager Ian Cunningham's first class has been a success, with big-time contributions from linebackers Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr., selected in the fourth and sixth rounds, respectively.
Cornerback Avieon Terrell, the team's first selection, has struggled to get healthy, but has played well when available, and wide receiver Zachariah Branch has shown flashes. Atlanta lost sixth-round defensive tackle Anterio Thompson to a medical condition, and seventh-round offensive tackle Ethan Onianwa has been getting experience on special teams.
Looking towards next season, the Falcons currently sit with the No. 13 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The jury is still out on Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback as he uses this season to prove he can be the long-term answer for Atlanta and keep them out of the quarterback market in the offseason.
Sunday's game in the Tampa monsoon notwithstanding, he's played well enough for the Falcons to look in another direction in the first round, but he'll need to bounce back from Sunday's four-interception performance and stay healthy for 15 games.
Taking quarterback off the table, offensive tackle is the biggest need on this team early in the draft. Jake Matthews is 34 years old, and the iron man has shown signs of Father Time catching up to him this year. At right tackle, Jawaan Taylor is on a one-year contract and scheduled to be a free agent at the end of the season.
Cornerback is arguably the No. 2 need on this team. The Falcons selected Terrell at No. 48, but he's the first Day 1 or Day 2 cornerback the Falcons have taken since they drafted his brother in the first round in 2020. Injuries forced Mike Hughes into being the Falcons' No. 1 option at times this year, and he should be at best a No. 3 and probably best suited for a No. 4.
Nickel has been a problem too. Billy Bowman Jr. was drafted for the position in 2025, but he's only been available for 10 of 25 games the Falcons have played since being drafted in the fourth round out of Oklahoma. The Falcons have had to piece together the secondary from game to game, and they need another infusion of talent and depth.
Wide receiver comes in at No. 3 on the team's list of needs. Drake London is set at No. 1 for the foreseeable future. Jahan Dotson was signed as a free agent this offseason. However, he's better suited to a slot / No. 3 role, and he's getting paid like it. Branch is a nice addition, but the Falcons need more size, explosiveness, and depth.
Recent mock drafts have the Falcons addressing their biggest need at offensive tackle. On SI draft analyst Justin Melo has Atlanta taking Lance Heard from the surprising No. 7 Kentucky Wildcats.
"Atlanta Falcons offensive line coach Bill Callahan will have a say if the organization drafts an offensive tackle. He'll love Kentucky's Lance Heard, who fits his mold from a size and physicality perspective. This is all about getting a Jake Matthews replacement," Melo wrote On SI Draft.
Tankathon also has the Falcons going with an offensive tackle in Texas Longhorns product Trevor Goosby . Goosby is out for the remainder of the 2026 season after having surgery to repair a torn left patellar tendon. Early this season, he was considered a top-10 prospect, but his stock has fallen a bit with the injury.
If the Falcons are picking No. 13 in April, it equates to a 7-10 or 8-9 type of record. It's hard to picture this team going 7-10 if Michael Penix Jr. has an excellent second half of the season.
That brings up a couple of what-if scenarios that Cunningham will ponder during the draft process.
1. Can Penix establish himself as a franchise quarterback and the team still struggles this year? Recent history would say "no." When the Falcons have gotten good quarterback play, they've won. When they've gotten bad quarterback play, they've lost. A 7-10 season would likely mean Penix struggled in the second half.
2. If they're picking No. 13, is there a quarterback available that would be worth taking without reaching?
The Rams used the Falcons' No. 13 overall pick in the last draft to take quarterback Ty Simpson out of Alabama. That felt like a reach, and the Falcons got good value for their trade of that pick in James Pearce Jr.
But this is supposed to be a deeper draft class at quarterback, though that sentiment seems to be waning as the season rolls along.
Melo has Arch Manning in range, selected by the Arizona Cardinals at No. 12. There's a better-than-average chance he's not in the draft and returns to college football. The Cleveland Browns select Trinidad Chambliss at No. 16 out of Ole Miss, and he's the final quarterback taken in the first round.
There's a scenario where the Falcons would like to draft a quarterback, but there isn't one they like enough in the middle of the draft, and they find themselves stuck in purgatory again.
The best-case scenario for the Falcons is that Penix plays well for the remainder of the season, and Atlanta finds itself picking in the late teens or even early 20s. Then they can address one of their needs with the prospect they like best. Goosby is still on Melo's board at No. 24. Offensive tackle Zereoue of Utah is taken by the Panthers at No. 19.
Cornerbacks Ellis Robinson IV from Georgia and Kelley Jones of Mississippi State go to the Cowboys and Bengals at No. 20 and No. 23 respectively.
The game on Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals has a must-win feeling to it. Win and move to 4-5, and the Falcons will be right in the thick of the NFC South.
Lose and drop to 3-6, and these mock drafts start becoming a lot more interesting.

title: Ravens Coach Jesse Minter Must Cede Play Calling Duties: And 3 Other Takeaways From Thursday's Debacle
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will need a full reboot on defense for 2027, and they have truly needed one since losing the AFC Championship Game in 2023, and Thursday night’s shameful display should be all the data points any reasonable front office would need to start dismembering this roster ahead of next week’s trade deadline.
The defense is a joke, allowing over eight yards per play in the first half and free runners all over the middle of the field and no semblance of a pass rush. Rookie head coach Jesse Minter looks like a foil for a power-hungry front office, because he is, and pushing out John Harbaugh to hire someone failing miserably as a head coach and a defensive coordinator is quite a trick. Baltimore lost for the fourth straight game, with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano pretending to play quarterback this time; they head to Week 10 with two AFC victories all season (horrible Colts and Titans) and they have become an utterly noncompetitive football entity.
Losing Lamar Jackson for the season (he isn’t coming back to play meaningless games after going to IR with a thumb injury) isn’t the problem The defense that is stocked with bad football players (far too many either overpaid by failure GM Eric DeCosta or over-drafted by failure GM Eric DeCosta), Minter has made them worse than they were under scapegoat coordinator Zach Orr the last two years and there is no reason for hope.
Malaki Starks, a supposed difference maker, got destroyed when he actually had to show up in coverage, on a 50-yard TD pass to Parker Washington that made it 17-3 at the end of the first and effective ended this game. The final was 33-10 at M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore (4-5) has now won three times in its last 12 home games and is 6-9 since last Thanksgiving and has been utterly noncompetitive against winning teams for years.
“Obviously, the results are not acceptable,” Minter said amid many rambling answers in which if he wasn’t excusing a lot of this garbage he was coming to close to it than he should.
Here’s what we learned from this slopfest, in which Kyle Hamilton left and did not return (Minter said he didn't have an update):
Derrick Henry running the Wild Cat is cute, but Jacoby Brissett, who just lost his job to Gardner Minshew and couldn’t function against the woeful Cowboys defense is fixing nothing. The Ravens have a lot of time between now and Tuesday afternoon’s deadline to make the decisions that need to be made.
Henry has to go . Ronnie Stanley, a middling left tackle nearing the end of his career, should go if at all possible . Calais Campbell, 40, is wasting the final year of his career here. Rashod Bateman should have been gone years ago. DeCosta having the guts to lecture the media and fans on how Marlon Humphrey (he is getting clowns by former Ravens players and coaches all over the country) was a $19M corner and he got picked on immediately in this game and has to be benched for TJ Tampa ( no one is trading for Humphrey , who got beat by a blocking TE for a 50 yard gain to open the game, seriously).
This is an unserious franchise that takes its fans for fools. I expect zero accountability from the failed GM or his boss, the billionaire owner who couldn't be bothered to do much during the coaching search, but if they don’t starting trying to reposition this franchise before they host the Chargers on Monday Night Football, it’s a new low.
Minter delivered a long filabuster about this team not being as awful as it clearly is when asked about direction at the deadline, which sums up their general MO when it comes to parable they push in Owings Mills and reality.
If you players are going to quiet quit from week to week, and the Ravens won’t admit defeat that they put together a cheap, naïve and sophomoric coaching staff (only the Ravens and Dolphins had no former NFL head coaches employed ) and they won’t bring in former head coaches to help Minter, then its time to let his “defensive coordinator,” Anthony Weaver, do the job and call the defense.
Minter is not anything close to a competent or even barely-functional head coach. He needs to learn how to have a spine and hold players accountable and establish protocols and standards in practices and games. He can’t be trying to fix a defense he keeps breaking at the same time. Pic a lane, but Minter has been an unquestioned disaster to this point and seems not cut out for this job in way form to this point.
They gave up 223 yards in the first half in the rain, at home, and had an 11% pressure rate (impossible, right?) with their alleged “closer,” $30M a year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson making no impact, again. This after having Josh Allen and Joe Burrow have perfect passer ratings in the second half against them the previous two weeks, and Deshaun Watson overcoming a 10-point lead in the second half to get DeCosta-ed ion that game.
DeCosta wanted a total puppet after winning the power struggle with Harbaugh after last year’s pathetic season. He got it. The middle of the field was open the entire game and the defense has no soul.
Part of the reason Minter is so horribly out of his depth that he can’t command a presence from this team and get them to focus and show attention to detail. Yeah, not with this crew.
They had a silly penalty on a return on special teams to back up Fagnano way deeper than he needed to be. They jumped off sides on a fourth-and-short when this was still a football game to give Jacksonville a big first down. They had false starts on successive plays in the first half, with veteran tight end Mark Andrews ( a colossal DeCosta mistake who did nothing of note again and botched a direct snap) committing the second one – he leads all tight ends in that category and in drop percentage.
In a desperate spot to start the second half … we got yet another brutal false start to further compromise a QB who was not ready for this assignment. But when your most overpaid players are also your worst players, and they are never held to account, then why wouldn’t these issues permeate the entire roster. A fumble on a kickoff return was as nice touch, too.
"It's ownership of players and coaches that keep happening … the pre-snap penalties are unnaceptable," Minter offered. Funny thing is they are acceptable but the biggest culprits - Andrews and Stanley - are made men from the GM and beyond reproach, apparently.
After the rookie offensive coordinator badly embarrassed himself and the entire organization with ridiculous play calling Sunday in playing a key role in his quarterback room getting decimated, Doyle finally grasped the severity of the situation Thursday.
He was committed to Wild Cat and gimmick plays and throws behind the line of scrimmage. He leaned heavily into tackle eligible and 13 personnel (three tight ends), trying to bleed the clock and keep this game as close as he could for as long as he could. Made sense, especially with Fagnano’s right ankle heavily taped in the rain.
Still wasn’t nearly enough, but at least he tried this time. Once the Jaguars opened up a 14-point lead Fagnano had to drop back (he threw one pass beyond the line of scrimmage in the first quarter) and he was under constant duress and it just got uglier from there.
Fagnano is incredibly raw and limited and even with a rudimentary game plan and all that scheming, in a short week he had no chance against this defense. Fagnano was quite poor in the second half. Brissett will start in primetime for this fallen franchise next.

title: Four Ways Ravens Offense Needs To Adjust Without A Mobile Quarterback Moving Forward
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be without the greatest dual-threat quarterback in NFL history for the foreseeable future and potentially the remainder of the 2026 season. On their first offensive play in a Week 8 road loss to the Buffalo Bills , two-time league MVP Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery.
This setback officially landed him, as well as his primary backup, Tyler Huntley, who suffered a significant turf toe injury in the same game, on injured reserve on Thursday . Both signal callers will require surgery to address their respective physical ailments.
While the Ravens are slated to start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football on a short week, they are reportedly finalizing a trade to acquire journeyman veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals.
Bringing in the well-traveled career backup and occasional spot-starter gives the Ravens a proven commodity under center with ties to the coaching staff, as he played under current quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork last year in Arizona. What it doesn't provide is a player at the position who is anywhere near a threat in the run game, like Jackson or even Huntley.
This means that the Ravens and first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle will need to adapt their plan of attack moving forward to better suit the strengths of their current quarterback room with Brissett and Fagnano, who is also more of a traditional pocket passer. Here are four key adjustments they need to make to give the offense its best chance to thrive without the greatest force multiplier in the game for the time being, and possibly the rest of the season.
The Ravens' rushing attack has struggled mightily to run the ball with any consistency and gain consistent traction on the ground over the past three weeks after posting a season-high 208 rushing yards in their first game without Jackson, following his high ankle sprain. They've averaged just 82 rushing yards during their three-game losing streak and will need to make five-time Pro Bowl running back Derrick Henry even more of a focal point of their offensive approach moving forward. The future Hall of Famer has been the subject of several trade rumors since Jackson's injury, but with him gone, Henry is the last star left standing in the Ravens' backfield.
No matter who is under center for this team for the rest of the season, Henry should be carrying the ball early and often, especially now that the offensive line is getting healthier and building more cohesion, with first-round rookie Vega Ioane slated to return from a one-week absence and two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens getting more acclimated since being acquired via trade.
Despite not having Jackson's electric mobility at their disposal, they still have several playmakers on that side of the ball who can make explosive plays in space with the ball in their hands. At the top of that list is two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, who, even after being held without a catch for the first time in his four-year career last week, still ranks eighth in the league in receiving yards. Since losing veteran blocking specialist tight end Durham Smythe to a season-ending torn Achilles, trying to run the ball or just simply operate out of multiple tight end sets, especially out of condensed formations, has been inefficient and downright futile far too often.
The Ravens should still keep the under center element in their offense to preserve and amplify the threat of play-action, but as far as personnel packages go, they should look to spread their formations out with multiple receiver sets. It'll force opposing defenses to have more ground to cover, lighten the boxes Henry has to run into at the line of scrimmage, and get more explosive wideouts such as veteran Rashod Bateman, rookie Ja'Kobi Lane and third-year pro Devontez Walker the ball more.
After having three quarterbacks go down in one game due to poor pass protection just four days ago, including the face of the franchise, the Ravens' offensive line can't be trusted to hold up for deep dropbacks or handle basic stunts, twists and blitzes until they prove otherwise. Doyle should be dialing up quick-developing plays and overemphasizing the necessity for his quarterbacks to not hold onto the ball too long after seeing two of them get strip-sacked this past Sunday. His screen designs and sequencing have been one of the most impressive aspects of his new offense this year. Leaning more into getting his dynamic receivers, running backs and tight ends in space with convoys in front of them should increase even more.
While the soon-to-be 34-year-old Brissett isn't nearly as fleet of foot as the Ravens' injured first and second-string quarterbacks, he is among the best in the league at using his legs to pick up first downs on sneaks. Baltimore's struggles to convert on third and fourth and short are a major reason why they've struggled to sustain drives and finish them in the end zone without Jackson under center, dating back to last year.
Brissett leads the NFL with 17 quarterback sneaks, four more than the Bills' Josh Allen, and is responsible for picking up 16 first downs and scoring a touchdown rushing through eight games. Having him lined up behind Jurgens, who successfully ran the famous 'Tush Push' play with Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles, should be the Ravens' go-to play anytime they find themselves needing two or fewer yards to move the chains. Against the Jaguars this week, with Fagnano on a bad ankle, the Ravens should line up one of their tight ends under center in those situations.

title: One Move The Ravens Can't Afford To Get Wrong At The NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens can be myopic and simplistic and sophomoric – and that’s been their brand as an ownership group and front office group, for the most part, the further removed they are from their heyday under legendary general manager Ozzie Newsome.
They can keep pretending that people like Eric DeCosta, who made a career getting promotions by leveraging Newsome’s accomplishments , have this team on the cusp of a Super Bowl or get real about an aging and bloated payroll, the worst salary cap situation in the NFL for 2027 ( it’s not even close ) and another showdown looming with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, whose contract talks they have butchered since the became eligible for his first extension back in 2020, and who can decided whatever he wants in 207 basically by virtue of some of the more unique contract language in the NFL ( as explained thoroughly here) .
They can come to grips with the fact they enter Thursday night’s home game against Jacksonville as 10-point dogs for a reason, and that them getting De-Costed 17 times since this feckless front office took over for Newsome (a historic pace of blowing double-digit leads in the second half to lose) is not some fluke. They should get real about the fact that come midnight, they’ll likely be 3-9 in their last 12 games at M&T Bank Stadium and 6-9 since last Thanksgiving. As it stands now, they are 3-7 in their last 10 against winning teams and win 33% of their games during Jackson’s tenure when he doesn’t start and he’s not throwing another pass this season with the way to rest of this will play out.
So the biggest mistake for them to avoid is simple.
It’s the same mistake they keep making when the owner fired a Hall of Fame coach to replace them with a bunch of kids in a total start-up to produce the worst second-half football in the NFL, but implied it’s a Super Bowl roster and called DeCosta the best GM in the league and said he “bats .800” in his personnel transactions so who cares about the whiffs. The team president said Minter had the immediate pedigree to keep them on their Lombardi path and DeCosta thumped his chest about his offensive line and ability to get Jackson signed and how Marlon Humphrey was worth $19M when he spoke before the season began.
The biggest mistake they can’t make is to continue to believe their own self-aggrandizing and self-mythologizing BS and do something about embracing change and fixing their cultural disease for once. The biggest mistake they can’t make is try to continue gaslighting and obfuscating the fans and taking them for fools, rather than actually start repositioning the team for the future.
It will be next to impossible, mind you, given the abysmal way they structure contracts and how DeCosta plays favorites with who he overpays. They are going to stink for years to come no matter what they do now. But if things are ever going to change here – they won’t, by the way, with these people in charge (it’s tragically similar to the Orioles across the board) – waiting til the offseason serves no one . For a multitude of reasons.
This ain’t much, especially consider this is a $370M payroll that, according to Bisciotti, is the envy of football with a true mastermind managing it. The Ravens are remarkably screwed this offseason, and punting all of this til January because optics and trying to protect their alleged reputation (so many in the NFL knew DeCosta is vastly over his skis before he took the reigns) is an afront to their covenant with the people who strain to make all of this possible.
And, yeah, this sell-off should include Bisciotti selling the team, cashing his chips, and finding a motivated and hungry and focused and sharp new steward of the franchise, like he used to be. But that was a long time ago, now. Start with moving Derrick Henry and do whatever you can to get something for Ronnie Stanley, too.
It’s imperative there is a runway to finding out if Trenton Simpson or Teddye Buchanan can wear the green dot and replace Roquan Smith who hasn’t been an impact football player since DeCosta vastly overpaid him. This is a blight and embarrassment either way, but we knew they are too prideful to bench him, and no one wants anything to do with this contract. They can spite themselves and their future by playing silly games (DeCosta always does), we’ll see how it plays out.
Same needs to start happening with tackle Carson Vinson and tight end Matthew Hibner and receiver Elijah Sarratt (going to make your fourth-round pick inactive on a terrible offense every week in a seven-win-at-best season?). It needs to happen for young vets like corner TJ Tampa, and receiver Devontez Walker with a long runway as a starter.
You know how you start to clean up a culture of entitlement and quitting in the second half and showing no pride at home and empowering losing football players who seem to enjoy trolling Ravens fans more than actually doing their jobs (Humphrey) – you admit it is your brand and you hold people accountable. I know it’s tough when the head coach comes off as a puppet (well) and the offensive coordinator also seems horribly out of his depth , but if you don’t want the locker room walking all over them forever, you do something now.
Call out the player stupidity and lack of effort at times, and get a former NFL head coach here to start coaching up your coaches on how to lead and message properly. Bench people immediately, in game (I know DeCosta is a preening annoyance on the sidelines, but he can’t stop you from doing the right thing in-game). The longer you continue this charade – and keeping all of your biggest mistakes past the deadline would be the most pathetic thing possible – the worse it will only become.
