title: Ravens Week 8 Rookie Report: Undrafted QB Sees First Regular Season Action Under Dire Circumstances
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's 36-10 road loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. They are in an AFC North division in which every other team has a record above .500, and after falling to 4-4, they deservedly sit at the bottom of the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. First-round stud interior offensive lineman Olaivavega Ioane missed his first game with an MCL sprain. The only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and fifth-round cornerback Chandler Rivers. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his fourth week of eligibility and seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
While the undrafted rookie had dressed for each of the Ravens' first seven games, it was as the emergency No. 3 quarterback, and in this game, it didn't even take a full half for his services to be needed after both of the team's veterans got hurt . Fagnano checked into the game for the offense's second drive of the second quarter and had an exciting start with back-to-back completions of 10-plus yards and then it kind of went downhill from there, largely due to poor pass protection.
Nonetheless, the preseason darling who earned his way onto the roster showed a lot of grit and toughness as he eventually got banged up with an ankle injury before this one was over, getting sacked three times. Fagnano finished 10-of-21 for 91 passing yards and an ill-advised interception off a tipped pass while he was staring down his intended target. The most impressive throw of his regular-season debut performance was a 22-yard completion to wide receiver Rashod Bateman on a key third down in the third quarter that he threw with anticipation and had 15 yards tacked onto the chunk play after he got taken out by the knees by Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver.
Joe Fagnano with a very nice anticipation throw outside the numbers here. If he can make this throw, he can make all the throws. Give him protection and he'll be just fine. pic.twitter.com/CuEoaASCbq
The second-rounder saw the sharp uptick in playing time on defense that many expected after the Ravens lost sack leader and stout run-defending fourth-year pro Tavius Robinson to a season-ending pectoral injury. Young's 35 defensive snaps set a new career high and accounted for 42.7% of the team total, and he played a key role in limiting the Bills' rushing attack to just 3.7 yards per rush with how well he set the edge and forced runs back inside. He finished with an assisted tackle on Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen on a quarterback sneak for no gain on third and short. Young was the Ravens' highest-graded rookie defender and second-highest overall, according to Pro Football Focus , with a grade of 71.8.
Decade long starter in the NFL pic.twitter.com/Kje0Z148Lh
With all the turnover at the quarterback position, the third-rounder didn't get many chances to make many plays in the passing game. He hauled in his lone target for 13 yards and a first down before getting pushed after moving the ball deep into the red zone to the Buffalo seven-yard line.
The fourth-rounder played the second-fewest offensive snaps of the season in his second week back from a hand injury. Hibner was targeted as a pass-catcher for the first time in his last three appearances but didn't record a catch. He had an up-and-down performance as a blocker in the running game, helping spring Derrick Henry for the Ravens' only touchdown of the game and struggling to execute other insert blocks fully.
Nice cleanup block by Matt Hibner, giving Derrick Henry room to cut back for the TD. pic.twitter.com/fdrWadzTxp
The fifth-rounder played his fewest offensive snaps since Week 2 for the second week in a row with 13, and once again, that didn't stop him from making his presence felt as he recorded at least one catch in his fourth straight game. He reeled in one of his two targets for 15 yards on a diving catch for Fagnano's first completion. Cuevas was overthrown by primary backup quarterback Tyler Huntley on his first target and finished as the Ravens' highest-graded rookie and overall offensive player per PFF, with an overall grade of 84.7.
The sixth-round specialist had a strong outing with five punts for 249 yards, including a season-high average of 49.8 yards per punt and a long of 62, tying for his longest of the season. Eckley didn't have any touchbacks and was able to pin the Bills back inside their own 20-yard line twice.
You have to look pretty hard for a silver lining with the Ravens right now. But I’ve found one. With Lamar Jackson out, we’re likely to punt more. That’ll give Ryan Eckley the reps he needs to settle in and find the consistency his game needs to truly succeed at the NFL level! pic.twitter.com/V4pcUK5ZZT
The undrafted free agent saw double his previous career-high in defensive snaps played with 34, which accounted for 41.5% of the team's total, and his 22 snaps on special teams ranked first among all rookies and was the second-most on the team. He has upside.

title: The Ravens Anointed Trey Hendrickson As A $30M/Year Closer. Turns Out He's An Opener
full_text:
When the Ravens got embarrassed by the Bills on Sunday, their second-half defense, worst in the NFL, up to its usual antics, coaches and execs around the league took note.
The Ravens lack of pass protection and competent play calling had a role in three quarterbacks getting injured in about a 12-play span – highly unusual stuff – and once again they had been unable to stop an opponent from marching all over the field on them after halftime, the same collapsing, listless unit that has been torpedoing this franchise for years. All of that was supposed to change, of course, after firing a legion of respected coaches, hiring young defensive wizard Jesse Minter as head coach/defensive play caller and, after raising the ire of folks around the NFL with the shady way they withdrew from a blockbuster trade for Maxx Crosby then giving Trey Hendrickson $60M for two years to attack the quarterback.
Minter immediately coronated the 32-year-old his “closer” with a checkered recent injury history and an ugly end to his esteemed Bengals career with holdouts and hold-ins and not a lot of impact football lately. There were plenty of reasons Hendrickson’s market was soft, allowing Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta’s stunt withdraw from the trade over alleged health concerns, and then having the audacity to claim to his fans that he had plans to land both payers.
On Sunday night, after that 36-10 defeat with the Bills averaging 7.5 yards/play in the second half and with Josh Allen under no duress like so many opposing QBs before him, one NFL GM noted the Ravens might be getting what was coming to them. “Karma,” he noted from how they handled Crosby. A longtime NFL head coach who was watching, used the same word: “Karma is real,” he noted.
Whether karma or not, Year 1 with Hendrickson has been a disaster.
He has been a no-show in the fourth quarter all season, and by Week 9, that season is effectively over. Whatever he does from here on out – extended garbage time – is tainted. Rather than put games away, the Ravens have extended their pathetic run of getting DeCosta-ed – blowing double-digit leads in the second half to lose. Hendrickson has been the antithesis of an opener; like his rookie head coach he has been a no-show when it matters most.
The Raiders have to pry Crosby off the field; Hendrickson got hurt in his first game for Baltimore, his production tailed, he missed time with a surgical procedure, and he has as many sacks as Roquan Smith (two). He hasn’t has an impact moment, he was absolutely shutdown and invisible in his big “revenge’ game with the Bengals, and the Ravens better hope he isn’t aging fast, and has a resurgence next year, because, again, 2026 is a wrap (and DeCosta should he trading veterans).
We’ve been suggesting for weeks on “The Daily Flock Show” how the Ravens should handle this. Maybe they’ll start to adjust. You’d think allowing the most points of any team in the second half, and the second-highest passer rating, and second most big plays and ranking 30th in yards per play might prompt somebody there to try something else.
Here’s what they need to do:
Hendrickson is generating a pass-rush rate near 21% in the first half of games. In the fourth quarter, he has just five pressures on 43 pass rush reps, a woeful 12%. The Ravens have three fourth-quarter sacks as a team (Ethan Burke, undrafted free agent, safety Malaki Starks and Tavius Ronbinson, on IR but still leading the team in sacks.
It’s not like Hendrickson is taking games over early, but he is definitely effective. The injury is probably a big deal, so then get him on more of a pitch count, and be willing to blitz more to keep him fresh. His age was a serious concern for teams in free agency. He isn’t getting home late in games, and he isn’t opening things up for others; the Ravens rank 27th in pressure rate as a team in the fourth quarter.
They need to ration his pass-rushh reps better and accept that he'd probably a designated pass rusher, no matter how much they paid him.
DeCosta made a big reach in the second round for edge run-defender, Zion Young, rather than address his massive center need (he could have had his pick). He needs to have the guts to pay him on run downs or just early downs in general, and stop pretending Hendrickson is something he’s not. He’s never been good against the run.
Longtime Ravens defensive coordinator Wink Martindale – very familiar with Hendrickson and the person who created the defense Minter is running, cut to the quick with what he sees on the film:
“Going against him when he was with the Bengals I think he is a very good pass rusher, and that's it,” Martindale told me on the show . “That's what he is. I think he's a third down, second-and-long type guy because he wants to get to the quarterback. The problem is, when they're playing in these games, especially with (backup) Snoop (Huntley) at quarterback, they've got the whole playbook that they're facing.
“They're not getting leads where people have to throw the ball to get back in the game. And when you get selfish, and you're rushing a passer on a run play, it exposes players. And that's what I'm seeing. That's what I'm seeing with him.”
Teams are going to start road grading the Ravens more and the Ravens aren’t going to win many games, so that closer stuff is basically out the door, anyway. They aren’t getting $10M out of Hendrickson this year, let alone $30M, and they are stuck with it all over again next season. Better find a way to make this age gracefully, while Crosby remains one of the unique every-down edge defenders in the NFL, and incredibly durable at that.
Turns out the Ravens started getting De Costa-ed even before the season began.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Things The Ravens Must Do To Upset The Jaguars Thursday
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are almost certain to lose Thursday night.
I’m not going to try to pretend otherwise. As best I can tell, since 2000, the Ravens have only bene an underdog of 10 points or more at home on three occasions – 2007 at the height of the Tom Brady Patriots dynasty, 2015 against the Legion of Boom Seahawks (with Jimmy Clausen at QB) and also that season against the Steelers (with Ryan Mallett at QB).
But they will play the game, with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano making his first NFL start before anyone could have possibly thought imaginable, and crazy things can happen in professional sports and there is at least a case to be build that the Ravens pull ff a shocker against the second-best scoring defense in the NFL. It’s kinda flimsy, sure, but it wouldn’t be the most bizarre in the world (although I do feel compelled to acknowledge that the Ravens are 3-7 in their last 10 home games.
Perhaps this is Fagnano's only shot before journeyman Jacoby Brissett takes over. This also might be the last time the Ravens (4-4) sit at .500 for quite some time unless they break some tendencies and experiment with new concepts:
Dude needs to acknowledge what Wink Martindale and Marvin Lewis discussed with us – trying to get this bad roster with aging players on bloated contracts to take to his zone concepts and playing all that dime coverage, without getting DBs involved nearly enough in the pass rush, ain’t working. It’s failing, miserably.
If you are going to go down, go down fighting with a chance to impact the QB. Because Trey Hendrickson hasn’t been a “closer” by a long shot (0 sacks and 12% pressure rate in  fourth quarter) and this second half defense gets not nearly enough pressure and never gets its hands on the football. The Ravens have forced one second-half turnover all season, tied for worst in the NFL. Time to bring some heat and activate Kyle Hamilton and Marlon Humphrey from the slot and start attacking with Trenton Simpson from the second level and get out of the dime looks.
Trevor Lawrence will carve up the zone stuff. Check out these splits:
Lawrence vs Bitz : 44.3% Success Rate, 57.6% completions, 12% off target throws, 87.2 rating
Lawrence When Not Blitzed: 53.2 Success, 69.7% comp, 7.6% off target, 127.7 rating
At least die by the sword. Doing it Minter’s way still has the Ravens allowing the second most big plays of any NFL defense in the second half of games.
Have Fagnano drop back five straight times in this game like you did in Buffalo . I dare you. Against a better defense with a joke defensive line. The Jags are dealing with some defensive line injuries and the only chance the Ravens have is to play keep away and bleed the clock. There has to be volume in the run game and Doyle will have to go old school for this to work.
Jumbo packages, extra offensive linemen a ton of blocking tight end Nick Vannett. If they can keep it close that way, maybe the defense actually makes a play late. They aren’t going to bully the Jags at the line of scrimmage if they do not commit extra manpower to do it. The line has far more of a fighting chance picking up three yards on the ground than doing anything downfield.
Spare me the genius talk. Let’s have a fairy competent game plan for a change and some cogent adjustments and he should probably be on the sidelines after producing three points in the second half the last three weeks. What they have been trying with Derrick Henry has been an epic fail , and they need to commit to tackle eligible quite a bit.
The Ravens haven’t had any jam in the return game for a looooong time. Thursday would be a nice time to change that up. And Jake Moody gets what could be his last chance to show he can be an NFL kicker with Tyer Loop on IR. They’re going to make some long field goals in this goal with this QB situation, undoubtedly.
Jacksonville is feeling pretty good right now. Two weeks in London, bye week, running away with the AFC South, had to exert themselves for maybe 10 minutes in a 42-7 win over the Colts Sunday and now traveling on a short week for what everyone thinks will be a beatdown game.
Yeah, they might be a little flat and think they can just show up. Might be vulnerable to a punch in the face. We’ll see if the Ravens deliver it, but this could be a letdown spot and if it is Baltimore must seize the moment and use it to its advantage. There is no way they can play this game from behind and win.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Two Ravens Players Who Benefit Most From The Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
Jacoby Brissett is not going to save the Ravens lost season.
He might not even keep it afloat much longer. And, saddest of all, he might soon meet a similar outcome to what befell all three Ravens quarterbacks who had to drop back behind this offensive line on Sunday – immediate pain and, in two cases, the end of their season . Those IR stints for Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Snoop Huntley (toe) are what led to the minor trade for Brissett (the Ravens only assume $650,00 in cash and cap charges; something even they can withstand) who had been demoted to third string in Arizona after a fairly remarkable career resurgence in 2025.
Brissett, 33, is near the end of his career, he is not going to be able to do a ton outside the pocket and he lacks the running skill now needed to unlock a ground game that is threatening to be among the worst in the NFL in Derrick Henry’s age 32 season, where most careers died at that position and all would behind this OL ( they should trade him to a contender ). This isn’t going to open up a world of opportunity for alleged genius Declan Doyle, who is taking major lumps as a rookie play caller (he needs to get down to the sidelines , for starters), or anything like that.
Let’s be real – Brissett got benched against a terrible Dallas defense for Gardner Minshew despite the Cardinals putting up with his “hold-in” all offseason and giving him an incentivized contract to come back. He has not performed to 2025’s standard; he’s thrown seven picks already (8 in 14 games last year) and his yards per attempt was down to an anemic 5.6, with a QB rating of just 79.7.
But I also know this – he is a far more adroit passer of the football than Huntley, who has played most for this team at QB since Jackson first got hurt in Week 4. He will spray the ball around and attack all quadrants in ways Huntley just never would, and while I wouldn’t mind seeing Fagnano get a run in an already lost season in which they should sell at the deadline … but trying to get a half-season out of him is a bit much. (This team is going to lose more QBs behind this line; it’s inevitable).
But at the very least the Ravens have a chance to have a semblance of a downfield passing game with Brissett running the show – virtually certain to be Monday night in Week 10 – and look for two Ravens to benefit most from this transaction:
While his yard/attempt figures and air yard figures are not special, Brissett does things Huntley never dreamed of. In the last two years with the Ravens, Huntley has attempted a pass 15 yards or more downfield barely 18% of the team and over 20 yards downfield less than 6% of the team. Brissett, over the last three years as a starter, is pushing it at least 15 yards on 33% of his attempts and 10% of his throws go 20 yards or more.
And as we’ve known for years, only one guy shows up in this offense in that regard – Flowers. After getting shutout last week in Buffalo – and putting up bonkers numbers before Jackson got hurt – you cannot put too fine a point on getting him activated again.
During the last two years, Brissett did his most efficient work throwing on crossing routes, with a 113.5 rating, completing 67% of his attempts at 8.1/pass. Hmm. Anyone who has watched a functioning version of Baltimore’s offense since Flowers entered the league knows he feasts going across the face of the defense. And Brissett has attempted more passes on out routes than anything else while with the Cardinals, completing 79% of those throws with a rating of 103.9. Flowers has been targeted on outs more than any other route.
His speed and ability to win after the catch simply must become a part of whatever this offense looks like the rest of the way. The fifth-round pick was starting to click with Jackson and win downfield in the slot before Jackson got hurt, then Hibner got hurt and now the QB position is spiraling. But this kid has the ability to excel on deeper stuff and blocks better than I thought and Brissett is going to love him.
Brissett just force-fed elite tight end Trey McBride two years; that offense was a funnel to the point receiver Marvin Harrison Jr, a fourth-overall pick, got dealt away. Brissett will let it rip (he’s got the “no risk it; no biscuit” mentality later in his career) and he will throw jump balls and attack with go balls in the seam. Mark Andrews, honestly, should be inactive at this point and we know that will never happen, but he needs to be below Hibner on the depth chart (routes run and targets must be slashed).
We are getting 9 yards of YAC/reception on the rare occasions this kid is targeted. Over the last two seasons Brissett leads the NFL with 32.4% of his passes going to TEs (guess who is second at 30.8%  - yeah, Lamar). This is Brissett’s favorite way to attack, and ain’t no way Andrews is winning downfield against anybody and Hibner should be a fixture in the slot (with fellow rookie Josh Cuevas more of the in-line guy).
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Bills' Josh Allen Reflects Moment vs. Vikings That Proved He Belonged in NFL
full_text:
This Monday, the Buffalo Bills have a major showdown on their hands as they face the No. 1 defense in the league , the Minnesota Vikings.
It's a chance for the Bills to prove they truly are the best offense in the NFL, and for Josh Allen, it's a chance to re-live a viral moment from his rookie season. Back in 2018, Allen made the highlight reels when he hurdled over Minnesota linebacker Anthony Barr.
On Thursday, Allen was asked about the play and admitted he was surprised by the fact that he lept over the 6-foot-5, 257-pounder. Allen also said that was the moment when he realized he belonged in the NFL.
"Honestly, it surprised me too. You know, like I was a good athlete in college. High school I was not. So as I got older and started to lift more weights, I guess I got a little more athletic," Allen said via Dan Fetes .
"But, yeah, I think it was just kind of a surprising thing for me too of what I was able to do, you know, especially early on in the career with the running stuff. I know I still run a little bit now, but that was, I think, the moment that I was like, you know what, I do belong here.
Since that rookie season, Allen has continued to prove he belongs in the NFL, even winning the MVP award following the 2024 season.
Year after year, he leads one of the league's top offenses and has Buffalo at No. 1 overall scoring offense through eight games. For Allen, it's not enough to have the stats, he wants to be tested. This week, that will be the case as the Bills take on the Vikings, and Allen welcomes the challenge, saying he's looking forward to facing a fantastic defense.
"As a competitor, you're like, yeah, heck yeah, I want to play the best. I want to go out there and prove why we are, what you say, the No. 1 offense," Allen said . "I know that's statistically speaking, but that's still a chip on our shoulder. We want to go out there and be the best offense that we can be. And again, we've got a great opportunity against a fantastic defense."
Both teams enter the game with a record of 6-1 , although the Vikings are coming off their first loss of the year in Week 8 to the Detroit Lions. They're going to be focused on getting back on track and will see the Bills as a great test for their defense as well.
This has the makings of a great game and Allen is more than ready for the challenge.

title: Advanced Analytics Reveal How Bills' Offense Can Stun Vikings' Historic Defense
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills face a major challenge on Monday night, facing off against an elite Minnesota Vikings defense.
A thread by SumerSports , an NFL data and analytics site, broke down the areas to exploit the Brian Flores-led unit, giving Joe Brady and Josh Allen a blueprint for how to survive against Minnesota's defense.
The Vikings have a 70.3% blitz rate, by far the highest in the NFL. They pressure opposing QBs 47.9% of the time and sack the QB 10.6% of the time. Their 63% pass rush win rate also ranks first in the NFL.
This absurd blitz rate is made possible because of the talent and versatility of the team's back end. Vikings DBs have been flagged only once for a coverage penalty this season, and record a pass breakup or interception on 20.4% of targets. They also miss just 9.7% of tackles, the ninth best mark in the league.
Their aggressiveness works only because of the team's elite personnel and coaching blending together to work perfectly in sync.
Nobody knows who’s coming. Flores mixes the alignment of his players and where the blitz comes from. That makes pre-snap reads extremely difficult. pic.twitter.com/6zNlAXqhcH
The Bills are currently third in pass block win rate , with a 60% success rate. Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown each sit at 88% win rates individually, while Alec Anderson ranks seventh among interior linemen at 93%. Connor McGovern's 91% ranks top 20 for interior linemen as well.
This suggests the Bills have the personnel necessary to counteract Minnesota's talented pass rushers, if they can properly diagnose which players crowding the line of scrimmage are actually going to rush the QB.
Nothing has worked consistently enough against this Vikings defense to be considered a slam dunk, but four types of plays have generated success from a limited sample size.
Quick throws, when the ball is out in under two seconds, have generated +0.24 EPA per play on 54 attempts, so Brady and Allen need to prioritize getting the ball out fast.
Targeting Minnesota's linebackers when they cheat close to the line of scrimmage has been the most successful type of pass play, generating +0.91 EPA per play on 17 attempts. This is where Dalton Kincaid will need to thrive, locating zones in the middle of the field or beating his man one-on-one fast enough for a quick completion.
The next type of play is bootlegs, which have averaged +0.37 EPA per play on 13 attempts. On play action passes outside of the pocket (aka bootlegs) Allen has generated 12.15 total EPA and 2.47 points above average. These marks are the second and fourth highest among all QBs this season according to Sports Info Solutions (SIS).
Lastly, while fans won't love that this is a play that could work in Buffalo's favor, screen passes have generated +0.39 EPA per play on 12 attempts against the Vikings. This season, Allen has completed eight screen passes for 87 yards, generating 2.7 total EPA and 1.16 points above average. While the raw production rank middle of the pack, the advanced analytics rank top 10 according to SIS.
Brady and Allen should prioritize quick throws over the middle, bootlegs and screens to counteract Brion Flores's aggressive defense.
Embracing the success the offense has had with RB screens should be a priority, taking advantage of their stable of backs in James Cook, Ray Davis and Ty Johnson. Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir should see work in the middle of the field, with the latter being utilized in the screen game as well.
Lean into what the analytics say works against this historic defense, and Buffalo's offense should be able to have enough success to earn their seventh win of the season.

title: Key Metric Shows Bills' Davison Igbinosun Separating Himself from Fellow Rookies
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' defense has had a somewhat erratic start to the 2026 campaign.
Although the team currently possesses the best record in the AFC at 6-1 behind an incredibly high-powered offense that is scoring at a rate of 33.3 points per game—nearly a full six points higher than the next closest team—the Bills appear to also have one of the most untrustworthy defenses in the entire league, nevermind just amongst the presumed playoff contenders this fall.
However, despite surrendering 25.9 points and 352.1 total yards per game through eight weeks of the season while subsequently also allowing 254.7 passing yards and 15 total touchdowns through the air, there is at least one player in the secondary right now who is shining through the darkness that is clouding the rest of the defensive picture .
And, it’s a player whom many fans and media members had questions about when the team first traded up to select him in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft in April at pick No. 62 out of Ohio State University: rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun.
Although it was unclear at the time why Buffalo made the move for Igbinosun after previously selecting fellow cornerback Maxwell Hairston in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft the spring prior, the results on the field through two full months of Igbinosun’s first NFL season are encouraging, to say the least, and it’s making some folks within Bills Mafia forget all about Hairston’s bountiful miscues over the past year-and-a-half.
With four starts now to his name through seven games, Igbinosun—or “IGB” as teammates call him—seems to be settling in nicely opposite Christian Benford on the outside at cornerback as the calendar turns toward the second week of November, and the stats more than support that notion.
Tallying 28 total tackles and eight pass breakups thus far, Igbinosun recently grabbed his first career interception in the professional ranks after recording 194 combined tackles, 27 pass deflections, four interceptions, four tackles for loss, and three fumble recoveries in four collegiate seasons between Ohio State (2023-2025) and Ole Miss (2022).
And, while it was undoubtedly a great sight to see, it was merely the culmination of a lot of hard work and stellar coverage through seven games this fall from the 22-year-old Union Township, New Jersey, native.
In fact, according to Pro Football Focus, Igbinosun has forced the highest incompletion rate to the opposition among any rookie cornerback this season at a clip of 23.3%, placing him ahead of other notable youngsters such as Kansas City’s Mansoor Delane ( 1st round, pick No. 6 ), Pittsburgh’s Daylen Everette ( 3rd round, pick No. 85 ), Carolina’s Will Lee III ( 4th round, pick No. 129 ), and Green Bay’s Brandon Cisse ( 2nd round, pick No. 52 ) in the top five for the specific statistic.
Davison Igbinosun isn't making it easy for the offense pic.twitter.com/O12DbTQmxq
Keeping that in mind, given that Igbinosun has seemingly overtaken Maxwell Hairston’s spot permanently in Buffalo’s starting lineup moving forward—which is part of a few other notable changes that paid dividends against Baltimore last Sunday —seeing the second-rounder mentioned amongst such good company is certainly a sign of hope for better production from the secondary overall in Western New York as the season progresses.
And, it appears that he’ll have another favorable matchup against Minnesota’s struggling passing offense this upcoming week on Monday Night Football .
Well, as it stands right now, the Bills will be facing a backup quarterback for a second straight week when they hit the field for a primetime matchup at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on Monday evening.
However, regardless of which quarterback the Vikings trot out , Jim Leonhard’s unit must be ready to capitalize on the golden opportunity once again.

title: Bills' First Week 9 Injury Update: DJ Moore Present, Two OL Starters Miss Practice
full_text:
There were both encouraging appearances and concerning absences at Buffalo Bills ' practice on Thursday in Orchard Park.
First, starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who missed the November 1 win due to back issues, was back on the practice field as the Bills kicked off preparations for their November 9 road matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
Making for more good news, both wide receiver DJ Moore and running back James Cook were seen participating during the media-viewing portion of practice (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ). Moore and Cook were both nicked up during the fourth quarter in Week 8 and received in-game evaluations.
Prior to practice, Bills' head coach Joe Brady, who is mostly tight lipped when it comes to player injuries, reported that both Moore and Brown would participate in some capacity.
In another encouraging development, starting slot cornerback Dee Alford was also practicing. Alford was unavailable this past Sunday due to an ankle injury.
On the other hand, starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and starting left guard Alec Anderson were not on the field when media were present.
The Dawkins revelation comes as a surprise. Although he sat out the game's final four snaps, as did center Connor McGovern and quarterback Josh Allen, Dawkins wasn't known to be dealing with any kind of injury issue.
As for Anderson, he was banged up on the game's opening possession, but returned to the lineup after two missed snaps.
Additionally, backup defensive tackle Greg Gaines, who was injured during practice last week, was absent. Third-down running back Ty Johnson and wide receiver Josh Palmer were not spotted either. While the reason for Johnson's absence is unknown, Palmer pulled his hamstring during the first quarter last time out. He is expected to miss multiple weeks.
Moore was questionable to play in Week 8 due to a shoulder injury that caused the wide receiver to miss back-to-back games heading into the team's bye.
On his final catch in the 36-10 victory, Moore was slow to get up after potentially hyperextending his leg on the tackle. After an evaluation, he emerged from the blue medical tent and appeared to share good news with Allen.
Josh Allen: "Is he in here?" *DJ Moore walks out of the blue tent* *Josh Allen smiles* #BillsMafia @BuffaloPlus pic.twitter.com/1uKDwF15H9
Moore spoke to reporters following the win , and he reported nothing other than normal football wear and tear. He was wearing a red non-contact jersey on Thursday as a precautionary measure to protect his shoulder.
"Like 90 percent, I feel good. Football, you always gonna have some nicks and bruises and probably got those. I don't feel them right now, but I probably feel them like in 15 minutes," said Moore.
Cook was folded in half on a fourth-quarter carry, remaining down on the turf after the play for a minute. After eventually springing to his feet, he went off to the the medical tent where the independent neurologist evaluated the running back for a head injury.
He was cleared to return, but remained on the sidelines with the Bills in firm control. Cook wore a guardian cap during Thursday's practice.
Anderson appeared to jam up his right left somehow on a first-quarter red zone play. With wide receiver Khalil Shakir scoring a touchdown, that was subsequently taken off the board after review, at the right pylon, Anderson was engaged with a defender across the field.
Backup Austin Corbett replaced Anderson for the remainder of the drive before the starter returned for the next possession. Anderson also spoke to reporters in the locker room afterwards, and he did not appear to be dealing with any issues.
Brown, who has a history of back issues, experienced a flare-up back on October 12, leaving the game after only 16 snaps. He returned to play the entire Week 6 game six days later in Las Vegas, but his back apparently did not respond well during the bye week.
After missing two consecutive practices, Brown participated in a limited capacity last Friday. He was questionable on the injury report with the Bills intending to take the decision up until game time. Eventually scratching Brown, the Bills started Tylan Grable at right tackle .
Spencer Brown pic.twitter.com/Ka1OdvGZcz

title: New Bills Mock Draft Lands Centerfielder for Buffalo Defense
full_text:
At 6-1, the Buffalo Bills are focused completely on the 2026 season, as they should be. They remain one of the top teams in the NFL and have a legitimate shot at making a deep run in the postseason.
Still, there are those of us who enjoy looking ahead. That’s especially true when a team has a glaring weakness that needs to be addressed, which is the case for the Bills. Entering Week 9 , they’re ranked 30th in the league in pass defense, having surrendered 1,783 yards through the air .
They have seen progress from rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun and if he continues to develop, they could have a solid duo with him and veteran Christian Benford. At safety, however, there's a lot to be desired.
Buffalo already admitted its mistake in signing C.J. Gardner-Johnson, releasing him following his suspension for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. They still have faith in Cole Bishop, but can use an upgrade over Damar Hamlin, who is starting now that Gardner-Johnson is gone. Fixing the safety position is the goal for Justin Melo of NFL Draft On SI, as he has the Bills selecting Ohio State's Jaylen McClain with their first pick in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
What makes McClain a good fit in Buffalo, according to Melo, is his ability to play a centerfield role. He's a more traditional free safety, which would allow Bishop to focus on playing in-the-box, which is where he's best utilized.
“In typical Buffalo Bills fashion, the offense is overcompensating for the defense right now. Safety is an obvious need, with C.J. Gardner-Johnson as a 2026 solution opposite Cole Bishop. Ohio State’s Jaylen McClain has flashed true centerfield ability, which would be a nice fit opposite Bishop’s in-the-box skillset,” Melo wrote.
McClain is in the midst of his best season with the Buckeyes, having recorded 37 tackles, four pass defenses, and two interceptions.
The 6-foot-3, 203-pound McClain already has plenty of experience. He was a contributor as a true freshman during the 2024 season and has been a full-time starter the past two seasons. He has a strong overall grade from PFF (77.0) and while his 73.5 coverage grade this season is encouraging, he's actually been even better in run defense, posting an 82.3.
His ability to contribute as an all-around safety is what makes him a first-round prospect, but his speed and ability to play deep coverage is what makes him a sensible target for the Bills.

title: Bills Will Face Another Backup After Kyler Murray Injury Update, But That Could Be a Bad Thing
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills' struggling defense caught a break last week when the Baltimore Ravens saw not one but two of their quarterbacks go down to injury.
The Bills saw Lamar Jackson go out after the first play of the game, and then Tyler Huntley got hurt not long after that and Baltimore was forced to deploy rookie Joe Fagnano, which obviously did not pan out for the Ravens.
Now, as they prepare to face the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9, the Bills will be facing yet another backup quarterback.
That's because Vikings starter Kyle Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury that will sideline him on Monday.
On Thursday, head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Murray has been ruled out and is week-to-week with his hamstring issue.
"Kyler Murray (hamstring strain) is OUT for Monday's game, per Kevin O'Connell. Carson Wentz will start vs. Bills," ESPN's Kevin Seifert wrote. "O'Connell says Murray is week to week."
This might be one of the rare instances where facing a backup quarterback could be worse for the Bills.
That's because Murray has struggled this season, especially with accuracy, and as a result the Vikings' offense has not been good and the defense has carried the load.
Now, we're not saying that Wentz is a great quarterback, but with how bad Murray has looked this season, it's conceivable he could provide an upgrade for Minnesota as a passer.
We've seen Wentz put up some big games with the Vikings in the past, also, with Wetnz throwing for north of 300 yards twice last season.
The last thing the Bills want is for Wentz to be the upgrade we think he might be.
That's because the Bills have sported one of the league's worst pass defenses, with Buffalo ceding the third-most passing yards per contest this season.
The Bills have seen their young cornerbacks in Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun struggle, and so much so that they felt compelled to bring Tre'Davious White back.
Adding to that, the Bills made a subtraction from their safeties room this week, with the team decided to cut ties with C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
If Wentz proves to be a better passer than Murray, it's going to make guarding guys like Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, among others, even more difficult for the Bills during a game in which points could be at a premium for Buffalo against Minnesota's elite defense.

title: How Much Salary Cap Space Did Bills Waste With Failed CJ Gardner-Johnson Experiment?
full_text:
It's not debilitating by any means, but the Buffalo Bills will still be paying for their failed Chauncey Gardner-Johnson experiment next year.
Making the situation somewhat palatable, it was always known to be a low-risk move with a potentially high reward.
As it turns out, however, there was zero reward, only multiple cringe moments beginning with a locker room livestream during training camp and ending with a spitting incident with a lot of underwhelming play in between.
The Bills signed Gardner-Johnson to a one-year contract reportedly worth $3.5 million . According to Spotrac, the combustible safety earned $3 million in guaranteed money.
As a result of his one-game suspension, and subsequent release, Spotrac reports that Gardner-Johnson forfeits $384,166 in 2026 salary and game active bonuses.
When it comes to the dead cap hit, the Bills will absorb a $2.3 million charge this season for sending the veteran safety packing. Additionally, they'll have $1 million less cap space in 2027 due to lingering dead money.
While $1 million of dead money is a minimal percentage of a team's allotted spending, mistakes like these can prove costly when compounded over time , and the Bills' current salary cap status perfectly illustrates that issue.
The Bills signed defensive end Joey Bosa and defensive tackle Larry Ogunjobi to one-year contracts for the 2025 season.
While Bosa and Ogunjobi are gone following disappointing one-year trials , both players are sucking up multimillion dollars of Bills' salary cap space in 2026. Buffalo has $7.2 million in dead cap space from Bosa while Ogunjobi costs $2.35 million against this year's spending limit.
Beane added free agent wide receiver Curtis Samuel prior to the 2024 season. The Bills finally cut bait at the end of the 2025 campaign, and he currently counts $3.45 million against the 2026 cap.
Per spotrac, the Bills have approximately $4 million in salary cap space heading into the NFL's November 10 trade deadline. That number ranks Buffalo 27th overall, meaning Beane doesn't have much room to maneuver compared to other general mangers.
A key factor in the spending constraints is the amount of dead money. The Bills have $51.3! million tied up in players who are no longer on the roster. That is 13th most amongst the league's 32 teams.

title: Josh Allen's History vs. Vikings' Defensive Coordinator Presents Clear Expectations
full_text:
Brian Flores is known for producing some of the best defenses in football, and on Monday Night Football , the Buffalo Bills and quarterback Josh Allen will face a Minnesota Vikings stop unit that ranks first in EPA per play and pressure rate .
Allen knows the Vikings' defensive coordinator very well from when he faced the Miami Dolphins from 2019 to 2021, when Flores was their head coach. If past results are any indication, Allen should have no problems picking up where he left off.
The Bills were 6-0 against the Dolphins in those three seasons, and they won those games by an average margin of about 18 points. Given how weak the Vikings' offense is (28th in EPA per play), Allen and Co. may not need to do much to reach that threshold.
Allen had yet to break out as a superstar in the league when he began facing Flores, and in his six games against him, he completed 64.4% of his passes for 1,525 yards and a 16-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio. He added 200 yards and two more scores on the ground in those contests.
These stats do not account for Allen sitting the entire second half of Buffalo's meaningless Week 17 contest against Miami in 2020, so these stats technically span five and a half games.
Though Allen has had success against Flores in the past, there is plenty more talent for the defensive wizard to work with in Minnesota to try to befuddle Allen than he ever had in Miami.
Outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel is one player Allen will know well from his matchups against the Dolphins. He's a do-it-all defender for Flores, as he leads the Vikings with 6.5 sacks and 8.5 tackles for loss. In the four games he played under Flores against Allen, he registered 13 tackles, two sacks and a forced fumble.
Flores did not have another elite edge defender in Miami, but Dallas Turner, with six sacks and 8.5 TFLs, is blossoming in his third season as that piece. Both Van Ginkel and Turner rank in the top 10 in the NFL in sacks.
In the linebacking core, veteran Blake Cashman is another chess piece for Flores to use, as he leads the Vikings with 64 tackles and also has 4.5 sacks and five passes defensed.
Cornerback Xavien Howard was the only All-Pro Flores had in Miami, but Isaiah Rodgers, Byron Murphy and James Pierre have combined for six of the Vikings' eight interceptions this season, forming a trio that is hard to complete passes against.
Safety Joshua Metellus is another versatile piece, as he often plays in the box or in the slot to shut down opposing playmakers.
Despite such a talented group of defenders, Allen has a couple of advantages he'll need to emphasize if the Bills are to win their seventh game of the season.
#Skol #Vikings DC Brian Flores on #BillsMafia QB Josh Allen: "Josh is one of the best players in our league." Allen enters MNF with 20 total TD so far this season for the 6-1 Bills. pic.twitter.com/K6owGJUpvT
The Vikings blitz on 72.8% of defensive plays, by far the most in the NFL by about 30 percentage points. They also lead the league with an 11% sack rate. Fortunately for Buffalo, Allen doesn't take a nosedive against pressure. In fact, he's one of the league's better quarterbacks against extra rushers.
Allen has an overall rate of 0.22 EPA per play, fourth-best among quarterbacks with at least 100 snaps. His 0.11 EPA per play against the blitz is 10th in the league and -0.03 EPA per play against pressure is third-best.
For reference, the seven quarterbacks Minnesota has faced so far have combined for 0.15 EPA per play against the blitz and -2.72 EPA per play against pressure.
Allen can also lean on James Cook and the running game to settle down the pass rush and keep it honest. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries against Minnesota on Sunday, so Cook having a similar performance will help massively.
Going against Flores' defense is a tough task for any quarterback, but if anyone can overcome it, Allen can.

title: Three Buffalo Bills With Most to Prove Entering Week 9 vs. Vikings
full_text:
After knocking off the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, the Buffalo Bills will now turn their attention to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9 . It's a huge showdown for the Bills, who will travel to Minnesota for a Monday Night Football showdown.
The Vikings enter this one feeling the pressure after suffering their first loss of the season, falling to the Detroit Lions 19-15. They're a defensive powerhouse and will be focused on slowing down the high-scoring Bills' offense.
As for Buffalo, they have a chance to prove themselves against one of the top teams in the NFC. There will be plenty of pressure on them as well, but no one will be feeling as much heat as the following three players.
In Week 8, Te'Cory Couch snuck up on everyone. He was asked to step up with C.J. Gardner-Johnson suspended and Dee Alford injured, and did exactly that. Filling in as a nickel corner, Couch was one of the highest-graded players on the team against the Ravens. His performance was solid enough that Buffalo felt confident in moving on from Gardner-Johnson once his suspension was officially over.
Now entering Week 9, Couch won't be able to sneak up on anyone. Initially signed as an undrafted free agent out of Miami in 2024, Couch has continued to develop for Buffalo and has earned a larger role on defense. Now, the pressure will be on as he needs to prove he can still get the job done even when big things are expected of him.
In all honesty, we could put the entire Buffalo offensive line on this list considering the task they're about to face. Minnesota boasts the No. 1 scoring defense in the NFL right now and that has a lot to do with the performance of its front seven. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores has never been shy about bringing the blitz and that's led to 25 sacks in the first seven games for the Vikings.
While all five starters on the O-line will be under attack, Dawkins is the leader of the group and needs to set the tone. He will also find himself matched up with Dallas Turner, who is second on the team with six sacks, but is currently the 13th highest-rated pass-rusher among all qualified EDGE players, according to PFF. If Dawkins can slow him down one-on-one, the Bills can send help to the other side and potentially slow down the overall pass rush.
After a slow start to the season , Christian Benford has once again hit his stride. He was fantastic in Week 7 against Brock Bowers and helped shut down Zay Flowers who had zero receptions on five targets in Week 8. His confidence should be at an all-time high, and Buffalo is going to need his performance to match this week.
Benford will find himself lined up across from Justin Jefferson for much of the game and that should be one of the best matchups to watch all weekend. Jefferson is a route-running wizard who is unguardable when he's on top of his game. He's been slowed down this season by a subpar offense overall, but Jefferson can still light up the scoreboard without warning.
That's why Benford will be facing more pressure this weekend than anyone else on the Bills' roster. He's going to be asked to slow down the one player who can turn this game into a track meet. If he succeeds, Buffalo's chances of winning improve exponentially.

title: Which Bills' Safety Should Replace C.J. Gardner-Johnson in Starting Lineup?
full_text:
In a somewhat surprising move, the Buffalo Bills decided to shake the roster up on Tuesday evening by releasing veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson after just seven games of the 2026 campaign after originally bringing the boastful defender on board via a one-year deal in free agency on March 12 that was worth up to $6 million.
237 days later and fresh off a one-game suspension, Gardner-Johnson finds himself looking for a new NFL home and the Bills are in search of a new starting safety to pair with third-year defensive back Cole Bishop.
Last week against the Baltimore Ravens it was sixth-year veteran Damar Hamlin who earned the nod alongside Bishop, but fellow veteran safety Geno Stone also saw time on the field and played quite well in limited action.
So what is the best plan of attack moving forward for Buffalo’s first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard ?
Let’s scour through the candidates.
Damar Hamlin might not be flashy, but he’s the definition of consistent.
In spite of all of the hardship that he’s endured since that fateful day in Cincinnati, Ohio, at Paycor Stadium on Monday Night Football in January of 2023, Hamlin has never wavered in his return to the gridiron.
And, it’s led him to possibly once again regaining a starting defensive spot for a Bills’ squad currently sitting atop the AFC standings entering Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season.
In 2022 and 2024—the two seasons he previously started a majority of Buffalo’s games—Hamlin tallied 180 total tackles, eight tackles for loss, seven pass deflections, two interceptions, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery while starting in 17 of the 19 games he appeared in during the regular season.
As for this year, Hamlin has recorded 23 total tackles and one pass breakup while appearing in seven games with two starts.
And, after tallying 16 total tackles in a more prominent role over the past three weeks, the 28-year-old defensive back appears to be odds-on favorite to start the remainder of the season.
Veteran Geno Stone was an interesting addition to Buffalo’s roster earlier this offseason after joining the team almost immediately following the signing of the previously mentioned Gardner-Johnson in March.
The questions surrounding the addition weren’t due to a lack of experience or track record from Stone, but rather the repetitiveness of adding a second player at the safety position at the time.
Now, though, it seems as if it was a smart move by Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane to bring Stone on board.
After being called up from the practice squad on Sunday due to a “numbers game”, Stone wound up playing 19 defensive snaps against the Ravens and posted a team-high six tackles to go along with one tackle for loss and one pass deflection, which actually led to an easy tip-drill interception by rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun.
Does Stone have warts to his game? Sure. But, he seems dependable and was in the right place at the right time more often than not against the Ravens, which led to him being named the top-ranked defender for Buffalo in the matchup according to Pro Football Focus .
That type of reliability and innate ability to make a play on the ball—which is evidenced by his 14 career interceptions—is exactly what Jim Leonhard’s youthful defense needs right now on the backend.
Rookie safety Jalon Kilgore had a lot of fanfare amongst Bills Mafia after being selected by the team at pick No. 167 in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and for good reason.
The versatile defensive back had plenty of production for the South Carolina Gamecocks’ defense during his three collegiate seasons, and his stellar combination of size ( 6-foot-1, 210 lbs ), speed ( 4.40-second time in the 40-yard-dash ), and overall athleticism ( 10-foot-10-inch broad, 37-inch vertical ) is something that Buffalo could use more of in the secondary.
Eventually, Kilgore should take over as the long-term starter opposite Cole Bishop, but will that begin to take shape sometime this season?
Kilgore has only appeared in two games so far this regular season after struggling with injuries in the summer months, and he was just inactive once again for the matchup against Baltimore.
It’ll be interesting to see if the rookie starts seeing more opportunities now that Gardner-Johnson is out of the picture.
Out of all of the possible outcomes, this may be the least likely . . . but should it be?
A former UDFA signing of Bills following the 2024 NFL Draft, Couch has been on Buffalo’s practice squad over the past two seasons, but was recently signed to the active roster ahead of the game against the Ravens.
And, in the absence of the injured Dee Alford, Couch started in the slot at nickel cornerback for Buffalo, playing 71% of the team’s defensive snaps.
The 27-year-old performed admirably in the role , too, as he finished tied for second on the team in total tackles with a total of five while only allowing one reception in coverage according to PFF.
Given his recent performance in a starting role, it’s possible that Couch takes over that spot for Alford permanently as the calendar turns toward the middle of November, but the idea of shifting him back to safety—an area he experimented with in training camp and the preseason—is also intriguing.
Bills ON SI mentioned Couch as a player who earned the right to a 53-man roster spot before final cuts were made back in August, and that’s proving to be the case now in November.
Could Brandon Beane make a swing for some help in the secondary before next Tuesday’s trade deadline?
And, with that in mind, Bills ON SI has covered several options on the market leading up to November 10.
However, as it stands right now, Bills Mafia shouldn’t hold their collective breath for a move to be made.
“Big Baller Beane” may have permanently switched to "Bargain Bin Beane” at this juncture.
Ultimately, the direction that Buffalo decides to go in the absence of Gardner-Johnson could go several different ways: clearly.
But, at the moment, it would seem prudent for the Bills to stick with what worked against the Ravens .
Yes, the total defensive output may have been slightly skewed due to the quarterback the team ended up facing on Sunday, but the smoothness of the overall operation seemed to be much better than it had been prior to the bye week.
So, for that reason—as well as the ones mentioned above—some sort of platoon between Hamlin and Stone seems to be the recipe for success moving forward.

title: Khalil Mack Could Give the Panthers a Much-Needed Boost, but the Price Might Be Too High
full_text:
One of the NFL's most accomplished pass rushers could be an option for the Carolina Panthers before the trade deadline. He would immediately fill a need for the Carolina Panthers’ defense. But acquiring Khalil Mack would not be easy for Dan Morgan and the Panthers’ front office.
At 35 years old, Mack is still one of the better pass rushers in the NFL. But the Panthers would need more than just his ability to get to the quarterback over the next couple of months.
According to reports, the Los Angeles Chargers have not shown interest in trading Mack. The team has reportedly refused to trade several of its veteran players, including Mack, who is in the final year of his contract with the team.
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that he wants Khalil Mack to stay with the team for the rest of the season and believes the veteran pass rusher wants to stay in Los Angeles as well.
But, as with most things in the NFL, situations can change quickly. Mack is in the final year of his contract, and the Chargers could receive something in return for the pass rusher rather than risk losing him in free agency.
NFL.com suggested that an early Day 3 draft pick could be a fair return for Mack’s services. This would likely involve a fourth-round pick being traded for the veteran pass rusher, although it is unclear whether the Chargers would be willing to make such a deal.
While a fourth-round pick would be worth considering for the Panthers, Carolina still has a number of holes to fill and they can’t afford to give away another draft pick for a player who will likely only play in a few games for the team.
A fifth-round pick would be more appropriate for a player of Mack’s age and current contract situation, though that might not be enough to convince the Chargers to make a deal.
The cost to acquire Mack would also include his contract, which is one year and $18 million. Carolina has very little cap space for the current season, according to Over the Cap, leaving Morgan with little financial flexibility to make a deal.
As Over the Cap reports, Mack’s contract with the Chargers is for one year and $18 million. He has an $8 million base salary for the season, and a $10 million signing bonus that the Chargers have already paid. The acquiring team would be on the hook for the remaining unpaid portion of Mack’s base salary for the season.
The amount of the unpaid portion of Mack’s base salary that the acquiring team would be responsible for could be several million dollars. This would likely be too much for the Panthers to handle given their current cap situation of less than $1 million.
Perhaps the Chargers would pay some of the remaining salary before a trade. Perhaps the Panthers can make some moves with some of the players on their roster to free up some space. But those are both big ifs.
Of course, giving up a draft pick for a player to help immediately is one thing. Giving up that pick and then having to make salary cap-related moves to get the player on the field is another.
In addition to acquiring a veteran pass rusher, Carolina would be acquiring a player who can become a free agent at the end of the season. Thus, Carolina would be spending money and draft picks for a short period of time to acquire a veteran pass rusher.
He would be able to give the Panthers another option to create pressure on opposing quarterbacks, even if they aren’t sending extra defenders to the quarterback. This would also allow other players to create pressure on the quarterback, as Mack would draw a lot of attention to the edge.
Mack has three sacks in his seven games this season for the Chargers. While his numbers may not be great, his presence on the field creates opportunities for his teammates and can force opposing offenses to change their game plan.
This would be particularly important for the Panthers right now, as they are suffering from a rash of injuries in the secondary. To have more players up front able to put pressure on the quarterback would allow for the cornerbacks to have more time to cover receivers downfield.
He can also bring a lot of leadership to a young team and help them to prepare for the big games.
But can Mack turn the Panthers’ defense around? No, because he would have to learn the team’s defense and adapt to his teammates. This would have to happen in short order because of Todd Wash taking over as the team’s interim defensive coordinator.
The Panthers are still building their roster and need to acquire several positions through the draft over the next couple of years.
Mack would be a great addition to the Panthers’ defense and Morgan should consider making a trade for the veteran pass rusher if the Chargers are willing to part with him for a fifth-round pick and some of his remaining salary.
A fourth-round pick would be more difficult to justify as the Panthers would need to believe that Mack would provide enough immediate impact to warrant the loss of another draft pick, possibly to be used on a younger player down the road.
If the Chargers want more than a fourth-round pick for Mack then Carolina would be better off looking for help elsewhere and keeping their draft picks.
The biggest issue with trying to trade for Mack is that Los Angeles head coach Jim Harbaugh has already said that he wants the veteran pass rusher to stay with the Chargers for the remainder of the season.
He is a big name and would be a great addition to the team but Morgan must not get caught up in chasing a big name and must make sure that the price is right for a team that is still trying to get better.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: One Move the Panthers Can't Afford to Get Wrong at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have plenty of moves they could make before the November 10 trade deadline, but Dan Morgan shouldn’t let injuries force his hand to make a bad deal. He can get help, but giving up too much to get by for a few weeks could cost Carolina much more in the long run.
There are only so many healthy bodies at cornerback on the Panthers’ roster. Jaycee Horn is on IR, as is Mike Jackson, and most recently Akayleb Evans was placed on IR with knee and triceps injuries. Will Lee III suffered a hamstring injury in the loss to the Packers and is out for an undetermined amount of time.
Of course Morgan would be looking for help to bolster the team’s secondary, but the problem is that he could end up paying too much for said help in a trade, and said player would likely only be with the team for a few months.
Among the possible options at cornerback are Riq Woolen and Donte Jackson. While both players could be beneficial to the Panthers, the asking price for each player must be taken into account as well as what they can bring to the team. Morgan shouldn’t overpay for a player who will likely only be with the team for a few months.
The Panthers have been trying to rebuild this roster for years. It would be a mistake to trade away future opportunities to add talent to this roster in order to add someone to the struggling secondary right now.
The team has very little money to spend as it is. Based on recent salary cap estimates for the Panthers, they have less than $1 million in available cap space. Therefore, Morgan would have to make some salary cap moves in order to bring in another player with a significant salary.
This does not mean Morgan should cease trying to find help at cornerback. There may be teams willing to trade veteran corners for late-round picks. It’s just that Morgan shouldn’t pay more than that in order to add another short-term solution to the team’s problems.
Woolen is in the last year of his contract, and the Panthers would have to consider what they are willing to give up to acquire him for the remainder of the season. If he walks in free agency then Morgan has given up an asset for a short-term fix that may not even produce on the field.
Additionally, how quickly will a new corner be able to acclimate to the Panthers’ defense? The Panthers recently named Todd Wash interim defensive coordinator. A new corner would have to learn a new scheme, likely on the fly, as the Panthers are in the midst of a playoff push.
This is not a team that is one trade away from being a Super Bowl contender. There are several other areas that need to be addressed on the roster and can be in the off-season with the draft picks that Morgan will have.
While it is frustrating that the Panthers are in this position with so many injuries at cornerback, Morgan should not make a long-term decision based on the current situation in November. Carolina needs Horn and Jackson to return to action as soon as possible, and the players currently filling in at cornerback have been placed in some very difficult situations. Jackson stated that he expects to return to action in a couple of weeks, so help is on the way.
But Morgan shouldn’t be too quick to say no to help. If Morgan is able to find an affordable veteran to add some depth, then that’s not something he should turn down.
The trade deadline can put a lot of pressure on general managers to make moves. But Morgan needs to be patient and not make any moves that are against his better judgment in order to appease the media and fans.
The Panthers need help at cornerback but not another bad decision that could make rebuilding the roster even harder next year.

title: Should Panthers Be Buyers or Sellers? Making the Argument for the Deadline
full_text:
The Trade Deadline is rapidly approaching. Unfortunately, the Carolina Panthers are caught in the middle here. They are, at full strength, an apparent playoff team, one that would warrant some acquisitions.
They're not full strength, and to be truthful, they won't ever be. We can't expect Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Jaelan Phillips, Taylor Moton, Xavier Legette, and Jonathon Brooks to all return and stay healthy without anyone else going down. It's not going to happen, so perhaps this season is better used as a chance to offload some dead weight.
So, should the Panthers be buyers or sellers? There's an argument for both.
The argument that the Panthers should buy is simple: They're banged up with holes on the roster and are still in first place. They are clearly a team capable of hanging with most teams when they're healthy, so why not add to make sure they can stay healthy?
Adding a cornerback to this roster would be the single-most justified move in the NFL. Adding an edge rusher, a wide receiver, or quite literally anything on the offensive line would also be pretty understandable.
Before injuries really piled up and the offensive line play fell off a cliff, this team was 3-2 and looked like the clear class of the NFC South. Adding players to help offset the recent issues would seemingly restore them to that level.
Health is one thing, but bad play is another, and after firing Ejiro Evero, it's clear that bad performance should be met with consequences. The Panthers have a number of players not playing to their standards, and some of them would bring in a nice return.
The Panthers could set themselves up for a brilliant offseason next year by trading Robert Hunt, Derrick Brown, and Tre'von Moehrig. They'd get back a pretty good haul for all three, even the struggling Hunt, due to either talent, demand, or financial flexibility.
They'd also clear a fair amount of cap space to extend Bryce Young and not be totally hamstrung. That salary cap is looming, and this is a way to get out from behind the eight-ball and get some draft capital.
The Panthers should buy, but they should not go crazy. Maybe it's a late-round pick for Jackson Powers-Johnson or Riq Woolen, but they can call it a day after that. The health issues mean this team is not going to be a true contender this year, and going all-in after that is foolish.
That said, the Panthers can't keep going this way. They're way too injured and have too many problems on a first-place team to sell assets or stand pat. They have to do something, but they can't afford to do too much.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Panthers in Season-Defining Matchup with Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have fallen to 3-4 after a really inspiring 3-2 start. Losing two games in a row in a demoralizing fashion, at least on the offensive side of the ball, is crushing, but it's especially bad when the schedule has no reprieve.
The Panthers have to turn it around. Unfortunately, they've got the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos coming to town. The Panthers are underdogs , and no one's picking them to win. It could be another ugly one.
But in the spirit of success, here are some bold predictions for the contest.
Being sacked twice in a game doesn't feel like a bold prediction. But Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times in the last two games. Getting back down to a normal number of sacks feels like an impossible task for everyone involved, especially the offensive line that can't seem to hold up for even two seconds.
The offensive line could look different (and should). Young's knee should be healthier, so he can get back to evading pressure as he did in the early going. And Brad Idzik should have enough data to call plays to help offset the porous line. Young's health, a better line, and smarter planning should help the sacks and pressure regress to the mean.
You'd be forgiven for checking the Panthers' depth chart and not knowing who the cornerbacks were. For an offense (Denver's) that has struggled to throw the ball down the field, Carolina's secondary has to feel like a gift from above.
But Marco Wilson was solid in his debut, and the Panthers should get Jaelan Phillips back. Nix hasn't challenged anyone down the field all year, and we don't expect that to start. That's the recipe for success, especially for a defense that wants to get downhill more with a new coordinator.
There's a temptation to expect Tetairoa McMillan to see Pat Surtain more often than not and produce like he did against the Cleveland Browns, when the defense put its best corner on him and sent pressure. Why shouldn't the Browns repeat that?
Well, they might, but as mentioned, the game plan should be better to offset that. And with Jalen Coker healthy, the Broncos won't be able to necessarily shade McMillan with Surtain 100% of the time. So, he should be able to bounce back.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Panthers Rightly Pitched as Ideal Landing Spot for Top-5 Trade Candidate
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is just five days away , and it's trending towards being one of the wilder deadlines in league history, with big names on the move. Huge trades have already taken place and made a huge impact, as seen with Jeffery Simmons joining the Chicago Bears.
Now, with less than a week until deadline day, the Carolina Panthers have a chance to join the party and make a move to save this season. No, the Panthers aren't going to get a superstar and use one or multiple first-round picks. However, Carolina can add a bona fide starter to improve any of the team's struggling units, and there are multiple.
There's an argument to be made that the worst facet of the Panthers is the run defense , allowing 140 rushing yards per game, which is the third-worst in the NFL. Carolina has had two games this season allowing over 250 rushing yards; both games were at home.
So what position will the Panthers need to target to bolster that room? Interior defensive line. Luckily, there's one team that could go into fire-sale mode and prepare for the draft with its roster decimated by injuries.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox dropped his trade block big board ahead of Week 9. Notable names like Jonathon Taylor, Khalil Mack, Riq Woolen, and more are listed, but one name in the top five was named a good fit for the Panthers, and it makes perfect sense.
Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo is a name to watch at the deadline, and Carolina could use him. The Eagles could pivot their focus toward April, as the roster has been riddled with injuries, including QB Jalen Hurts, who is out for the season with blood clots.
Ojomo is a high motor tackle, who plays gap run schemes very well, and is still just 25. The Panthers already have an elite DT in Derrick Brown, but aren't extremely talented around him; adding a stud like Ojomo could fix that.
So far this season, Ojomo has posted just 7 solo tackles, which isn't much production, but thats what happens when Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis are on that defensive line as well.
Knox pointed out that Philadelphia has a lot of money tied up in those two defensive tackles, which is why Ojomo could be on the table. All thats left to figure out is what the Panthers would give up.
The likely price for the Panthers to trade for Ojomo would be a 2027 third-round pick. Carolina owns its own third-round pick in 2027, so that works out perfectly.
Another key part of this potential deal that needs to be mentioned is that Ojomo will be a free agent after this season. Philadelphia probably won't re-sign him because of the money they have invested in Carter and Davis.
So Carolina would need to prioritize re-signing Ojomo in that case, adding young depth to a defensive line that needs it.
