title: Deep Dive: It's Not Time to Panic on Carolina Panthers QB Bryce Young Yet
full_text:
Media analysts and pundits are selling their Bryce Young stock. The Carolina Panthers QB has come under fire for being unable to contend with the highest pressure rate in the NFL (which he has all season) the last two weeks. A roughly 50% pressure rate is borderline untenable for all players.
Mina Kimes said the offensive line is a big problem, but then you have Colin Cowherd and Jason McIntyre talking about Young being someone you just "can't extend." They may be out, but they probably shouldn't be.
Just consider the facts: Bryce Young has had an injured knee since Week 3, he's faced the most pressure all season, and he's still performing at a high level. Sure, the first few weeks of the season help skew that, but the awful games from the last two weeks do, too.
If we're not ignoring those games, we're also not ignoring the good ones. In other words, we're still taking the overall sample size, which is seven weeks of really strong quarterback play. Don't believe me? Check the stats.
The Carolina Panthers can't pass-protect, and Bryce Young is currently (or has been) too banged up to avoid sacks like he used to. That is ultimately a failing of the team around him, though he's receiving most of the blame.
But the overall numbers don't lie. They still paint a picture of a really good quarterback. We all knew deep down that his scorching start, when he was arguably the best in the NFL, would cool off. It has, but the overall performance is still good.
Look at this chart. Young's turnover-worthy play rate is at the bottom of the league. Only Caleb Williams does a better job at not putting the ball in harm's way. The last two weeks would suggest Young has been careless, but overall, he's keeping the ball very safe.
QB Big Time Throw Rate & Turnover Worthy Plays pic.twitter.com/C0k5SWBH6K
The big-time throws have trailed off to the middle of the pack, but Young has always been good at making those plays, even in 2024 and 2025. Once he's healthy or the line figures out how to block, those numbers should rise to the positive side of the mean once more.
How often each QB was pressured in Week 8 and his EPA when pressured Drake Maye 👀 Data: @FantasyPtsData , Week 8 only pic.twitter.com/QB0z3g1Bm9
How about this one exclusively from Week 8? Young had a pretty bad week against a ferocious pass rush, seeing the third-most pressure of any quarterback. Yet, he was barely worse than average against pressure. Over the course of a full season, that's a fine place to be at.
Trevor Lawrence makes it look easy pic.twitter.com/zUMTwbeLEI
Zooming back out to the full season, here's a chart showcasing which QBs are being carried by their weapons in yards after catch. In other words, Young is firmly in the "airing it out and not getting a ton of help from playmakers" area, which is where you want to be. Look at the company he's in: Josh Allen, Trevor Lawrence, Jordan Love, Lamar Jackson, etc. The future MVP is probably in that cluster.
Out of sight, out of mind for Kyler Murray pic.twitter.com/3P2u699HNM
And one more for good measure.  The middle of the field is seen as harder to access for shorter QBs, but it's also seen as the most valuable place to throw to. Yet, the 5'10" quarterback is doing that very well. He is again in the good quadrant of throwing to the middle frequently and having success doing it.
He's there with Caleb Williams, Brock Purdy, Trevor Lawrence, Jared Goff, and Lamar Jackson. Again, that's really good company to be in. The more times Young shows up in those places on these charts, the better we know he's playing. And overall, he's still playing well.
Young does sit in the middle of the pack in EPA numbers, but that's by and large a function of the offense as a whole. When Young drops back, he's dependent on his offensive line, the receivers, and sometimes what the defense is doing. That all goes into EPA/play, so it's not the best when applied solely to a QB.
Still, on the year, he is positive in EPA/dropback, which is another feather in the cap here. Young's season may have lost some luster recently, but it's still a fantastic year for the QB.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Bryce Young's Reported Extension Update is Bad News for Panthers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers ' season through seven games has been a roller coaster . With that, so has Bryce Young's. Sitting at 3-4, there have been major highs and, more recently,  major lows. Young hasn't been the clear worst piece of Carolina's latest struggles , but he hasn't elevated Carolina to make up for roster deficiencies.
Through the first five games of the season, Young was playing as well as almost any QB in the league. Leading the league in passing yards per game, had an exceptional touchdown-to-interception ratio, and looked as poised as ever.
Young was the only QB throwing for over 300 yards per game, but after a two-game skid, that number has dropped. It was exactly how he needed to start the season because, as most football fans know, Young has a multi-year contract extension looming
Entering the 2026 season, Carolina opted not to extend Young and instead exercised his fifth-year option. That move by GM Dan Morgan and the Panthers' move signaled that Young would have to go out and earn a lucrative, multi-year deal to solidify him as the long-term QB1.
Now with almost half the season in the books, there is intel and updates on the status of Young's long-term future.
NBC Sports' Mike Florio gave updates on both Bryce Young and CJ Stroud. The top two picks in the 2023 NFL Draft, both of whom have had low moments in their careers, are awaiting new contracts.
When mentioning Young, Florio leans toward him getting an extension worth more than $50 million annually. It's a steep price tag, but thats where the QB market is if Young is going to be locked in long-term.
Florio even said that he "caught wind" of Carolina trending towards granting Young that huge contract
“As to Bryce Young, we’ve recently caught wind of chatter that the Panthers are “far down the road” toward signing him to a second deal in excess of $50 million per year” https://t.co/EIgSWogpw3
There are two sides to the argument over whether Young deserves a massive contract. This season has already shown both sides of that argument to a degree.
Young hasn't been nearly as efficient through the last two weeks, which has dropped his completion percentage for the season down to 58.7%, thats 29th in the NFL.
On the flip side, Young is still eighth in total passing yards, with 1921 through seven games. The argument against Young being the problem is that he's been pressured constantly behind a depleted offensive line.
Carolina's offensive line ranks 31st in pass-block win rate. Young has been pressured 64 times this season; that's the second most in the league. That said, there are certainly other problems than the QB himself.
However, over $50 million per year means that Young must be productive even in dire situations. The Panthers need a QB who can keep the offense steady despite injuries or poor offensive line play. So far, Young still has to show he can do that week to week.
Young is clearly a starting-level talent, but if Carolina commits to him long-term, it will hinder the roster's flexibility. By the end of this season, there should be no doubt that Young can carry a heavy burden.
Young has been solid this season and has clearly improved, but if this season continues to go in the wrong way, then there has to be a heavy evaluation of the QB first and foremost.
This isn't to say that Young and Carolina can't turn this around, but right now there should be no inclination one way or the other of what happens after this season.

title: NFL Week 9 Expert Picks: Can the Panthers Turn It Around?
full_text:
It has been rough sledding for the Carolina Panthers over the last two weeks. They've been obliterated by two strong defenses that smelled blood in the water in Carolina's pass protection. Up next, the Denver Broncos. It's not ideal .
The Panthers were widely picked to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but after being trounced by them at home, almost no one had any faith in them to beat the Green Bay Packers. Has that sentiment changed back home vs. the Broncos?
CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Panthers to lose every single time out until he picked them to beat the Buccaneers. He's back to picking them to lose, and it's hard to blame him. He predicts a 26-20 Broncos win.
"The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix. This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line," he wrote.
His CBS colleague John Breech thinks the Panthers lose by one, thus covering the spread. Mike Spector of Sportsbook Review believes the Panthers can cover the spread and potentially win outright.
"Denver is fortunate to be sitting at 6-2, as it has been outgained by 221-plus yards twice (and is 1-1 in those games), while going 2-0 in games it has also been outgained by 105 and 187 yards," he wrote. "This comes with risk, as the Broncos have tied an NFL record with 15 straight regular-season wins decided by one score. But I’m hoping for an even narrower Broncos win or a double-digit Panthers win."
Erich Richter of The New York Post thinks the Broncos win in a blowout. "The Broncos are rated No. 8 in defensive DVOA and they’re allowing just 4.9 yards per play in their last three games, eighth best in the NFL," he said. "The Panthers are 18th in total DVOA and I think they’re even worse on the field than that ranking suggest. Target the Broncos to win this one big."
Bill Bender of Sporting News predicts a 28-20 Broncos win. "Is this a trap spot for the Broncos after the comeback victory against Kansas City? It's a chance to turn up the heat on Carolina quarterback Bryce Young. Denver has 23 sacks, and running back Jonah Coleman is becoming a factor in the running game. The Broncos will extend their winning streak to five games."
His colleague, Vinnie Iyer , believes this is a potential trap game for the Broncos, but he still thinks it's a double-digit Broncos win because they've found the running game "just in time" to continue "pounding on the Panthers."
Surprisingly, not many believe this can be an actual trap game. The Broncos are coming off an emotional high and traveling across multiple time zones. They're also not as good as their record would suggest.
That's telling. The Panthers are getting no respect here, and it's quite hard to argue with that.

title: Monroe Freeling Gets Midseason Grade That Might Be Too High for Panthers Rookie
full_text:
Monroe Freeling has had a rough start with the Panthers. Carolina used its first-round pick on the former Georgia tackle, hoping he'd eventually become a big part of its offensive line. His first half of the season hasn't given the team much to feel good about.
CBS Sports gave Freeling a C- in its midseason rookie grades. That might seem a little generous based on his performance, although there are some reasons to give him the benefit of the doubt.
Freeling wasn't expected to start this early, and he's been dealing with a knee injury. Those circumstances deserve some consideration. Still, the Panthers used the 19th overall pick on him, and his performance has raised some concerns.
Freeling hasn't done a good job keeping defenders away from Bryce Young. He's been beaten around the edge too many times, and Carolina has paid for it.
The numbers aren't much better. Pro Football Focus had Freeling giving up at least four pressures in four of his first five starts. That's not what the Panthers wanted from their first-round pick.
Freeling spent most of his time at Georgia playing left tackle. Now he's on the right side, and it's been a rough adjustment. He's still learning, but the Panthers need him to figure things out.
Freeling has the size to play in this league. He wouldn't have been been a first-round pick if Carolina didn't see something it liked. But right now, he needs to do a better job keeping defenders away from Young.
Freeling still has time to get things straightened out. He's only a rookie, and the Panthers aren't ready to give up on him. But they need to start seeing some improvement.
The Green Bay game was a rough one. Freeling gave up four pressures and two sacks. It wasn't a good afternoon for Carolina's offensive line.
Freeling's knee has been bothering him, and he's had to play through it. At Georgia, he spent most of his time at left tackle. Carolina has him playing on the right, and he's still getting used to it.
CBS Sports gave him a C-. Considering the injury and everything else, that's understandable. But there have been too many bad plays to say he's had a good rookie season.
The Panthers drafted Freeling because they liked what they saw at Georgia. There's still a chance he becomes a good NFL tackle. He just has a lot to prove between now and the end of the season.

title: The Case For—and Against—the Panthers Trading for Donte Jackson
full_text:
When the Panthers traded Donte Jackson to Pittsburgh, I figured his days in Carolina were over . I certainly wasn't expecting to hear his name mentioned as somebody the Panthers might want back. But with all the problems they've had at cornerback, I guess I shouldn't be surprised.
The Panthers have been trying to get by without Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, and it hasn't always been pretty. They've had to rely on guys who probably weren't expected to play this much when the season started.
Jackson spent six seasons with the Panthers before they traded him. He's with the Chargers now, and with the November 10 trade deadline coming up, I wouldn't completely rule out Carolina making a call about him.
I wouldn't mind seeing Jackson back in a Panthers uniform. I just don't know how much sense it makes to give up something to get him, especially with the injury concerns that have followed him throughout his career.
Donte Jackson wasn't nearly as good as some made him out to be during his first stint in Carolina. He had his moments, but there were also plenty of times when his coverage left a lot to be desired. Still, bringing him back isn't the worst idea considering where the Panthers are right now.
Carolina has been forced to rely on cornerbacks who probably weren't expected to play this much. That's not where a team wants to be when it's trying to stay in the playoff race. Jackson isn't going to fix everything, but he would at least give the Panthers another experienced player to put on the field.
The price would have to be right, though. Giving up an early draft pick for Jackson wouldn't make much sense. A late-round selection would be a different conversation, especially if Carolina believes it can make a run over the final stretch of the season.
Jackson doesn't have to be the player some thought he was when Carolina drafted him. He just has to be better than what the Panthers are getting from the bottom of their cornerback depth chart. And given the injuries they've dealt with, that's an argument worth considering.
There's a reason the Panthers moved on from Jackson in the first place. He could make plays, but he also had a habit of giving up some big ones. His speed helped him recover when he got beat, but that didn't always make up for the mistakes.
The bigger concern now is his health. Jackson has dealt with injuries throughout his career, and he's had trouble staying on the field this season. Carolina already has enough injured cornerbacks. Trading for another one doesn't make much sense unless the Panthers are certain he can play.
Then there's the question of what Carolina would have to give up. Even a late-round draft pick has value, especially for a team that's still trying to build its roster. Giving away picks for a short-term fix can become a problem if those moves don't work out.
The Panthers need help at cornerback, but that doesn't mean they should make a trade just to say they did something. Jackson might be worth considering if he's healthy and the price is low. Otherwise, Carolina would be better off keeping its draft picks and looking elsewhere.

title: Giants Can Help Bears by Beating Vikings, Packers to Jonathan Taylor at the Deadline
full_text:
The New York Giants could be a major asset to the Chicago Bears between now and the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
Not with any players to offer, to be clear.
The Giants, like the Bears, are buyers at this year's deadline because of how well the 2026 season has gone. New York is first place in the NFC East and has successfully resurrected J.J. McCarthy's career after two directionless seasons on the Minnesota Vikings. The Giants could be in store for the best season since Eli Manning was around. John Harbaugh has been a massive success in year one at the helm in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Instead, New York could help Chicago in the trade market by beating out the Bears' NFC North rivals that have the same needs as Big Blue.
The Vikings and, to a lesser degree, the Detroit Lions, could use a defensive run-stopper in the middle. Detroit is getting exactly what it needs from Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams, but McNeill is playing his first season back after an ACL tear and Williams is a rookie.
It's unlikely that the Lions would be willing to get in for a top defensive tackle target, but Minnesota might. The Vikings are giving up too many chunk plays and aren't getting reliable play outside of Jalen Redmond in the middle.
Of course, Chicago already filled that need with the Jeffery Simmons trade . Simmons' Bears debut, a 34-17 whooping of the defending champion Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field, proved that Chicago got in and out of the market at the right time.
The Giants could drive up the price for a defensive tackle like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Vita Vea or the Miami Dolphins' Zach Sieler.
New York could also make life tough for Minnesota and the Green Bay Packers in the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
Taylor has insisted that he doesn't want out, but the Indianapolis Colts are already in sell mode and he seems to have softened on that stance . Taylor might not have a choice in the matter either way, and he may be increasingly accepting of that fact.
"Until the past couple weeks, it's kind of been the same thing. But it won't be until Tuesday at [4 p.m.] where you'll know exactly what's going on, you'll know exactly what the verdict is," Taylor said on Thursday.
With Green Bay not knowing Josh Jacobs' future, and the Vikings owning no clear top back in one of the lowest-rated running back rooms, they are both major Taylor bidders. The Giants may be one Taylor trade away from being one of the Bears' top competitors in the NFC.
You'd rather it be New York than anyone in the NFC North. Here's to Harbaugh and Joe Schoen getting work done over the next few days.

title: Bears DC Dennis Allen Regrets Leaving Tyrique Stevenson One-on-One With Jaxon Smith-Njigba
full_text:
Some of the thinking of Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen came into focus following a disastrous play against the Seattle Seahawks.
To put it clearly, Allen is a "big-game hunter." This much was apparent from all of the blitzes he dialed up in various attempts to get pressure on quarterbacks in the pre-Jeffery Simmons days. This could be different going forward with Simmons available to apply pressure, but Allen did get caught in one gamble on Monday night in Seattle that he now regrets.
The gamble, of course, was when cornerback Tyrique Stevenson got left out by himself trying to cover one on one with NFL receiving leader Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the final minute of the first half. Stevenson committed to a Smith-Njigba slant, based on Seattle's formation. The hunch proved wrong and resulted in an easy touchdown to get the Seahawks back into a game the Bears eventually won, 34-17.
"Well look, hindsight's 20-20, right?" Allen said. "Like everybody can look at it and say hindsight is 20-20 and you wish you would have done something different and so you make the call, it doesn't work out and you think 'Aww man, maybe I should've done this.'
Double dip with Tennessee? Alontae Taylor was a versatile playmaker during his time in New Orleans under Dennis Allen. He recorded 293 tackles, 52 pass breakups, 7 sacks, and 4 INTs. While his coverage had inconsistencies, he excelled as a physical & aggressive defender.… pic.twitter.com/UV9js1iT1C
"And yet there's been games where you make a call very similar and you run back there and hit the quarterback and everybody thinks it's a great call. And so we can't judge the play based on the outcome of the play. You know, we have to really look at the whole scenario. And so, yeah, certainly when it doesn't work out you kind of wish you had it back. And yet, look, we're going big-game hunting. You know what I mean?"
Over the course of a game, Allen says it's about getting far more wins than losses. Gambling to get the QB or turnovers is all a part of it.
Dennis Allen sending a blitz with 30 seconds left and leaving his corner 1 on 1 against the best receiver in all of football! Just a dumb decision with total control of the situation. #Bears pic.twitter.com/c7QP1s7Sa7
"Look, you can’t play this game ... you’re never stealing second with your foot sitting there on first base, right?" Allen said. "You have to be aggressive. You have to be confident. And you have to try to dictate the terms to the offense.
"I’ve been in games where you’re kinda sitting back and trying to play defensive mode, and that just doesn’t really suit me, nor do I think it suits us. So we’re gonna try to do whatever it is that we think gives us the best chance for success."
Having Simmons probably doesn't mean exclusively going four-man rush all year. Blitzing would depend on the opponent. On Monday, they blitzed only 15% of downs. They had come in blitzing a third of the time, according to Pro Football Reference.
Allen's history has not always been that of a blitzing defensive coordinator. They blitzed more or less depending on personnel. In his last three full seasons they blitzed at a 22% rate or less. They were over 30% most of the season prior to that.
Tyrique Stevenson allowed a 126 passer rating when targeted and 82 yards and 2 TDs. Not good. But I honestly can’t blame him on this one. Massive push off by Cooper Kupp. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/4PFpZAUnTy
They can do what they want now up front with Simmons available.
"Like thank you he's on our team," safety Cam Lewis said. "Like I said, just makes our job on the back end easier, like we're covering from 2 1/2, three seconds and sack, or affecting the quarterback. You know what I'm saying? So it's good so far. So I'm just thankful he's here."
If Allen wants to go big-game hunting, though, it might be better to make sure he's doing it with someone else responsible for covering a receiver like Smith-Njigba.
Jeffery Simmons changes the whole equation for Dennis Allen and the Bears' defensive game plan, @olin_kreutz told @HaughPayton . The Bears already had solid players on their defensive line, but Simmons is the only one who keeps opponents up at night. pic.twitter.com/jNxRLEE0vA
What was largely hidden in Monday's win was how well they shut down Smith Njigba in the second half. Although he had six catches for 118 yards and the 43-yarder against Stevenson, he had only two catches in five targets for 26 yards in the second half.
"Look, we devoted a few more resources to him and tried to take him away," Allen said.
Going for big game doesn't necessarily have to mean sacking the quarterback. Apparently it can be shutting down one of the league's top receivers.

title: Bears' Biggest Roadblock for Khalil Mack Trade Might Not Be the Chargers After All
full_text:
Throughout the last few weeks, reports have suggested that the Los Angeles Chargers are not interested in trading anyone despite their disastrous season, which amounts to bad news for the Chicago Bears and their potential pursuit of Khalil Mack.
However, it appears that may not even be the Bears' biggest roadblock if they are indeed looking to acquire him.
According to Noah Furtado of The Athletic , Mack admitted to reporters on Thursday that he wants to stay in Los Angeles, something he has told his head coach and general manager.
"Yeah, they know how I feel, man," Mack said when asked if he told the team he wants to stay. "It's just tough with all the outside noise. And so, ultimately I want to be here and I want to help them win. Even though it's tough right now, you always see the light at the end of the tunnel."
Mack's level of loyalty is impressive, to say the least.
But this also means he might be the biggest roadblock to a trade to the Bears because if he wanted out and requested a trade, the Chargers would likely oblige and work to send him where he is looking to go out of respect.
That same respect also probably means the Chargers aren't going to trade Mack against his wishes, even though doing so would be best for the team since it would nab the Chargers a draft pick.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh has made it clear he wants to keep Mack.
“I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here. He’s one of the pillars of our team," Harbaugh said on Monday .
From the Bears' side of things, we know they have at least put in a call to the Chargers to inquire about Mack, according to FOX's Jay Glazer last week.
"I know they've already talked to, you know, the Chargers, saying, 'Hey, what about a guy like Khalil Mack?' I think they're going to be very aggressive. Ryan Poles, that's what he does. More aggressive than the other teams in that division," Glazer said of the Bears.
That is really the most concrete connection we've gotten for the Bears' interest in Mack.
Other insiders have mentioned a potential Mack to Bears trade, but those instances have sounded more like dot-connecting instead of actual reports.
The Bears could certainly use more depth at edge rusher, especially with Dayo Odeyingbo currently injured .
But EDGE might not be their biggest issue on defense right now with the struggles Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson have had at cornerback. Malik Muhammad is also battling an injury, although it doesn't appear to be anything serious.
ESPN's Dan Graziano recently reported that the Bears are indeed looking around for a cornerback, so that's something to monitor with the deadline rapidly approaching.
"The Bears made their big move for Simmons, but they're still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions," Graziano wrote.
As for Mack, we're becoming less and less optimistic each day about a possible trade for the nine-time Pro Bowler and his aforementioned quote only drives that home further.

title: Caleb Williams Reveals Ben Johnson Scraps Plays He Doesn't Like, and Why it Works
full_text:
Few relationships in any professional sport are more important than a quarterback and his head coach or play-caller. Many analysts compare it to a marriage because it's a relationship that requires constant communication and compromise. Many of these pairings don't work out (looking at you, Indianapolis), but for the Chicago Bears, they may have struck gold with Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson .
While speaking to the media on Wednesday afternoon, Williams was asked about how Johnson will try to push him out of his comfort zone as a quarterback , specifically when it comes to play calls. "I trust Ben with it," Williams replied. "If he calls something and I don't like it, we go up into his office. We sit down, we talk about it, he shows me clips, and if I still don't like it... he won't call it."
But it's not a one-way road. Williams went on to add, "A lot of time we'll go up into the office and talk about it. We'll watch multiple, multiple, multiple clips, and at the end of it I typically feel pretty good about it and where we want to go with the ball."
Reading between the lines, we can see that Williams and Johnson have developed the kind of mutual trust in each other that often leads to winning. It'd be easy for Johnson to simply throw his authority in Williams' face and make him run a concept he doesn't believe in. Likewise, Williams could easily retreat into a shell and stop communicating. Instead, we get a relationship that works and it's pushing the Bears closer to a Super Bowl.
When the dust settled following the Bears' hiring of Ben Johnson as their head coach , some NFL analysts publicly doubted the wisdom of pairing a play-caller known for meticulously detailed offenses with a quarterback who made a living off of improvising. Colin Cowherd said on his The Herd with Colin Cowherd radio program that Williams can't play in structure , and that would lead inevitably to a failed head coach-quarterback pairing.
But Cowherd and other analysts completely missed the point of this duo. Johnson may have ran a different style of offense while he was in Detroit, and Williams may have preferred to run around playing backyard football, but they're cut from the same cloth. Both Johnson and Williams are obsessed with winning and going down in history as all-time greats.
Of course Johnson was not going to ask Williams to run the same kind of offense he designed for Jared Goff of the Lions, at least not right away. Johnson knew that he had to find a system that worked for his new quarterback. One that allowed him to go off-script but also would gradually and inexoribly pull him into a regimented structure. That's how winning is done in the NFL.
As for Williams, he's mature enough to take the hard coaching that Johnson dishes out and use it as fuel. He won't stand on his pride and let some hurt feelings get in the way of greatness. He wants Johnson to mold him into an elite quarterback, and we're finally seeing that take shape.
As aforementioned, Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams seem to have a strong give-and-take in their relationship. Johnson will push for Williams to trust him on a play, and Williams often will. But if the quarterback feels very strongly about a play, the head coach cans it. That's a major amount of trust for Johnson to have in Williams, and so far Williams has proven worthy of it. They seem to have a perfect understanding of what they need to do, both individually and together, to accomplish their goals.
Time will tell whether this duo can take the Chicago Bears back to the Promised Land and add a second Lombardi trophy to Halas Hall. They certainly seem the part of Super Bowl favorites after their statement primetime victory over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8.

title: Bucs Just Ran for 324 Yards, But Baker Mayfield Is Worried About One Bears Defender
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulled off a remarkable feat in last week's 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons. They won with -2 net passing yards, as quarterback Baker Mayfield went 0/3 and took a two-yard sack under monsoon-like conditions that would've made Chicago's Week 2 matchup against Minnesota look like a drizzle.
Luckily for Tampa Bay, their rushing attack was more than equipped to carry the load. Bucky Irving, currently fourth in the league with 728 yards on the ground, led the team with 27 attempts for 170 yards. Meanwhile, backup Kenny Gainwell added 25 attempts for 140 yards.
That performance has become somewhat of a trend for Tampa Bay over the past month, as they've eclipsed 240 yards on the ground in three of their last four games. They're the only team with more rushing yards than Chicago, and they're averaging nearly 20 more rushing yards per game (168.6 vs. 150.8 yards).
The Bucs boast an offense that looks like it could run over anyone. Mayfield is concerned that Jeffery Simmons might throw a wrench into their plans, though.
"Obviously, he's a game-wrecker. Even when he was in Tennessee, all eyes are on figuring out where he is," Mayfield said. "He's a guy that could truly make a difference in a ball game.
"They already had a good defense, so all he does is add to that and allows their talented guys up front to get individual pass rush reps. He definitely adds an element to their D."
Before the Bears acquired Simmons, the only player that opposing offenses had to gameplan against was Kyler Gordon , and he didn't even play over their first five games. With him playing nickelback, he's also less vital to a defense's success than a defensive lineman who can impact every snap.
To their credit, Austin Booker and Montez Sweat are solid starters and good pass-rushers. They don't strike fear into offenses the way Simmons does, though. Unlike No. 99, they also don't offer much in terms of run defense.
Simmons' impact on Chicago's defense was felt immediately . If you remove Sam Darnold's two scrambles (for 20 yards) from the equation, the Bears gave up only 61 yards off 17 Seattle rushing attempts on Monday night.
Notably, the Seahawks averaged only three yards per play when he was on the field, as opposed to 13.3 yards when he was on the sideline. That's the reason Mayfield highlighted him as an X-factor for Chicago's defense.
Jeffery Simmons is as advertised The Bears are the team to beat in the NFC pic.twitter.com/s0PZbj8LNQ
Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen knows what the Bears have in Simmons , as well.
"I don't know if I've had anybody that's been what I'd consider this dominant," Allen told reporters last week. "I've had some good players that have played inside for us. David Onyemata comes to mind, but I don't know that I've had anybody this disruptive."
Well, the Bears do now, and opposing offenses have clearly taken notice. A 34-17 statement victory against the defending Super Bowl champions will do that.
Simmons will hopefully help the defense make another statement against the Buccaneers' elite rushing attack on Sunday night.

title: Kyle Monangai Injury Update & Everything Else From Bears' Thursday Practice Report
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' Thursday practice report is out and it has both good news and bad news for the Bears ahead of their Week 9 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.
The bad news comes from the fact that two players on the injury report didn't see any progress from yesterday's estimated version , and Chicago saw a new addition with linebacker D'Marco Jackson.
The good news is that two other players who were estimated non-participants to start the week saw an uptick in participation on Thursday.
Now, a full look at the injury report.
Good news for left tackle Theo Benedet and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett, as both were upgraded from non-participants to limited. T.J. Edwards was upgraded, also, but his lack of participation Wednesday wasn't injury-related.
With Benedet and Jarrett getting in a limited session, that puts them back on track to suit up.
Earlier in the day, offensive coordinator Press Taylor sounded optimistic that Ozzy Trapilo would be ready to play a full complement of snaps if Benedet can't go.
"I feel pretty good about the path we've put him on to be able to do that if needed," Taylor said, according to Sean Hammond of The Chicago Tribune .
The new addition, Jackson, is dealing with an ankle injury. He was listed on last week's injury report with an ankle issue, but it isn't clear if it's the same one.
With Monangai failing to practice yet again, we can pretty much rule him out for Week 9 already, which means another week of Roschon Johnson filling in as RB2.
The Bears willl have a new RB3, though, as Zavier Scott was placed on injured reserve earlier in the day with a thumb injury. Scott will miss at least the next four games, and that is all he is expected to miss, per Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune .
When it comes to who will replace Scott, the only other healthy back on the roster other than Swift and Johnson is Salvon Ahmed, who was one of the Bears' standouts during the offseason.
We could see Chicago add another back to the practice squad, but Ahmed will likely be the guy who gets the nod for Week 9.

title: Bill Barnwell Confirms the Bears Have One More Hole to Fill After Jeffery Simmons Trade
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is still five days away, but the Chicago Bears already got on the board last week with a blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons . They sent two first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for the superstar defensive tackle, along with a Day 3 pick swap, and it already paid dividends with Simmons' impressive debut with the Bears on Monday.
That trade was the biggest swing the Bears have taken since 2018, but ESPN's Bill Barnwell believes they have one more hole to fill. In a Thursday morning article examining 18 contenders ahead of the trade deadline , Barnwell lumped the Bears in his "Should be Selectively Adding" group and rightly identifies the cornerback room as the team's biggest liability.
To that end, Barnwell provides two options for the Bears. On one hand, they could swing a 'luxury' trade for the expensive Alontae Taylor, who flourished under Dennis Allen in New Orleans but has wildly underperformed in Tennessee. On the other, they could opt for a reunion with Nahshon Wright, who has not seen a single defensive snap for the New York Jets this season after signing a one-year contract with them.
Taylor would likely be a good addition for the Bears' secondary, and would certainly be a step up from Jaylon Johnon or Tyrique Stevenson. And his familiarity with Dennis Allen is a good sweetener. However, his contract is one of the worst in the NFL, and the Bears would be on the hook for $21 million in 2027, according to Barnwell. They would basically be swapping one bloated cornerback contract for another.
As for Wright, it has to be pointed out how badly he struggled last year. Yes, he led the league in takeaways, and Bears fans will always be greatful for that. But takeaways tend to flux quite a bit from year to year; just ask Kevin Byard III in New England, who only has one pick a year after leading the league with seven.
The truth is that Wright's Pro Bowl honors last year were mostly smoke and mirrors as he struggled badly when he wasn't getting takeaways, and he almost certainly would not replicate last year's performance in that regard. When he wasn't taking the ball away, Wright was getting burned in coverage at an alarming rate. Plus, if even the Jets can't see any use for him on defense, why should the Bears expect any different?
Luckily for the Bears, these are not their only two options for addressing the weakness in their cornerback room. They could, and in my opinion should, swing a trade for Riq Woolen. When I wrote last week that the Bears should make one more trade before the deadline , Woolen was who I had in mind as a good-not-great option.
Compared to Taylor and Wright, Woolen is a good compromise. His contract is not nearly as bad as Taylor's, and a trade for Woolen would likely be cheap on draft capital, too. But he also offers considerably more upside than Wright.

title: Bears' Backfield Takes Another Hit With RB Placed on IR Amid Kyle Monangai Injury
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' backfield was already dealing with an injury to Kyle Monangai and now they've lost another running back.
The Bears announced on Thursday that they have placed running back Zavier Scott on injured reserve because of the thumb injury suffered in the Week 8 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
We did not hear of Scott suffering an injury during the game and first found out about his issue when he was listed on the injury report on Wednesday.
Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune reports that while Scott was listed with a wrist injury, it's actually a thumb. Biggs adds that Scott is probably looking at a minimum stay on IR, which is four games.
Scott was signed to the practice squad after cutdown day and has been serving as the team's No. 3 running back behind D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson while Monangai has been out.
Scott hasn't played a snap on offense over four games, but he did become a key member of the special teams unit, which is part of the reason why he was recently promoted to the active roster.
Monangai has been out for four games with his turf toe injury and, at least for now, he's on track to sit out yet again in Week 9 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Monangai was listed as a non-participant once again in practice on Wednesday. The injury report was an estimate, but that is status quo for him because he has not practiced once since suffering his injury in Week 4 against the New York Jets.
“No, I think every time a player has an Injury, you don’t know how a player will bounce back from that. Obviously, we didn’t think it was warranted to put him on IR, and yet we’re hopefully we’ll get him back sooner rather than later," head coach Ben Johnson said when asked about Monangai's status last week.
We'll see if Monangai can finally get back to practice on Thursday, but if not, he's almost certainly headed for another absence.
Barring the Bears signing another running back, the last man standing other than Swift and Johnson is Salvon Ahmed.
Ahmed has been on the practice squad all season long but has not gotten into a game yet.
The veteran running back had an impressive training camp and preseason and was actually a better runner than Johnson, but Ahmed's lack of special teams ability led to the Bears keeping Johnson over him.
And that could lead to Chicago potentially going out-of-house for Scott's replacement if Monangai can't go, but we'll have to wait and see if that's indeed the case.

title: Did the Bears Get a Steal in Jeffery Simmons? Other Teams Say They Would Have Paid More
full_text:
Today marks one week since the Chicago Bears poached defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.
Two first-round picks, and a fourth-round pick for the game-wrecker, and a fifth-round pick. If Monday night's 34-17 win against Seattle ( in Seattle) is any indication, those first-rounders will be very late .
If that contest is a sign of things to come, it's abundantly clear Chicago's trade package was too light. Simmons was a force to be reckoned with on every snap, and they allowed only three yards per play when he was on the field (as opposed to allowing 13.3 yards per play with him on the sideline).
Jeffery Simmons' first sack as a Bear! What an animal! pic.twitter.com/cREmg2m9SA
The Titans reportedly maintained that Simmons wasn't for sale, but Bears general manager Ryan Poles began the negotiation by mentioning the two first-round selections. That's the key disparity that eventually got the deal over the finish line.
The Bears weren't bidding against other teams. As it turns out, other general managers wish they had gotten a chance to get in on the action. NFL insider Ari Meirov provided some insight into those conversations this morning.
"I still do have a couple of issues with what Tennessee did because I do think they could've opened this up, have more of a bidding war here, maybe get more [compensation]," Meirov said. "But they felt like that package was good enough and this was not going to leak anywhere and the player is not going to find out in the media before he gets traded.
"There are teams out there who told me, and maybe they're just saying this because it's after the face, they told me they would've offered more for Jeffery Simmons. This was not shopped by the Titans."
The Simmons deal was the third blockbuster of its kind in the last calendar year. The first of which occurred ahead of the trade deadline last season, when the then 7-2 Colts traded two first-round picks and receiver Adonai Mitchell to the Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner.
Mitchell had struggled to carve out a role in the Colts' offense, but he's looked much more promising this season in New York. Meanwhile, Indianapolis won only one game the rest of the way (after QB Daniel Jones tore his Achilles tendon) and only three games since. The trade looks like a fleece for New York.
The Browns also traded reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett to the Rams for edge rusher Jared Verse and a first-, second-, and third-round selection this offseason. Sure, Garrett was coming off one of the best defensive seasons we've ever seen from a defensive lineman (his 23 sacks set an NFL record), but that's a much steeper price than what the Bears gave up for a similarly impactful player.
Verse made a Pro Bowl in each of his first two seasons and still had two years remaining on his rookie contract (and a relatively inexpensive fifth-year option). He would've probably fetched a first- and second-round pick on his own. Garrett is also a year and a half older than Simmons.
Just throwing guys around pic.twitter.com/tXv08td7gu
The hefty compensation was a small price to pay for the impact that he's already had on their defense . Other GMs clearly had foresight that the situation might play out that way, as well.

title: 3 Wide Receivers That Bengals Could Trade for to Bolster Their Offense
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals could've pursued receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. before the Arizona Cardinals traded him to the Houston Texans. Harrison would have come to Cincinnati and slotted in as a much-needed wide receiver No. 3.
The Bengals need to add another playmaker on offense. Coming into Week 8, the Bengals had seen little production from their wide receiver room aside from Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
If they opt for a trade, who could the Bengals target?
The Indianapolis Colts will almost certainly sell at the trade deadline, and they could look to move on from wide receiver Josh Downs.
Downs is a very talented option, but he needs a better offense with a more consistent quarterback. The Bengals would give him that with an offense centered around Chase, Higgins, and Joe Burrow. Downs would be a massive upgrade over what the Bengals have on their roster right now. This season, Downs has caught 26 passes for 307 yards coming into Week 8.
Another wide receiver who could be on the move is Jacksonville Jaguars pass catcher Brian Thomas Jr. Thomas has been moved down on the depth chart in Jacksonville and could desperately use a change of scenery.
Adding him to the Bengals' offense, which is high-powered and relies on throwing the ball, could be exactly what he needs. He hasn't done much this season, though he's tallied a few touchdowns.
The Bengals could also make a move for wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who hasn't made much of an impact in Minnesota this season.
Still, he has some potential left to provide to a high-powered offense. Jennings would be very affordable to acquire in a deal, and he would give the Bengals a veteran to add to their depleted wide receiver room. At the very least, he would be a solid veteran in a room with multiple young wide receivers.

title: Zac Taylor Drops Friday Injury Status Update For DJ Turner, Cedric Johnson Ahead of Falcons Spain Game
full_text:
The Bengals look likely to field Cedric Johnson (ankle) and DJ Turner (heel) to defend against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, barring any big setbacks. Alas, Zac Taylor spoke to the media on Friday before the team's final practice in Madrid, Spain, and noted the two are continuing with "day-to-day" status.
Their official statuses will come out on the final injury report.
Turner practiced fully on Thursday, while Johnson went limited, so it would be pretty shocking if they didn't play. Jordan Battle (hamstring) was limited as well, and Kyle Dugger (quad) looks like he'll miss another game after not practicing again on Thursday.
"Everyone is progressing ahead. We'll take it day-to-day for both DJ and Ced," Taylor said before touching on the team's acclimation to the new country/setting. "We feel acclimated. We had a great day of practice yesterday. Field held up really well. Our guys have handled the week really well."
Cincinnati has a couple more days in Spain before battling the Falcons at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday and returning to Cincinnati ahead of the most important game of the season so far: A home AFC North battle against Pittsburgh for control of the division on Sunday Night Football.
They need to take out another NFC opponent first.
"I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," Taylor said on Thursday about the travel plans. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far."
All in all, Cincinnati is in a new country, but on a normal practice schedule.
"Normal Thursday for us," Taylor said. "We did our Wednesday practice on Tuesday before we left town. So now we're back on schedule. Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based."
The Bengals can enjoy the city even more on Saturday before Sunday showtime.

title: Colts' Jonathan Taylor Timeline Could Impact Bengals' Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have been connected to a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the NFL trade deadline. The Colts are listening to offers for Taylor and the Bengals are one of the teams reportedly interested in the star running back .
The deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 and the Bengals need to make their run at Taylor if they're going to land him.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz recently provided an update on the Colts' trade timeline, reporting that Indianapolis won't look to make a deal until after Week 9's games unless they're blown away by a trade offer.
"The Colts have received plenty of calls on several players, including Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, Grover Stewart and others," Schultz wrote on X. "But the belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline."
The Bengals have been connected to Taylor and Downs over the last few weeks. Having an additional week to separate themselves from the rest of the AFC is a good thing. If the Bengals win this week, it's another reason why they should go all in this season. They're not just a contender, but they're one of the best teams in the league. The difference between getting bounced in the AFC Championship and bringing home the Super Bowl might be having Taylor in the backfield next to Joe Burrow. If the Bengals have another big win this week while the running game struggles, it would reinforce the idea that Taylor would help them tremendously.
Downs would be a good target, too. The Bengals need a No. 3 wide receiver, and he has what it takes to help them out. The dream scenario would see the Bengals package draft picks to send to Indianapolis in exchange for Taylor and Downs.
The Bengals could land a playmaker on offense or some help on defense ahead of Tuesday's deadline. In the meantime, they're in Spain getting ready to play the Falcons on Sunday. Kickoff is at 9:30 am ET.

title: Referee for Bengals-Falcons Game Leads League in Defensive Pass Interference Flags
full_text:
CINCINNATI – The referee who worked the game with one of the worst calls of the Zac Taylor era will be on the call Sunday when the Cincinnati Bengals face the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid.
In a 2021 road game against the New York Jets , what looked like a routine tackle by Mike Hilton on a third-and-11checkdown should have result in the Bengals getting the ball back down three points with two minutes to go.
It looked as though Jets running back Michael Carter initiated the helmet-to-helmet contact as Hilton was going for his legs, but Hilton drew the flag, and the Jets killed the clock to win 34-31 as 11-point underdogs
It wasn’t Wrolstad who threw that flag. It was line judge Tripp Sutter, who has had multiple run-ins with the Bengals coaching staff.
Sutter won’t be working Sunday’s Bengals game as he is on fellow Cincinnati villain Ron Torbert’s crew this season.
The Bengals are 6-5 with Wrolstad as the head referee. The last Cincinnati game he worked was last year’s Thanksgiving night win in Baltimore.
Wrolstad and his crew rank third this year with an average of 17.14 accepted penalties per game.
Last year they were 12th (11.61), but in 2024 they were second (14.82).
In 2023, Wrolstad was 13th (9.88), and in 2022 he was 16th (9.35).
Wrolstad’s crew has called 17 defensive pass interference penalties this year, most in the league. No other crew has more than 13.
Ironically, the crew ranks last in defensive holding flags with just one all season.
The group also has five roughing-the-passer penalties, which are one shy of the league lead this year. And their 26 offensive holding penalties rank fifth.
Wrolstad has been a head official since 2014 and has earned playoff assignments in each of the four three seasons after being left off the postseason schedule in five of his first seven seasons.

title: Bengals Injury Report: Cincinnati's Injured Defenders Working Back to Action in Spain
full_text:
The Bengals hit the practice field in Spain for the first time this week as multiple defenders try to work back onto the field from injuries. DJ Turner II (heel), Cedric Johnson (ankle), and Kyle Dugger (quad) are fighting through issues this week, as is Jordan Battle (hamstring).
Turner was a full participant on Thursday meaning he is set to play barring any setbacks on Friday. Johnson and Battle went limited on Thursday, while Dugger continued missing practice. It's a good sign for most of that group to be able to play on Sunday morning against the Falcons.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor noted Turner and Johnson would be day-to-day on Tuesday before the team left for Spain, and he didn't have many specific comments on the injured group during his Thursday media session.
He did go in-depth on the logistics that went into making this international trip happen.
"We've got a team of people that logistically have handled this stuff for us that have been just top-notch," Taylor said. "And so my hats off to everybody who's helped us get set up and hit the ground running here. There are two teams here, and your job is to handle the week better than the other team as much as possible. And so again, I don't have Atlanta's itinerary. I'm not going to be able to watch their practices or anything like that.
"But just challenge our guys. We're only playing one other team, not playing 31 other teams. Playing one. And so you've got to control everything you can control to play your best on Sunday. I don't know that it's getting away from the monotony of this season. This is something we've got to be able to control to the best of our abilities and be able to play well on Sunday. And this game is going to count just like all the others. And so shame on us if we do something that steps out of line and we're not prepared."
Cincinnati kicks off Week 9 on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET.

title: 'I Don't Think Anybody's Happy' - Jonathan Allen, Bengals Defense Can Resettle Across Spain Trip
full_text:
Jonathan Allen and the Bengals are far from satisfied nearing the midway point of the 2026 NFL season at 5-2. Allen spoke to the media at his locker on Monday afternoon before he and the team left for Spain on Tuesday.
They have another strong winning opportunity this week as betting favorites against the Atlanta Falcons, and plenty to clean up on defense after allowing the Titans to score 36 points this past weekend.
It was Tennessee's highest point total dating back to Oct. 10, 2021. Since Week 5, Cincinnati is slipping on defense, ranking 18th in EPA/play allowed in that span and a lowly 26th in success rate allowed.
"You know we're sitting at 5-2, and I don't think anybody's happy about how we've played as a team up to this point. I think it's probably only one game defense can say we played a complete game, and I'm sure offense will say the same thing. So for us, we're just trying to get better every day," Allen said.
Allen is flashing here and there this season and has been largely solid in counting stats, but is posting a 59 overall Pro Football Focus grade across 294 snaps.
He's had two 80-plus grades this season and will look to have that type of impact again in an international setting. Allen has 20 tackles, three sacks, and a forced fumble this season. One more sack and he'll beat out his 2024 and 2025 production.
Unfortunately for Atlanta, it melted in the rain against Tampa Bay this past weekend, and it's forecasted to be wet again across the pond. The Bengals can't count on another hapless performance in the elements, though.
"You have to defend every blade of grass. With a guy like Bijan (Robinson), he can jump cut, reverse field. So it's going to be interesting, and you know we're excited about it," Allen said about the Falcons and Michael Penix. "That's definitely a guy who can make all the throws, has a great group, a great weapon, and a great coaching scheme. So, it's definitely going to be a fun challenge for us. But we're looking forward to the opportunity."
Even when taking out the horrible backup QB play Atlanta had in the first month, the Falcons still rank 30th in offensive EPA/play since Week 5 began. Cincinnati has the chance to get right on defense if Jonathan Allen & Co. can execute the right way.
We know the offense should hold up its end of the bargain. The Bengals rank first in EPA/play by a wide margin in that window, and Joe Burrow just became the first QB in NFL history with a 70% completion rate and four-plus pass TDs in three straight games.

title: Super Bowl Champion Labels Bengals as Contenders During 2026 Season
full_text:
After a 5-2 start, the Bengals have once again firmly established themselves among the best teams in the AFC. That said, the team still has plenty of flaws, but legends like Rob Gronkowski haven't stopped acknowledging them as a contender.
Gronkowski acknowledged the tackling issues and inability to run the football. However, he also clarified that Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins, Ja'Marr Chase, and the team's tight ends make the team a must-watch spectacle week in and week out.
"They're contenders, but they're also a little pretend a little bit because of the miscues, a lot of turnovers still, they can't run the ball, their defense can't tackle," Gronkowski said on the Gronk and Jules show. "But their offense is so fire, and we love watching them go, Tee Higgins, Ja'Marr Chase, Joe Burrow, they got a couple tight ends as well, you gotta tune in to the Cincinnati Bengals, they are a fireworks show basically every weekend."
Burrow set new career highs against the Titans in the team's 43-36 overtime win, totaling six touchdowns, while Higgins and Chase combined for 21 catches, 296 yards, and three touchdowns.
Both the defense and run game failed to impress against the lowly Titans, and neither has maintained the consistency that fans crave. However, the Bengals' offense can still beat any team in the league with its explosiveness.
Burrow and the team's other stars have consistently proven they can hold their own in shootouts over the last three years. The difference between now and those last three years, however, is the defense's ability to make a big play in a big moment. While the unit failed to make a play in key moments in the past, Dexter Lawrence changed that trend with a late-fourth-quarter sack of Cam Ward on Sunday to force overtime.
That moment, combined with a Boye Mafe strip-sack in the third quarter after Burrow threw an interception, shows this team can win high-scoring games after years of failure. Burrow himself confirmed this in his postgame press conference when he acknowledged that the Bengals win over the Titans has resulted in a loss in the past three seasons.
“We found a way to win today, we are 5-2, we lose that game the last three years.” Burrow said.
With the defense showing it can close out games on Sunday, the Bengals offense alone makes this team a true contender for the rest of the season.

title: Zac Taylor Comments on Team Health After Bengals Arrival in Spain
full_text:
Zac Taylor spoke to the media in Madrid, Spain, on Thursday morning, Cincinnati time.
The schedules are shifted in a big way for the Bengals, with all of their practices happening in the afternoon locally and in the morning on Eastern Standard Time.
Taylor gave the latest update on injuries to DJ Turner (heel) and Cedric Johnson (ankle).
According to The Enquirer's Kelsey Conway, Taylor noted a few players would be limited today but did not specify who. A good sign for Turner and Johnson's health that they weren't specificially ruled out.
Cincinnati is 5-2 this season in a close AFC North race with the Pittsburgh Steelers. They have had one of the best offenses in the NFL this season, and by far the best over the past month.
Taylor's unit is posting 0.216 EPA/play on offense since Week 5 began (first in the league by a wide margin). They are also first in success rate (58%).
Getting Turner and Johnson back on the field would be a boost for everyone, including that humming offense. Cornerback is a fluid position this week. Cincinnati still doesn't have Jalen Davis back from injured reserve yet.
"Thought he came in there and provided a lot of energy and competed and got Dax back outside," Taylor said about Josh Newton's repps in the game. "This time DJ is down, so now you got different grouping in there. And so that was a little bit of the plan going into the game, and then it evolves when you have an injury. But because those guys keep competing, and they're all ready when their numbers go on."
Cincinnati has practices today and tomorrow before the off day Saturday and show time on Sunday. Joe Burrow is healthy and ready to attack the Falcons as the most impactful passer in the league right now.
"We found a way to win today," Burrow said after beating the Titans. "We're 5-2. We've lost that game for the last three years. It's hard to win. You want to be great, snap in, snap out, but it's not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and get better. You win from wins and losses and good plays and bad plays. That's what the NFL and getting better is. We'll continue to do that."
Cincinnati takes on the Falcons Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET.

title: Multiple Outlets Believe Bengals Are Perfect Fit for Star Running Back Breece Hall
full_text:
It's a big weekend for the Cincinnati Bengals. Fresh off of their dramatic win over the Tennessee Titans, the Bengals are in Spain as they prepare for battle with the Atlanta Falcons.
A win over the Falcons on Sunday morning would put the Bengals in a prime position as the postseason race heats up. To compete with the rest of the top teams in the league, the Bengals could make a few additions to the roster prior to the trade deadline on November 10th.
There has been a lot of talk about this team adding a running back before the deadline, and a lot of fans are hoping that running back is Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor. However, the Bengals have now been linked to one of the more underrated backfield stars in the league.
B/R Gridiron has listed the Bengals as one of the next teams to make a potential blockbuster trade. The potential trade has the team landing New York Jets running back Breece Hall.
Hall has only appeared in three games this season, as he suffered a quad injury. However, NFL insider Ian Rapoport has revealed that Hall is good to go and should play this week.
There's no doubt that the veteran running back would elevate the backfield in Cincinnati. In his three games this season, Hall has rushed for 163 yards and one touchdown. Last season, the former second-round pick had his best season, rushing for over 1,000 yards for the first time in his career.
Bleacher report isn't the only one to mention the Bengals as a trade fit for Hall.
Jason Buechler of New York Jets On SI listed the Bengals as a trade fit for Hall.
"The Bengals have had one of the league's worst rushing attacks throughout Joe Burrow's career. They have trusted Chase Brown, but the fourth-year RB has managed only 340 rushing yards in seven games in 2027. Hall could be the perfect replacement for a Bengals team that has struggled to establish the run," Buechler wrote. "Hall makes an impact in both the rushing and passing game. That is exactly what Cincinnati needs. They are almost too dedicated to the pass, having had a bottom-five rushing offense over the past five years. Hall's ability to shine in both aspects of the offense may matter more to a team like Cincy than some think.
"Hall is in the first year of a three-year contract, so this is more than a rental. Hall could slot into the Bengals' offense and take over the backfield immediately. With the Ohio team holding all its 2027 draft picks, including an extra third-rounder, New York could push for the Bengals' second-round pick."
The Bengals would prefer to keep their second round pick. Would a third rounder get it done?
There shouldn't be any injury worries with Hall from an injury standpoint. He started at least 16 games for the Jets every single season.
Taylor is probably the dream addition still, and rightfully so, but if the Jets plan on moving players at the deadline, the Bengals shouldn't hesitate to reach out.
The biggest holdup in the Bengals making a move would have to be what the front office is willing to give up. If Taylor is the route they go, the Bengals may have to say goodbye to a second-round pick, and other assets. One would have to think the asking price for Hall would be lower.
Worrying about a discount shouldn't matter, but the front office has to take the future into account. This team can win with either running back discussed. As the trade deadline approaches, things are getting really interesting.

title: NFL Legends Make Case for Bengals to Trade for NFL All-Pro Before Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals are one of several teams "aggressively" pursuing Colts running back Jonathan Taylor according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. The Bengals should add Taylor for plenty of reasons, given his elite ability and their lack of run-game production. Future Hall of Famer and current CBS Sports announcer J.J. Watt chimed in on the fit for Taylor in Cincinnati and why it makes more sense than any other trade destination.
"I really do believe the Cincinnati Bengals make sense for a guy like him because of what their offense has in terms of the passing game and they just haven't been able to get going on the ground," Watt said on the CBS "Set Hut" show
Taylor has shined as one of the only bright spots of a subpar Colts roster in Indianapolis with 812 total yards and eight touchdowns on 169 touches. Meanwhile, Chase Brown and Samaje Perine have combined for 735 yards and three scores on 173 touches for the Bengals so far this season.
While those stats look similar, the difference is night and day in terms of who the bigger threat is on the field. Taylor is a threat to score every time he touches the ball as evidenced from his 40 touchdowns over the last three seasons.
Watt is not alone in believing the Bengals should target Taylor. Bengals legend Cris Collinsworth and his son Jac pointed out that the team is in a position to fix a glaring hole, similar to how the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons.
"With what Jeffery Simmons did in that game the other day for the Chicago Bears, who can match that, and can you do it with the guys that you currently have on your roster or are you now forced to do what the Bears did, which is to go out and fix that glaring hole on your football team," Collinsworth asked.
Collinsworth pointed to the Pro Football Focus grades of the Bengals' offensive line and the success of the new defensive additions as reasons to go all in and acquire Taylor.
"Dalton Risner is coming off an 80.0 grade, Amarius Mims coming off a 75.2 grade," Collinsworth said . "Now with the defense and Dexter Lawrence comes in and Boye Mafe comes in and the Bengals make moves that they've just never made, it's right now, it's this year, so go do it."
After sending the 10th overall pick to Dexter Lawrence this offseason and adding other pieces to the defense to complement the offense, the Bengals must now continue their all-in approach. Acquiring Taylor would potentially add another dynamic facet to the offense, similar to that of Colts Hall of Famer Edgerrin James.
James consistently created big plays for the Colts alongside Peyton Manning, Marvin Harrison, and Reggie Wayne in the early 2000s, helping field some of the greatest offenses the NFL has ever seen.
Taylor could create that same dynamic in Cincinnati in an offense featuring Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. The most important part of that dynamic is that the Bengals offense could efficiently run the ball and close out games down the stretch.
The trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10 at 4 pm ET.

title: What Shedeur Sanders Needs to do to Win First 2026 Start
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are preparing to head into their Week 9 matchup without their starting quarterback, Deshaun Watson .
The good news for Cleveland is that Shedeur Sanders is the backup. Don't forget Sanders and Watson battled it out in training camp, with many fans believing Shedeur should have been selected as the guy.
Now that he will be starting on the road against the New Orleans Saints , here are some things Sanders needs to do to get a win in his first start of 2026.
Currently, the Browns have allowed the most sacks in the entire NFL this season, with 33.
While a lot of fault goes to the offensive line, a handful of sacks and really lots of plays that didn't work successfully come from Deshaun Watson holding onto the football for far too long.
Especially with Sanders, if he sits in the pocket too long, he will most likely turn the ball over. Last season, we saw this on display as he finished his rookie season with 10 interceptions thrown.
If Shedeur can find targets quickly, Cleveland has some great playmakers that can take the majority of the workload. That leads me into my next key to starting Sanders
KC Concepcion is already one of the SHIFTIEST slot WR’s in the entire NFL. Through 7 GP, Concepcion has recorded 30 receptions and 383 total yards. The Browns rookie WR is IMPOSSIBLE to stop in open space 😳🕹️ https://t.co/AzawKHVuhW pic.twitter.com/d1OnKCQkgE
While Sanders does have some nice athletic talent and playmaking ability, it is still pretty raw as the quarterback is only in his second season.
With that being said, head coach Todd Monken needs to treat this start for Sanders like the week two matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
In that game, Deshaun Watson was able to bounce back from a really poor week one performance in Jacksonville. Not only did he look great, he built confidence that carried into the next games that followed.
For Monken and Sanders, they must take the same approach. Keep the game plan simple, and when Sanders needs to pass have him get the ball out quickly to the numorous young playmkaers this team has to offer.
Finally, the Browns were able to get their run game going against the Tennessee Titans. However, Pittsburgh did a great job once again at stopping Cleveland from gaining yards on the ground.
Looking at the Saints, in over 200 rushing attempts from opponents, they have allowed about 4.8 yards per carry.
This is great news for Cleveland. If Quinshon Judkins can move the ball down the field and capitalize on red zone drives, maybe the Browns can take a page out of the Buccaneers' playbook and not have to rely on the quarterback as much.
While it will be nice to see how much improvement Shedeur Sanders has made since last season, this game is a must win for the Browns.
Last season, there wasn't much on the line when Sanders stepped in. Now, Cleveland not only has a chance for their first playoff appearance since 2023, but their first AFC North title ever.

title: Sunday's Outcome Will Be Determined By One Thing The Browns And Saints Have In Common
full_text:
A movable object will meet a stopping force in New Orleans as the Cleveland Browns head south to take on the Saints. The Browns are coming off a thrashing by the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the Saints will be rested after their bye week.
They need to keep pace in a very competitive AFC North as they sit in third place with a 5-3 record.
The Browns are finishing a three-game road trip, in which they are 1-1. In their win, they were able to run the ball, and it was their best rushing game of the season. The contrary happened in their loss, as the ground game was nonexistent. The rushing offense has been lackluster all season; however, the Saints’ biggest issue is stopping the run.
The Saints are 29th in the league in stopping the run, giving up an average of 139.4 yards per game. However, the Browns are 24th, averaging 92.6 rushing yards per game. Quinshon Judkins has only 342 yards so far this season , and Deshaun Watson’s 217 yards help the offense’s rushing average.
Running the ball will be imperative to a Browns’ victory, as it is likely that Shedeur Sanders will start , as Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol. Sanders can be successful if the offense can run, as it will allow fewer defenders in the secondary to mix up coverages and try to confuse the second-year quarterback. The Browns could also be missing Watson’s rushing ability to extend plays and get first downs.
#Browns Deshaun Watson (concussion) didn’t practice again today on Thursday of #Saints week. Shedeur Sanders very likely to start.
If Watson does start, then the Browns have to be able to run the ball to get it out of his hands. He took eight sacks last week and had more hits on top of that. He could use a game where he is on his feet more than his back, with the bye week looming.
On the other hand, the Browns have played five road games so far this season and have struggled to stop the run. They have given up over 100 rushing yards in each road game, averaging 147 yards per game. They just allowed the Steelers to rush for 200 yards, and the defense has looked tired.
Mason Graham, Michael Hall Jr., Carson Schwesinger, and Quincy Williams are banged up, and the defense relies on them to stop the run. Their defense is 24th in the NFL against the run. The line needs to be better disciplined and maintain containment of the line of scrimmage.
It is not all doom and gloom for the Browns' defense trying to stop the run. The Saints rank 28th in running the ball, averaging 86 yards per game. Their leading rusher is Kendre Miller with 159 yards. Travis Etienne has been out with an injury, but he may be available to return after their bye week . Alvin Kamara has shown his age this season by only amassing 125 yards.
If the trends continue and both offenses cannot run the ball, then the game will be in the Saints’ favor. They are 14th in passing with 229 yards per game, which is eight spots better than the Browns. If Sanders plays, then it will be his first start of the season. His best ability is throwing an accurate deep pass, but if they cannot run the ball, then the Saints' secondary will be ready.
Sunday’s game in the Superdome presents an interesting storyline, as both teams have a hard time running the ball and stopping the run. Something will have to give, and the Browns need to figure out a way to end the road trip with a win by controlling the run game on both sides of the ball.
