title: 2 Browns Players Who Could Be on the Trade Block Before the NFL Deadline
full_text:
With the trade deadline quickly approaching on November 10th, we have already seen some massive trades around the league like Jefferey Simmons going to Chicago and Quenton Nelson shipped to Seattle.
In Cleveland, the Browns are in a tough spot of whether the team is buyers or sellers at the deadline as they sit at 5-3 and right outside of a playoff spot in the AFC. The idea of trading for a talented quarterback, who might command at minimum two first-round picks , has come into conversation along with trading for offensive line help.
There are some players however, who are also in the conversation of discarding before the deadline.
Anyone heard this one before? But seriously, Jeudy is the most expendable player on the Browns right now, and it’s not completely his fault. Except it mostly is; his inconsistency last season on a team that lacked offensive weapons was a huge signal for Browns GM Andrew Berry to go out and get young receiver talent immediately.
And that receiver talent has been on full display through eight games this season; both Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion have doubled Jeudy’s output of just 171 yards this season. Jeudy is still under contract next season for a cap hit of a little over $13 million; Cleveland would love to pawn that off to another franchise, but will definitely have to pitch in a draft pick for a team to take that on.
Harden continues to be the Browns starting slot corner despite below-average play, and that has been prevalent this season. Quarterbacks have a passer rating of 108.7 when targeting Harden, for reference, that’s higher than the passer rating of Caleb Williams, Josh Allen, and Drake Maye this year.
Playing slot is a very tough position to play with all of the great slot receivers in the game right now like Jaxon Smith-Njiba, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Puka Nacua, and Cedee Lamb. The problem is that Cleveland hasn’t played any of those guys this season, and while players like Zay Flowers and Parker Washington are close to that level, they weren’t exactly locked down against the Browns.
The good thing about Harden is that he’s cheap, he’s making just over a million dollars this season and next. You can’t rationalize keeping him as a starter just because he doesn’t cost a lot of money when he has allowed the 8th-most receiving yards by a defensive back this season, though.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Why Shedeur Sanders' Expected Start Comes at the Perfect Time
full_text:
Two years ago, Shedeur Sanders expanded his skill set beyond the football field and released a song called “Perfect Timing.”
Now, as Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol, the second-year quarterback is gearing up to make his first start of the 2026 season, and the timing couldn’t be more in his – and in the Browns’ – favor.
Here’s three reasons why Sanders getting the Week 9 nod comes at a pretty much the perfect time :
During his media availability on Wednesday afternoon , Sanders was asked what he’s seen from the Saints' defense.
“Um, yeah, I've seen a lot," he answered. "When I smile, just know that means… something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing.”
It seems Sanders doesn’t see Saints' defensive coordinator, Brandon Staley’s, unit as much of a threat.
And, the numbers don’t disagree with the quarterback’s (lack of) thoughts.
The Saints’ total defense ranks 28th overall in the league, giving up 372.7 yards per game and allowing 22 touchdowns so far this year. Its passing defense ranks 23rd overall, allowing 233.3 yards per game, and it doesn’t bring a lot of pressure up front.
New Orleans has also been pretty easy to score on this season. According to Pro Football Reference, 46.8% of the Saints’ defensive drives have ended in an offensive score, the second-highest among all 32 teams.
While the Saints aren’t the worst defense in the league, they’re far from the best – something that could make Sanders’ job a little easier on Sunday.
While it’s been reported that the Browns have no interest in trading Sanders by the November 10 deadline, it’s no secret there’s a lot of uncertainty in the future of Cleveland’s quarterback room.
When Watson was named the starter this offseason, it sent a clear message: Sanders is not the answer to the Browns’ struggles. At least not yet.
While Watson is doing just enough to keep the Browns a competitive team, he isn’t a top quarterback. During his time in Cleveland, he has yet to prove he’s the long-term solution. So who is?
Sanders has yet to prove it, either, despite flashes of his abilities when he took over under center last season.
Todd Monken, though, is excited to see what his young quarterback does with this week’s opportunity.
“He’s done his work,” Monken said. “All he’s done is be diligent and ask great questions. In every meeting, he’s dialed in.”
When it comes to the trade deadline, the Browns have some decisions to make.
This weekend could help solidify Sanders’ spot in the quarterback room, especially with Dillon Gabriel no longer on injured reserve.
After beating Pittsburgh in primetime the first time around, the Steelers got revenge on their home field to claim the top spot in the AFC North.
It was a tough outing for Watson, who was sacked eight times. He’s the most-sacked quarterback in the league so far this year.
The Browns need a morale boost, and it potentially coming from a different quarterback could be beneficial.
Cleveland has a stretch of winnable games ahead. After the Saints, the team hosts the 2-5 Texans, then the 4-4 Raiders after a bye week.
If Sanders wants to prove himself to his team and to Cleveland fans, starting with a win against New Orleans might just be the way to do that. Getting the Browns back on track after losing to their rival is the perfect opportunity to show he still has something to offer to the team that drafted him.
A Northeast Ohio native, Rachel grew up following all things Cleveland sports. She has experience in broadcast and digital media and graduated from West Virginia University with a degree in sports media.

title: Browns Have 4 Young Players Who Deserve More Playing Time as Season Hits Halfway Point
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns season hits the half way point and they sit as the eighth seed in the AFC at 5-3. They only play three more games against teams over .500 and have a chance to make a push for the playoffs. The team has arrived sooner than anyone thought because their roster is filled with rookies and second-year players.
Almost 30 percent of the game-day roster is composed of players from the last two draft classes. Eight such players are starters that have heavily contributed to winning. Carson Schwesinger was Defensive Rookie of the Year last season and KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston are competing for Offensive Rookie of the Year this season.
The young players have stepped up on both sides of the ball, but these non-starters need to get more playing time in the second half of the season to make the playoffs.
Sampson started the season as the backup running back to Quinshon Judkins, but got hurt in the first game. He returned in Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans and showed off his speed by averaging 7.5 yards per rush and 10.7 yards per reception in the win. Sampson only got one carry for seven yards in last week’s blow-out loss against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The offense has struggled to run the ball all season and Sampson should be given more opportunities to find a spark. He can run on the outside and catch screen passes to keep the defense on its toes. The offense is night and day when he touches the ball.
The second-year receiver only has five catches this season for 86 yards. He got most of his playing time at the beginning of the season when Jerry Jeudy struggled and KC Concepcion left a game with a concussion. Jeudy improved and Concepcion did not miss any other time, so Bond got pushed to the sideline.
The speedster can take the top off of the defense and open up the middle of the field for Concepcion and Boston. He had a couple of bad drops in their loss against the New York Jets, but the weather conditions made things difficult. If Shedeur Sanders starts for the Browns , then Bond should get more playing time as they had chemistry last season and Sanders throws a better deep ball than Watson.
Huntington has gotten plenty of playing time and has played really well by stacking up 3.5 sacks. He anchored the middle of the defensive line when Mason Graham and Michael Hall Jr. were out with injury. Both players returned to the lineup and Huntington’s snaps will decrease.
Both Graham and Hall Jr. still look like they are playing injured and Huntington should start over Hall Jr. He has been providing pressure over the center and has gotten in the backfield to help stop the run. The defensive line needs him to help them slow down the rushing attack, which they have struggled to do this season.
The strong safety out of the University of Toledo was considered a “steal” in the second round of the NFL draft. His playing time has steadily been increasing and he has shown why. McNeil-Warren has laid some big hits on running backs and helped them stop the Titans at the goal line. He is behind Grand Delpit on the depth chart.
Ronnie Hickman has started at free safety and there have been a couple of communication breakdowns in the secondary. McNeil-Warren’s college film suggests he can play in the middle of the field and read the offense. He should get more opportunities to be a ball hawk in the secondary.
The young players are contributing up and down the roster and if the Browns wish to play their way into the playoffs, then these four players should be utilized more in the second half.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Browns QB Trade Value Should Improve After Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
One by one, quarterbacks keep getting plucked off the trade block.
On Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Arizona Cardinals joined the fun by trading veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Brissett will look to bolster the Ravens' QB room following a wave of injuries to both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.
But while the move not only puts a band-aid on an AFC North squad that is still in contention to make a run for the top spot, it also puts the Cleveland Browns in a position to reevaluate the group they have on the roster.
With four quarterbacks on staff, a group that includes two second-year signal callers and a rookie, the Browns will be able to skew the market a bit as one of the last remaining teams left with depth at the position.
If any other team needs to add an extra arm to their roster at the deadline , Cleveland is going to likely be on the call list.
The Browns have rolled out controversial quarterback Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback through the first eight weeks of the 2026 season.
However, in the early morning hours on Wednesday , that storyline hit a roadblock.
Second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders was thrust into the spotlight after Watson entered concussion protocol, with the 24-year-old now being projected to start Sunday's game for the Browns against the New Orleans Saints. This would be Watson's first missed game of the season.
With Sanders not expected to be the long-term starter, though, especially with this injury pretty much being a waiting game, Sunday could ultimately serve as a test to see if any teams in need of a quarterback could make Sanders their No. 1.
It would be surprising to not see any scouts in New Orleans, especially with the deadline approaching.
There's also an opportunity for both Gabriel's and Green's values to grow as well, even without taking the field this season. Both being so young and raw allows them to be molded into something that fits a specific team's system, particularly if they believe a 2026 playoff spot is a lost cause.
That same case can be made for Sanders; he just has a bit more experience on the gridiron under his belt than the other two.
Quarterbacks across the board, not just the Browns', probably saw a jump of roughly a pick's worth of trade value on Wednesday following the Brissett trade. For example, if Gabriel were valued as a fifth-round pick before the last few weeks, he has likely jumped up to fourth-round status, especially with very few quarterbacks still available on the open market.
With how many quarterbacks have been injured this season, including the likes of Seattle's Sam Darnold, the Eagles' Jalen Hurts, Jackson and many more, teams have to be readier than ever to embody that next-man-up mentality.
A season can't just fall off the rails completely after a quarterback goes down.
Over the next few days, it will be interesting to watch and see how the market continues to move, and values change with the trade deadline approaching.
And if one of Cleveland's four active quarterbacks on the 53-man roster is forced to put on a new jersey.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Shedeur Sanders Backs Deshaun Watson Ahead of Potential Start Against Saints
full_text:
Shedeur Sanders could have used Wednesday’s media session to explain how he might change the Cleveland Browns’ offense. Instead, he made a point of defending the quarterback he could replace this week.
With Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol and Sanders potentially in line to start against the New Orleans Saints, the second-year quarterback pushed back when asked how he could get Cleveland’s offense going earlier in games.
“Just my job. I don’t think it been bad . How many wins we got? It can’t be that bad, you know,” Sanders said. “I don’t want to just come in here and just try to discredit, you know, what Deshaun done and everything he done.”
The Browns enter the matchup at 5–3, and Sanders sees his responsibility as helping the team continue winning. He wasn’t interested in making his case at Watson’s expense, choosing instead to focus on the opportunity in front of him.
“That don’t make me feel good as a person,” Sanders said. “I think it’s just doing my job, not doing too much, doing what I have to do.”
According to the team’s injury statement, Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday’s game against Pittsburgh. He passed his initial evaluation and subsequent checks after the game and Monday morning before reporting Tuesday that symptoms began Monday night.
Head coach Todd Monken confirmed Watson’s placement in concussion protocol. Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported Wednesday that the expectation around Browns headquarters was that Sanders would start against New Orleans, although Monken had not ruled Watson out.
Sanders said he learned of the possibility at the same time reporters did. Asked about his preparation, he offered a straightforward response.
“The same way how I’ve been preparing every week. No different.”
Shedeur emphasized the relationships already established inside the locker room when asked about working with the offensive line. He suggested the adjustment appeared more complicated to people outside the building than it did to the players themselves.
“Deshaun led us this far and it’s unfortunate he wasn’t able to go out there, you know, but on my end, you know, I just got to step up for the quarterback room, for the team and do what I have to do,” Sanders said.
His description of what the offense needs from him was equally direct. "Just go out there and trust my teammates, trust the game plan and do everything I can...I ain’t really trying to ride the roller coaster life, you know, I like to keep everything even,” said Shedeur.

title: What This Browns Veteran Had To Say About Shedeur Sanders' Opportunity To Start Sunday
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns cannot escape the injury bug.
And ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the New Orleans Saints, the offense may look completely different.
On Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Browns announced a shocking update on quarterback Deshaun Watson, revealing the 31-year-old signal caller was in concussion protocol. He took a pretty nasty hit early in the Browns' loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers this past weekend, but cleared any concerns both during the game and on Monday.
"During the first quarter of Sunday’s game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit. The ATC spotter called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a game-day concussion evaluation," the Browns' press release read. "Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns’ next offensive series. As part of the protocol, the team’s medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning. Both times, he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared.
"On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol."
Fortunately, many of Cleveland's leaders spoke out in support of backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, whom the Browns may have to turn to for Sunday's road game against the New Orleans Saints.
Browns star cornerback Denzel Ward was one of the first players to Sanders' praise, speaking to media in the late morning hours on Wednesday.
Browns CB Denzel Ward on Shedeur Sanders possibly making his first start of the season: “I know he’s ready.” pic.twitter.com/LjFZIgTYN2
"We've got all the confidence in Shedeur," Ward began. "We know he will be ready to play once he is out there, so, you know, we always offer our support when needed, but we know he is ready."
Getting that extra confidence boost from a leader like Ward should go a long way for Sanders, especially if he is given the opportunity to make his first start of the 2026 season.
During his rookie campaign in 2025, the 24-year-old started seven games, throwing for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns on 212 passing attempts. He also rushed 21 times for 169 yards and one touchdown, adding a bit of versatility to his game.
While he seemingly did enough to earn the starting job in 2026, Watson's offseason surge pushed him to the top of the depth chart.
Fortunately, Sanders hasn't been completely out of the picture. He has still had the opportunity to serve as the No. 2, sitting and learning behind Watson , all while getting valuable reps in practice.
Such an experience has allowed him to welcome the challenge that sits ahead of him heading into this weekend.
"...Deshaun led us this far and it is unfortunate he wasn't able to go out there [this week]," Sanders said. "But on my end, I just got to step up for the quarterback room, for the team and do what I have to do."
With Ward's endorsement, the rest of the team rallying around him and a head full of confidence, Sanders has the perfect storm following him into his first potential start of the 2026 season.
For now, the focus will be on giving him first-team reps and preparing for a weekend without Watson.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns’ Latest Injury News Opens Door for Shedeur Sanders
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns dropped a bombshell on social media Wednesday morning. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol after a hit sustained during the first quarter of the Browns-Steelers game on Sunday:
Brisker flagged for hit on Watson #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/FCOv8QtjJA
Watson began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and reported them to the medical staff Tuesday morning, when he was placed in concussion protocol . An unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant cleared Watson to return during Sunday’s game. He also passed evaluations after the game and on Monday morning.
Watson has helped the Browns reach 5-3, engineering a game-winning drive in each of their five victories. He has 1,806 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and three interceptions this season. This start, while unexpected, had many believing that Watson would remain the starter for the season, barring injury.
Unfortunately for Watson, that injury came.
Watson’s injury could open the door for backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders to show his capabilities once again. Sanders made seven starts as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions.
some of Shedeur Sanders best throws vs. the Titans from the All-22 tape. #Browns The first ball to Fannin with a DE barreling down in his face is just silly... pic.twitter.com/zsZSNHxgbT
While it wasn’t all pretty, Sanders did show flashes of potential, specifically in the Browns’ matchup against the Titans in 2025. In that game, Sanders threw for 364 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while adding a rushing touchdown. Many assumed the Browns would continue to start Sanders into the 2026 season, but ultimately that was not the case.
The Browns held a highly publicized quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders during training camp for the 2026 season. Sanders ultimately lost the battle to the veteran Watson, but a comment Browns head coach Todd Monken made during OTAs on June 3 still stands out today:
#Browns HC Todd Monken said he has not yet decided who will start at quarterback between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, nor has he finalized the offensive line heading into training camp. "I think both quarterbacks have played well enough. We really haven't been in pads,… pic.twitter.com/LFLUlv99mL
Todd Monken said, “But I’m fired up by the quarterbacks. I'll tell you, we got two starting-level quarterbacks. We really do.” Now, Sanders has the opportunity to prove his head coach right.
Sanders has not been confirmed as the starter against the Saints, as Watson could still clear concussion protocol before Sunday. Sanders will take the first-team practice reps Wednesday as Cleveland prepares for the possibility of playing without Watson.
The question now, if Sanders gets the start, is whether he can seize his opportunity. If Sanders performs better than Watson has to start the season, it may be difficult for the Browns to turn back to the veteran. However, Sanders must avoid holding the ball too long. That issue surfaced against Pittsburgh, contributing to two penalties for ineligible players downfield on screen passes.
If those struggles resurface, the Browns could quickly return to Watson, who has led five game-winning drives this season.

title: A Blockbuster Trade the Browns Could Make to Completely Change the Franchise
full_text:
Rumors have begun to run wild around the NFL about the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.
After an unprecedented 0-7 start to the season, the Chargers may be enticed by the right offer to blow up the entire operation and go into rebuild mode.
With these rumors going around, some people, including ESPN Cleveland, have called for the Cleveland Browns to reach out and potentially make an offer for the former Oregon Duck.
Here are some of the pros and cons to a potential Justin Herbert trade.
. @BenjaminSolak lists the 3 teams that should try and trade for Justin Herbert: - Vikings - Jets - The Cleveland Browns 👀👀👀 Should the Browns explore a Herbert trade? pic.twitter.com/zpMT9W4yx9
In 2022, the Browns gave up pretty much their entire future to go out and trade for Deshaun Watson. We all know how that went before 2026 began.
Now, Watson is 31 years old and in the final year of his contract. If the Browns want to move on from Watson and go after Herbert, it would take another gigantic package.
While Herbert doesn't have legal issues off the field, his play on the field is still questionable. While some argue it's the poor system he's playing in, or the tough teams he's facing, Herbert still leads the NFL with 10 interceptions.
All in all, the move seems to be too risky for the Browns to make, especially with a potentially loaded 2027 rookie quarterback class.
While we are still looking back to the Deshaun Watson trade, let's not forget the slim amount of hope Cleveland fans had right when the trade went down.
If the Browns got Herbert, they would most likely have their best quarterback since Baker Mayfield. At times, it is easy to say Herbert is far better than Mayfield as well.
With the second-youngest team in the NFL, along with the back-to-back incredible draft classes, Herbert would come in surrounded by an incredibly talented team.
Before 2026, many argued that the Browns were a quarterback away from being a serious contender. Maybe Cleveland looks at Herbert as their "missing piece"?
While it is very unrealistic that the Browns will go make a move for Madison Beer's fiancé, there is another world of possibilities people are overlooking if the quarterback gets moved to another team.
Like I said, Moving Justin Herbert is the initial indicator that the Chargers are going into rebuild mode.
With that being said, the Browns' biggest need by far at the moment is help on that offensive line. Of course, it would be pricey, but if the Chargers are willing to move their quarterback, who's to say they wouldn't trade away guys like Joe Alt or Rashawn Slater?
If anything, the Browns should be hoping the Chargers are willing to trade Justin Herbert. Maybe then they could take a swing at a big trade, yet not for the guy you would have first thought of.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: NFL Legend Delivers Ominous Prediction For Jerry Jones, Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have not returned to the NFC Championship Game or hoisted a Lombardi Trophy since winning Super Bowl XXX over the Pittsburgh Steelers in 1996. Not only is the team in the midst of a brutal championship drought , but they have never been real contenders in that time frame.
This season, there was some hope that the Cowboys could begin trending in the right direction, but that hasn't been the case as they enter Week 9 with three losses in four weeks .
Dallas' struggles have reignited the conversation about whether Jerry Jones is capable of leading a championship-winning team as general manager, and at least one NFL legend believes it's over for The Gambler and America's Team .
Pro Football Hall of Famer Cris Carter and the Inside Football crew were discussing whether Jones is to blame for holding the team back, and not only did the crew believe that he is completely out of touch, but Carter also believes that Jones will never taste Super Bowl glory again .
Cris Carter doesn't believe Jerry Jones will ever hoist another Lombardi Trophy. The Inside Football crew discusses why Jerry's approach to running the Cowboys may be holding the franchise back. pic.twitter.com/JKsmRyStWq
"Jerry, and I hope he lives a long time, but he will not hoist that Lombardi trophy again. He will not. He does not have a business plan that's effective in this current NFL," Carter said. "He is lost.
Former Arizona Cardinals executive Steve Keim was asked whether Jones was capable of changing his ways, and delivered a damning statement: "I say no, number one, to answer your question. And two, like, listen, at his age, Dallas Cowboys are keeping him alive, are keeping him getting out of bed in the morning.
"So he writes the checks. He owns a team. That's his prerogative. But he's got to take the sh*t that comes with it.
It's a brutal assessment that Cowboys fans won't want to hear, but it seems closer to reality than the team actually winning. The lack of improvement that the team has shown in recent years and Jones' inability to target a top-tier head coach in the midst of their rebuild only highlights how far away the team really is.
Cowboys fans are used to entering a season with high hopes or expectations before being let down, but there's something about the 2026 version of this letdown that stings more than any in recent memory.
And with the trade deadline approaching in a matter of days, we'll have to see whether the team makes an effort to get any closer.

title: Cowboys QB Dak Prescott Isn't Sure Dallas Should Be Proud of Its Offense
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys entered the season with plenty of hype, but after eight weeks, they've been one of the biggest disappointments in the NFL.
While we all knew their defense could be a problem , which it has been, their offense was supposed to be talented enough to mask the deficiencies on the other side of the ball. Overall, the offense has put up plenty of points, but they have been far from consistent.
They've also fallen flat when needed the most. That was true in their Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers when they managed a mere 16 points. They followed that up with 13 points against the Green Bay Packers in Week 6. What might be more frustrating is the way they performed in Week 8 against the Arizona Cardinals .
Dallas managed to score 30 points, but when they simply needed a couple of first downs to put the game away at the end, they fell flat on their face and ultimately lost. Now, they're preparing for a Week 9 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts and are facing questions about their play-calling and offensive identity. What's most concerning, however, is the fact that star quarterback Dak Prescott is now openly questioning their offensive identity.
When asked if Dallas even had one, Prescott said they did, but admitted it's not one they should neccesarily be proud of.
"Yeah sure, I mean, is it one we're proud of? I don't know," Prescott said via Clarence Hill . "We'll be better, I can promise.”
Prescott also expressed frustration with the way the offense is failing to perform, especially durung crunch time.
“Yeah, I mean it's frustrating. That's what you're asking? Yeah, absolutely. It's frustrating and just to your point of whether it's us squeezing the grip too hard or whatever it may be, when you have the standards and expectations to go out there and to score every play and you're not doing that, yeah, it's frustrating. And each and every guy, I'd be lying to you off if I didnt say guys feel that and each and every guy feels it in their own way."
Many fans are praising Prescott for expressing frustration with the offense. He also seemed to shade the play-calling earlier in the day when discussing why George Pickens hasn't been receiving more targets.
It is good that Prescott is speaking up, but there are some concerns when it comes to him as well. One is the fact that he put a lot of pressure on himself and the offense as a whole by speaking about the Super Bowl this offseason and giving the offense the bold nickname GOTI (Greatest Offense There Is).
He's also the one who makes the decisions when the ball is in his hands. Regardless of play-calling, the best quarterbacks know when to check out of a play and when to start force-feeding a game-changing player.
Sure, head coach Brian Schottenheimer is the one calling the plays, but Prescott deserves criticism for the fact that he targeted Brevyn Spann-Ford more times than Pickens during their loss to the Cardinals.
All that said, the fact that Prescott is beginning to speak up is a good sign. Now, we just need him to take that same approach on the field and begin to take matters into his own hands. Only then will the offense have any chance of finding an identity they can be proud of.

title: Dak Prescott  Appears To Shade Cowboys' Play-Calling George Pickens Trade Chatter
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and there are questions about whether the Dallas Cowboys could be buyers or sellers when the Tuesday, November 10, deadline arrives.
Dallas has been struggling over the past month, including three losses in four weeks in very winnable games, which has reignited conversations about potentially trading away star wide receiver George Pickens .
Pickens is playing on the franchise tag and has seen his production take a dip this season, but he still has plenty of supporters in the locker room.
One of Pickens' biggest supporters has been star quarterback Dak Prescott , who was asked about the trade chatter when speaking to the media ahead of the team's Week 9 showdown against the Indianapolis Colts.
Prescott was asked for his message to those who think the Cowboys should move Pickens at the deadline, and  his response raised some eyebrows.
Not only did Prescott praise Pickens as a teammate, but he also seemingly appeared to shade the team's play-calling for not putting the star pass catcher in the right opportunities.
"People say a lot of things I don’t believe, so I’m not listening to that one, either ," Prescott said. "George is a great teammate. And I say that in the sense of, he’s gonna do whatever is asked, he’s gonna do whatever is called.
"If it’s to go block, if it’s to just go run a guy off, he’s gonna do that. He believes in just doing the right thing, and the ball will come his way at times. And so, that’s not on George.”
This season, Pickens has hauled in 39 catches for 533 yards, while finding the end zone just two times. Pickens has also been pulled off the field in key situations in favor of Ryan Flournoy, while Brian Schottenheimer and others have hinted it was because of run-blocking and/or injuries .
Whatever the case, the Cowboys have one week to determine what to do with Pickens before this season's deadline, and if he remains in Dallas, his contract situation will turn into one of the biggest storylines in the NFL offseason.
So, we'll have to see what role Pickens plays on Sunday afternoon, but it appears that he and others on the offense are itching for him to get more involved.

title: Joey Porter Jr. Takes Step Back on Latest Cowboys Injury Report, Caleb Downs Improves

title: Cowboys CB DaRon Bland Gets Blunt Assessment From Christian Parker
full_text:
DaRon Bland burst onto the scene for the Dallas Cowboys during his rookie season in 2022. The fifth-round pick out of Fresno State recorded five interceptions, earning a key role in the secondary going forward.
He was even better in year two, recording nine interceptions, five of which he returned for touchdowns. Since then, however, Bland has been trending in the wrong direction .
Foot injuries cost him time in 2024 and 2025 and he had just one interception during that span. The Cowboys still (for some reason) decided to sign Bland to a lucrative extnesion last year, giving him a four-year, $92 million deal . As many predicted, Bland has continued to look like the player we saw in 2024 and 2025 rather than the one we saw during his first two seasons in the league.
In fact, it's fair to argue that he's been even worse this season. Entering Week 9, Bland has an overall PFF grade of 43.1 , which is 91st out of 102 qualified cornerbacks. His coverage has been especially worrisome as Bland has surrendered 375 yards and four touchdowns while allowing a quarterback rating of 124.6 when targeted . That's why defensive coordinator Christian Parker recently said he and Bland have discussed the need for improvement from the fifth-year defensive back.
“We need more from him. He knows that, we’ve had some good talks about that. I think he’s battling. The frustrating thing for him and for us has been he’s been close and contesting. Now, it’s about the final piece of just finishing those plays," Parker said via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . "We just got to get back to making that consistent.”
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has been preaching accountability throughout his tenure, but the way they're handling Bland's slump is the exact opposite.
Bland isn't just struggling to make plays as Parker suggested, but he's actually a major liability in coverage. Opposing defenses know to look in his direction and they're having tremendous success when doing so.
Rather than hold Bland accountable for his poor play, they continue to trot him out on the field, even with a superior option available. Cobie Durant, who enters Week 9 with an overall PFF grade of 62.4 , has had far more success than Bland. Even so, Bland is given more snaps each week while Durant has played behind him and Joey Porter Jr.
If the Cowboys are serious about improvong on defense and holding players accountable, they need to be willing to make difficult decisions. Benching Bland in favor of Durant could give the defense a much-needed spark while putting pressure on the veteran cornerback to regroup and elevate his performance.

title: Ex-Giants Coach Unloads on Cowboys' Defense, Feels Bad For Jerry Jones
full_text:
There is no bigger critic of the Dallas Cowboys out there than ESPN talking head Stephen A. Smith, but former New York Giants defensive coordinator Don "Wink" Martindale is challenging him.
Martindale has been very critical of the Cowboys' defense and its play-caller, defensive coordinator Christian Parker, and was once again after the Week 8 debacle against the Arizona Cardinals.
Martindale said he has to "have a trash can" next to him when he watches the Cowboys' defense on a weekly basis because it the unit makes him sick. He also thinks Dallas' unit is the worst he's ever seen.
"It's not just the worst defense in the league right now. It's one of the worst I've [ever] seen," Martindale said on the Talkin' Ball With Pat Leonard podcast. "(Parker is) behind on play-calling and I feel bad for Jerry (Jones)."
"I told my wife, I'm starting to feel like Stephen A. Smith just killing the Cowboys, but it's the truth," Martindale said. "I gotta to have a trash can next to me when I'm watching the Dallas Cowboys defense hit the field."
It is, unfortunately for Cowboys fans, the truth.
In a past criticism, Martindale ripped Parker, saying the Cowboys defensive coordinator has been "outclassed." He also offered to provide his services to help Parker get the unit on track before Dallas hired Mike Pettine as a defensive consultant.
"I don't wanna be an a******, but he's just being outclassed right now," Martindale said of Parker. "He was in the home opener against the Giants. They gotta stop the run."
"Sundays are frustrating for me when I see there's simple things that guys are just letting go right by them," Martindale added. "And watching Dallas, that's frustrating. So, Jerry can call me and I'll go help him, but I'm talking about helping the coordinator."
Nothing Martindale is saying is untrue. The Cowboys are once again the worst defense in the NFL this season, a theme we've seen going back to 2024.
Just when the Cowboys showed some improvement in the first half of the game against the Arizona Cardinals, the unit totally collapsed en route to a historic loss .
We'd like to chalk it up to more Minshew Magic, but we've seen far too much ugly from the Cowboys' defense this season to simply leave it at that. This unit just stinks, plain and simple.
Where the Cowboys go from here remains to be seen.
There is no appetite to fire any coaches , which might be the only hope this team has. Sure, Dallas could make a trade for an edge rusher, but this defense doesn't appear to be one player away from righting the ship. It's going to take a lot more than that.
And the type of edge rusher the Cowboys need, which is an elite one, is highly unlikely to be available at the trade deadline. Even if there is one, the Cowboys are so low on draft capital that it will make competing against other teams nearly impossible.
At this point, Jerry Jones should just cut his losses, save his draft capital and ride this storm out to wherever it takes him. There is no hope for this 2026 Cowboys team.

title: Dallas Cowboys Could Play Major Role in NFL Trade Deadline Win or Lose vs Colts
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys enter Week 9 of the 2026-27 NFL season with three wins in their last four games and are quickly losing ground in the NFC East. That has led to some increased conversations about whether Dallas will be a buyer or seller at the NFL trade deadline .
Regardless of whether the Cowboys come away from Sunday afternoon's game with a win, they could end up playing a key part in the value of some of the Indianapolis Colts' key offensive stars.
Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs are among the players who could be shipped away at the deadline, but NFL insider Jordan Schultz believes some teams are waiting until after the Colts play the Cowboys' putrid defense , which is currently ranked No. 32 overall.
Because players have consistently had their best games of the season against the Cowboys, the value for players like Taylor and Downs could ultimately skyrocket which means some teams could be scared away.
"The Colts have received plenty of calls on several players, including Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, Grover Stewart and others," Schultz wrote on X.
"But the belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs. the Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline."
That's another L for the Cowboys' defense this season. Not only have they been run and thrown all over throughout the season, but now teams know playing against them can increase the value of players on their roster and what they can get back in return.
It's a sign of how far the Cowboys' defense has fallen, even after investing several resources during the offseason to bring in new talent and turn things around. Just look at Gardner Minshew's fourth-quarter performance at Dallas as another example of how someone can win a starting job by playing the Cowboys' defense and make someone else on the roster expendable.
It's a cruel world to live in for Cowboys fans. Entering Week 9, the Cowboys rank dead last in total defense, No. 22 in pass defense, and No. 32 in run defense. Have yourself a day, Jonathan Taylor.

title: Quinnen Williams Calls Out Cowboys' Biggest Problem After Latest Loss
full_text:
For 45 minutes, it seemed as though the Dallas Cowboys were set to defeat the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8. Then during the final 15 minutes of the game, everything fell apart .
Their defense suddenly had no answer for Gardner Minshew or Tyler Allgeier, and the offense forgot how to move the ball forward. That resulted in a 14-point comeback for the Cardinals and an eventual 33-30 overtime defeat for the Cowboys.
After the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he took accountability for the loss, but then shocked everyone by claiming to be a “problem-solver” despite spending the past year and a half battling the same problems.
Not everyone in Dallas is busy praising themselves for what they believe they do well, thankfully. Star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams took real accountability, saying that the Cowboys proved for three quarters that they can play. The problem is that he says they also showed that they’re beating themselves with the mistakes.
“Tells you we’re beating ourselves as a defense. We’re the problem. We’re the reason we’re losing these games. If we execute, we can be the reason why we win,” Williams told reporters on Wednesday .
Not only did Williams say the defense is the reason for the losses, but he also refused to take credit for playing well this season. Despite recording two sacks in Week 8, Williams said he’s the reason they can’t stop the run and that he’s the reason they’re giving up touchdowns.
“I don’t focus on that at all. I’m a part of this defense. I’m the reason why we’ve given up touchdowns in the fourth quarter. I’m the reason why we haven’t been stopping the run as well. And I got to do better,” Williams said.
“I take accountability, first and foremost. When it comes down to executing, I try to execute at the highest level each and every day, and not let words be just words and let it be by action.”
Williams had a slow start to the season as he adjusted to a new scheme under Christian Parker. In recent weeks, he’s caught fire and has four sacks over the past three games and five on the season.
Still, he refuses to pat himself on the back and is trying to pinpoint the problems. His approach is admirable, and if everyone in Dallas was willing to look inward the way Williams is, they might have a chance to turn things around.

title: Cowboys-Saints Trade Rumor Links NFC Squads for Potential Deadline Deal
full_text:
There appears to be some buzz about a potential trade between the Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints.
NFL insider Jason La Canfora says he has had some people in the league "whisper" to him about a possible pairing with the Cowboys and Saints for a deal involving edge rusher Cam Jordan.
La Canfora cited "behind-the-scenes talks" as the source of the information he's putting out there. Here's what he said exactly:
"Boy, the Dallas Cowboys, I know we talked about edge rushers with them more so than interior defensive linemen," La Canfora said .
"Cam Jordan’s a versatile guy. Cam Jordan could fit in their mix up front. I’ve had some people whisper to me: ‘Maybe Cam Jordan (goes) to the Cowboys’," La Canfora added.
The Cowboys shouldn't need an edge rusher after ramping the edge rusher spot in during the offseason, with the team adding Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence and Von Miller.
But those three have combined for just three sacks, and when you include Donovan Ezeiruaku and James Houston, Dallas has gotten only 6.5 sacks from their edge rushers this season.
Because of how ineffective the edge rushers have been, the Cowboys have just 15 sacks in total and their secondary has gotten exposed each and every week because of the group's inability to finish off pressures.
Since nobody in-house is getting it done, the Cowboys now have to bring in help from outside, but they can't just bring in anyone. Dallas needs someone who is going to make a huge impact.
If the Cowboys are going to trade for an edge rusher and cut their draft stockpile down even more , they need to add a locked-in difference-maker at the position.
While Jordan was once that guy, he hasn't looked like it this year. The Saints edge rusher has yet to tally a sack over the six games he's played in and is far from a guarantee to pan out.
Jordan did post 10.5 sacks last season, but pointing at past stats was what made us believe Miller could make an impact, yet here we are.
Jordan is going to cost a draft pick, and while it might not be more than a Day 3 pick, that still isn't worth it. The 37-year-old will be a free agent in 2027, so the Cowboys may be giving up up yet another draft pick for a rental that may provide nothing.
Even if he can get his season on track in Dallas, it's doubtful Jordan can make enough of a dent to save this defense, which needs a much bigger jolt than Jordan will be able to provide.

title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order Entering Week 9: Dallas Cowboys Clinging To Top 20 Pick
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' 2026-27 NFL campaign has been a complete disaster, with the team currently losing three of their last four as we prepare for a Week 9 showdown with the Indianapolis Colts .
To make matters worse for the Cowboys, one of those losses was against the Green Bay Packers, who will determine where Dallas picks in the 2027 NFL Draft . Dallas owns the Packers' first-round pick as part of the Micah Parsons trade last season , while the Cowboys' highest first-round pick will be sent to the New York Jets because of the Quinnen Williams deal at last year's trade deadline .
Currently, Dallas' own pick is a top-10 selection because of their 3-5 start, but that would be on its way to East Rutherford. Instead, the Cowboys would be on the clock with the No. 20 overall pick.
While the Cowboys have found some success picking in the 20s this year, it still presents a problem for a team that is in desperate need of elite talent. Dallas needs to continue adding to its defense, but risks losing out on a top prospect at a position of need if the Packers continue to win.

title: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: Concerning Brandon Jones Update
full_text:
Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers.
Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction.
Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina.
In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady.
Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9.
WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury.
On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos.
“You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.”
Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs .
Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut.
Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian.

title: Broncos ILB Alex Singleton Captures Esteemed NFL Award
full_text:
One year after being diagnosed with testicular cancer , Denver Broncos inside linebacker Alex Singleton was awarded one of the high honors of the NFL regular season.
The league announced Thursday that Singleton has been named AFC Defensive Player of the Month for October.
In the midst of a fantastic fifth year in Denver, Singleton is indeed deserving of the award for his work from Weeks 4-8, when he notched 68 total tackles, five tackles for loss, five quarterback hits, and two sacks. He won Defensive Player of the Week for his 19-tackle effort against the Cardinals.
“It was sick," he said of taking home DPOW. "It is one of those really cool things that when my kids don’t believe me one day that this is what I did that I can be able to show them.”
Singleton, a longtime defensive captain, currently leads the league in tackles (101) — 19 more than the second-leading tackler, Titans LB Anthony Hill Jr. He's also grading out as the sport's 10th-best LB among 76 qualifiers, according to Pro Football Focus .
“He’s very important. He’s the green dot," Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said of Singleton on Oct. 29. "He’s been with us four years now, and there are certain things that he can fix during the week that I don’t have to fix any longer. It’s meetings on Fridays where it’s him and his teammates. That’s the way it has to be with a veteran like Alex. His tackling has been always very good. So it’s fun to see him get recognized for being a big-time player because to me, he’s been a special player for four years now. He’s had 171 tackles, 156 tackles. I think what, 137 last year and he missed two games. So he’s been special in my mind for four seasons.”
Singleton is on pace for roughly 215 tackles this season, which would break the NFL single-season record (214) set by Hardy Nickerson in 1993. He'd also become the first Broncos player with 200-plus tackles in a single year since Randy Gradishar accomplished that feat in 1983.
The veteran 'backer will have a chance to add to his growing total in Week 9 , facing a Carolina Panthers offense that ranks 22nd in rushing offense, with RB Chuba Hubbard accounting for about 70 percent of Carolina's total carries per game.

title: Jonathan Taylor's New Price Tag Just Changed Things for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are still being linked to the running back trade market ahead of November 10's NFL deadline.
The Broncos became the favorites to land Jonathan Taylor after Sunday's 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but a significant obstacle could be in the way. According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter, the Indianapolis Colts have received at least one offer of a second-round pick plus additional compensation for Taylor, but they've yet to pull the trigger on a trade.
The Colts are holding out for a better offer — and they could be looking for a first-round pick. The Colts are now trying to send the signal that they want to hold onto Taylor as the cornerstone of their rebuild, but in an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday, NFL insider Ian Rapoport implied that Indy is looking for a first-round offer to part with their Pro Bowl back.
Would Taylor be worth a first-round pick to a team like the Broncos? That's the question.
As the Colts try to raise Taylor's value ahead of the deadline, the Broncos have to resist the temptation to overpay. As reliable and consistent as the veteran back is, he'll turn 28 in January, and he's rapidly approaching the dreaded 2,000-carry milestone.
Taylor just signed a two-year, $44 million extension this summer, but his 2027 and 2028 salaries are $15 million and $9.46 million, respectively. His contract isn't prohibitive, especially for the caliber of back he is, but it's the cost to acquire him that could be the hitch in the Broncos' giddyup.
The Broncos have only made two first-round picks in the past five years, due to costly trades involving Russell Wilson, Sean Payton, and Jaylen Waddle. Nobody is questioning the compensation Denver gave to New Orleans to acquire Payton's rights — he's been worth every penny, so to speak — but the Wilson trade blew up in the Broncos' face, and the jury is still out on Waddle.
As the Broncos begin to age into one of the NFL's older rosters, keeping the draft pipeline flowing could become increasingly important. That's especially true as it pertains to a future Bo Nix contract, as that'll limit the number of salary-cap dollars available to pay veterans.
Giving up a second-round pick for Taylor, plus perhaps a couple of mid-round selections, would already be pushing the envelope for Denver. But if the Broncos believed he would be the missing piece to get them over the Super Bowl hump, it would quickly become a case of ' F(orget) them picks ' — a phrase the Los Angeles Rams have made famous.
I'm not convinced Taylor is worth a second-round pick, let alone a first-rounder, especially given the emergence of Jonah Coleman. Plus, the Broncos expect to get RJ Harvey back from injured reserve in a few weeks, and they still have J.K. Dobbins, whom Payton vociferously claimed on Wednesday is still a "huge part of what we're doing."
If the Broncos were to acquire Taylor, he'd be the de facto No. 1 running back, pushing everyone else, including Coleman, down the depth chart. Again, that's a collateral effect the Broncos could live with, if Taylor was the answer to unlocking this offense.
And he very well could be. The Broncos are the NFL's worst third-down offense halfway through the season, mainly because of their inefficiency on first and second down. Taylor could ostensibly help fix that in a hurry, moving the chains and giving Bo Nix much more favorable third-down situations.
I could see Taylor being an immediate difference-maker, but the idea that Denver would have to go another year without making a first-round selection... it would put a lot of pressure on Payton to win a Super Bowl this year.
Another option could be to trade for a guy who could simply fit into the Broncos' running back committee. Payton often laments the difficulty of feeding more than two running backs on game day, though a third back often gets some usage in the offense, like Harvey on third down and in the passing game.
This is much more of an issue for Denver now, only because Harvey is out of reach for the next three games. The Broncos' next three games are at the Carolina Panthers, home against the Las Vegas Raiders, and on the road against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
If the Broncos believe they can weather that three-game storm without Harvey, with Coleman and Dobbins, they probably don't make a trade for a running back. But if they're worried about it, maybe they don't swing for the fences with Taylor and instead look at a more affordable option like Tennessee's Tony Pollard , who already has 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns in a terrible Titans offense.
It's a pickle. Since the Broncos have become competitive, we know GM George Paton has considered making trades ahead of the deadline as recently as last year (Waddle). But Paton has never actually pulled the in-season trigger.
At the same time, Paton never got close to a Lombardi Trophy until last year, and that, ladies and gentlemen, is why all bets are off. If the Colts stick to their guns, looking for a first-round value in exchange for Taylor, the Broncos may look elsewhere for help. They'll still be looking, though.
But if it's just a negotiating tactic, Taylor could end up going for much less, just as we saw when the Colts dealt away All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson (for a third- and a fifth-rounder) and veteran defensive lineman DeForest Buckner (a fourth-rounder). The Colts gave up both trenchmen for much less than was expected.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Addresses Trade Chatter
full_text:
Sean Payton wouldn't outright dismiss the idea of the 6-2, first-place Denver Broncos being "buyers" — acquiring star-level talent at a likely costly price — ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, as many within the fan base are hoping for.
But the veteran head coach did shoot down any speculation about the club being "sellers" — shipping off key pieces amid a potential championship run .
“Well, we’re a team that’s playing better, so we’re not looking to sell," Payton told reporters following Wednesday's practice.
The Broncos don't have a trade chip like the Colts do with running back Jonathan Taylor, whom Denver is the current betting favorite to land. Their highest-value commodities are players on expiring contracts.
That group includes wide receiver Marvin Mims, cornerbacks Riley Moss and Ja'Quan McMillian, safety Brandon Jones, offensive guard Ben Powers, tight end Evan Engram, and backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham.
A group that Payton isn't rushing to break up, realizing the landscape of today's NFL.
“I always think there’s buyers and sellers, right?" Payton said Wednesday. "It’s probably more noticeable in the last five years than maybe in our… Or at least I notice it more. Teams that are playing well are the potential buyers. The teams maybe that aren’t are the potential sellers.”
Taking Payton at his word, the Broncos rightfully have no business doing other teams any favors by giving away crucial pieces of their roster. Not when they're competing in a wide-open AFC. Not with their Super Bowl window wide open. Not here, not now.
Perhaps if Denver was 2-6, the "sellers" argument would be justified. But as of now, they hold the No. 2 seed in the conference, seemingly on track to capture the AFC West for the second consecutive year.
Trading Moss, a starting corner, for a hypothetical fourth-round pick isn't more valuable than simply retaining him for the remainder of the 2026 campaign. Ditto for Jones. Ditto for McMillian. Ditto for Mims. Each player is a significant contributor, if not a full-blown starter. Why fix what isn't broken?
Some fans don't want to hear this, but it'd actually be better if the Broncos maintained the status quo — did nothing — than suddenly face-lifted the lineups before Tuesday's deadline.
The options are on the table for Payton and his right-hand man, general manager George Paton, as the decision-making process remains fluid.
“We would meet and meet in the evening. The early part of it, all the GMs, they all talk with each other, but he and I’ll visit daily," Payton said. "So it’s not like it’s consuming two hours. His group is spending a lot of time separate from the time that I’m involved with our group. In other words, they’re doing their evaluation, we’re doing football, but he and I daily will visit about a bunch of things.”

title: Broncos Get Good News on Pat Bryant, Concerning Update on Talanoa Hufanga
full_text:
After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster.
That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina .
Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve.
Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown.
WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers.
What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday.
Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up.
Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming.
Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together.
Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season.
With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air.

title: Broncos-Panthers Matchups: Pat Surtain II vs. Tet McMillan Looms Large
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have a nice four-game winning streak going, and they now sit atop the AFC West after beating the Kansas City Chiefs .
However, the Broncos must guard against riding the high of the win and dropping this coming game against the Carolina Panthers. The Broncos have to travel east for an early game, a trip that has historically challenged them, though that track record has significantly improved under Sean Payton.
To avoid a potential upset by the Panthers, which would be costly heading into the bye week, the Broncos will need to win two critical matchups. The biggest matchups come down to a wide receiver vs. a cornerback on both sides of the ball.
Let's dig into these matchups and why they're so important to the Broncos.
The Broncos have struggled to find consistency with Sutton and rekindle his connection with Bo Nix . Sutton has been the Broncos' second-most-targeted receiver, behind Jaylen Waddle, with 36 targets, but ranks third in receptions, with only 20.
Sutton has 221 yards with a single touchdown through eight games. His usual strength in contested catches hasn't been there, with only three contested catches on eight such targets, though he did come down with one last week against the Chiefs.
The Panthers' secondary isn't a good unit, and it's largely because of the injuries they've sustained. Denver should look at getting Sutton matched up on Lee, forcing Waddle to a different cornerback, which is a topic I'll dig into in a different article.
Before getting into Lee in coverage, one reason the Broncos should like this matchup is his tackling issues against bigger receivers. Denver needs Sutton to find his footing in that regard.
As for coverage, Lee has been targeted 42 times, allowing 27 catches. He plays aggressively in coverage and does have five pass break-ups this season, but that has also led to some big plays being relinquished, as his aggressiveness can burn him.
Lee has given up two plays over 40 yards and allowed 335 total receiving yards, the 11th-most among NFL cornerbacks. Denver needs to win this matchup to help out its other favorable matchup with Waddle.
This is the obvious one. The Panthers' offense runs through McMillan, who has the NFL's 12th-most targets, 12th-most receptions, and 11th-most yards among 33 qualifying receivers. He is the majority of the Panthers' offense, and if you can limit or eliminate him, you're setting yourself up for major success.
Denver must put its top corner on McMillan and let Surtain do his thing. It won't be easy, and Surtain isn't infallible, but he is one of the best corners in the NFL and is trustworthy.
The challenge comes in the routes McMillan runs the most. McMillan's main route-running hits correspond to the ones Surtain typically struggles against. Vance Joseph could make slight coverage adjustments to give Surtain a hand.
"He's a big receiver. He has great body control," Surtain said of McMillan on Wednesday. "He can run every route in the route tree, so I'm looking forward to that matchup."
If Surtain and the Broncos can't limit or eliminate McMillan, this game will be much harder to win, especially in front of the Panthers' home crowd. The Broncos could still win the game if McMillan has a day, because there's too much in football for one area to have that big an impact, outside of the quarterback.
It's about making the defense's job easier. Limiting McMillan would help Denver put some extra focus on stopping the Panthers' run game.

title: 3 Positions Broncos Should Target at Trade Deadline to Boost Super Bowl Hopes
full_text:
After beating the Kansas City Chiefs and moving into first place in the AFC West , there's the hope that the Denver Broncos might do more than win the division, but also clinch the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs, just as they did last year.
The Broncos still have some tough games ahead, with the Pittsburgh Steelers sitting at 5-2 and awaiting them in Week 12, plus the Buffalo Bills and the New England Patriots in two of the final weeks. But most of Denver's remaining games are against opponents far from the NFL's top tiers.
With the Broncos in position to chase the No. 1 seed, a midseason trade makes sense — and finding an offensive playmaker would be the fastest upgrade.
Of course, the Broncos are rumored to be interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and are the new betting favorites to land him. But there are other running backs who might be available, along with tight ends and wide receivers, who could help the Broncos' offense.
With the NFL trade deadline now less than a week away (November 10), let's examine the positions to see what makes the most sense for Denver to acquire and which players might be available on the block.
Let's start with the position that may be getting the most attention. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on injured reserve for at least a few weeks, and J.K. Dobbins continues to underperform, so the Broncos could use some help here.
It makes the most sense to acquire a running back, but it may be best to find one for the short term rather than the long term. That's because Jonah Coleman has shown he could be a No. 1 back for the long term, and Harvey, while not a primary back, has shown he is a quality No. 2 option.
In this case, the Broncos may be better off with a short-term option who can replace Dobbins. That means that, as appealing as Taylor would be, he might not be the right option because he would be a long-term solution — and would push Coleman and Harvey down the depth chart.
Tennessee's Tony Pollard might actually be the best option. He's in the final year of his contract, and the Broncos might be able to include Dobbins in a deal. A possible deal could be the Broncos sending Dobbins and their fifth- and sixth-round picks to the Titans for Pollard and their sixth-rounder.
And if Lamar Jackson is going to miss the bulk of the season because of his thumb injury, the Baltimore Ravens could be talked into dealing Derrick Henry. A deal involving Dobbins, plus draft pick swaps, is possible here.
The Broncos would also get Henry on a cheap salary for 2026, and they could easily cut him next season with no dead money charges. Don't rule out Henry as a potential option.
This would be the position to pursue if Broncos fans want a player here for 2026 and beyond. With Evan Engram's deal expiring after the season and no other tight end on the roster standing out, it makes sense to find one.
However, the trade options aren't ideal if you're trying to get a long-term option. Trey McBride would be the dream scenario, but all indications are that the Arizona Cardinals are unwilling to trade him.
The Philadelphia Eagles are rumored to be ready to move players and could make Dallas Goedert available. Goedert would be a cheap player to acquire because of how the Eagles structured his deal.
However, Goedert would be a rental for the remainder of the season and not a long-term guy, as he's 31 this season. That doesn't mean the Broncos would have to dismiss Goedert as a possibility — only that they wouldn't be acquiring him for anything more than the short term.
In this case, the Broncos could find lots of options to add a playmaker. Among the names that have been mentioned are Calvin Ridley, Jerry Jeudy, Quentin Johnston, Brian Thomas Jr., and Josh Downs.
However, this is the least likely option among the offensive playmaker positions. The Broncos have a viable option who should be available after the bye week: Pat Bryant.
Bryant was placed on injured reserve after he sprained his ankle in Week 4 . He's eligible to come off injured reserve this week, though the Broncos could wait until after the Week 10 bye to give him more time to get healthy.
But once Bryant is back in the lineup, that should give the Broncos the receiving boost they need. The Broncos need not worry about seeking a trade here.
A running back to replace Dobbins for the rest of the season makes the most sense here. It would allow the Broncos to get help now in their pursuit of a Super Bowl and have a player who can provide help until Harvey returns from injury, but make it clear that Coleman is the top guy moving forward.
Doing so would mean the Broncos would have to part ways with some draft capital but not a lot — and while it's easy to say "forget them picks," Broncos fans must remember there are key players with expiring contracts or one year left after 2026 who need to be replaced.
It's easy to look at a trade like the Jeffery Simmons deal, but it's better to think about somebody like Rashid Shaheed, whom the Seattle Seahawks acquired last season for 2026 fourth- and fifth-round picks. Shaheed not only provided immediate help but was a key reason the Seahawks won the Super Bowl.
Sometimes the best trades to make are not of the blockbuster variety. It's often the under-the-radar deals involving Day 3 picks that turn out to be important for a deep playoff run.
It's my belief that the Broncos need to talk to the Titans about Pollard, while keeping an eye on the Ravens situation when it comes to Henry. A deal for Pollard or Henry might not be as sexy as Taylor, but it could do just as much to boost the Broncos' Super Bowl chances.

title: 3 Things Still on My Mind After Broncos' Huge Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
The Denver Broncos beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, avenging their season-opening loss at Arrowhead Stadium, and taking a half-game lead in the AFC West.
The Broncos are now the betting favorites to win the division , and all of their goals are still in front of them. At 6-2, the Broncos are poised to extend their four-game winning streak, while the Chiefs have yet to face the toughest stretch of their schedule.
But I'm still sifting through the aftermath of Broncos-Chiefs. Coming off Denver’s sixth win of the season, here are three things on my mind.
Nix’s ankle may have healed and felt good enough to begin the season as the starter, but psychologically, he wasn’t at that same level of recovery. It was clear he didn’t trust his eyes or his weapons to make plays around him.
And yet, the Broncos kept winning, thanks, in part, to Nix stepping up in some critical moments in Week 2 and Week 3. After an ugly showing against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 (Denver won that game, by the way), the Nix pile-on reached epic proportions around the league, as fans finally rushed to social media to voice their fears that something was indeed wrong with the Broncos’ quarterback.
However, Nix kept plugging away, and in Week 7, we finally saw him take some chances downfield and utilize his legs as the weapon they can be against the Arizona Cardinals. His 62-yard rushing touchdown seemed to snap him out of his funk, as his confidence came flooding back.
Nix had four explosive passing plays against the Cardinals, and he followed that up with four more against the Chiefs. He finished with 200-plus passing yards in both games, passing for three touchdowns with zero interceptions over that span.
Some say we should pump the brakes. That it’s too early to say that Nix has fully returned to his pre-injury form, but he’s clearly taken some big leaps in that direction over the past two weeks. He’s trusting his eyes again, and he’s unafraid to use his legs to help move the chains.
Nix wants to be peaking as the Broncos hit their stretch run, and the signs are pointing in that direction. I’ll say it, Broncos Country, even if some pundits won’t:
I don’t know if, like Nix, Dobbins is struggling with the mental aspects of bouncing back from the Lisfranc injury that ended his 2025 season in Week 10, or if it’s the cumulative effect of having dealt with three major injuries as a pro, but he’s not the same guy we saw last year.
The Broncos re-signed Dobbins in the spring, giving him a 4x raise , and they’ve tried to extract some blood from that turnip, but nothing has worked. He’s having a career-low season as a rusher, and he’s purportedly healthy.
But something isn’t right with Dobbins. Meanwhile, rookie Jonah Coleman has sparked the Broncos’ offense, and his efficiency and productivity have rendered Dobbins a spectator.
Against the Chiefs, Coleman had 41 snaps to Dobbins’s 13. Payton doesn’t typically take the bell-cow approach with running backs, but that’s the way this thing is trending with Coleman.
Dobbins has proven that he can’t be trusted to move the chains. And until he does something to show that he can be a net-positive for this offense, Payton would be foolish to take any snaps away from the ascending Coleman.
I’m not sure if we’re getting the full story with Dobbins. When healthy, he’s always been one of the NFL’s most productive backs, so he’s either nursing a top-secret ailment (unlikely), or Father Time has combined with his injury history to force a rapid decline.
It’s a shame. But the Broncos can’t overthink it. Until and unless they orchestrate a trade ahead of the November 10 deadline, it’s the Jonah Coleman show moving forward.
But it's worth remembering the Broncos are the betting favorites to land Jonathan Taylor.
With Talanoa Hufanga still out of commission (maybe he’ll return to practice this week), and Brandon Jones now nursing a hamstring injury, the Broncos have relied on Taylor Rapp and Devon Key as the backup safeties, though they left much to be desired against the Chiefs.
However, Week 8 proved that Skinner is deserving of a bigger seat at the table. He’s not the greatest in coverage — okay, fine — but he could be used to devastating effect as a dime-backer and big nickel.
Skinner took on Kenneth Walker III on the goal line, in a situation where the game was on the line, and he single-handedly stopped one of the NFL’s toughest running backs to tackle from scoring. It was impressive, and it showed how big Skinner’s heart is.
JL Skinner is like, "Not today, Kenneth!" pic.twitter.com/v8pcr1BYk6
Skinner is big, he’s physical, and he’s in a contract year. He might not be the best coverage safety, but he’s probably better than linebacker Justin Strnad in coverage.
The Broncos would be wise to reward Skinner with a slightly expanded role, using him as a dime-backer on first and second down when the opponent is in multiple tight-end sets.
I’d trust Skinner to run with a tight end more than I would Strnad, and if the opponent calls a run, he’s more than equipped to sift through the muss and make the tackle, as we saw on the goal line against the Chiefs.
Skinner is in a contract year, and he’s screaming for an opportunity to prove he offers more than mere third-phase value. It’s time the Broncos start giving him a few more snaps each week, even if Hufanga returns this week for the Carolina Panthers game.
