title: Broncos Dethrone Chiefs as AFC West Betting Favorites—What Lies Ahead
full_text:
Sean Payton stopped short of calling the Denver Broncos' rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs a "must-win" game, but the stakes were about as high as they could get at the mid-season point.
The Broncos came out on top 28-24 on Sunday , overcoming an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Chiefs and overtake them as the AFC West leaders. At 6-2, the Broncos are winners of four in a row and are in the driver's seat in the division.
Even the oddsmakers see the Broncos as the new favorites to win the AFC West. DraftKings Sportsbook has Denver as -130 favorites, with the Chiefs at +115, the Las Vegas Raiders at +2500, and the Los Angeles Chargers at +1500.
As the defending AFC West champions, the Broncos were always going to draw a first-place schedule in 2026. Add to that the rotation of the AFC West drawing the NFC West and AFC East on the schedule this season, and the Broncos' road to repeating as division champs got a little tougher.
Then the NFL front-loaded the Broncos' schedule with most of their toughest opponents coming through the first eight weeks. The NFC West and AFC East produced five playoff teams last season. The Broncos played all four NFC West opponents within the first seven weeks, going 3-1 against them, losing only to the San Francisco 49ers.
The Chiefs in Week 8 were the last big test to end the Broncos' brutal first-half-of-the-season gauntlet, and they passed with flying colors. Now, the Broncos' schedule opens up dramatically.
The Broncos will go on the road this week to face the 3-4 Carolina Panthers, followed by their Week 10 bye. From there, it's home against the 4-4 Raiders in Week 11, then back on the road to play the 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday.
The Steelers have out-kicked their coverage thus far, so that game could end up being tougher than it appeared to be at first glance. The Broncos then come back home to host the 1-6 Miami Dolphins in Week 12, followed by a two-game road trip to play the 2-6 New York Jets and the Raiders.
That's when the schedule begins to stiffen again. The Broncos come home for a Week 16 game on Christmas Day against the 6-1 Buffalo Bills, followed by a road trip to face the 5-3 New England Patriots, and a home stand against the winless Chargers in the season finale.
The Steelers, Bills, and Patriots could be tough, but if the Broncos take care of business, and beat the teams they're supposed to, they could hit Week 16 at 12-2 or 11-3 at worst. The Chiefs, though, have a much more treacherous road ahead.
The next three weeks aren't too bad for the Chiefs, with a home game against the Jets, a road trip to face the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons, and then back home to play the 3-5 Arizona Cardinals. But it gets gnarly from there.
From Week 12 on, the Chiefs will play the Bills, Patriots, 49ers (6-1), and Raiders at home, and the Los Angeles Rams (4-4), Cincinnati Bengals (5-2), and Chargers on the road. It's about as a brutal a closing stretch as the Broncos' initial schedule was.
The difference is that, in theory, by the time a team hits its stretch run, it's had the chance to build up a callus to begin peaking at the right time before the playoffs. The Broncos went from summer football straight into a playoff guantlet, which forced them to quickly build a callus against such fierce resistance training.
As I wrote when the NFL first dropped the schedule last spring, the Broncos' initial slate of games could be a blessing in disguise — so long as they emerge from Week 8 no worse than 4-4. The Broncos did even better than that, and that's why they're in firm control of the division from here on out.
As the Broncos emerge from the first half of the season, Bo Nix has regained his confidence after suffering a fractured ankle in the playoffs. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman has emerged as a bona fide RB1, and the Broncos have much bigger plans for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.
Vance Joseph's defense is getting healthier, and has done an amazing job of keeping the who's-who list of elite NFL quarterbacks at bay long enough for Nix and the offense to get their fourth-quarter licks in and win games.
Nobody will want to face the Broncos down the stretch.

title: Broncos Sign RB Amid Trade Rumors
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have added a running back — just not the running back everyone's hoping for .
Denver announced Tuesday that it has signed former Chargers RB Jarett Patterson to the practice squad, along with defensive lineman Jordan Miller and defensive back Ugo Amadi.
In corresponding moves, the club released wide receivers Eli Pancol and Cameron Ross from the practice squad.
Undrafted in 2021, Patterson (5-8, 195) has six years of NFL service and 27 games of experience, split between time with the Washington Commanders (then the Football Team) and the Los Angeles Chargers. He's handled 126 career carries for 503 yards and three rushing touchdowns.
Patterson, who turns 28 in December, is now the senior-most RB on Denver's practice squad. The other back, third-year man Cody Schrader, was promoted to the 53-man active roster prior to Week 8 and figures to again earn an elevation with the Broncos relatively thin at the position.
This will be Miller's second stint in the Mile High City after spending the majority of 2024 and 2025 on Denver's taxi squad. He was signed to — and eventually released from — the Miami Dolphins' practice team in September.
Amadi initially joined the Broncos' practice squad last month but was cut loose ahead of Week 8 with the club's secondary nearing full strength.
The defensive additions come only one day after head coach Sean Payton rued the fact that Denver currently leads the NFL in snaps taken on that side of the ball.
“There’s a lot that goes into that. That’s a stat I don’t like," Payton told reporters via conference call on Monday. "It’s a stat that on offense, we have to do a good job of possessing the ball. So that’s something that we pay attention to.”
Many among Broncos Country have already taken to social media following Patterson's addition, vexed over the possibility that his signing rules Denver out of contention for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, who's been consistently linked in trade rumors.
The reality is, the Broncos have one more game (at Carolina) until the Week 10 bye, and two of their running backs (RJ Harvey, Tyler Badie) remain on short-term injured reserve. With rookie Jonah Coleman and aging vet J.K. Dobbins left primarily in the backfield, this is as much about temporary insurance as anything else.
If you're one of the many who want Denver to land Taylor, fret not. "Jaret Patterson" would not prevent them from making that move ... if they want to make the move in the first place.
"(General manager) George (Paton) and I will spend time looking at the team and anywhere we can improve it, but I’m not going to answer questions about internet gossip,” Payton said Monday.

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Miami Dolphins in Week 9
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will head down South to take on the 1-6 Miami Dolphins this Sunday.
Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game).
Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25.
Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7).
The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings.
In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami.
“Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.”
As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10).
And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota.
They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami.
As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit .
Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair.
At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory .

title: Exploring If Dolphins LB Jordyn Brooks Fits Detroit Lions Defense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions could get a look at multiple potential trade targets when they travel to Miami to take on the Dolphins on Sunday.
Miami enters the matchup with a 1-6 record under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Because of the state of their organization, the Dolphins could be looking to offload some of their assets ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
One potential player they could be willing to deal is linebacker Jordyn Brooks. He's an interesting option for Detroit, as he just signed a three-year contract extension in July that will keep him under team control through the 2029 season.
While this would be a hefty financial ask for the Lions to take on the remainder of Brooks' contract that comes with $35 million guaranteed and $51.3 in total new money, the possibility of the Lions making that move was brought up by Sports Illustrated NFL insider Albert Breer .
Breer noted that the injury to Jack Campbell, a defensive captain and All-Pro contributor for the Lions, leaves a big void in the middle of Detroit's defense. In Brooks, they would be getting a reliable veteran that could help stabilize the group for a lengthy period of time.
"There is the fact that that leaves a significant hole for the Lions at the linebacker position," Breer said. "And so, would you make a call on somebody like Jordyn Brooks in Miami? I don't think Miami wants to let go of its veteran leaders, but they're another team that needs players. I look at Jordyn Brooks as somebody that you could potentially make a move for if you're willing to put something valuable in front of the Dolphins.
"I think it's somebody that could be around for an extended period. A lot of that is going to depend on Jack Campbell's status," Breer continued. "I don't want to talk too much about this in football terms because I think we're more worried about him as a human being right now, but again there are football implications to that."
Jordyn Brooks @PoupartNFL Let’s save the Dolphins and raid their team pic.twitter.com/prs49CPMV0
Brooks would be a player that would absolutely fit Detroit's defense . As an inside linebacker in Miami's defense, he has had a phenomenal season. Per Pro Football Reference, Brooks has recorded 63 tackles without missing any which is the most without a missed tackle by any player this season.
The veteran is also the eighth-fastest player to reach 900 career tackles since 1994, doing so in 104 games. He's a steady tackler and a phenomenal producer from the second level of the Dolphins' defense.
However, the Dolphins likely wouldn't be inclined to move him for a minimal price. This would be a big ask for Detroit, given the level of team control the Dolphins have and how they could utilize not only his on-field abilities but also his leadership to rebuild under Hafley.
In general manager Brad Holmes' tenure, the Lions have not been apt to make big moves at the deadline and instead have made marginal moves to supplement the roster they've already built.
Because of this, adding Brooks would be unlikely despite of how well he would fit Detroit's defense moving forward.

title: Calvin Johnson Shares Important Sentiment About Team Spending
full_text:
Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receiver Calvin Johnson raised eyebrows during his recent appearance on the "Chasing No. 1" podcast that features Bengals wideout Ja'Marr Chase.
Nearing the NFL trade deadline, many supporters of the Detroit Lions are again clamoring for the team to be willing to add high-end talent.
Johnson referenced his team in Motown and how the organization was not willing to make an all-in move when Matthew Stafford was under center.
"The biggest thing for me is that, I used to always say, we tell everybody we got the team here in Detroit," said Johnson. "We had the dudes, but you can't win a Super Bowl on a budget, man. You got to go all in. You got to go all in. That's what you see teams do. They go all-in and get that one piece or two pieces that they're missing, to get them all the way there over the last couple seasons."
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Week 9 Officiating Crew For Dolphins Game Are Favorable
“You can’t win a Super Bowl on a budget” pic.twitter.com/1YYn6olWgm
The Rams were willing to make a blockbuster trade in 2020, shipping the Lions two first-round draft picks in order to land the former No. 1 overall pick.
In his first season away from Detroit, Stafford was able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy for the first time.
Johnson expressed he believed the Lions could have had more success, had the organization been more willing to go all-in.
"We had most of the pieces there in Detroit," Johnson noted. "And so for me, when he won Super Bowl, literally the first year after he left Detroit, I'm out there like, 'I mean, I told y'all what we had.'"
A recent ESPN report indicated general manager Brad Holmes has been inquiring about available cornerbacks in the trade market.
Unfortunately, the Lions may also be competing with the Chicago Bears for the same quality defenders.
“The Bears made their big move for Jeffery Simmons, but they’re still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions,” Graziano wrote earlier this week. “Detroit might also be in the market for help at linebacker, particularly in the wake of the terrible injury to mainstay Jack Campbell.”

title: Lions Second Year Defensive End Could Prove Himself Against Dolphins
full_text:
With injuries on defense, the Detroit Lions could give a second-year defensive end his first opportunity in the NFL.
An injury cut Ahmed Hassanein's rookie season short, as he was waived with an injury diagnosis last season and returned on the practice squad once the injury settlement expired. However, he was never elevated to the active roster and as a result never made his official debut.
Hassanein had a strong training camp this year and made the team, but has been a healthy scratch for every game up to this point. As a result, he's still awaiting his NFL debut midway through his second season as a professional.
Things could change for Hassanein on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins, as veteran DJ Wonnum is currently in the NFL's concussion protocol after a collision with safety Brian Branch against the Minnesota Vikings.
In fact, Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson went as far as to say he believes Hassanein will get an opportunity Sunday against the Dolphins in an interview with 97.1 The Ticket .
"If I was a betting man I'd say Ahmed's probably getting his opportunity this weekend. Derrick Moore is gonna be out there for sure, both those guys," Hutchinson said. "D-Mo's shown a ton of progression these first few weeks, and I know Ahmed's just itching to get out there, man. He can't wait. I think it's going to be a good opportunity for those guys, and couldn't be happier for them."
A bigger update regarding Wonnum's status could be forthcoming this week at practice, and this will likely be telling as to whether or not the veteran could suit up for Detroit on Sunday. If he can't, it would potentially pave the way for Hassanein to be active for the first time in his career.
If Hassanein is active for the first time, it will be an intriguing look at the 2025 sixth-round pick out of Boise State. His journey to the NFL has been well-known, as he took an unlikely path after being born in Egypt and worked his way to an opportunity with Boise State.
After being drafted by the Lions, Hassanein has traveled a long journey toward what could be his first chance with the team. He underwent a position change this offseason, moving from a rush end to a big end with more responsibilities in the run game as well as more versatility as far as where he lines up.
Still, he found his way into the backfield on multiple occasions throughout the preseason including a sack of Cincinnati Bengals starting quarterback Joe Burrow in the opener this year.
Now, with injuries creating an opportunity for him, Hassanein has a chance to prove himself on the biggest stage Sunday against the Dolphins.

title: Feud Emerges at Lions Flagship Radio Over Jack Campbell Coverage
full_text:
It is not uncommon when sports talk radio hosts have differing opinions on a topic and debate their viewpoints.
Unfortunately, things possibly went a little too far, when a popular host at the Detroit Lions flagship radio station called out another host, who he had previously hosted a gambling podcast with.
97.1 The Ticket host Mike Valenti, host during the afternoon drive slot, upset his colleague Jim Costa and others, after calling out how the morning show host handled the Jack Campbell news on Monday morning.
"I want to be very sincere with my audience, the Jack Campbell injury really messed me up. I like Jim Costa, I think Jim has a massive career ahead of him in radio, but I think Jim sounded like a massive J.O. this morning," Valenti shared with a large afternoon audience. "Bottom line, I can't dance about a win because I can't get it out of my head Jack Campbell lying motionless on the field.
"And yes, it's a big win, and no, you're not a bad person if privately you're celebrating it, and you should. I'm watching players cry. You don't see that. And when he was getting carted off, I can't lie to you, man, it choked up me. It messed me up. I can't get it out of my head."
Costa, an established sports talk host with a growing following and reputation, was hesitant to respond, but was compelled to share his reaction, due to the overwhelming amount of individuals messaging on Tuesday morning to hear his response.
"We were incredibly sensitive to Jack Campbell yesterday on the show, dedicating time in every hour. And I would contend that you can do both. A good show can do both," Costa shared. "Can talk both football and humanity. So I don't know why that's such an issue. Valenti hates when he's misrepresented. Don't do it to other people. Do not make it out that I or this show was insensitive about a very scary and very real issue going on with Jack Campbell. If he wants to dunk on me for a dumb sports take, I've had plenty, I will have plenty.
"All of that is fair game, but it (Valenti's words) bothered me. You do not need to insinuate that somehow by us talking football yesterday that we don't care about Jack Campbell the person, or we are doing a tone-deaf radio show," Costa added further. "It's a four-hour radio show. We can say thoughts and prayers to Jack Campbell and mean it sincerely. What are we going to do or the other three hours? I like Mike. I do. We have a great relationship, friendship. I thought that was bush league yesterday."
Valenti was not on the air on Wednesday and has not yet commented on Costa's retort.
The "Cash The Ticket" podcast, featuring both Valenti and Costs, is not airing this fall.

title: Detroit Lions Draw Week 9 Officiating Crew With Favorable Trend
full_text:
The officiating crew for the Detroit Lions ' Week 9 game against the Miami Dolphins has been revealed.
For the matchup, Land Clark will serve as the head referee. Clark began his career as an official as a field judge, and also served as a side judge before being promoted to a head referee during the 2020 NFL season.
This will be Clark's seventh Lions game in his career as a head ref, and Detroit is 5-0-1 in games he's presided over. Notably, he served as the top official for the Lions' tie with the Pittsburgh Steelers during the 2021 season.
He also officiated over the Lions' win over the Minnesota Vikings on Christmas Eve, 2023 when Detroit won 30-24 to cement their first division title since 1993.
Clark last reffed a Lions game in Week 2 of the 2025 season, when they defeated the Chicago Bears in a 52-21 rout. He has also worked six Dolphins games in his career, with Miami being 2-4 in those games.
In 2026, Clark has worked seven games with road teams being 6-1 in those games. This is favorable for Detroit, as they enter Sunday's game as a favorite heading into Miami's Hard Rock Stadium.
According to NFL Penalties , Clark's crew ranks tied-for-third-lowest in terms of total flags thrown up to this point in the season with 94. Of those flags, 51 have been thrown on the home team and 43 have been on visiting teams.
The highest count of penalties he's had this season was the Week 3 tilt between the Cleveland Browns and Carolina Panthers, when 19 total flags were thrown. By contrast, he officiated the Week 6 game between Tampa Bay and Pittsburgh where only nine penalties were called.
Clark's crew ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of offensive holding penalties called with 19 total, while the Lions have 11 total this season. This crew has called 18 false starts, and the Lions have 14 as a team so far this season.
Because Clark's penalties align with Detroit's tendencies, this is something to watch throughout Sunday's game.

title: Jack Campbell Statement: Has Lower Body Movement, Issues With Upper Body
full_text:
The Detroit Lions and Jack Campbell have released another update regarding his current health status.
Campbell was hospitalized Sunday after a collision in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. After the hit, he remained on the turf while being tended to by the team's medical staff before being carted to the ambulance and taken to the hospital.
Head coach Dan Campbell has spoken multiple times since the injury, noting the duality between the concern he and the team faces regarding Campbell's situation while also taking into account the necessary preparation required for their upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins.
Teammates and fans alike have shown an outpouring of support for their injured teammate, with several players speaking at length about the impact Jack Campbell has both in the locker room as a leader as well as on the field as a player.
The Lions will have to brace for the reality of being without their middle linebacker and defensive on-field play-caller. Campbell, an All-Pro in 2025, handled a hefty responsibility that will not be easily replaceable for coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.
Detroit's linebacker room currently is headlined by a trio of veterans in Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske. Amen Ogbongbemiga is also a journeyman in his first year with the Lions, while they added KJ Britt off of the New England Patriots' practice squad.
It is shaping up to be a challenging week for Detroit, who also has multiple other key contributors dealing with ailments. Defensive end DJ Wonnum and safety Brian Branch are both in concussion protocol, while D.J. Reed is dealing with a hip injury.
On offense, the Lions could be without center Cade Mays, who suffered an ankle injury in the first half of the Vikings game, as well as running back/kick returner Jacob Saylors (neck).
Detroit is currently 5-2, with back-to-back wins over NFC North opponents heading into Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins. It begins a challenging stretch, as this upcoming game will be followed by a trip to Germany, a home game against the Buccaneers and then a Thanksgiving showdown with the Chicago Bears.
Here is the Campbell statement in full, released by the team on Wednesday afternoon.
"My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. God is good. My faith is strong."

title: Goff, St. Brown, Hutchinson React to Serious Jack Campbell Injury
full_text:
Several key members of the Detroit Lions roster have shared their support, prayers and reaction to linebacker Jack Campbell suffering a serious injury and being carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings.
Both quarterback Jared Goff and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson have weekly scheduled interviews on 97.1 The Ticket, the Lions flagship station.
"We're doing all right," said Goff on Tuesday, the players day off this week. "There were a lot of injuries that affected a lot of guys' seasons, but certainly the one that's scariest is Jack (Campbell's). The positive updates are great and we know that things are heading in the right direction right now and hoping for the best for him."
Hutchinson indicated the game left him feeling drained, due to all the events surrounding Campbell and other key defenders leaving the game injured.
"After that game, it was just the weirdest feeling, just with Jack and everything. You know, even D.J. (Wonnum) leaving the game on a cart, if I remember correctly. And then with B.B. (Brian Branch). So many things happened, and it was just a lot on my mind after the game," said Hutchinson. "So much stuff happened on defense where it was just a lot to process. A lot of stuff is still up in the air right now. Once we get into tomorrow, into our first- and second-down game plan for Miami, we can kind of really put our focus on that. Definitely, still processing, for sure."
Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown shared his thoughts on the latest episode of the St. Brown Bros. podcast.
"I don't know any more than anybody else does," said St. Brown. "Obviously, the Lions posted. I just want to say, all you guys that are watching is to keep him in your thoughts and your prayers. You hate to see anyone go down in this game, whether it is someone on our team, someone on their team. Any team in this league. I think injuries is something that makes this game so tough, so real at the same time. I remember being out there on the field watching. Seeing him on the ground from a distance. All I could think about was his wife and his newborn baby that he just had a few months ago. I just want him to be okay to go play with his kid, honestly. And to be normal.
"When things like that happen throughout the game or throughout the season, it does make it hard for us to go back and play. Its like, 'Damn.' We took care of him, put him on a stretcher and sent him out back to the hospital and now we have to play again," St. Brown added. "That kind of sucks. It is what I signed up for. What we signed up for. We get paid a lot of money to play this sport that we love. We have got to finish the game. Injuries like that, it makes you put things in perspective . He has done that for a lot of us on that team. I'm think about Jack. We are all thinking about Jack. I hope he continues to get better and all we can do is pray for him."

title: Pros and Cons of Detroit Lions Trading For Mike Sainristil
full_text:
The Detroit Lions find themselves in dire need of cornerback help at the present moment.
Since day one of the 2026 season, the Lions have needed to strengthen the position. And now with D.J. Reed, Detroit's No. 1 cornerback , going down with a hip injury this past Sunday against Minnesota, the void has only increased.
To add insult to injury, Reed was just hitting his stride. The ninth-year defensive back had morphed into a shutdown corner over the last three games, earning no less than a 78.9 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus for his efforts in each contest.
And he was especially stout in coverage in the Lions’ Week 8 victory over the Vikings, recording an interception and allowing just one completion on five passes thrown his way by QB Kyler Murray. It was an elite-level performance from Reed, and as a result, he earned his best coverage mark (91.3) and overall grade (88.2) from PFF for the season.
Consequently, if the 29-year-old has to miss an extended period of time, it will be a significant blow to Detroit's secondary.
It furthers the reason why Lions general manager Brad Holmes needs to make a concerted effort to land a cornerback prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
With that said, one of the corners he could target is Washington Commanders defensive back Mike Sainristil. He was named by Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer, in his most recent video mailbag, as a defensive back Detroit could pursue.
Sainristil has had a brutal start to the season, highlighted by his league-worst PFF coverage grade (28.5) and overall mark (29.4). Furthermore, he failed to log a single defensive snap for the first time in his career on Sunday against the Eagles.
As a result, he could be had on the cheap right now by Holmes & Co., likely only costing a late-round pick. And fans and pundits alike both know that the sixth-year Lions front-office executive is a big proponent of bargain shopping, and trading for Sainristil would be the definition of that, considering his myriad of struggles so far in 2026.
Plus, he could have some good football still ahead of him and could benefit from a change of scenery, since he's only 26 years old. Additionally, if he could re-find his rookie form (two interceptions, nine passes defensed and a 64.1 PFF coverage grade), it'd make giving up a late-round draft choice for him well worth it.
Still, adding Sainristil, who's in the midst of the worst season of his three-year NFL career, would do little to move the needle for Detroit's defensive backs group. He'd be more of a depth piece than anything for the team's depleted cornerbacks room at this juncture.
Subsequently, even if Holmes were to pull the trigger on a deal involving Sainristil, he'd still definitely need to make another move for a higher-impact corner.

title: Packers Placed Big Bet on Christian Watson, And Everyone Is Cashing In
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers receiver Christian Watson has set career highs for receptions and receiving yards.
The Packers gave Watson a huge contract extension with a base value of $92 million in June. Their offseason decisions at the position and the contract were bets that a player who hadn’t quite reached his potential during his first four seasons would do it in Year 5 and beyond.
The Packers, obviously, won the bets, because it’s almost impossible to believed they’d be taking a 5-3 record into Sunday’s game at the New England Patriots without him having by far the best season of his career.
Watson entered the season with career highs of 41 catches (in 14 games as a rookie in 2022), 620 yards (in 15 games before a torn ACL in 2024) and seven touchdowns (as a rookie). This year, with the Packers hitching their wagon to Watson instead of Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, he’s caught 42 passes for 708 yards and six touchdowns.
Watson ranks fourth in the league in receiving yards and seventh in receiving yards per game. Among receivers with at least 20 catches, he’s second with a 16.86-yard average – 0.02 yards behind Cincinnati’s Tee Higgins.
Watson’s 17-game pace is 89 receptions for 1,505 yards and 13 touchdowns. That’s noteworthy because of the escalators in his contract, which would increase his 2027 base salary.
If Watson finishes with 85-plus receptions, there is a $750,000 escalator. So, he’s on pace to hit that one. If he gets to 95 receptions, the escalator increases to $1.15 million.
If Watson finishes with 1,200-plus receiving yards, he’d also hit the $1.15 million escalator.
If Watson reaches a dozen touchdowns, there’s another $1.15 million escalator.
At his current pace, Watson would hit $3.05 million in escalators, with an opportunity to max it out at $3.45 million if he cranks up the catch production a bit. If Watson is selected to the Pro Bowl, that would be an additional $250,000.
Watson’s production has exploded because of the additional opportunities. His hard work to become much more than just a size-speed threat has come to the forefront.
“He just had some nagging injuries, stuff like that, so he never really got to have a training camp that first year,” passing-game coordinator Jason Vrable said this week. “I think that puts you behind the 8-ball a lot, and that kind of happened to Savion last year. And it’s not an excuse; it’s just a reality.
“To get better in this league, you have to grind out reps at a high level. You have to go against good corners – like some of the guys we have now – and you have to battle one-on-one. You have to callous yourself, or else you’re just going to do the same stuff you did in college. So, if you weren’t good at a slant route in college, and you’re not going to come into the pros and run it on air and be good. It’s a sport that demands you to go against a man across me who’s a good player and build yourself.”
Watson, of course, suffered a broken rib in last week’s win against Carolina. After a brief trip to the hospital, he was back on the field to finish the game .
If the injury didn’t keep him from returning to that game, he sure as heck will be on the field against the Patriots with a little additional padding.
“There’s only so much you can do,” he said after Wednesday’s practice. “It definitely still hurts. But I’ve been hurting out there plenty of times before, and I’m sure a lot of guys are dealing with other stuff. So, that’s just part of the game.”
Watson missed the end of the 2024 season and the first half of the 2025 season with a torn ACL. In the 18 games back in the lineup, Watson has 77 receptions for 1,319 yards and 12 touchdowns. He ranks 13th in yards and third in touchdowns over that span.
So, to be sidelined was difficult beyond the pain.
“I mean, just frustration, to be honest, because once I was able to catch my breath, obviously the pain and stuff was still there,” he said. “But if felt like that I could kind of just play through and still be out there. So, just frustrating that I had to go miss the game and potentially miss the rest of the game.
“I was definitely frustrated, but I understand that doctors have a job to keep us safe and, obviously, I knew that there could be a possibility for something more serious or whatnot. So, I was just trusting the doctors to do their job and keep me safe. I was frustrated, for sure, but understanding, as well.”
Watson is on a prolific pace that could have him challenging Davante Adams (1,553 yards in 2021) and Jordy Nelson (1,519 yards in 2014) as the most productive receiver in Packers history.
“He’s playing at a high level right now,” Vrable said. “I’m happy for him to finally get some respect that I do believe that he deserves.”

title: Packers-Patriots Thursday Injury Report: Injuries Impacting Specific Matchup
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have an injury concern at quarterback. The New England Patriots have all sorts of problems at receiver.
Those injuries highlight Thursday’s injury report and could play a role in Sunday’s showdown between five-win teams.
Five players didn’t practice for the Packers. One of them was starting cornerback Keisean Nixon, who once again is dealing with a groin injury . He was limited participation at Wednesday’s practice.
Nixon missed the Wednesday practice before the Dallas game because of a groin injury but started and played every snap in a big-time performance against the high-flying Cowboys passing game.
Nixon signed with the Packers in free agency in 2022. He has played in every regular-season game during the past four-plus seasons and a total of 80 in a row with the team including playoffs.
As defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said recently, Nixon is playing like a “starting-caliber” cornerback. Last year, Nixon allowed seven touchdowns and was penalized 12 times. This year, according to Pro Football Focus, he has allowed zero touchdowns and only been flagged three times.
“He’s competitive,” Gannon said. “He really is competitive and he plays the game with an edge. He doesn’t back down. I love that about him.”
Also not practicing for the Packers were starting linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle), former starting guard Travis Glover (knee) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Whyle’s status could get Jonnu Smith back on the field after he was inactive for the Carolina game.
Superstar edge rusher Micah Parsons practiced for the second consecutive day as he knocks off the rust following last year’s torn ACL. He’s only doing individual drills this week so was limited participation.
“Any time you get a player like that, it makes your job a lot easier,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said. “So, look forward to having him back soon, whenever that time is. He's an unbelievable player, unbelievable talent, so any time you get somebody like that rushing the passer, it makes your job a lot easier. So, yeah, I've been looking at him. Just excited to have him back.”
Also, running back MarShawn Lloyd, whose first two seasons were ruined by lower-body injuries, didn’t miss a practice during the offseason or training camp and hasn’t even been on the injury report this season.
Until now. Lloyd was limited participation with a knee injury.
Other than the addition of Lloyd and the status of Nixon, Green Bay’s injury report is unchanged from Wednesday.
The Patriots’ offense could be depleted.
Former Packers receiver Romeo Doubs is on injured reserve for at least a couple more weeks. Premier receiver A.J. Brown, who is battling ankle and knee injuries and has played in only three games this season, didn’t practice again. The knee is the big issue and “is threatening to hold him out this week,” according to ESPN.com’s Adam Schefter.
Making matters worse, tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, did not participate for a second consecutive day due to a foot injury.
DeMario Douglas, a sixth-round pick in 2023 who stands only 5-foot-8, has filled the void as much as possible. He’s second on the team with 26 receptions and leads the way with 332 yards and four touchdowns.
“I was telling somebody the other day, it’s hard not to love a teammate like Pop,” quarterback Drake Maye said. “He’s constantly the same. He’s always laughing and smiling. I love when he starts dancing in the end zone; we got him in the end zone a couple times this year.
“He can turn an easy catch and he’s hard to tackle. So, like I’ve always said, you can’t guard him in a phone booth, so he’s fun. We’ve got to get him the ball in space more and let him go do his thing because he’s fun to watch.”
New England’s premier punt returner, cornerback Marcus Jones, did not practice because of a foot injury. He had two punt-return touchdowns last season.
“He’s very, very dynamic. He can break the game open at any point,” Packers special teams coordinator Cam Achord said this week. “I’ve played a lot of good returners; he’s in that bunch – top three guys – in the National Football League.”

title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Two Key Updates on Defense
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Including playoffs, Keisean Nixon has played in all 80 games since joining the Green Bay Packers in 2022.
Is that streak in jeopardy?
There’s plenty of time before the Packers play at the New England Patriots on Sunday, but Nixon was one of five players who did not practice on Thursday. He was limited participation with a groin injury on Wednesday.
Nixon has a history of playing through pain, including this season.
Last week, he was limited participation all week with a shoulder injury but started and played all but one snap against Carolina. A couple weeks earlier, Nixon did not participate in the Wednesday practice due to a groin injury, was limited the next two days and played every snap in the win against Dallas.
“I take my body serious,” he said before the Dallas game. “It’s my resume, it’s my life. I take pride playing every Sunday. That’s just my goal, what I want to do.”
While it might not be showing up in the stats, Nixon is having an excellent season. He has one interception and six passes defensed – he ranked among the NFL leaders with 17 passes defensed last season – but has been sharp while playing a lot of man coverage.
He’s allowed a catch rate of 68.1 percent, compared to 61.0 percent last season, according to Pro Football Focus. However, he’s allowing only 9.0 yards per catch, he’s been guilty of just three penalties and hasn’t allowed a touchdown.
Along with Nixon, these four players did not practice: Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion).
Rhyan suffered an ankle injury early in the win against Detroit but the team opted to not place him on injured reserve, with coach Matt LaFleur saying before Thursday’s practice that it was only a short-term injury.
Micah Parsons made his practice debut on Wednesday. A big mile marker for a player returning from a major injury is his ability to stack practices. So, so far, so good for Parsons.
In the second big update on Thursday, one day after being limited participation in his debut, Parsons was back at it again.
Not babying Parsons back into it. Here he is playing the role of an o-lineman for big Chris McClellan. pic.twitter.com/jpcs1ABbDW
As was the case on Wednesday , perhaps the most noteworthy part of what Parsons did in front of reporters wasn’t his work as a defensive player. It’s that he stood in as an offensive lineman while getting knocked backward by big rookie defensive tackle Chris McClellan.
“It was good just to get him back out there,” LaFleur said.
The Packers' closer, Micah Parsons, delivered the perfect closing line at the end of his 14-minute conversation with reporters following his first practice today. ⬇️ https://t.co/PwSwqluMNq
The NFL on Thursday named safety Evan Williams its NFC Defensive Player of Month and cornerback Brandon Cisse its NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month.
“Yeah, it's in the rearview mirror,” Cisse said on Wednesday of the first half of his rookie season. “Yeah, just on it this week. How great can I be this week? How can I get better each day in practice? That's just kind of what my mindset is on that.
“I just try to make sure I come to work every day with something to get better at. I don't try to look back in the past or all the plays I made or all the plays I've been wrong, and because all that matters is what's here now and it's going about this weekend. So, I'm just preparing the right way.”
Cisse led all rookies with seven passes defensed in October.
Brandon Cisse is the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month. Here are the notes from the league. pic.twitter.com/vmw4Cm6Lxx
Williams, according to the league, became the third safety since 2000 to record at least 40 tackles and three takeaways in a month, joining Rodney Harrison (October 2003 with New England) and George Wilson (October 2011 with Buffalo).
Evan Williams is the NFC Defensive Player of the Month. Here are the notes from the league. pic.twitter.com/DCeWQi9bWY
Among the players who did not practice for the Patriots on Wednesday was standout tight end Hunter Henry. He is leading the team with 29 receptions and is second with 326 yards but is dealing with an injured foot.
“I think he’s been someone for me that I can count on since my first snap in there my rookie year,” quarterback Drake Maye told reporters on Wednesday. “He’s been a security blanket and a great guy in the huddle, a great leader on this team.
“So, anytime you lose a guy like Hunter, a captain that does everything the right way, talks to the guys in the huddle, knows what I like, my body language, route running, does stuff in the run game. It’s tough. But I know he’ll do his best to get back out there as quick as he can.”
The teams will release their updated injury reports after Thursday’s practices. For now, here are the reports from Wednesday.
Packers Wednesday Injury Report
Did not participate: LB Zaire Franklin (shin), G Travis Glover (knee), C Sean Rhyan (ankle), TE Josh Whyle (concussion).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), CB Keisean Nixon (groin), edge Micah Parsons (knee), WR Christian Watson (rib).
Patriots Wednesday Injury Report
Did not participate: DT Christian Barmore (illness), WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), TE Hunter Henry (foot).
Limited participation: S Kevin Byard (chest), CB Carlton Davis (neck), WR Mack Hollins (calf), OLB Gabe Jacas (knee), LB Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder/knee), RT Morgan Moses (foot), G Greg Van Roten (hamstring).

title: Two Trades That Could Save Packers’ Season (And Two Deals They Should Avoid)
full_text:
The trade deadline is looming, and while the Green Bay Packers are historically inactive on the day, they have changed their ways under general manager Brian Gutekunst. The Packers never signed big-money free agents, traded up in the draft or made aggressive moves for players like Micah Parsons until they did.
This year, the Packers reportedly have been making calls to gather some price points ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline.
Gutekunst has said before he wants to be in every conversation, even if he is unable to pull the trigger on every potential trade.
As a result, the Packers could acquire some help before the deadline strikes. They probably should. The NFC North is a blood war that just got tougher with Chicago’s addition of Jeffery Simmons last week. Simmons was incredibly impactful in his first game with the Bears. The Lions and Vikings have beaten the Packers this season.
Yes, Parsons will return to the lineup, which could be argued as just as good as making a deadline acquisition. He does not, however, solve the issues of Green Bay’s terrible run game or perilously thin defensive tackle group.
With that in mind, here are some moves the Packers should be looking at making, and others they should avoid.
Jonathan Taylor is awesome. There’s no denying that. He’s one of the top running backs in football but stuck on a terrible team. The Indianapolis Colts are mired in a rebuild and started selling off some pieces starting in late October when Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were sent to two other NFC contenders, the Seahawks and 49ers, respectively.
Taylor would be the next logical piece to potentially get moved, and the Packers have a need in their run game .
So why should the Packers avoid acquiring the former Wisconsin Badgers legend?
Simply put, it would be a misuse of resources. The Colts are reportedly looking for either a first-round pick or something similar to the package of second- through fifth-round picks that the Carolina Panthers got when they traded Christian McCaffery to the San Francisco 49ers.
The Packers, of course, do not have a first-round pick thanks to last year’s deal for Micah Parsons.
As good as Taylor is, can he save the Packers’ putrid run game on his own? The answer is that it is unlikely.
While it should be noted that a team can only acquire what is on the market, if the Packers are willing to move significant draft capital, they should be looking for other spots on the roster.
According to ESPN, the Packers were interested in potentially acquiring Quenton Nelson before he was sent to Seattle.
ESPN has since connected the Packers to the market of Philadelphia Eagles star Landon Dickerson. Dickerson would give the offensive line some toughness and championship pedigree.
Dickerson has played mostly left guard with the Eagles, though he won the Rimington Award as the nation’s best center while at Alabama and started the 2024 NFC Championship Game against Washington with Cam Jurgens on the shelf for a back injury.
Dickerson and left tackle Jordan Mailata are the last men standing from the Eagles’ powerful 2024 offensive line that steamrolled its way to a title. Jurgens was traded to Baltimore and Lane Johnson retired with physical issues and a desire to focus on his mental health.
The issue with Dickerson are the injuries from his career are starting to pile up. He had two separate ACL injuries from college and struggled with a meniscus injury and bone bruise as recently as this year.
The Packers have enough issues with offensive linemen with uncertain injury histories. The other issue, which is a solvable problem of sorts, is where would he play?
Including playoffs, Dickerson has played 5,478 snaps at left guard, 81 snaps at center and 91 snaps at right guard, according to Pro Football Focus. The Packers have a need at center with Sean Rhyan sidelined with a high-ankle sprain. Left guard, however, belongs to Aaron Banks as evidenced by their actions.
Trading for Dickerson, only to ask him to play right guard, would be another misuse of resources and another case of playing musical chairs along the offensive line when it’s unnecessary.
With the asking price likely to be a mid-round pick, there could be better options that present themselves.
We just finished saying not to trade for Jonathan Taylor because of the price point. That is different than saying the Packers should not be in the market for a running back at all.
The Packers need help at running back, regardless of whether or not Josh Jacobs remains on the field. Jacobs’ backups have done little to inspire confidence in their ability to do much of anything in his absence or since his return to action.
Jacobs’ future is uncertain because of new information that emerged during the legal process of his situation.
Enter Tony Pollard. Pollard is stuck on a bad Tennessee team but is averaging 4.5 yards per carry and has forced 23 missed tackles, according to PFF. When Jacobs is at his best, he is good at breaking tackles, but the rest of the backfield depth chart appears to go down at first contact. Pollard could be a starter in Jacobs’ place or someone who could capably back him up.
Since he’s not nearly as accomplished as Taylor, Pollard will likely be much less expensive. That could put him in the price range the Packers should be shopping in.
Reports surfaced earlier this week that the Patriots were looking to move defensive lineman Christian Barmore.
“They have listened and talked to other teams about trading him. My understanding is the price would be about a fourth-round pick,” Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer told NBC Sports Boston . “This is a player that very clearly is available, and if somebody’s willing to swing the Patriots a fourth-round pick, I think something could happen.”
If that’s the case, the Packers should be all over a move like that one as they are slated to have a surplus of fourth-round picks. They own their own pick as well as Dallas’ fourth-round pick thanks to an offseason deal of Rashan Gary. Plus, the free-agent departure of Romeo Doubs could net a fourth-round compensatory pick.
That surplus could help the Packers add to a defensive tackle room that is one rolled ankle away from getting very thin.
They could also use some more impact in that room. Devonte Wyatt has not lived up to his billing following last year’s season-ending injury. Chris McClellan has had some nice moments but is a rookie. Karl Brooks has worn down each of the last two seasons and is better suited when he’s in a rotational role.
Javon Hargrave is out for the season, Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and Anthony Campbell is a former undrafted free agent.
Barmore has 3.5 sacks and 10 pressures this season. Last year, he had 50 pressures, according to PFF.
The Packers could use more disruption in the middle of their defensive line, and Barmore fits the bill.
The Patriots are unlikely to move Barmore to Green Bay when they are slated to play each other this weekend, but if the price is truly a fourth-round pick, that is a move the Packers should be all over as soon as Monday.

title: Jordan Love Leads NFL in Passing But That’s Not Number He Cares About
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love enters Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots with the NFL lead in passing yards and is considered among the MVP front-runners. Plus, he is on the verge of throwing his 100th career touchdown pass.
One of those accomplishments means much more than the others.
“I think 100th career touchdown pass – me and Tom were just talking about it – I think that’ll be pretty cool,” Love said after Wednesday’s practice, referencing assistant director of communications Tom Fanning.
“It’s a cool stat but, no, I think my job is to go out there and be the best player, throw for a lot of yards. The main goal is to win the game. However you get that done, you get that done. It’s cool to look at, cool to see some of the things. I’m definitely excited to get that 100th touchdown pass and who’ll it go to. So, that’ll be cool.”
Love will be making his 57th career start against the Patriots. Through 56 starts, here is the franchise leaderboard.
Aaron Rodgers, 115 touchdown passes.
Jordan Love, 99 touchdown passes.
Brett Favre, 95 touchdown passes.
That’s some pretty good company. Favre is a first-ballot Hall of Famer and Rodgers probably will be, too. Both players have more than 500 touchdown passes, with Rodgers ranked third all-time with 540 (and counting) and Favre fifth with 508.
“It’s cool. It’s definitely an honor to know the guys who played before me and to be up there with the stats,” Love said. “It’s one of those things where you just need to keep going. We obviously know the type of career those guys had. They’ve had some long journeys. It’s one of those things I just focus on my job, doing the best I can and take it day by day.”
Love is having the best statistical season of his career. With no running game whatsoever, Love has had to carry the entire offense on his back. That’s why he leads the league in passing yards; he’s third in passing yards per game.
In terms of total yardage, Love is responsible for 82.0 percent of Green Bay’s offensive production. That’s the most in the NFL entering Week 9. Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow (80.9 percent) is the only other quarterback with 80-plus percent.
“I think he’s just doing his job,” quarterbacks coach Luke Getsy said on Monday. “I think he’s gotten so comfortable with what we’re doing and how we’re doing it. He’s in really good command of what we’re asking him to do. It’s more about whatever it takes to win the game. …
“I don’t think it’s been something that’s over the top. It’s about doing whatever you’ve got to do to win the game, and that’s just kind of where we’ve found our niche so far.”
With the Packers at 5-3 despite the worst rushing attack in NFL history , Love ranks eighth in the NFL MVP odds at DraftKings .
“The run game isn’t where it needs to be, but I think we’ve still been able to adjust and still make plays,” Love said. “Like I always talk about, there’s a lot more out there, but we’ve done a great job just being able to win these games by putting up some points, and that’s what it comes down to.
“I think our defense is doing such a great job at holding teams to low points and, really, it’s our job, we always tell them all the time, I’m going to go out there and put up as many points as I can, but I think the goal is always you want to put up 30-plus and put the defense in a safe spot. But I think we’ve been doing some good things in the pass game.”
Back to the NFL’s career leaders for touchdown passes, Tom Brady holds that record with 649 – 78 more than Drew Brees. Brady spent most of his career playing for New England, where the Packers will play this week.
Brady is part of Fox’s No. 1 broadcast team. This week, Brady raved about the play of Love.
“It’s been like, ‘OK, we’re going to put this on your shoulders, and you’re going to have to carry us,’” Brady told Fox’s Colin Cowherd. “And he goes into practice every day knowing it’s about his level of execution that’s going to make the offense go, and he’s just done a great job of that.”
Asked about Brady and what he had to say on Wednesday, Love said:
“It’s definitely cool. I saw the comments he made. It’s awesome. I don’t know Tom too well – we’ve talked here and there – but got a lot of respect for him and obviously the success he had, the career he’s had. Nothing but respect for that guy and definitely looking forward to more conversations down the road.”
Love is on pace for 4,772 passing yards and 34 touchdowns. His career highs are 4,159 yards and 32 touchdowns in 2023. Rodgers holds the franchise record with 4,643 yards in 2011 and 48 touchdowns in 2020.
Love and the Raiders’ Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with multiple touchdown passes in seven games this season, so chances are he’ll throw his 100th to New England.
But to whom? Christian Watson leads the team with six, followed by Matthew Golden with four and Tucker Kraft with three.
Whoever catches it better not throw it into the stands, like James Jones did with Rodgers’ 100th touchdown pass.
https://x.com/89JonesNTAF/status/1976449520906170492
“We’re just talking about that,” Love said. “We’ll definitely have to let them know. You don’t know who’s going to catch it. You don’t know where that ball’s going to go. We’ll definitely make sure the guys don’t throw it in the stands and we get it back. Hope that doesn’t happen.”

title: Packers-Patriots Wednesday Injury Report: Micah Parsons Provides Glowing Update
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers defensive start Micah Parsons was designated for return from the physically unable to perform list on Wednesday and was limited participation in his first practice since mid-December.
“Right now, my knee feels great,” Parsons said . “It feels really great. Before, I could be like, ‘I feel like I’m not getting my power.’ Now, I’m stronger.”
Parsons will be limited to individual drills this week. Most of what he did with his teammates on the practice field is what he’s been doing behind the scenes with trainers.
“When you miss over 300 days and are working over 300 days, pretty much no nerves,” he said. “As I told them guys, I’m excited about next week, when I can actually practice and really see what I’ve got and see where I’m at. I’m excited for that.”
Parsons called his patience “amazing.” He was hoping to get back on the field sooner but had to deal with the ebbs and flows from ACL surgery and meniscus repair.
Together with head trainer Nate Weir, they plotted the course that led to Wednesday's practice.
“It really started when I got here in July” for the start of training camp, Parsons said. “I tested again and they were like, ‘Hey, this is a possibility. We’ll see what happens.’ Here comes Nate. He’s like, ‘Aww, we don’t want it now. This isn’t right.’ So, we’re going to wait again. Then, we’ve got a different date. Then it’s, ‘We still don’t like it.’ Then we test again. It’s kind of like, it was sad in that sense, every time you kind of get your hopes up, we might be here, it was kind of like, ‘Oh, no, we’re not ready yet.’”
That comment lines up with general manager Brian Gutekunst's statement at the end of training camp about Parsons potentially being ready for practice much earlier and Parsons himself saying the Week 6 game against Dallas was an option.
But Parsons and the team took a patient approach, which Parsons appreciated.
“When you’re going through this injury and this time, everyone was like, ‘When, when, when, when, when,’” he said. “Also, as a player, you’re like, ‘Damn, when am I going to be ready? When am I going to feel like I’m normal again.’ In reality, it’s never going to be the perfect time. You’re going to have to battle through what feels like it hurts and pushing through uncomfort and embracing every challenge that comes your way to put yourself in a position where you’re just going to feel OK.
“That’s why I think it’s important to have a great staff around you, like Nate. When I needed a fatherly figure, he was a father. When I needed a friend, he was a friend. When I needed a trainer, he was a trainer. He adapted. He grew. He brought in people, like experts, things like that, to help me and really take me off. That’s kind of what happened.
“When the Wisconsin people came down, it was, ‘You need to focus on this, this, this.’ I just really propelled. I think we all had a learning experience and we all kind of found out what I needed because everyone’s different. I’ve been just taking off from there.”
Four Packers players did not practice, including starting linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle).
Running back Chris Brooks, who was designated for return following his Week 4 ankle injury, was limited participation in his return.
Three starters – left guard Aaron Banks (knee), cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and receiver Christian Watson (rib) – were limited, as well.
Watson, of course, suffered a broken rib and was briefly hospitalized during the win against Carolina, only to return for most of the second half.
“We have a good plan in place,” Watson said. “You know, obviously, there'll be pads and stuff on it, but kind of just what it is. It's one of those things that'll probably be a little bothersome, but can still play.”
Three Patriots starters – defensive tackle Christian Barmore (illness), receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and tight end Hunter Henry (foot) – did not practice. Neither did No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness).
Brown and Henry are top weapons for quarterback Drake Maye, who was full participation with an injured throwing shoulder.
Asked about Brown, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters : “My concern is about trying to prepare for the Packers. That's really my only concern. ... Certainly, the health of the team is critical, but we have to make sure that the guys that are practicing are preparing for Green Bay.”

title: Packers Closer Micah Parsons Returns to Practice, Delivers Perfect Closing Line
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers superstar Micah Parsons practiced for the first time on Wednesday following last year’s torn ACL. The team’s All-Pro pass rusher and closer last season, Parsons will have missed more than half of the season before he makes his season debut.
That’s OK, though, because Parsons – unlike last year – will be on the field for the most important games of the season.
“I came back for the greatest time of football, and that’s November football and December football. Let the show begin,” Parsons, his face covered in sweat, said at the end of a 14-minute conversation with reporters outside the Lambeau Field locker room.
The Packers opened Parsons’ 21-day return-to-play window on Wednesday. That window will close on Nov. 25. That’s Thanksgiving Eve, when the Packers will play the Los Angeles Rams. Before that happens, he’s got to get into football shape and “keep stacking days” alongside Nate Weir, the team’s head athletic trainer who has been a “fatherly figure” alongside Parsons every step of the way.
“I just want it to be a surprise and I just want it to be a fulfilling moment for myself, the staff, and just to enjoy that day and not put too much pressure on that day,” Parsons said. “My family even been asking me, ‘You going to play? Should we buy flights to come out there?’ And I’m telling them, I still got two weeks of practice. Hey, we just got to pay for last minute flights. It is what it is.
“You can buy your flight and cancel last minute, that’s up to you, but I’m not going to pinpoint a day to disappoint anyone or get people expectations that I can’t meet. I got to stack 20 days and, hopefully, on that 21st day, I feel incredible.”
With the question of when Parsons will return to practice answered and when he’ll return to game action perhaps answered, the real question is when Parsons will return to his All-Pro form. With 12.5 sacks in 14 games last season, he became the first player in NFL history with five consecutive seasons of 12-plus sacks to start his career.
That’s the dominant player the Packers acquired last year in hopes of pushing them over the top.
Can that version of Parsons be on the field right away?
Parsons is taking an honest approach.
“I think it’s realistic and I think I’m going to have terrible plays,” he said. “I would say this: When I play, there’s two things that I don’t think anyone in this room or anyone on the team will ever question, and that’s going to be my effort and how I play every snap. I don’t think that my motor is going to change, dictate how I play. If I can’t do my motor, I’ll come off the field and I’ll come right back if I need air. I’m not going to be prideful about that. My conditioning right now is probably the worst it’s been in my career. That’s just the reality of it.”
Parsons averaged 50 snaps per game last season, including two games of 61 snaps. That version of Parsons “absolutely” won’t be on the field, at least to start.
“It’s just not realistic,” he said. “My body’s not there yet. I don’t think my knee’s built for that yet. I didn’t go through training camp. So, am I going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person I once was this year? Probably not until later, after I go through all my phases and things like that, but I think what people will see is they’re going to see, ‘This guy’s ready to play football and he’s going to play hard and he’s going to help boost this defense, which is already doing a great job.’
“I think those type of things you won’t question. I think you’ll see flashes of All-Pro Micah when I get to pass rush, and there’s going to be times when you’re going to be like, ‘Dang, what was Micah doing?’ There’s going to be times when I question myself, too. Like, what was I doing right there? I’m not ashamed of that. I’m not afraid of seeing the failure because I just came back from 11-month injury. So, I’m not shying away from the possibility of my bad plays, but I will look forward to is things that I do do good. And when I do wrong, I’m going to look at it, I’m going to do it right the next time. The best players don’t make the same mistakes twice, so that’s all it is.”
Parsons said his knee feels “great.” And after a long recovery, which was slowed by a “full lateral and medial meniscus repair” that kept him on crutches for seven or eight weeks, he went out on the practice field on Wednesday with “no nerves.”
This week is a ramp-up week. He’s looking forward to next week, when he can “actually practice and … see where I’m at.”
Where Parsons is at is returning to a winning team.
The Packers are 5-3 this season after going 0-5 following Parsons’ injury last season. It’s been a borderline top-10 defense, which is rather astounding .
Now, after missing the closing games of last season, Parsons is ready to be the closer this season.
“Yeah, I think it’s always important that your team gets out to a good start, regardless of what the record is,” he said. “Myself, I don’t really buy into records because you’ve seen teams that lose a lot of games, finish strong, or last year we started strong, finished terrible. It doesn’t really matter about how you start, it’s about how you finish.”
Parsons recalled a conversation he’d just had with rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton.
“As I told DDS now, I said, ‘It’s November time. You’ve got to lock in,’” he said. “He’s like, ‘What’s November time?’ I said, ‘I get it, you’re at Penn State last year, you’re getting ready to think about what bowl game you’re heading to.’
“But I said November gets ready for December, and December tells us who we’re going to be for playoffs. Everyone steps up. You’re going to have all the film out, six, seven games, so it’s going to get harder, it’s going to be more challenging, but we’ve got to be ready to step up. That’s what I’m excited for. I came back for the greatest time of football, and that’s November football and December football. Let the show begin.”

title: Packers Wednesday Update From Practice: Micah Parsons Returns; Here’s What He Did
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Micah Parsons is back.
After weeks of speculation about when he’d return to action for the Green Bay Packers, the All-Pro edge defender made his practice debut on Wednesday.
Parsons missed the first eight games of the season and definitely will not play against the New England Patriots on Sunday. After a home game against the Minnesota Vikings, the hope is he’ll make his season debut at the Los Angeles Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.
Parsons was limited to individual drills on Wednesday. That’ll be the case this week before potentially moving him into 11-on-11 work next week.
Parsons appeared to take as many reps as the rest of the edge players during the media viewing window. That includes working on his get-off, bull rush and run-defending technique. He even caught an interception, though the pick required little effort. Perhaps what was most noteworthy was Parsons even stood in as an offensive player to help his defensive teammates work their techniques.
“I think it’s great,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice. “I think it’s been a long time coming and he’s put a lot of effort and work into this. To get him back out there will be a big boost for our team.”
Parsons wasn’t the only player back on the practice field.
Running back Chris Brooks has been designated for return from the ankle injury sustained in Week 4 against Tampa Bay. After the minimum four-game absence, Brooks is back.
Once Brooks is fully back in the flow, the Packers will have a real full-house backfield with Josh Jacobs, Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson. Johnson has become the obvious odd man out in the backfield the past few weeks and was inactive against Carolina.
Brooks’ niche had been as a third-down pass protector, but he received more opportunities during Jacobs’ absence.
“We’ve been utilizing different guys to try to help in that respect,” running backs coach Ben Sirmans said this week. “Pierre has come in and has filled in a little bit with that role and from a protection standpoint, understanding who he has as well as you saw some of the success that he’s had at times on checkdowns, turning 5-yard checkdowns into first downs. So, he’s filled in that role for us a little bit and everybody has.”
With the Packers coming off an extended break after beating Carolina on Thursday, four players did not practice:
Linebacker Zaire Franklin “is making a lot of progress,” LaFleur said, but he did not practice due to the shin injury sustained at practice before the game against Detroit. Franklin missed the last two games.
“Hopeful sooner than later,” LaFleur said.
Center Sean Rhyan remains sidelined by the high-ankle sprain sustained during the opening series at Detroit. John Williams started the last two games.
Right guard Travis Glover remains sidelined by the knee injury that he played through against Detroit. Laken Tomlinson started against Carolina.
Tight end Josh Whyle suffered a concussion against Carolina.
The Packers probably feel good about being 5-3 without their superstar defender. In fact, their defense is just about the same without Parsons this season as it was last season.
“He’s a generational talent,” LaFleur said. “He definitely flips the favor of the field into your court in regards to his ability to win his one on ones and I think like we saw a year ago, the thing that impressed me most about him was his impact in the run game as well. So he’s a dominant force.”
The Packers are 12th in the league in sack percentage without Parsons even though they have no players in the top 15 in sacks and only one in the top 44. With defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon taking a committee approach to rushing the passer, they have league highs of 11 players with at least one sack and 13 players with at least a half-sack.
“I think the guys up front have been doing a nice job, and I think JG’s been aggressive at times and has put some of our guys in some pretty good matchups or getting free runners,” LaFleur said. “So, I would say it’s a combination of everything, just the scheme and then our guys being able to go out there and win.”
While Parsons is being eased into things with individual drills this week and perhaps team drills next week, he’s not being eased into things from a tempo perspective. Parsons is cleared, so it’s go time.
This will be a big stretch for him to gain additional confidence in the knee.
“I think you trust it by the work you put in during the 9- to 10-month extensive process that you have,” Parsons said during training camp.
Parsons missed the stretch run to last season, with his injury being the pivotal moment that turned a 9-3-1 start into a five-game losing streak. Now, Parsons – who had been the team’s closer in games last season – will be back for the closing stretch of games.
“I think it’s a reason why I got brought here, right? I got brought here to win big-time games and close games and do what I do when there’s a lead,” he said during camp. “I feel fully confident if Jordan Love gives me 21 points, I can get to the quarterback because he has to hold the ball. That’s where my biggest impact on the game can come into place. But in a position I am now, that’s why it’s in my power and my ability to help these guys understand finishing and understand that you got to hold this standard of what it means to finish.”
