title: With Micah Parsons Returning to Practice, Today Could Change Everything for Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers didn’t exactly thrive without Micah Parsons but they certainly survived with their 5-3 record.
Parsons is expected to practice for the first time on Wednesday following last year’s torn ACL. He won’t play on Sunday against the Patriots and probably won’t play the following week against the Vikings, but he’ll be available for the stretch run.
Acknowledging that “everything around here (is) pretty fluid,” coach Matt LaFleur said: “If I had a bet on it, it’s going to be more towards the longer end than the shorter end.”
Only time will tell if Parsons will be Peak Parsons upon his return, but he will provide a jolt to a defense that defied expectations during the first half of the season.
Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said he thinks “every day” about how he will incorporate Parsons.
His unit has been surprisingly good without him. The Packers emerged from Week 8 ranked 10th with 20.5 points allowed per game, a number skewed by the Week 1 avalanche at Minnesota stemming from the offense’s late-game implosion, and the one bad game at Atlanta in Week 3.
They are 10th in total defense (314.9 yards allowed per game), 13th in yards allowed per rushing play (3.89) and third in yards allowed per passing play (5.75). They are second with 15 takeaways – they had 14 all of last season – and 12th in sack percentage.
The sack production – and the impact it’s had on the pass defense in general – is the shocker. They are tied for sixth with 22 sacks even without a single player in the top 15 in sacks and only one (Lukas Van Ness) in the top 44.
For the Packers, it’s been a strength-in-numbers approach. With Gannon deploying his rushers from here, there and everywhere, they have an NFL-high 11 players with at least one full sack.
“Wins and losses are the only stat I’m worried about,” Gannon said, “but, yeah, I think our guys have done a good job of taking the coaching and affecting the game in a positive way, executing the game plan as much as we can and we got some guys winning at a pretty good rate of one-on-ones right now. It’s about the players.”
That’s good deflection from Gannon. Statistically, his defense has been slightly better without Parsons than it was with Parsons under Jeff Hafley. Last year, the Packers finished 11th in points allowed (21.2) and 12th in total defense (311.8 yards per game). Even with Parsons having an All-Pro season, they wound up 22nd in sack percentage and tied for 26th in takeaways.
After Thursday’s victory over Carolina, Packers coach Matt LaFleur called Gannon a “savant.”
“I wouldn’t use that word because I’m not,” Gannon said on Tuesday.
But the proof is in the pudding. Without Parsons, who is his best player, and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper, who is his second-best player, the Packers are on a five-game streak of not allowing more than 20 points.
The defense is in the top 10 in numerous categories. One of them is “havoc plays,” a TruMedia stat that combines sacks, tackles or losses, forced fumbles, interception and pass breakups. Green Bay is second with 107. It’s ninth in explosive plays allowed (12-yard runs and 16-yard passes), first in stuffs (a running play that gains 0 yards or less) and fourth in opponent passer rating.
“When we went through Phase 1, Phase 2, then we went from OTAs and then we took the summer off, kind of adapted,” Gannon said. “‘Here’s some things we want to add.’ Then we went through training camp and added a few things, took out a few things that I always thought, ‘Oh this is going to be good,’ and our guys, for whatever reason, it wasn’t really good for us. (So), take it out.
“Then I think week to week, they’ve done a good job of executing staples that we have and then taking a couple different things, the different wrinkles – the wrinkles are only in because of the opponent you’re going against or who you have available – they’ve done a good job of taking the wrinkles, curveballs so to speak, and executing on that. And they understand the why behind why we’re doing it and those typically change week-to-week.”
To one of the NFL’s surprisingly strong defenses, the Packers will be adding one of its most dominating defenders. He is the only player in NFL history to start his career with five consecutive seasons of 12-plus sacks. That streak presumably will end this year. If he returns for Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams, he’d have seven games.
Still, while offensive coordinators and quarterbacks are losing sleep over who Gannon is blitzing from where, they probably aren’t especially fearful of Lukas Van Ness, who leads the team with 4.5 sacks. The entire edge group has 9.5 sacks; Parsons had 10.5 sacks in a seven-game span last year.
There’s also a bit of an elephant in the room. Of the top-10 teams in scoring, the Packers have played four. The Lions, who are third in the NFL in scoring, scored only 20 points, though they had more than 400 yards and two freakish turnovers. The Bears are eighth in scoring but played a backup quarterback. The Panthers are ninth in scoring but played without three-fifths of their starting line.
The one game in which there’s no asterisk was against Dallas. The Cowboys are seventh in scoring but managed only 13 points.
More challenges are coming. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye almost won NFL MVP last year. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford did win MVP last year. Bills quarterback Josh Allen is the MVP front-runner this year. There are rematches looming against the Bears and Lions.
The Packers have survived without Parsons. Now, they’ve got a chance to thrive with a difference-making player who has the potential of making a greater impact than any player available at the trade deadline.
The Packers were 9-3-1 last season headed into the Denver game during which he was injured. Without him for the stretch run, the Packers crumbled.
This year, Parsons will be on the field for the stretch run with the goal of making opponents pay for his pain.
“I think when you come out of these situations, you’re either going to be better or you’re worse,” Parsons said during training camp. “And for me, I’ve done everything I possibly can to be better. So, I think people are worried about if I come back. You know, I just feel like people should just be worried about how I’m going to be when I come back. You know? That’s kind of like my mentality – how I feel, and how I’m going to approach when I’m back.
“Like, people are worried about the knee. They should be worried about how I’m going to play when I get back. The anger, the frustration, the things that I’m going to have to let out because of how long it’s been since I played. So, I think that’s what people should really worry about. Like, how great is Micah going to be when he gets back? Not about when I get back, because that’s the short term. It’s about how great I’m going to be, how I can help my teammates, and how far we’re going to go into a playoff run.”

title: New Packers Safety John Saunders Jr., Who Has NFL Cousin, Had to Learn How to Practice
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Among a wave of moves on the practice squad, the Green Bay Packers signed promising safety John Saunders Jr.
Saunders is the cousin of Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker – more on that later. He played three seasons at Miami (Ohio) before closing his college career at Ole Miss in 2023 and 2024. He had three interceptions in both seasons, giving him 11 for his college career, and led the SEC with four forced fumbles in 2024.
“He’s amazing. He knows all 11 positions on defense,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said . “He could coach me and a second later he is coaching a defensive tackle. He is so versatile and knows where everyone is supposed to be. He coaches my technique a lot and pushes me to become a better player every day.”
Despite a strong combination of size (6-foot-2 3/8) and athleticism (4.57 in the 40), Saunders went undrafted in 2025. He signed with the Dolphins, failed to make their roster during training camp and spent the first two months of the season on their practice squad before being poached by the Patriots. In three games on their roster, he did not play in a game. He was released and spent the rest of last season on their practice squad.
This year, he competed with the Patriots during training camp but didn’t earn a roster spot despite a big-time preseason of 13 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and two passes defensed.
Saunders also led the team in interceptions on the practice field.
“He’s been balling out of control. He’s a ballhawk,” safety Kevin Byard said at the time.
After his release from the Patriots, he served practice-squad stints with the Jets and Browns, meaning the Packers will be his fourth team this year.
When Saunders joined the Patriots’ practice squad last season, he wasn’t practicing to coach Mike Vrable’s standard.
“John showed up, and we just asked him to practice a little better and use practice," Vrabel said during training camp . “We talked about those days where we're letting the show team go and letting them try to really improve throughout the season. When John was back, we just said, ‘Hey, you have to practice better. You have to have better practice habits. That's the only place you're going to get your reps.’
“And it got to the point where we had to dial him back where he was blitzing or tackling, and I was like, ‘This is great.’ And I think he used those examples in practice to improve, and mentally he's kept working, and it's been great to see him show up and get into that competition.”
So, Saunders started practicing harder. Too hard, as it turns out, so he had to dial it back.
“In practice, it’s about taking care of the team. So that’s something I really had to learn, like practicing like a pro,” he said.
To create a spot on the practice squad, the Packers released safety Kahlef Hailassie.
Saunders was among three additions to the practice squad who will be on the field on Wednesday.
With quarterback Kedon Slovis signing to the Ravens’ 53-man roster, the Packers signed Cam Miller , who was drafted by the Raiders in 2025 and got this incredible endorsement from possibly the greatest quarterback of all-time.
The Packers also signed D.J. Johnson , third-round pick by Carolina in 2023. While he played on both sides of the ball at Oregon, he will work on the edge for Green Bay.
Saunders can turn to a veteran NFL starter for advice. Jaquan Brisker spent his first four seasons with the Bears before signing with the Steelers in free agency. He’s started all eight games this season.
“It’s been amazing, honestly. Growing up, he was from the east side of Pittsburgh and I moved to North Carolina, so we didn’t really talk that much,” Saunders told On3’s Andy Staples in 2023. “But then once we got back in contact, it’s just been amazing man. Like, I just talked to him yesterday. He’s just telling me to just make sure to stay focused.
“When I first got to college, one of the things he told me was to listen to the coaches. And most players in college think they know it all. But I’ve been making sure that everywhere I go — because the coaches are extremely knowledgeable. They know their stuff. That was one of the main things he told me and that just stuck with me ever since. It sounds so simple to just listen to your coaches, but when you actually do it and apply what your coaches are telling you — it’s been great. I’m really appreciative of him, too.”
Saunders was impressed by the Patriots’ Super Bowl pedigree. So, this quote probably holds up now that he’s joined by the Packers.
“The main thing I remember is when you walk in the player entrance, you’ve got all the Super Bowls right there,” Saunders said. “Then, outside the doors, all the Super Bowl titles. This is football tradition. Serious, rich tradition. Winners. This is the winningest team since I’ve been born. Being a part of this is a blessing. Just excited to help continue this legacy.”

title: Texans Injury Report: Who's Trending Up, Down for Week 9 vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Houston Texans have released their second of three injury reports for the week heading into their upcoming matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers –– meaning we have a bit more intel around who might be trending to play in Week 9, along with who could be stuck on the sidelines.
Here's a look at the latest on the injury front for the Texans ahead of their next matchup facing the Chargers in Week 9:
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot) OT Braden Smith (ankle) OT Blake Fisher (thumb)
S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) RB David Montgomery (groin)
Two key starting pieces on the Texans' defense appear to be good to go heading into the weekend: that's Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and star nickel Jalen Pitre.
Al-Shaair has been working his way back from a lingering groin injury that kept him out for Week 4's game against the Dallas Cowboys. Now, after continuing to get back to 100% from said groin issue, it seems like he's all set to play on Sunday.
As for Pitre, his return to the lineup is due for a bit more attention. Pitre has been sidelined for the Texans since suffering an AC joint sprain in his shoulder against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5.
That injury inevitably led to Pitre missing Weeks 6 and 7, where the Texans managed to go 1-1, but did face some ups and downs in the secondary.
Now that Pitre is preparing to fill back into his rightful spot as Houston's starting nickel, his presence certainly adds another layer of versatility for this talented defense that's been struggling as of late.
Head coach DeMeco Ryans made it clear on Wednesday that David Montgomery will be missing his third-straight game this weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers. And on Thursday, he logged his second DNP of the week .
Expect to see Woody Marks as the bellcow back in the Texans' run game, perhaps with some Dare Ogunbowale and newly-signed Emari Demercado sprinkled in alongside him.
Through the past three games that Marks has claimed the Texans' lead back role, he's averaged over 16 rushing attempts per game for 3.8 yards per carry, while remaining on the offensive side of the ball for over 83% of the total snaps.
Another starter who's been missing time for the Texans–– but on the defensive side of the ball–– is safety Reed Blankenship, who's missed his fifth-straight practice as a DNP, and is trending towards being out against Los Angeles for Week 9 .
If Blankenship was just dealing with concussion protocol, there's a chance that if he is able to practice in limited capacity on Friday and clear protocol within 24 hours. But Blankenship is also dealing with a hand issue that might be making his return to play more complicated.
As to who you should expect to fill the Texans' safety spot opposite of Calen Bullock, it'll most likely be veteran M.J. Stewart, who filled that role in Week 7 against the New York Giants. Stewart led the Texans' defense in total tackles that game with 12.

title: Texans Need to Trade for RB After David Montgomery Injury Update
full_text:
The Houston Texans will be without veteran running back David Montgomery for at least one more game –– per head coach DeMeco Ryans.
According to Ryans after the Texans' first practice of the week before facing the LA Chargers, Montgomery has already been ruled out for this weekend as he continues to rehab from his lingering groin injury he's been working back from since Week 5 .
DeMeco Ryans said RB David Montgomery has made some progress but added that he'll be out on Sunday vs. the Chargers.
Montgomery will continue to be listed as week-to-week, but there's still no exact date to circle just yet for when the Texans' lead running back will return to the lineup.
And with that mysterious timeline in mind, perhaps there's a case to be made for the Texans to go out and trade for another running back before the NFL trade deadline arrives early next week.
Now, it wasn't too long ago when the Texans made their initial trade to bring Montgomery into the building in the first place.
Houston sent multiple day three draft picks and Juice Scruggs to the Detroit Lions earlier this offseason to add Montgomery as a one-two punch for Woody Marks, and hope to elevate this lackluster rushing attack for their 2026 campaign.
But as we now arrive to the halfway point of the Texans' 2026 season, those improvements in the run game haven't quite come to fruition as expected.
While C.J. Stroud has helped lead the way in the passing game for positive strides, Houston ranks 29th in the NFL for total rushing yards (593) and yards per attempt (3.6) through their first seven games.
When Montgomery has been on the field for the Texans, he's been largely inefficient and ineffective . He's averaging just 2.7 yards per carry and less than 30 yards on the ground per game.
Marks has managed to be a bright spot in the Texans' ground game. But otherwise, the rushing production could certainly use a facelift heading into the second half of the season, as well as a healthy counterpart for Marks to lean on if Montgomery is sidelined longer than expected.
The Texans have a couple of different approaches to take here when it comes to improving their running back room at the deadline.
On one hand, Houston could take a massive swing at the position to push the chips in for this season. But that might not be a super realistic result to expect.
Jonathan Taylor might be too hard to pry away from the Texans' AFC South rivals, the Indianapolis Colts, and the Philadelphia Eagles have already made it clear to Saquon Barkley that he won't be traded at the deadline .
Or, the Texans can take a different approach: add a depth piece at a lower cost who can work alongside Marks, and Montgomery whenever he's back to 100%.
That route seems like a much more favorable bet to see the Texans consider. As to which running backs fall into that bucket? Guys like TreVeyon Henderson, Devin Singletary and Tony Pollard have all seen their names in some lingering trade rumors in the past several days, and could give Houston some targets to keep an eye on.
However, at the very least, running back should be a position of need on the Texans' radar from now up until next week's trade deadline.
This is one of the final moments of the season in which the front office can go out to add an immediate upgrade to their roster before taking on the second half of their schedule (and the postseason), and being without a stable ground game will only hurt the Texans' offense long-term.
Adding one more reliable ball carrier into the room could add some much-needed security and stability on the ground, while also providing a backup plan in case Montgomery is at all limited after recovering from his lengthy groin injury absence.

title: Why Texans' Week 9 Game vs. Chargers Matters More Than You Think
full_text:
The Houston Texans are just days away from their Week 9 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers –– a game that sets up as a pivotal one as this team sits at a 2-5 record through their first seven games.
But the Texans' game against the Chargers might be more than just pivotal.
A win, of course, would be a nice lift for Houston's chances at a late-season turnaround at a 3-5 record. And with a few more winnable matchups up ahead on their schedule, the tide can turn pretty quickly for this team as it did around this time last season.
However, a loss against the Chargers that puts the Texans to just 2-6 might hold even more gravity moving forward. Especially with the NFL trade deadline right around the corner , a loss here in Week 9 might be what pushes Houston over the edge to sell off some assets on a potentially lost season.
If the Texans were to drop to a 2-6 record on the year, they'd be up against a pretty uphill climb to make the postseason, especially when looking back at just how many times it's been done across NFL history.
Only three teams in the history of the league have climbed out of a 2-6 hole for a spot in the playoffs: the 1970 Cincinnati Bengals, the 2020 Washington Football Team, and the 2022 Jacksonville Jaguars.
Simply put, it's not easy for a team to pull off seven or more wins in the second half of the season after facing some immense struggles early in the year. The Texans did manage to do similar last year as they came back from 0-3, then 3-5, but a loss here against the Chargers would feel a little bit different.
The Chargers, at many times over the past several weeks, have looked like the worst team in football this season.
Los Angeles has had the lowest scoring offense in the NFL through eight weeks, is the 20th-best scoring defense, and has given up the most turnovers in the league.
If the Texans were to lose back-to-back games against the New York Giants , then the winless Chargers––especially knowing that Houston is coming fresh off a bye––it'd be pretty tough to have optimism that this team is capable of making the climb to the postseason, let alone make a deep run with multiple playoff wins.
So then, the Texans could turn their attention to some trade deadline moves; and moves with a mindset to sell off some of their talent on the roster, rather than be buyers.
Perhaps Jadeveon Clowney can get shipped off to a contender . Maybe a receiver gets dealt. Wyatt Teller and Braden Smith could be on their way out. And then, the tone of Houston's remaining season changes for the worst.
That's what makes this weekend's game so important against the Chargers. A win sets up for a much-needed bounce back after the bye, and puts Houston at the same record they sat at this time last year.
A loss, though, might just be the first domino to fall for what could inevitably be a lost season in Houston.

title: 3 Players Texans Should Call About Before the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are less than a week away from the NFL trade deadline.
And when taking a step back to look at where this team stands heading into Week 9 with their 2-5 record, it's hard to tell whether or not the Texans will be true buyers or sellers over the course of the next few days.
However, the Texans and their front office are still bound to do their due diligence by calling around the league and asking about the availability of a select few players in a potential deal––if the price is right.
With that in mind, let's sort through three players who could be deemed trade candidates at the deadline that the Texans should call about in the days ahead:
The Texans' run game has been–– to put things bluntly–– lackluster through the first half of their 2026 campaign. And heading into Week 9 against the LA Chargers, Houston will be without their offseason trade addition David Montgomery for a third-straight game due to a lingering groin injury .
That's left this Texans' run game lacking in both production and overall depth. So there's a good case to be made that Houston could go out and add a low-cost veteran to their backfield at the deadline to iron out some of those concerns.
So why not try to spark a reunion with a former Texan in Devin Singletary? While he projects to have a bigger role in New York with Tyrone Tracy being placed on injured reserve, it wouldn't hurt for Houston to at least give the Giants a call on the eight-year veteran.
Singletary brings in another layer of depth in the backfield, has proven to be productive in multiple situations throughout his career, and even had one of his most impressive seasons back in 2023 with the Texans, logging over 1,000 scrimmage yards and four touchdowns.
For a day three pick (or a couple), maybe the Texans could strike a deal with the Giants in hopes that Singletary can complement this backfield led by Woody Marks, and hopefully Montgomery in the next couple of weeks.
This would certainly be the biggest swing the Texans could take on this list, but adding Eagles offensive lineman Landon Dickerson might not be out of the realm of imagination.
The Eagles are 2-6 and could be due to hit the trade market as sellers at the trade deadline. Someone like Dickerson could be a premier piece on their roster who can generate a good bit of value if the front office were to ship him out.
And the Texans could have a perfect spot for Dickerson up front as their starting left guard . Dickerson would allow Keylan Rutledge to slide over at center, paired with Ed Ingram at right guard, and forge together a really solid three-man unit on the interior.
Dickerson hasn't played extremely well this season. He's logged a 54.5 overall grade on the season via Pro Football Focus , and ranks in the bottom five of eligible guards for his pass-blocking grade (36.2).
However, that allows the Texans to potentially buy low on his value and hope that a new situation in Houston can spark production from earlier in his career. Maybe a fourth-round pick and another day-three pick could pique the Eagles' interest.
It also helps knowing that Dickerson has just one penalty called against him so far this season. Limiting those flags on the offensive line will be key for the Texans' offensive success moving into the second half of the season, and Dickerson could be an easy plug-and-play guard to do just that.
The Texans' secondary has really struggled this season compared to how elite they looked over the course of their 2026 campaign.
Houston currently ranks 28th in the NFL for total passing yards allowed (1,708), and 20th for net yards gained per pass (6.4) through their first eight games of the season.
And those struggles have really shown in games that Jalen Pitre has been on the sidelines, which has been the case for the Texans' last two games.
This week against the Chargers, Pitre is expected to make his return after he was able to practice on Wednesday. That's good news for the Texans and their hopes of turning things around in the secondary. But that shouldn't stop Houston from adding more depth at the nickel position if the price is right.
One name that could make sense for the Texans is Taron Johnson of the Las Vegas Raiders, who's in his age-30 season under contract for this year and next, and has been relatively productive between his time with both the Raiders and the Buffalo Bills.
Could the Texans part ways with a mid-round pick for Johnson? Maybe the Raiders want to hang onto their starting nickel, knowing that they could be within reach of a Wild Card spot this season.
But in the event Las Vegas wants to sell off an aging veteran for a Houston team that's desperate for a lift in their secondary, this is a move that could add up for both sides.

title: Texans' Latest David Montgomery Injury Update Should Raise Concerns
full_text:
The Houston Texans have been a bit depleted in their running back room because of their recent injury to veteran David Montgomery, who's been sidelined with a groin injury dating back to the first half of their Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans .
Since Montgomery first went down, the Texans had labeled his status as "week-to-week," expecting to be an issue that could resolve itself after the bye, but wasn't anything that required the veteran running back to be placed on injured reserve.
However, now nearly a month removed from the injury to Montgomery, it seems like Houston still won't be getting him back in the lineup ahead of their Week 9 game vs. the LA Chargers .
According to Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans, the Texans will be without Montgomery for another week against the Chargers because of his lingering groin injury, but adds that the running back has made "some progress" in his recovery.
"David is still sidelined. He'll be out still," Ryans said on Wednesday. "We're trying to get him out on the field; trying to get him going. But right now, it's still week-to-week. But he has made some progress."
That's not exactly the most optimistically sounding update for the Texans' starting running back–– especially coming so early in the week.
Rather than the Texans attempting to give Montgomery a few attempts to go in practice over the course of this week before facing the Chargers, Houston has prematurely ruled him out multiple days before the weekend even arrives.
That means Montgomery will be missing over a month and at least three games while still recovering from said injury, and still might not be officially ready by the time the Texans are ready to take on the Cleveland Browns in Week 10.
In reality, Montgomery seems to have a real chance of missing four games on the Texans' schedule (on top of the extra time he was able to get during the bye last week). That's the stint of any player taken out of the lineup to then be placed on short-term injured reserve; an approach that Montgomery and Houston did not take.
So what's really going on with Montgomery here? In reality, we might not have a clear picture until arriving at next week's practice. If he's able to participate in any capacity then, that'll be a good sign for his in-game availability next weekend.
But until then, it'll be Woody Marks continuing to take the lead as the Texans' No. 1 running back against the Chargers, which is a role he's started to find his grove in quite well.
Over the course of the past three games, the Texans have given Marks at least 19 touches a game to average over 80 yards from scrimmage throughout those matchups.
Expect Houston to continue leaning on Marks in the backfield until further notice while still patiently waiting for his veteran counterpart to return from injury.

title: How DeMeco Ryans Plans to Fix Texans' Excessive Penalty Issues
full_text:
The Houston Texans are coming out of their bye week with a glaring hole in their game plan to fix: the sheer amount of penalties called against them .
Houston currently ranks top five in the NFL for average penalties per game, are one of 10 teams to have given up over 500 total yards due to penalties, and are one of eight teams with 70 or more total flags called against them.
Those penalty issues are far from a winning recipe. It's a considerable reason as to why Houston has fallen three games under .500 heading into Week 9, and sets up as a weakness that DeMeco Ryans and the Texans staff have to address for the second half of the year if they want to turn things around.
And with a week of time off thanks to the Texans' Week 8 bye , Ryans has come back with a mindset wired to fix those penalty issues this team has fallen into one too many times this season.
For Ryan’s, the blame for the Texans' penalty issues falls on the shoulders of both the coaching staff and the players. So heading into this weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers, improving those shortcomings will be a clear focus throughout practice.
"For penalties, we all have to clean it up from a coaching perspective, a player perspective, and we'll emphasize that more in practice and see how it translates to the game," Ryans said on Monday.
One aspect of the Texans excessive penalties that Ryans highlighted as a key point of emphasis is their offensive holding calls–– which have been a problem, to say the least.
Houston currently ranks third-most offensive holding calls per game against them heading into Week 7, and are one of five teams in the NFL to lose over 20 yards per game because of those holds.
That's something that Ryans wants everyone on the Texans' offensive front to get right. And if those penalties are able to be limited in the weeks ahead––especially when it comes to holding––it'll pay major dividends for Houston as a result.
"For all of us with the penalties, specifically holding penalties, we've got to know when to let go on the edges," Ryans said on Monday. "That's been called a lot more this year, and we've got to know when to let go. Understanding that's a point of emphasis for our officials. So we've got to do a better job playing cleaner."
"Some of our biggest runs–– not only [Aireontae Ersery], but our tight ends and guys on the edge specifically–– have been called back because of the holding penalties. And that leads to the questions on the running game. We've had 20-plus yard gains. It's just been, you know, nullified by penalties."
"So, can we clean that up? Can we play smarter knowing when to let up on the edge? And I think that'll definitely help our numbers in the run game."
We'll see if that plan of attack ends up coming together against the Chargers come Sunday in Los Angeles; a team that's also struggled when limiting their flags on both sides of the ball.
The Chargers currently sit as one of seven teams in the NFL to average over eight penalties called against them per game, and rank top eight in the league for average pre-snap penalties per game. So if the Texans can clean things up on their end, this can be a matchup they can take advantage of.

title: What We're Hearing About the Texans Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are now less than a week away from the NFL trade deadline .
And compared to the rest of the league and their potential activity around this time of year, the Texans aren't being viewed as the most active on the trade market. They already made one big mid-season move earlier this year by trading for Marvin Harrison Jr., and are still looking to see how that investment pays off.
However, that doesn't mean the Texans shouldn't be expected to make a move or two in the coming days.
There are a select few situations for players either in Houston or around the league that make sense to consider a potential trade on, and if the right deal comes across the table of Nick Caserio, perhaps we could see this front office pull the trigger.
With that in mind, let's sort through a bit about what we're hearing around the Texans and their trade deadline plans, along with who around the roster could be viewed as a potential mover in the near future:
Now, it might not come as a major surprise to hear that there haven't been any rumblings around a major move being in store for the Texans . But Houston's current situation doesn't exactly put them in a bucket of being a true buyer or a seller.
The Texans are three games under .500 heading into Week 9 without a second, fifth, or sixth-round pick in this year's draft. Trading away another one of those picks for this offseason could be seen as a little too short-sighted, or even reckless to a degree.
But a selling move doesn't make a whole lot of sense either. The Texans entered this year with expectations of being one of the top teams in the AFC, and while their record might not show that right now, Houston has proven to be more than capable of a late-season turnaround, as recently as 2025.
So while the Texans could still be prone to one or two moves around the edges of the roster, a big-time swing doesn't seem to be in the cards.
A name from the Texans who did pop up in some lingering trade rumors this past weekend was one of their more recent signings heading into the season: veteran edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney, who reportedly had interest building around the league from those looking to acquire help on their defensive line.
And perhaps if the Texans get an intriguing enough offer on Clowney and his expiring contract, maybe that's a move to keep in consideration. But it seems as if Clowney's entry into trade rumors is stemming more from external interest in his services rather than Houston's own desire to pivot off of him.
Clowney still fills a key role on the Texans' defensive line as a rotational edge rusher behind Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson, and the defense doesn't have any direct replacements to turn to in the event that Clowney is shipped out.
So at the very least, keep this trade idea on the radar. But don't get your hopes up that anything will come of it.
This is more of a speculative gauge on the Texans' current roster. Not much buzz has come out around the front office's intentions over the next few days, and who around this current group could potentially be on the move.
But one area of the Texans' roster to keep watch for a potential surprise shakeup is the offensive line . It's a group that has improved a bit this season from their turbulent state of the past few years, but the position group has a couple of bigger-name veterans not getting the playing time you would've expected coming into the year.
Former Pro Bowler Wyatt Teller has been stuck as a reserve on the interior for all but two games this season, and veteran Braden Smith has also been stuck on the bench after starting the new season off on injured reserve.
Both names were viewed as plug-and-play starters for the Texans heading into the season, but now have seen their stock take a turn for the worst as Keylan Rutledge and Trent Brown have been the ones winning the starting gig in their respective positions.
Maybe, if the Texans are able to find another offensive-line-needy team over the coming days, they could strike on some minimal draft value to send off both Teller and Smith. Doing so could replenish Houston's lack of capital in 2027, while also giving both veterans a chance to compete for a starting spot elsewhere.

title: Texans Cost Themselves Millions by Delaying C.J. Stroud Extension
full_text:
Throughout the most recent NFL offseason, the Houston Texans had been stuck in contract negotiations with their quarterback, C.J. Stroud for several months.
After an up-and-down first three years, Stroud was eligible for a new deal after the 2025 season to make him the Texans' starting signal-caller for the foreseeable future. He had been fresh off a third-straight playoff appearance and Wild Card win for the franchise, but also paired that with a four-interception performance in Houston's divisional loss vs. the New England Patriots.
Houston's lead decision-makers had publicly backed Stroud over the course of the offseason, but finding terms to that extension proved to be a task much easier said than done. Both sides had different visions for what Stroud's value should be worth.
Eventually, Week 1 arrived, and the decision was made that Stroud would not sign a new deal with the Texans and enter the 2026 season with just two years remaining on his current rookie contract.
It was effectively a decision that sent a message from both sides. Stroud was essentially betting on himself and his chances at netting a better contract offer after the 2026 season was over. The Texans felt as if they could hold off on that deal and be well off.
However, now eight weeks into the 2026 season, and it seems like there's a clear winner within this ongoing saga. And that's especially so based on some new intel stemming from ESPN 's D.J Bien-Aime and Jeremy Fowler .
According to ESPN , the Texans had made an initial offer for Stroud to be paid "well within the $50 million-per-year club," which was an effort that was then matched with a counteroffer from Stroud's representation.
The Texans felt as if that counteroffer wasn't worthy enough to be accepted. And as a result, Stroud and his camp were ready and willing to hold off on the extension until next offseason, and bet on himself in hopes that his value can jump in the meantime.
"Before camp, Houston made an initial offer to Stroud that reached what sources called a 'respectable' range -- not at the top of the quarterback market but well within the $50 million-per-year club that 13 quarterbacks now occupy," Bien-Aime and Fowler wrote.
"Stroud and his agent, David Mulugheta, made a counteroffer... But despite the back-and-forth, a deal was not imminent. Meanwhile, Stroud had made clear he was comfortable playing without a new deal, per sources. 'Unless there's a better offer, we're good,' is how one source recalled the messaging from Stroud."
In hindsight, that decision from the Texans to hold off on paying Stroud a new deal might now be costing them in the form of millions of dollars––which becomes even more costly knowing how much money Houston paid out to the defensive side of the ball earlier this offseason.
Houston's gone from offering Stroud a deal "well into the $50 million range," declining a counter that was presumably a slightly higher offer, and are now forced into paying an even higher offer than that first counter come next offseason when negotiations are back at the table.
Executives around the league are well aware of Stroud's jump in value, with one in the AFC outlining a scenario where the Texans might be due to make their quarterback the highest-paid in the NFL.
"He's making himself a lot of money,' an AFC executive said, via ESPN . 'New tax bracket. If he keeps playing like this and they somehow get in the playoffs and make a run, there's no reason why he can't be somewhere close to the highest paid."
Now, if Stroud were to help command a turnaround in the AFC, get the Texans into the playoffs for the fourth straight season, and help lead a deep run into the postseason, that's all a positive for Houston. After all, putting together a team that can make those victories deep in the postseason possible is the end goal for any front office.
But there's no question that if Stroud is able to continue on the strong run he's put together so far this season, the Texans' decision to hold off on an extension for their starting quarterback will be an extremely expensive one.
And if the Texans do wind up being forced to pay Stroud as one of the highest-paid quarterbacks in the NFL, they'll be due to pay for it in the form of making some big sacrifices around a talented roster.

title: What the Texans Can Realistically Afford at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are just a week away from the NFL trade deadline.
And for a team that sits with a record of 2-5 , it's pretty noteworthy knowing that there's a world where the Texans could approach this deadline with the mindset of being buyers on the market.
While the first half of the season hasn't gone the way anyone in Houston would've anticipated, this roster still has a ton of talent to bank on for their second half stretch. And if the Texans are able to pull out a win in Week 9 to sit just two games back from .500, there's a case to be made for this team to take a swing on the trade market, if the right opportunity presents itself.
But what might the Texans have the ability to spend on if they wanted to go and make a trade at the deadline? Houston only has a finite number of resources in terms of draft picks and cap space for a potential deal, and thus holds back just how aggressive they'll be able to be.
However, knowing that, let's break down just what those limitations look like for the Texans, and how it might affect any trade deadline plans they may have over the coming days:
1st (own) 3rd (own) 4th (own) 3 7ths (ARI, PHI, SF)
When it comes to draft capital, the Texans do have a good bit of flexibility to work with beyond the 2027 draft. Through both 2028 and 2029, Houston will be without only one of their own draft picks, that being their 2028 sixth-round pick.
But Houston will be without a decent amount of wiggle room for how many picks they can pivot off of in this year's draft. Houston has only three of their own selections between the first, third, and fourth round, then has three sevenths from others around the league.
Perhaps the Texans will make a minor "selling" move on their roster to replenish some of that day three capital that's been lost from previous trades. But if not, it's hard to imagine Houston gutting their share of picks in this year's draft any further than its current setup.
The Texans don't have a ton of flexibility in terms of cap space, as they have just under $10 million in free money to spend on other acquisitions.
However, that number does put them right in the middle of the league in terms of available cap space. Houston is ranked 15th in the NFL when it comes to cap space, and might be able to provide some room to bring in a short-term, smaller contract rather than a big splash from a high-cost veteran.
Another factor to keep an eye on as it relates to the Texans' future cost of the roster is that they are ranked with the second-lowest available cap space for 2027 with -$41.5 million on the books. That's even further reason for Houston not to go out and be crazy spenders at the deadline.
So when taking a step back to look at the Texans' situation and the amount of assets they have on hand, it's pretty clear to recognize that a big splash deadline move probably isn't in the cards for this team.
Unless the Texans found a player on an affordable contract that they'd be willing to move off of multiple first-round picks for––which is a task much easier said than done––Houston simply doesn't have the chips or financial flexibility to make such a move go down.
Now, that doesn't mean that the Texans can't at least involve themselves in some form of deadline activity to bring in new talent. If Houston is able to get back on track with a win in Week 9 against the LA Chargers, it's certainly possible that this front office wants to build up this roster even further.
But if that were to happen, expect the Texans to make a minor addition on the edges of this roster to help propel their current core forward, rather than making a big-time star investment like the Chicago Bears just did for Jeffery Simmons.

title: Texans Week 9 Consensus Power Rankings: Where Houston Sits After the Bye
full_text:
The Houston Texans got some much-needed time off during their Week 8 bye week that can only hope to recharge this group and help rally back from the 2-5 deficit they're currently stuck in .
But as the Texans were taking their time off in Week 8, teams around the league continued to fight on. The action that unfolded tended to shift the stock of several teams around Houston –– for better or for worse–– and has since led to a few changes across multiple power rankings because of it.
With that in mind, let's sort through a new batch of consensus power rankings to see just where the Texans stack up around the league as they head into their Week 9 game against the LA Chargers :
Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr was one of the highest pundits on this list when it came to the Texans earlier this season. But now, he's dropped them to just barely inside the top 25 teams in the NFL. A disappointing falloff.
"The Texans will face the Chargers this weekend in a battle of the two most confoundingly disappointing teams I can ever remember. This is the kind of hype that forces me to never trust again."
NFL.com 's Nick Shook does see reason for optimism surrounding the Texans moving forward, simply because of their upcoming schedule facing a batch of beatable opponents. But that still didn't stop him from dropping Houston one spot in his rankings.
"While we can officially agree Houston’s defense isn’t the unit we’ve known it to be in recent years, the Texans have a favorable road out of the bye. Dates with the Chargers and Colts sandwich a meeting with the Browns, so while 2-5 is a tough place to be after eight weeks, there’s still a path back to relevance. Keep an eye on Marvin Harrison Jr.’s role in the offense, too."
ESPN 's writers also dropped the Texans by one spot in their rankings and continue to keep them outside of the top 20. D.J. Bien-Aime was tasked with finding Houston's best in-season trade acquisition within franchise history, landing on wide receiver Demariyus Thomas in 2018.
"Historically, the Texans haven't made many in-season trades. Zero have resulted in Houston receiving a game-changing player. The hope is Marvin Harrison Jr., who was acquired from the Cardinals in early October, could become exactly that. Thomas was at least the most effective player out of all the choices. In 2018, Houston started 0-3 and reeled off nine consecutive wins to finish 11-5. Houston acquired Thomas after five wins in a row, and in his first game, he had 61 receiving yards against his former team, the Broncos. He finished the season with 275 receiving yards for Houston with two touchdowns."
The Athletic 's Josh Kendall and Chad Graff aren't ready to count the Texans out of playoff contention just yet. However, that isn't to say that they still aren't disappointed with the results of Houston's latest loss to the New York Giants.
"It’s frustrating, honestly. Houston started 0-4, showed a spark of life, but then disappointed in a 27-21 loss to the Giants in Week 7.The Athletic’s most recent playoff projections have the Texans with just a 19 percent chance to make the playoffs. But here’s the problem: Houston has the second-easiest remaining schedule, according to Tankathon."
CBS Sports ' Pete Prisco highlights the defensive woes Houston has faced as his biggest cause for concern on the Texans now and moving forward.
"It's hard for many to see how this team is down this low in the rankings. Here's why: the defense has been a mess. They can't afford another loss or they might be done."
FOX Sports ' Ralph Vacchiano tends to have a bit more to like about the Texans compared to the consensus. Not only does he have them within the top 20 teams of his current rankings, but he's the only pundit who ranked Houston higher than their previous spot heading into Week 8––which becomes especially surprising knowing that this team didn't play a snap this weekend.
"Here’s the good news for the Texans coming out of their bye: They’re in second place in the AFC South despite a 2-5 record. They’re 2.5 games out of a wild-card spot, but the point is that their division is pretty awful and they still have to play the two worst teams — the Titans and Colts — one more time each. They also get the Chargers, Ravens, Commanders and Eagles, so there are a lot of soft spots in the second half of their schedule. If they can get over their pre-bye loss to the Giants, they still have an outside chance to be OK."

title: Colts Shoved Adonai Mitchell Out, and Now Are Paying the Price
full_text:
Last year, when the Indianapolis Colts appeared on a fast track to the Super Bowl, then-general manager Chris Ballard executed a blockbuster trade.
He sent Indy's 2026 and 2027 first-rounders to the New York Jets for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner.
Sadly, Gardner hasn't played full capacity since the trade due to injuries, but even when his high-level talent is on the field, the Colts still can't win consistently. In short, the Jets have won this trade.
But everyone talks about the first-rounders Indianapolis surrendered; one part of that trade has been overlooked: Giving away the ultra-talented wide receiver, Adonai Mitchell.
Mitchell was drafted by the Colts with the 52nd-overall pick in Round 2 of the 2024 NFL Draft with expectations to blossom under future Hall-of-Famer and Indy wide receivers coach, Reggie Wayne.
2024 was a tough year for Mitchell, who caught only 23 passes for 312 receiving yards. The worst statistic was his catch percentage, which was an underwhelming 41.8.
Year two wasn't much better for the former Texas Longhorn, but he looked to be hitting a stride in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Rams - that was, until disaster struck in the third quarter.
Mitchell hauled in a beautiful deep pass from Daniel Jones, proceeded to spin out of the tackle after a highlight catch, and took the pill to the house for a touchdown.
However, Mitchell got caught up in the moment too soon and fumbled the ball before crossing the goal line, which negated the score and resulted in a touchback, giving possession to the Rams.
"UNBELIEVABLE!" Kevin Kugler on the Colts-Rams call as Adonai Mitchell has a play that starts out great and ends quite poorly. #NFL pic.twitter.com/jyTigKoqwJ
Along with a bad holding penalty later in the game that cost Jonathan Taylor a rushing score, this was a brutal game for Mitchell.
However, Mitchell was only 23 and still navigating the NFL way. Instead of letting him learn his lesson and continue building as a pro in Indy, the Colts opted to get rid of him.
Now in 2026, Indianapolis' wide receiver corps is a barren wasteland.
Alec Pierce was given a mountainous contract but is sidelined with a heel injury and has no timeline to return. This already put the Colts' wide receiver room in a bind.
Now, top pass-catcher Josh Downs is over the situation with the Colts, and has requested a trade in the process.
Josh Downs has requested a trade from the Colts, per @JFowlerESPN pic.twitter.com/0eMonnkhne
If we remove Downs from the equation and assume he's dealt before the November 10th deadline, below is what Indianapolis has in their razor-thin receiver room.
Indianapolis could desperately use Mitchell, but that ship has sailed.
Mitchell has only seen four games this year for the Jets after dealing with a finger injury that required surgery. However, he's looked great and appears to be finding his footing in the NFL.
Mitchell has been explosive, hauling in 16 catches for 265 receiving yards and a touchdown.
He's also riding serious momentum after a monstrous seven-catch, 142-yard, one-touchdown performance in Week 8 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Geno drops it to AD for a TD! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Cqbp8f0YsS
Ballard made some baffling decisions during his tenure in Indianapolis, but letting go of such a promising weapon after a few struggles early in his young career is inexcusable.
Mitchell looks like a future star, while Indianapolis is desperately trying to operate an offense with a mentally absent Downs and an over-the-hill Keenan Allen as the top wide receivers.
The past is the past, but with every play the ascending Mitchell makes for the Jets, it just pours salt in the wound of the rebuilding Colts, whose 2026 season is all but lost.
But at the end of the day, the NFL is all about making good decisions. Forcing Mitchell out of the organization and alienating him is on Indianapolis, and they have nobody to blame but themselves.

title: Week 9 Injury Report: Colts Could Catch a Break Against Cowboys
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys released their latest injury reports Thursday ahead of Sunday's matchup in Indianapolis.
While the Colts received some encouraging news regarding several potential returnees, Dallas is dealing with significant questions at tight end and in the secondary.
Let’s take a look at both teams’ Thursday practice reports.
Did Not Participate - DT Grover Stewart (rest) - LB Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) - CB Justin Walley (knee)
Limited Participants - TE Drew Ogletree (knee)
Full Participants - WR Keenan Allen (rest) - LB Bryce Boettcher (groin) - WR Anthony Gould (concussion) - RB Jonathan Taylor (rest) - OT Jalen Travis (thumb) - CB Charvarius Ward Sr. (rest)
The Colts received some encouraging injury news Thursday as several key players made progress ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys.
Jonathan Taylor, Keenan Allen, and Charvarius Ward all returned to full participation after sitting out Wednesday on rest days. None of the three absences appears particularly concerning, and all should be in a good position to play Sunday barring an unexpected setback.
It's worth noting that despite the Nov. 10 trade deadline quickly approaching, Taylor remains a regular piece of the Colts' plans despite being the most discussed name on the market.
Indianapolis could also receive reinforcements at a couple of positions. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher and wide receiver Anthony Gould have both logged consecutive full practices after missing the previous two games. Gould is still required to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before returning to game action, but his progress is an encouraging sign. Boettcher's potential return would be particularly helpful for a linebacker group dealing with some uncertainty.
Akeem Davis-Gaither and Justin Walley, meanwhile, have both missed the first two practices of the week. Davis-Gaither's continued absence leaves the Colts with questions about their linebacker depth, though Boettcher trending in the right direction could aid in that department. Still, being without their usual playcaller on defense could present several problems for the Colts. Walley's situation is worth monitoring in a secondary that could use the additional depth. Without participating at all this week, both Walley and Davis-Gaither are trending in the wrong direction heading into Friday.
Tight end Drew Ogletree also showed some progress, moving from a DNP designation Wednesday to limited participation Thursday. His availability remains unclear, but the progression is a positive development.
Defensive tackle Grover Stewart was the other notable absence Thursday, although his designation was rest-related. His absence shouldn't necessarily raise any concerns, particularly given the nature of the designation, but his status will be worth monitoring Friday.
Overall, the Colts appear to be trending in a positive direction with several potential contributors moving closer to returning. Boettcher and Gould could provide meaningful reinforcements as their respective positions are lacking solid depth, while the continued absences of Davis-Gaither and Walley call for close monitoring. Friday's final report will give a clearer picture of who will be active and who will be sidelined.
Did Not Participate - TE Jake Ferguson (ankle) - OLB Malachi Lawrence (ankle) - WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs)
Limited Participants - DB Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle) - S P.J. Locke III (concussion) - LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) - WR George Pickens (hamstring) - CB Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) - TE Luke Schoonmaker (groin) - OG Tyler Smith (ankle)
Full Participants - DT Jonathan Bullard (calf) - DT Kenny Clark (back) - OT Broderick Jones (personal) - OLB Marist Liufau (forearm) - OLB Von Miller (rest) - OT Drew Shelton (hamstring) - LB Dee Winters (calf)
The Cowboys have several injury concerns heading into Sunday's matchup with the Colts, particularly in the secondary and at tight end. While there have been some encouraging developments, Dallas still has a laundry list of guys whose availability remains uncertain.
The Cowboys could receive some reinforcements at linebacker, with Dee Winters progressing from limited participation Wednesday to a full practice Thursday. Winters' potential return would be particularly helpful with DeMarvion Overshown being limited with hamstring and back issues. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau has also returned to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, potentially giving Dallas another option at linebacker.
The secondary is another area worth monitoring. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke both progressed from not participating Wednesday to limited participation Thursday while dealing with concussions, an encouraging sign for Dallas. Both players must complete the NFL's concussion return-to-participation protocol. Their return to practice is encouraging, but neither is guaranteed to be available Sunday.
This matchup was circled on the calendar as soon as the Dallas Cowboys selected safety Caleb Downs with their first-round draft pick, given that his brother, wide receiver Josh Downs, is on the Indianapolis Colts.
With Josh Downs being a popular name in trade circles ahead of the deadline next Tuesday, it was starting to look like he may be shut down and/or traded before the Colts' Week 9 matchup against the Cowboys, but now it's looking like he will at least play in one more contest for the team that drafted him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft.
First and foremost, we're hoping that Caleb Downs isn't seriously injured for the sake of his long-term health, but also because the thought of two brothers playing against each other at the next level is an exciting storyline.
Joey Porter Jr. also went from a full participant on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with an ankle injury. With multiple defensive backs dealing with injuries, Dallas could be facing some significant depth concerns against Indianapolis.
At tight end, Jake Ferguson has missed the first two practices of the week with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday in question. Luke Schoonmaker has been limited in consecutive practices while dealing with a groin injury, but his participation is an encouraging sign. Getting Schoonmaker back would be particularly important if Ferguson remains sidelined, as Dallas could otherwise be severely shorthanded.
The Cowboys also have some questions at wide receiver, where George Pickens has been limited for two consecutive days with a hamstring injury. His continued participation is encouraging, but his status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday. KaVontae Turpin, meanwhile, has missed both practices with a rib injury. His potential absence would affect both the receiving corps and special teams, where he provides an explosive return option.
Defensively, Dallas could also be without rookie pass rusher Malachi Lawrence, who has missed the first two practices dealing with an ankle issue. Defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard has progressed to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, which could eventually provide some additional depth up front if he's activated off injured reserve ahead of Sunday.
Overall, Dallas has several more injury concerns than Indianapolis heading into Friday's final practice sessions. The potential absences of Ferguson, Downs and Locke are particularly noteworthy given the impact they could have on the Cowboys' offensive and defensive personnel. There is some positive news with Winters, Bullard and Liufau progressing, but Dallas still has plenty of questions to answer before Sunday's matchup.

title: Indianapolis Colts Fire Sale Tracker: Analysis, Trades, Rumors, and More
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts will be the center of the NFL world for the foreseeable future.
This is the second consecutive season that Indianapolis will be featured in trade talks at the midway point, but unlike last year, it's not because they're the number one seed in the AFC.
Instead of buying at the deadline, the Colts will be selling.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline (November 10th, 4 PM EST) is quickly approaching, and the Colts are amidst a complete teardown of their franchise.
The Colts fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard after they fell to 2-4 in a humiliating loss, and have been active in the trade market ever since as they look to recoup any valuable draft capital they can after Ballard traded away their 2027 first-round pick, as well as their 2026 first-rounder and WR Adonai Mitchell.
It was the beginning of a poetic end, as the last Ballard-led Colts game was a loss to the 0-5 Tennessee Titans, a team that many still consider the worst team in the NFL. Even then, this version of the Colts may very well be the league's worst.
On top of only one playoff win in three appearances, the Colts failed to win the lowly AFC South across 9.5 seasons (2017-2026) under Chris Ballard.
Despite ample evidence to suggest otherwise, Indianapolis Colts' Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon decided to bring back both Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen for the 2026 season, referencing their hot start to the previous year as a reason to give them another chance.
The former had been given far too many chances to that point, but to be fair to Irsay-Gordon and her sisters, Co-Owners Kalen Jackson and Casey Foyt, this was the organization's first full offseason under new ownership.
Following the decision to give Ballard and Steichen one last shot in her postseason press conference, Irsay-Gordon said that the "sense of urgency has never been higher" for the GM/HC tandem.
Many didn't believe her, given that she was entering her first full offseason as an NFL Owner/CEO and appeared to be betting on an inevitable collapse, but Irsay-Gordon did what needed to be done, even if it came a bit too late.
In the past 14 days, the Indianapolis Colts have fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard, fallen to 2-6 on the season, and traded away two of their franchise cornerstones.
This article is meant to serve as a one-stop shop for all things Indianapolis Colts-related ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline. I will be updating this story as new information presents itself, so be sure to regularly check back in.
Navigate our trade central (finalized trades, rumors, etc.), future outlook, and more below.
Outside of players still on their rookie contract, as well as some exceptions such as cornerback Sauce Gardner, wide receiver Alec Pierce, left tackle Bernhard Raimann, and a few others, nobody on the Colts roster is safe.
Although the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is on November 10th at 4 PM EST, the Colts have already gotten a head start on their fire sale.
In order, our trade central will featured finalized trades, a rumor mill, and will conclude with analysis on the team's overall outlook.
A current third-round pick and a future fifth-rounder may seem scoff-worthy at first glance, but when you break down the history of traded compensation for other guards across the league, Nelson's haul starts to make more sense.
Indianapolis' return of a 3rd and a 5th for Quenton Nelson is the most pure draft capital for a guard since at least 2011, per Spotrac. only 4 have netted a 4th: 2013: G. Carimi, 4th 2014: L. Mankins, 4th + player 2021: B. Bredeson + 5th + 7th, 4th 2025: J. Thuney, 4th
I think this is both the best example of why the return for Quenton Nelson isn’t as irresponsible as some are suggesting, and also why the Chris Ballard era needed to end: non-premium positions.
It stings to see any team trade their homegrown future Hall of Famer, but this is the bed the Colts made, and now they must sleep in it.
The Colts' 2026 fourth-round rookie guard Jalen Farmer is Nelson's immediate replacement.
Buckner's departure creates a similar challenge on the defensive line. More responsibility will fall on the remaining interior defenders, including Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore.
Not only is the opportunity there, but Adebawore has earned the increased role in question.
After seven weeks, Adebawore is undeniably the Colts' best pass rusher. He is currently tied for second with the most sacks among interior defensive linemen league-wide and leads the team in most major pass-rush statistics.
We've known that Adebawore has some nasty pass-rushing chops, but the biggest development has been his improvement in run defense.
Adebawore has blossomed into a legitimate starting defensive tackle, and it comes at no better time as the Colts have parted ways with their longtime pillar across the defensive line.
However, the Colts' newfound star is on an expiring deal. Adebawore is playing in the final year of his rookie contract, so a big payday is set to come his way.
Update (11/3) : The Indianapolis Colts have signed Adetomiwa Adebawore to a two-year, $35 million contract extension that includes a $13 million signing bonus and $22.5 in new money through 2027.
Update (11/5) : NFL Insider Jordan Schultz : "The belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline.
ESPN's NFL Insider Adam Schefter confirmed on Halloween that the Indianapolis Colts are officially open to trading Jonathan Taylor and have been active in talks.
Schefter added that the Colts have already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick along with additional compensation for Taylor's services.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to Schefter and fellow ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Taylor's most comparable trade package is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league. According to Schefter, multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
"The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants," Schefter wrote.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz added on Monday that the Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks have entered the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
"My understanding is that 5-6 teams have been aggressively pursuing him: Giants, Packers, Broncos, Seahawks, Bengals, Vikings," Schultz said on The Pivot .
"I think it'll take at least a second-round plus additional compensation to get it done, and I actually do expect that to happen."
The aforementioned Christian McCaffrey blockbuster haul remains the ideal return for the Indianapolis Colts.

title: Jonathan Taylor Sweepstakes Tracker: Colts Analysis, Trade Rumors, and More
full_text:
Unfortunately for Indianapolis Colts fans, Jonathan Taylor and trade request are two terms that have been used together in a sentence before.
Back in 2023, the Colts' prolific running back requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts amid ongoing contract disputes. Taylor infamously showed up to practice in a black hoodie during his subsequent hold-in, signifying the trying times of a franchise that was entering its first season with then-rookie Anthony Richardson at quarterback.
Following the reporting of Taylor's trade request, former longtime Owner Jim Irsay made sure the league knew he was going to do whatever it takes to keep the star rusher around for the then-rebuild, which was really more of a slight re-tooling, a more conventional dart throw, but I digress.
“We’re not trading Jonathan [Taylor]... end of discussion,” Irsay said in a text to Sports Illustrated ’s Albert Breer . “Not now and not in October!”
And as fate would have it, the Colts would up re-signing Jonathan Taylor in October to a three-year $42 million contract extension, which included $26.5 million in guaranteed payments.
But just three years later, the star running back is back at the center of trade talks.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline at 4 PM EST on November 10th is quickly approaching, and it's become increasingly likely that Jonathan Taylor has played his last snap as a member of the Indianapolis Colts.
We're breaking down everything we know about the state of the sweepstakes in question, and will update this article as new information presents itself.
Without further ado, let's dive into how we got here, which teams are reportedly interested in Jonathan Taylor's services and what they're offering.
Despite loud rumors and an ongoing fire sale suggesting otherwise, Taylor has not requested a trade.
In all honesty, it feels and looks like Taylor is one of the few remaining longtime veterans on the Colts roster who genuinely still wants to be in Indianapolis.
Earlier in the offseason, Taylor signed a two-year extension to stay in Indianapolis through the 2028 season. Taylor said he wanted to remain a Colt for life before the extension, hinting toward the goal of a long-term deal, but he and the Colts found a solution that satisfied both parties.
Chris Ballard was already on the hottest seat in general manager history as he entered the final year of his deal, and the Colts didn't want to fully commit to another era under his rule.
And it was smart to think that way, considering we are wrapping up Week 8 and Ballard has been out of the building for two weeks now. Along with him went longtime franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and all eyes have been on Jonathan Taylor ever since.
Mere months after committing to stay in Indianapolis for the next three seasons, Taylor appears to be on his way out.
In his first game without Quenton Nelson leading the way, Taylor rushed for just 23 yards on eight carries. The Colts failed to establish any sort of rushing attack against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and Taylor saw just five carries come his way in the first half.
After the game, Taylor appeared to be rather emotional and was giving multiple teammates and coaches hugs. Sure, it could've just been a lot to take in, or perhaps I am looking too far into it, but it truly felt like this was the last we've seen of Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis.
Couple this with the fact that ESPN's NFL Insider Adam Schefter confirmed on Halloween, the day prior, that the Indianapolis Colts are officially open to trading Taylor and have been active in talks, and it seems like he's as good as gone.
Schefter also reported that the Colts have already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick, along with additional compensation, for Taylor's services.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to Schefter and fellow ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Taylor's most comparable trade package, or at least the one Indianapolis is seeking, is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Taylor doesn't quite warrant the first-round consideration as a pure rusher who is a subpar back in the passing game, though he does have an argument.
Regardless of his flaws as a third-down back, Taylor's ability as a true rusher is nearly unmatched. He remains at the top of his game at 27 years old, is durable, and carries a favorable contract for the next two seasons.
The Colts already paid Taylor his $15 million signing bonus before the season, so a potential suitor would only be on the hook for $15 milllion in 2027 and $9.46 million in 2028.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help the next regime's outlook tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league.
According to Schefter, the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
Per Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk, the New York Giants appear to be all-in on Taylor, but it must be at the right price.
"The Giants are one of those teams, and they are very interested. They view Jonathan Taylor as being on par with Derrick Henry in that second tier, just below the best running backs in the NFL. The general concern at this point, though, is that the Colts want too much," Florio said following Week 8's Sunday slate .
“One source with one of the teams currently in the mix with Taylor puts it at 50-50 as to whether it gets done before the trade deadline."
Furthermore, Denver Broncos beat reporter, The DNVR's Zac Stevens, said that he feels the Broncos are truly all-in on Taylor.
"I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor...." Stevens said in a postgame reaction piece on the DNVR Broncos Podcast. "The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now."
That wraps up just about everything we're aware of as of Monday, November 2nd. Be sure to check back in for any updates regarding the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz added on Monday that the Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks have entered the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
