title: Colts-Cowboys History Suggests Sunday Could Get Weird
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colt s are 2-6, fresh off a 42-7 beatdown in Jacksonville, and five days away from the NFL trade deadline.
So, instead of thinking about the fire currently burning through this franchise , let's take our minds somewhere else for a minute.
The Dallas Cowboys are coming to Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, and these two franchises have a history that stretches all the way back to 1960. It has included blowouts, Hall of Famers, overtime chaos, and somehow, one of the strangest Super Bowls ever played.
Dallas leads the all-time series 11-7, including an 11-6 advantage in the regular season. But the Colts own the only postseason meeting, and that one happens to be the biggest game these teams have ever played.
Super Bowl V was an absolute disaster. The Baltimore Colts and Cowboys combined for 11 turnovers; Baltimore committed seven of them, and Dallas was penalized 10 times for 133 yards.
Johnny Unitas left with an injury, Earl Morrall finished the game and Cowboys linebacker Chuck Howley became the only player from a losing team to win Super Bowl MVP.
Still, the Colts somehow survived.
Rookie kicker Jim O'Brien drilled a 32-yard field goal with five seconds remaining to give Baltimore a 16-13 win and the franchise its first Super Bowl championship.
That game probably sums this series up better than anything: weird, messy and unpredictable.
The first meeting was not nearly as dramatic.
Baltimore destroyed the expansion Cowboys 45-7 in 1960, setting the tone for what has become a series filled with lopsided results. Dallas eventually flipped the matchup, including a six-game winning streak over the Colts from 1972 through 1993.
Indianapolis finally snapped that run in 1996, when Jim Harbaugh led a second-half comeback in Dallas and the Colts escaped with a 25-24 win.
Since then, the absurdity has continued.
Peyton Manning threw four interceptions in a 38-35 overtime loss in 2010. Eight years later, Marlon Mack ran for 139 yards and two touchdowns as Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0, snapping the Cowboys' five-game winning streak.
Indianapolis trailed just 21-19 after three quarters before Dallas scored a franchise-record 33 points in the fourth, turning a competitive game into a 54-19 embarrassment. Former Colt Malik Hooker even added an interception and a fumble-return touchdown against his old team.
Probably nothing predictive. History from 1960 is not going to help Shane Steichen win a football game in 2026.
But one thing is certain: these matchups have rarely gone according to plan.
The Colts' last two meetings with Dallas ended 23-0 and 54-19. Before that came an overtime thriller, and buried deeper was a Super Bowl remembered as the "Blunder Bowl."
Now a 2-6 Colts team welcomes a 3-5 Cowboys team to Indianapolis with both seasons already hanging in the balance.
If history has taught us anything, it's that when these two teams meet, just about anything can happen.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts Trade Talks Have Stalled as NFL Deadline Approaches
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have made it clear that their plans for the future are beginning to take priority over the remainder of the 2026 season. After trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Indianapolis has continued to field calls on several of its other players with the NFL trade deadline approaching.
Jonathan Taylor remains the biggest name in that conversation, and while plenty of buzz has been created around the superstar running back, a deal is far from guaranteed. According to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, the Colts have reached a standstill with Taylor and their other trade candidates, leaving the situation unresolved with less than a week to go before the Nov. 10 deadline.
“Where we're at is essentially where we've been,” Rapaport said on Good Morning Football Thursday morning. “Which is several teams interested in Taylor, willing to offer a significant pick package, but maybe not quite what (Colts interim GM) Ed Dodds…or the organization wants.”
From @GMFB : The #Colts are at a standstill with RB Jonathan Taylor and the rest of their trade candidates. pic.twitter.com/u7NkvO18rr
The Colts' asking price for Taylor helps explain why a deal has yet to materialize. According to Rapoport, Indianapolis is seeking a package comparable to the one the San Francisco 49ers surrendered to acquire Christian McCaffrey from the Carolina Panthers in 2022. That deal included second, third, fourth and fifth-round draft picks, setting a considerable benchmark for any team hoping to land Taylor.
However, interested teams don't appear willing to part with that level of draft capital. While there is no shortage of interest in the three-time Pro Bowler, the gap between what the Colts want and what potential suitors are prepared to offer has kept negotiations from progressing.
There is also another important factor at play: the Colts aren't necessarily eager to move on from Taylor in the first place.
"This is not someone they really want to trade," Rapoport said. "This is someone that they believe is a big part of their future. They'd like to build around him, so it would take a big package to get the Colts to move on from him."
That adds a layer of complexity to the situation. Indianapolis has already demonstrated a willingness to move established players as it reshapes its roster, but Taylor remains someone the organization would prefer to keep if no trade partner reaches their asking price.
With the Nov. 10 deadline approaching, the Colts will have to determine whether they are willing to adjust their expectations or stand firm and keep one of their most valuable players.
Taylor isn't the only prominent Colts player who could be moved. Wide receiver Josh Downs is also a potential trade candidate after requesting a trade out of Indianapolis.
According to Rapoport, Indianapolis is seeking a third or fourth-round pick in exchange for the 25-year-old. There are several teams around the league in need of help at the position, giving the Colts potential opportunities to find a trade partner before the deadline.
However, much like the Taylor situation, it remains unclear whether another team is willing to meet Indianapolis' asking price.
Downs' situation is worth monitoring over the final days before the deadline. With Indianapolis already undergoing significant roster changes, moving another established offensive player could provide additional draft capital as the organization continues looking toward the future.
The Colts have made significant changes to their roster in recent weeks, but their work ahead of the trade deadline may not be finished. Taylor and Downs remain the two most notable names to watch, though Indianapolis could potentially consider moving other veterans like defensive tackle Grover Stewart, tight end Mo Alie-Cox, quarterback Daniel Jones or cornerback Charvarius Ward.
With the Nov. 10 deadline approaching, the next few days should provide a clearer picture of how aggressive the Colts intend to be as they continue reshaping their roster.

title: Jonathan Taylor's Trade Value Just Unexpectedly Went Up
full_text:
The Jonathan Taylor Sweepstakes has taken an unexpected turn.
The star running back has been at the center of NFL Trade Deadline rumors since the Indianapolis Colts decided to kick off an early-season rebuild after firing longtime general manager Chris Ballard following a disastrous Week 6 loss to the winless Tennessee Titans.
The rebuild began with a fire sale of their roster as the Colts traded away franchise cornerstones in LG Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner following a Week 7 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and Taylor has been the top trade candidate on the market ever since.
Several championship contenders have been active in trade talks for running backs, and a recent trade from a team looking to save its season may have inadvertently increased Jonathan Taylor's value.
Follow along as I break down what this move in question means for Taylor and the Colts as we inch closer toward the NFL Trade Deadline on November 10th at 4 PM EST .
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Jonathan Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to ESPN NFL Insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport .
However, the Colts are also open to dealing Taylor if the price is right.
The reported asking price of a 2027 first-round pick has remained firm, but most believe that Irsay-Gordon and Co. would be willing to deal Taylor if they could net first-round value. Ian Rapoport implied on the Pat McAfee Show yesterday
A first-round pick is the easiest way to satisfy such a request, but the Colts can also achieve this goal by adding multiple Day 2 (rounds 2-3) draft selections.
Schefter also reported that Indianapolis already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick, along with additional compensation, for Taylor's services, but the Colts have been standing pat as they believe their storied rusher warrants such a return.
Yesterday on the Pat McAfee Show, Ian Rapoport implied that the Colts' early trades of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner have resulted in teams being reluctant to match Taylor's asking price, given they think Indianapolis undersold two of their biggest assets.
However, unlike Nelson and Buckner, whose deals were expiring, Taylor's recent two-year extension earlier this offseason has him under contract through the 2028 season.
The running back role has been deemed a non-premium position for quite some time now, which has made the Colts' first-round asking price feel far-fetched.
Furthermore, the Colts are reportedly seeking compensation simliar to what the Carolina Panthers got for running back Christian McCaffrey back in 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
At the time, McCaffrey was one of the NFL's undisputed best offensive weapons, but he still couldn't net a first-round draft selection.
His $12 million annual salary made him the NFL's highest-paid running back at the time and he had 3.5 years left on his contract, yet teams were reluctant to pay such a premium for a position they typically disregarded.
Four years later, Taylor's current contract averages $22 million per year, putting him just behind Bijan Robinson for the second-highest-paid running back in the league. So while this was a pricey deal at the time of signing, it's worth noting that we're starting to see the NFL pay more of a premium for running backs.
A hypothetical suitor would be on the hook for Taylor's expensive next two seasons, but given that the Colts already paid him his $15 million signing bonus before the season, they would only owe Taylor $15 milllion in 2027 and $9.46 million in 2028.
As of Monday, the reported interested teams for Jonathan Taylor are the New York Giants, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos, Cincinnati Bengals, and Green Bay Packers.
The aforementioned contract layer gives interested teams some wiggle room financially, and Taylor looks even more enticing once you taken into account the fact Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry may be off the market ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline.
Jonathan Taylor has headlined all NFL trade talks , but there are still a few quality running backs on the market who have hurt his value as a result.
New York Jets' Breece Hall, Tennessee Titans' Tony Pollard, and Baltimore Ravens' Derrick Henry have been regularly mentioned as trade candidates, but the latter of which may be off the market entirely come trade deadline day.
It may not appear that way as the Baltimore Ravens sit with a 4-4 record and are last in their division entering Week 9.
The AFC North is the only division in the NFL that features all four teams with an even record (.500) or better, and given that their outlook at quarterback is bleak, they'd be wise to sell off any remaining assets, and Henry is the first name that comes to mind.
Ravens' superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson (thumb) and backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) could both be out for the rest of the season.
Jackson was placed on Injured Reserve earlier this week, meaning that he'll have to miss at least the next four games, but given that his thumb injury will require surgery, there's a good chance he'll be shut down for the rest of the season.
Furthermore, Huntley's toe injury is confirmed to be season-ending, and the Ravens are now set to start rookie undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday, November 5th.
However, the Baltimore Ravens have seemingly decided that they aren't punting on the 2026 regular season just yet.
On Wednesday, the Ravens made a trade with the Arizona Cardinals to bring in longtime veteran journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .
Trade: the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, per @RapSheet and me. Deal is expected to be completed until this weekend. The Ravens lost QB Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury, and his backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley to turf… pic.twitter.com/BYEqcHA1jq
The deal is expected to be finalized by this weekend, meaning that Brissett will not be active for the Ravens' Thursday Night Football matchup, though it does speak to the organization's long-term plans.
The Ravens aren't prepared to give up on the season just yet, and while things may change between now and Tuesday's highly anticipated trade deadline, the Colts have been granted some extra leeway in negotiations for Jonathan Taylor's services in the meantime.
With Derrick Henry seemingly off the market, Taylor's price has increased.
RB-hungry teams may still be more inclined to entertain Tony Pollard or Breece Hall's asking price(s), but regardless, Taylor has separated himself as the definitive best option on the market.
You'd expect Taylor to be sidelined until his fate is decided, but Indianapolis Colts' head coach Shane Steichen still plans to play Taylor in the team's Week 9 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
"He's on our football team, and he's excited for this opportunity to go play," Steichen said on Wednesday as to why the Colts continue to play Taylor amid trade rumors. "He wants to go win this game, and he's on our football team right now.”
"There is a lot of outside noise, trades, all this stuff. I mean, just with anything during this time of year, people are going to call. That's just part of the business, but again, you’ve got to be a professional and show up to work.”
Trotting Jonathan Taylor out onto the field amid trade talks feels like malpractice, but as long as he stays healthy and the Colts are able to net first-round value, Indianapolis is shaping up to have a strong start to their much-needed rebuild.
The Indianapolis Colts would be wise to trade Jonathan Taylor , and the Baltimore Ravens bringing in an old friend may be the indirect needle-mover they need to get the job done.

title: Two Trade Suitors Have Emerged for Colts QB Daniel Jones
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts may not have to wait until the offseason to find a new home for Daniel Jones.
The veteran quarterback is now appearing on the radar of multiple teams as a possible trade target , meaning Indianapolis could have an opportunity to move on from Jones before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
Jones was always viewed as a short-term solution for the Colts, and the team's recent moves have made its rebuilding direction increasingly clearer.
A trade would give Indianapolis another chance to recoup draft capital while allowing Jones to continue his career elsewhere rather than letting his time with the organization run its course at the end of the season.
The Baltimore Ravens have emerged as perhaps the most logical landing spot for Daniel Jones, given their current situation at quarterback.
Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve after suffering a thumb injury against the Buffalo Bills, while backup Tyler Huntley has been ruled out for the remainder of the season with turf toe, an injury he picked up in the same game.
That leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in line to make his first NFL start Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Sources: tests revealed that Ravens’ QB Tyler “Snoop” Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is out indefinitely with a thumb injury, Huntley’s season is over due to turf toe, and QB Joe Fagnano will start Thursday night vs. Jacksonville. pic.twitter.com/Cok4gbSvH3
With both of their top quarterbacks sidelined, the Ravens have an obvious incentive to explore the trade market before the Nov. 10 deadline.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that conversations around the league led him to believe Jones was at least on Baltimore's radar. Adam Schefter also identified the Ravens as a potential landing spot, although neither report suggests a deal is imminent.
The 29-year-old Jones is far from a perfect solution, particularly after throwing five touchdowns against nine interceptions this season, but the Ravens wouldn't necessarily need him to be their long-term answer. If Jackson is unavailable for an extended period, Jones could provide a more established option than turning the offense over to an undrafted rookie with virtually no NFL experience.
Jones would have running back Derrick Henry and wide receiver Zay Flowers at his disposal, giving him an excellent supporting cast as he tries to regain some of the form he showed before tearing his Achilles tendon last season.
Baltimore's offensive system could also help take some of the pressure off Jones by leaning on its ground game, rather than asking him to carry the offense on his own. That doesn't guarantee a turnaround, but it would give him a better opportunity to succeed than his current circumstances in Indianapolis.
Jones' 2026 base salary is $5.49 million and is fully guaranteed, but Fowler noted that the salary is tradable. Baltimore would take on the remaining contractual obligations, while the Colts would retain the salary-cap charges associated with the signing bonus they already paid. Jones also has a $10 million salary in 2027 that becomes fully guaranteed in March, giving a potential acquiring team a window to evaluate him before that commitment kicks in.
As for the trade compensation, it is difficult to envision Indianapolis demanding a significant return. Jones has struggled this season, while his contract and uncertain future would limit the number of teams willing to make a substantial investment. A late-round pick, potentially with conditions attached, could be a reasonable starting point for negotiations.
The Colts would also be inclined to move on from Jones, as getting his contract off the books before next year would clear up $38 million in cap space for their next general manager to utilize at his own discretion.
If the Colts release Daniel Jones after June 1st, they will create $38 million in cap space in the upcoming offseason. Seems like a no-brainer at this point. pic.twitter.com/gsK78a9JVN
Baltimore needs help immediately, and Jones offers a blend of experience, a manageable remaining salary and enough upside to make the gamble worthwhile.
The Minnesota Vikings present a different kind of opportunity for Daniel Jones, one that could be appealing for a team with legitimate postseason aspirations. Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season and has dealt with inconsistent quarterback play from Kyler Murray, who is also now dealing with a hamstring injury that could affect his availability for the team's Week 9 matchup against the Bills.
Murray's injury adds another reason for Minnesota to consider its options ahead of the deadline. While head coach Kevin O'Connell has maintained that Murray will remain the starter when healthy, the Vikings' offensive struggles have raised questions about whether the team has enough consistency at quarterback to compete. Carson Wentz is currently the primary alternative, but Jones could offer a more appealing option given his more recent experience as a starter.
Adam Schefter recently floated Minnesota as a potential landing spot for Jones, and the idea has gained some traction around the league. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has also argued that the Vikings should consider making a move for the Colts quarterback, pointing to the team's inconsistent offensive production and growing frustration with its quarterback play.
The Vikings should explore a possible trade for Colts QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/8XFK85ogYI
There's also a familiarity factor. Jones spent the final portion of the 2024 season in Minnesota after being released by the New York Giants, where he worked with O'Connell and became familiar with the team's offensive system, giving Jones a potential advantage over other quarterback options.
Jones would have a talented supporting cast headlined by wide receiver Justin Jefferson and a defense capable of keeping the team competitive. He wouldn't necessarily need to arrive and immediately take over the starting job, but he could be an option for Minnesota to pivot to if Murray's injury lingers or his struggles continue. Given his previous experience in O'Connell's offense, Jones would have a shorter adjustment period than an unfamiliar quarterback.
Financially, the same considerations that apply to Baltimore would also apply to Minnesota. Jones carries a $5.49 million base salary for 2026, along with a $510,000 per-game roster bonus. The Vikings would assume the remaining contractual obligations in a trade, although Indianapolis could potentially absorb some of the cost to make a deal more appealing.
A trade would still represent a calculated gamble for Minnesota. Jones has struggled considerably this season. However, the Vikings wouldn't necessarily need to make a significant investment to bring him back into the building. If the Colts are willing to move him for a late-round selection, Minnesota could be inclined to add an experienced quarterback without sacrificing too much of its future.
Of the two potential destinations, Minnesota may be the more intriguing fit for Jones, even if Baltimore has the more pressing need. The Vikings already know what he brings to the table, and a reunion could give both sides an opportunity to revisit a relationship that never fully developed in 2024.

title: 3 Under-the-Radar Colts Who Could Be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have already made it clear what direction this franchise is heading .
Quenton Nelson is in Seattle, and DeForest Buckner is back in San Francisco. With the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs have dominated the Colts trade conversation.
But those aren't the only names worth watching.
Here are three under-the-radar Colts trade candidates contending teams could see real value in before the deadline.
Let's start with the most complicated one.
Jones has been about as bad as we have seen him since his days in New York. Through eight games, he has thrown for 1,542 yards, five touchdowns and nine interceptions with a 68.7 passer rating.
His trade value is probably close to rock bottom. But that doesn't mean there isn't a market.
His massive contract certainly complicates things, but for a team that believes it can get him back to his 2025 form, there could still be value in buying low.
Minnesota makes the most sense to me. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk has floated a reunion, and Jones spent time with Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings late in 2024.
The Vikings have a championship-caliber defense and dangerous weapons. They don't need Jones to be Superman; they need a veteran quarterback to manage the game and keep the offense on schedule.
Could O'Connell get more out of Jones than Indianapolis currently is? I absolutely think so.
Bynum is the player on this list I would be the most hesitant to move.
After recording 81 tackles, four interceptions and eight passes defended in 2025, Bynum has been much quieter this season with 26 tackles, one interception and two passes defended through seven games.
But I'm not convinced Bynum suddenly forgot how to play safety.
This Colts defense has forced just four turnovers through eight games and is allowing 27.8 points per game. Bynum is playing on the back end of a unit that consistently puts its secondary in difficult situations.
At 28 years old and under contract through 2028, he could help bridge this rebuild. His trade value is lower now than it was a year ago, which is exactly why I wouldn't be in a rush to sell.
Alie-Cox has been in Indianapolis since 2017, but with Tyler Warren leading the tight end room, his role has shrunk to mostly blocking work.
He has just four catches for 31 yards and a touchdown this season, but his value has never been about box-score production.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported there is trade-market interest in Alie-Cox because of his ability as a run blocker. At 33 years old on a cheap one-year deal, he is exactly the type of veteran a contender could add for a specific role.
The return wouldn't be massive, but that's not the point.
This franchise is entering a new chapter, and Alie-Cox may not be around when Indianapolis is ready to compete again. If someone offers a late-round pick, it might finally be time to let one of the last pieces from the old Colts era go.
The Colts have already made it clear that nobody is untouchable. With six days until the deadline, don't be surprised if a few more familiar faces are wearing different uniforms next week.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Pair of Promising Rookies Have Golden Opportunity if Colts Trade Taylor and Downs
full_text:
Anticipation is in the air around the Indianapolis Colts as the trade deadline approaches on November 10th.
Indianapolis already traded off long-time superstar guard Quenton Nelson (Seattle Seahawks) and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (San Francisco 49ers). Now, two big names remain who could possibly be dealt.
Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs .
Given how Indianapolis parted ways with staples like Nelson and Buckner to begin a rebuild, it seems like a matter of time until they trade away Taylor and Downs.
While this is somber for Colts fans, it's necessary seeing how this team has completely fallen apart in year four of Shane Steichen's leadership.
It's never easy to see serious contributors or stars leave a team, but it opens up opportunities for others to step up and show their mettle.
In this case, two Colts rookies stand out as beneficiaries if Taylor and Downs get traded.
That duo is Seth McGowan and Deion Burks.
It's time to discuss what may lie ahead for both.
Indianapolis drafted McGowan with the 237th-overall pick in Round 7 of the 2026 NFL Draft. McGowan's journey to the Colts was quite the trek after having to overcome past issues with the law.
In short, McGowan was charged with felony robbery in 2021 as a member of the Oklahoma Sooners. This led to his dismissal, which put his football future in serious jeopardy.
McGowan wouldn't play in another Division I football game until 2024, when he joined the New Mexico State Aggies, and he'd conclude his collegiate career with excellence for the Kentucky Wildcats.
That year, he amassed 725 rushing yards, 126 receiving yards, and 12 rushing touchdowns. His stock likely tanked due to the past legal issues, but Indianapolis took a swing on McGowan, and it's paid off.
#Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon on her draft call with RB Seth McGowan: “Are you ready to prove everyone that they’re **** wrong?” 🎥: @Colts pic.twitter.com/ByKcF3QshT
McGowan beat out DJ Giddens to be the RB2 behind Taylor, and he's been used to give the superstar running back relief from his heavy usage.
But McGowan hasn't just overshot expectations; he's looked great behind Taylor and has made the most of his opportunities.
McGowan isn't the most elusive, fastest, or slippery, but that isn't his style or what makes him a threat. Instead, it's his relentless running style and refusal to be tackled without a fight.
Seth McGowan is a really fun complementary back for the Colts. Doesn't have explosive long speed, but a really hard runner that can rip of some small chunk plays every now and then pic.twitter.com/aWMuD5tyfI
So far through the year, McGowan has tallied 37 carries for 163 rushing yards and 10 first downs. While he's yet to find the end zone, Indianapolis typically goes with Taylor in those goal line situations.
If Taylor is traded, McGowan will immediately start. It's fair to assume there will be somewhat of a committee approach with McGowan, Giddens, and whoever Indianapolis brings onto the roster to join.
But even with that approach, this would be a massive opportunity for McGowan to show Indianapolis that he can be the guy going forward.
If Taylor leaves, McGowan will get the bulk of the work in that backfield, regardless of which running back they bring onto the depth chart to flesh out the position.
McGowan has already shown promise, and if Taylor is traded, he'll get ample chances to show Indianapolis he belongs as a starter in the midst of a tough rebuild.
Burks was drafted in the same round as McGowan out of Oklahoma with the 254th-overall pick. What jumps off the page about Burks is his ridiculous speed that can leave any defender eating dust.
While Burks averaged a modest 11.1 yards per catch in 48 college games, that statistic grossly undersells how fast he is, and how many problems he can cause if defenses lose track of him.
Burks hasn't seen too much of the field this year, but the Colts have tried to get him involved as a pass-catcher, runner, and returner.
He's caught five passes for 60 yards, run the ball three times for 21 rushing yards, and returned five kicks for 110 yards.
While Burks hasn't seen much action as a receiver, he's still been used in the slot on 11 out of his 42 passing snaps, and if Downs is traded, it's hard to imagine he won't get used more in that fashion.
DEION BURKS THE ROOK 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/lVrJ9wyQfG
It's worth talking about Indy's current receiver situation. If we remove Downs from the depth chart, it leaves Keenan Allen, Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould, and Burks.
Allen has done what he can without Alec Pierce on the field, and Treadwell has put together a respectable campaign given his NFL journey; as for Dulin and Gould, they're mostly special teamers.
When I look at that receiver room without Downs, it's almost impossible to think that Burks won't get more looks. Given how he's played inside and out as a wideout, the Colts would be able to move him all around the formations.
There isn't a faster or deadlier receiver on the Colts right now than Burks.
If Downs is shipped out, Burks will get more snaps in the offense. This would be good for Indianapolis, as Burks is the only pass-catcher with the speed to loosen defensive coverage.

title: Game Balls From Jaguars' Primetime Trouncing of Ravens: Cam Little Goes Perfect
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are all smiles after their latest blowout win.
The Jaguars took care of business on the road on Thursday Night, taking down the Baltimore Ravens with a 33-10 win that was not really as close as the score indicated. The Jaguars were never in danger of losing this one, and they did exactly what they were supposed to do.
So, who earned the game balls this week as the Jaguars improved to 6-2 after yet another win? We break it down below.
For the second week in a row, Trevor Lawrence was able to get things popping right out of the gate. Lawrence has been playing like an MVP all season long and he once again was able to get off to a hot start on Thursday. He threw for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns before the rain really came in and turned it into a running attack. This included a 52-yard completion to rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher, the rookie tight end's third big play in the last three games.
"To go down two weeks in a row now to start the season – which is something that we’ve been struggling at [and] has been a point of emphasis – starting faster and being better on the first drive of the game," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said after the game.
"I’m kind of yelling at [Trevor Lawrence] to run out of bounds, and he just finds 'Boerk' [Nate Boerkircher], and I just think he was very on when it was really a game. Like when it was mattering and things were going and it’s a back-and-forth football game early on, he was extremely sharp, accurate, and he played a really solid football game for us.”
Lawrence has been Steady Eddie for the Jaguars all year long, and Thursday was another example. The Jaguars have rarely needed Lawrence to make big plays at the end of games this year, and that is largely due to the amount of big plays he is making at the start of games ... such as the big completion to Boerkircher.
Ventrell Miller gets the nod this week after recording a team-high seven tackles and a key pass-breakup. Had Miller not tipped a pass during the first-half, it would have surely resulted in an explosive gain for the Ravens. Add in a few stellar tackles in space, and Miller once again looked like an ascending young linebacker who can only improve moving forward.
There are a few other players who also deserve consideration. Foyesade Oluokun had seven tackles, including the Jaguars' only sack of the night. Montaric Brown and Jourdan Lewis each had interceptions, while Travon Walker recorded two tackles for loss despite not being 100%. But it was Miller who was consistently getting the Jaguars off the field both against the run and the pass, and it is Miller who wins this week's defensive game ball.
The conditions were not exactly favorable for things like kicking or passing the ball, especially as the rain came down even harder during the second-half. That didn't stop Cam Little, though, with the Jaguars' third-year kicker making all four of his field goals and all three of his extra points. Little is now 14-of-16 on field goals this season, and he has not missed a kick since Week 3 against the New England Patriots.
“Dialed," Coen said about Little's performance. "I was very pleased with his – he has a lot of confidence. He has a lot of confidence right now. We have a lot of confidence in him, and he’s hitting it really good right now.”
John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. Previously, he covered UCF's undefeated season as a beat reporter for NSM.Today, covered high school prep sports in Central Florida, and covered local sports and news for the Palatka Daily News. Follow John Shipley on Twitter at @_john_shipley.

title: 7 Winners, 3 Losers from Jaguars' Domination of Ravens: Trevor Lawrence, Parker Washington Lead the Way
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- All things considered, that was one of the easier games of the Liam Coen era.
The Jacksonville Jaguars took apart a depleted Baltimore Ravens team with a 33-10 win on Thursday Night Football, with the favored Jaguars doing what everyone expected them to do entering Week 9. As a result, the Jaguars are 6-2 and in a good spot moving into their mini-bye.
So, who were the winners and losers from the latest Jaguars blowout win? We break it all down below.
Trevor Lawrence didn't light up the box score, but that is largely because he didn't need to. Lawrence has gotten used to going into chew the clock mode during second-half of games, but that is largely because of how well he and the offense are operating when the game is, well, still a game. Lawrence looks like a clear MVP candidate , and the only thing that might be standing in his way is the Jaguars' own offensive dominance.
Trevor Lawrence has averaged 5.1 dropbacks per game in the 4th quarter this season, the fewest among qualified QB. Lawrence has 36 total dropbacks in the 4th quarter.
Lawrence hit a few throws during the first-half, where he had nearly 200 passing yards, that showed he has developed a full skill-set. He is beating defenses before the snap, beating the blitz after the snap, and is doing a little bit of everything else in between. Lawrence is the real deal and then some, and there is no more hiding that.
If there was ever a reminder that the Jaguars' passing game starts and ends with Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, this was it. Washington and Meyers combined for 13 of Lawrence's 26 targets, with the rest of the Jaguars' receivers cdombining for two catches for five yards. Brian Thomas Jr. did not even see a pass go his way, but that didn't stop Washington and Meyers for record 126 receiving yards, including a 50-yard touchdown from Washington.
PARKER WASHINGTON TO THE CRIB. JAXvsBAL on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/M79mYxS3b2
Washington and Meyers are more than good enough to each be the focal point of the offense, which is a moving target that is bound to change a bit more each week. But when the Jaguars' offense does go through its wide receivers, it is very clear which receivers are going to get the bulk of the work between these two.
The Jaguars needed their entire defensive front to step up against the Ravens considering the loss of Davon Hamilton , and that is exactly what the Jaguars got against Derrick Henry. One player who flashed consistently in the place of Hamilton was Albert Regis, the Jaguars' third-round nose tackle who has been a healthy scratch for the last few weeks. Regis showed good effort, some real range as a tackler for a defensive tackle, and some juice as well. It was a strong showing from the rook.
The Jaguars' defense has been much improved in the back-end since they officially got Montaric Brown back healthy. It has allowed the Jaguars to utilize their entire cornerback room with a four-man rotation that allows them to put players in different spots depending on the situation and foe. On Thursday, we saw this rotating come up big for the Jaguars on two different occasions.
Brown and Lewis each recorded an interception, with it being Brown's first interception of the season and the third interception from Lewis. Both interceptions set up field goals, and they were strong signs that the Jaguars' secondary is taking steps forward, one way or another. It was a strong night for both cornerbacks in general, and Jarrian Jones deserves some love too for a quarterback hit and a pass breakup.
Montaric Brown INT! pic.twitter.com/EgwLFjcTrt
It has been a good last few weeks for second-year linebacker Jalen McLeod on special teams, and he made the biggest play of his NFL career thus far during the second-half on Thursday. McLeod made a terrific tackle on a coverage unit and ended up forcing the ball out for the first forced fumble of his career, with the Jaguars scooping up the fumble and eventually kicking a field goal shortly after as a result. That is now three turnovers forced in the last two weeks by second-year Jaguars, which is becoming a bit of a trend for James Gladstone's team moving forward.
Brian Thomas Jr's stat line over the Jaguars' last four games: 1 catch for 12 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. Thomas did not get a ton of playing time seemingly on Thursday as the Jaguars went with 12 and 13 personnel more than 11, and this meant there were limited chances for Thomas to get in on the action. Considering the Jaguars' relatively conservative game-plan on offense, that left little for Thomas to do.
The Jaguars' wide receiver ended Thursday with zero targets despite nine other players getting targets, with Travis Hunter, LeQuint Allen, Chris Rodriguez, Josh Cameron, and Tanner Koziol all getting more looks than him. It remains to be seen if this was his last game as a Jaguar, but this game was clearly not about showcasing his talent ahead of the trade deadline.
Jaguars rookie left guard Emmanuel Pregnon looks like a rookie, which is far from a bad thing. Still, the Jaguars are hopeful Super Bowl contenders and even rookies will have to be held to a high standard for the Jaguars to reach their ultimate goals. Pregnon is a big part of that, and the Jaguars will likely see much better performances from him moving forward than they saw from him on Thursday.
Part of this was due to penalties, with Pregnon getting called for three different false starts. He also had some issues when left on an island in pass-protection, making this a game for Pregnon that has to be about lessons and development. Pregnon is getting some valuable experience, and he did do some good things in the running game, but this wasn't his best game.
Even in a game where the Jaguars sat Bhayshul Tuten down with a few minutes left in the third-quarter to rest him after he entered the game banged up, there still just wasn't much there for LeQuint Allen to do. Allen was seemingly set to enter the year as the No. 3 running back before a training camp injury sidelined him for a few weeks, and he hasn't quite taken the role back from Ameer Abdullah since.
Allen was targeted twice as a check-down in the passing game, but those were the only looks he got with the ball despite the Jaguars' other three running backs toting the ball for 29 carries and two other catches. Allen is a gifted pass-blocker and a key part of the Jaguars' culture, but it seems like his role is set to be capped out there.

title: 8 Instant Observations on Jaguars' Blowout of Ravens: King Henry Gets Slayed
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are 6-2 and hitting their stride.
The Jaguars were big favorites entering Thursday's game, and for good reason after their 33-10 domination over the Baltimore Ravens. The Jaguars have kept it rolling, and here is everything we saw from them on Thursday.
Jesse Minter is one of the best defensive minds in football. He has produced elite units at both the college and the NFL level, and there is a good reason the Ravens tabbed him as the man to replace the legendary John Harbaugh. With that said, there is a decent chance that Minter checks underneath his bed and his closet for Liam Coen offenses after how Coen's unit have performed against Minter's defenses over the years.
Coen-led offenses scored 75 points in two games against Minter's defense over the last two seasons. After the way the Jaguars were able to hit explosive plays when they needed to on Thursday with relative ease, there is no questioning which coach gets the better of their peer whenever Coen and Minter line up on opposite sidelines. Coen offenses have simply gotten the job done every time, and this was another example.
The Ravens went with an offense that looked more like Ribault High School than an NFL unit, largely because of their injury issues at quarterback. With the Ravens starting third-string undrafted free agent quarterback Joe Fagnano
 under center after injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, offensive coordinator Declan Doyle went with a ton of Wildcat and screens to try to take the ball out of his hand. This meant a ton of Derrick Henry, especially early on.
Henry was getting a few solid gains against the Jaguars, more than they normally give up. That should be expected after the loss of Davon Hamilton to a season-ending injury, but it is not like Henry killed them, either. Henry had more success against the Jaguars' run defense than he would have if Hamilton was in the game, but he also did not have any long breakaway run that broke things open. He ran hard, but the Jaguars would likely take this run-game performance each and every time against Henry. Justice Hill had a 65-yard run at the end of the game with the backups in, but this was still a strong game by the run defense.
The Jaguars came out with a ton of 13 personnel on the first drive of the game. It paid off big near the goal-line, of course, but it was just as big at the very start. The Jaguars hit rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher for a big play for the third time in three games with a 52-yard catch to set up the opening drive touchdown, yet another evolution in the Jaguars' usage of the rookie tight end. The Jaguars entered the game with the second-best EPA/dropback in 2+ tight end formations, and this played a big role to start the game.
This is the biggest area where the Jaguars' scheme has grown this year. After mainly being an 11 personnel team a year ago, the Jaguars have really started to lean into their talented and developing tight end room. The Boerkircher pick was panned to a hyperbolic level in April, and the Jaguars are starting to show why it was such a priority for them.
Jaguars linebacker Foyesade Oluokun has been playing some darn good football all season, but especially since the bye week. Oluokun had nine tackles, two tackles for loss and a sack last week, and he was key against the Ravens on Thursday. Oluokun had a big third-down sack in the first-half to get the Jaguars' defense off the field after the Ravens had some momentum, and he didn't stop there.
Oluokun and the Jaguars had a tough task tonight against a Derrick Henry-led attack that featured a lot of Wildcat and unbalanced lines. Oluokun has been playing some of the best football of his career in 2026, and Week 9 was just another example of his game aging like fine wine over the last few seasons. With Ventrell Miller also playing at a high level, the Jaguars have one of the more underrated LB duos in the NFL. The Jaguars need help at a few depth spots on defense, but not at linebacker.
The Jaguars only had four drives in the first half due to the Ravens killing the clock with a run-heavy attack, but that didn't really stop Trevor Lawrence from producing early on. Lawrence had two passes of 50 yards or more in the first-half with his 52-yard throw to Boerkircher and his 50-yard touchdown pass to Parker Washington before halftime. Before Lawrence's big throw to Washington, he had one of his best throws of the season on a tight-window throw to Brenton Strange for a first-down that he threw between three Ravens defenders. Three!
RIDICULOUS tight window throw here from Trevor Lawrence. pic.twitter.com/3eHN5FGfl5
Lawrence should have already been an MVP candidate entering the game. After the flashes he showed in Thursday's game before the rain started really coming down, Lawrence should be right in the mix with Joe Burrow, Josh Allen, and anyone else. Lawrence is making high-level throws at a consistent clip and he is the biggest reason the Jaguars are 6-2 right now.
Have a day, Jaylon Jones. The Jaguars' cornerback and special teamer was signed to the roster after Week 4 with the expectation of him making a very real impact on special teams to replace former core special teamer Christian Braswell. Jones has not played a ton of football for the Jaguars after a hamstring injury early on in his Jaguars tenure, but he was easy to spot on the field during Thursday's win.
Jones made a pair of tackles on coverage units Thursday that showed why he can be exactly the kind of depth piece the Jaguars need moving forward. They need Antonio Johnson and Jarrian Jones on defense instead of special teams, so anything Jones can do for them on special teams is a big boost for them moving forward.
With the Jaguars set to be without star nose tackle Davon Hamilton for the rest of the season, they will need third-round rookie Albert Regis to develop quickly. Regis had barely played up to this point in the season and has been a healthy scratch for the last few weeks, but he was needed on Thursday night after Hamilton went on IR and the Jaguars had no real time to add any true outside reinforcements.
Regis certainly stood out when given a chance to play on Thursday night. He made several impressive plays against the run, showing off the motor and anchor the Jaguars liked in the third-round of the NFL Draft in April. It looked like the best performance he has had so far as a pro, and the Jaguars badly needed it to happen.
If there was one rookie who has been thrown to the fire who did not have a great night, it felt like it was left guard Emmanuel Pregnon. Pregnon has done some solid things for the Jaguars as an every-week starter at guard, and the fact that he has been so reliable for the Jaguars in terms of his availability has been big for a unit that has had some moving pieces. With that said, Sunday felt like one of his weaker games.
Pregnon had a few issues with penalties, which has been an issue throughout the season. He even had one on a PAT attempt, which kind of sums up some of his issues with false starts, holds, and more. Add in a few pressures allowed and this feels like one of the games to forget for the rookie guard.

title: Jaguars' Bhayshul Tuten Will Play vs. Ravens, Which Leaves One Big Question
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Make it 27 out of 28.
Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten is active for the team's Thursday Night Football battle with the Baltimore Ravens, making him the first player in the Coen era to suit up for a game despite not practicing that week. The previous 27 player sin the Coen era who had not practiced before a game did not play that week.
Getting Tuten back is a big deal considering the Jaguars should have the upper hand on paper when it comes to running the ball against the Baltimore Ravens. T he big question now, though, is whether he leads the backfield like he has each week.
Tuten has been the Jaguars' clear RB1 each week, getting more carries than backup running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. in 6-of-7 games. But will Rodriguez get more volume tonight now that Tuten has been injured coming off a short week? The Jaguars have clear trust in the veteran back who they added in free agency, and this seems like a favorable matchup.
Tuten has been the Jaguars' star at running back and if the Jaguars just roll with his usual workload, he could be in for another big performance. If the Jaguars hold him back, we could see something closer to the split backfield many though it would be coming into the season, myself included.
Tuten is coming off the best game of his NFL career in Week 8 against the Indianapolis Colts, recording his first-ever 100-yard rushing game. In the process, he became the first Jaguars running back to have 100-plus rushing yards, 50-plus receiving yards, a rushing touchdown and a receving touchdown in a game.
In seven games this season, Tuten has led the Jaguars' offense with 110 carries for 492 yards and three touchdowns. Add in his 15 catches for 181 yards and three touchdowns, and Tuten is the Jaguars' most productive skill player from scrimmage. In 2026, Tuten ranks tied sixth in touchdowns scored (six) and eighth in scrimmage yards (673) and rushing yards (492) in the AFC.
“It’s really cool. It's one of the really special parts about coaching, seeing guys like Tuten who come in as a rookie and they put their head down and work, and they work, and they work, and it doesn't maybe materialize immediately, but over the course of time, we see it on the practice field, it shows up then on Sundays, and he's still just scratching the surface," Jaguars offensive coordinator Grant Udinski said earlier this week.
"And he knows, and we know, there's even so much more that he can do and accomplish. But it's so special to see a guy like that who does it for all the right reasons, selflessly, cares about his teammates, runs so hard, works hard in pass protection, works hard in the pass game. And maybe we didn't give him the opportunities, but to see some of those things actually materialize on Sunday is really special."
Meanwhile, the Jaguars will have the following players inactive: wide receiver CJ Williams, cornerback Alijah Huzzie, safety Cam'Ron Silmon-Craig, defensive end Wesley Williams. The Jaguars will have rookie nose tackle Albert Regis active and ready to go to help replace Davon Hamilton.

title: Short Week Set Up Could Give Jaguars Fascinating Trade Deadline Window
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have much bigger things on their plate Thursday night than the NFL Trade Deadline. But that could change in a quick 24 hours.
The Jaguars need to take care of business on Thursday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens before they do anything else. The Jaguars are big favorites against a third-string undrafted free agent at quarterback, however, and they should be 6-2 by the end of the night if they are the team they have shown to be.
If/when the Jaguars make it to Friday with another win, they can turn their focus completely to the trade deadline , set for next Tuesday. With obvious needs at a few positions on defense and the never-ending speculation on Brian Thomas Jr., the trade deadline could prove to be eventful for Jacksonville for a few reasons.
Could one of those reasons be in part due to the Jaguars' schedule, though? With the Jaguars playing on Thursday Night Football, they could get a window to attack the trade deadline that other teams have used in recent seasons.
With the Jaguars playing on Thursday night, they can get a few days head start on the deadline. Most moves happen between the end of Sunday's games and the day of the deadline each season, which means that any previous trade movements in the weeks ahead typically do not mean much when it comes to how much action there is on the actual deadline.
In short, deadlines force moves. With this being the final week of games before the deadline, this is the week where many teams have to make decisions to either address their needs toward a playoff push or start selling off roster pieces in a lost season. We have seen each happen over the last two seasons.
In four of the last five seasons, teams playing on Thursday Night Football ended up making deals at the deadline after playing on Thursday. Sometimes, like in 2022 with the Ravens, it was a blockbuster in the form of adding Roquan Smith. Sometimes like last season, it was the Dolphins dealing Jaelan Phillips after falling to 2-7 following a Thursday Night loss to ... the Ravens.
Deadline Trades from TNF Teams
This is not to say we should look too deeply into the trend, but it is worth noting that teams who play on Thursday at least get clarity a bit earlier than the other 28 teams that are set to play before the trade deadline on Tuesday. There are a few teams among those 28 who are worth watching, too.
Could the Arizona Cardinals go into sell mode if a loss to the Seattle Seahawks on the road drops them to 3-6? They have pieces at EDGE, defensive tackle, and safety. The same goes for the Los Angeles Chargers, who would drop to 0-8 with a loss to the Houston Texans. Perhaps the team worth watching the most is the Philadelphia Eagles, who would be 2-7 with a loss to the New York Giants, which could make them more inclined to move a piece like Moro Ojomo.
The Jaguars can underline their targets and know exactly what and who they need a few days earlier than the rest of these teams, especially when it comes to taking a look at their run defense without Davon Hamilton. The Jaguars feel like a real candidate to make a move over the next week, and Thursday could prove to be a big piece of the equation.

title: Jaguars-Ravens Week 9 Picks Roundup: Golden Chance in AFC is at Stake
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The lights of an island game on national telivision are here, and the stage is set for the Jacksonville Jaguars.
There will not be any Trevor Lawrence-Lamar Jackson round three due to an injury to Jackson. We won't see Tyler Huntley either, with Ravens undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano set to make the start. But there will still be a big stage for the Jaguars, along with a big opportunity.
The Jaguars are fighting through their own injuries , losing Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray to season-ending injuries during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Add in running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker being questionable, and the Jaguars are a bit dinged up themselves.
But if the Jaguars can overcome the challenge of a road trip against a talented team on a short week, they can do more than prove their mettle. They can be 6-2 entering a stretch where they play the Tennessee Titans twice in a three-week span, giving them a chance to have real-deal playoff-clinching scenarios in December.
How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below.
Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars
Matt Bowen: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                       Mike Clay: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                     Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                  Dan Graziano: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                  Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                   Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                     Jason Reid: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                          Ben Solak: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                           Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                   Seth Wickersham: Jaguars
Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars
It is hard not to pick the Jaguars here, and they once again get a clean sweep. It feels weird on the Jaguars end of things, but that is because every game has stakes when you are a good team, and the Jaguars are indeed a good team.
The Jaguars have a big chance to make some clear headway toward a potential No. 1 seed in the AFC. They are clumped together right now with the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but they have to get by a rookie quarterback tonight before facing Cam Ward twice and J.J. McCarthy. If the Jaguars go on a run, they could be 9-2 by right after Thanksgiving. That would make them far more than just contenders in the AFC, and it would start with beating Baltimore.
Things could have gotten much more interesting had Jackson been available, but the Jaguars will instead face the dreaded backup quarterback in primetime. Weirdly enough, two of the six losses in the Liam Coen era have been to backup quarterbacks after the Jaguars lost to Jake Browning and Davis Mills a year ago. The only other quarterbacks to beat the Jaguars in the regular-season in that span: Sam Darnold, Matt Stafford, Bo Nix, and CJ Stroud.
The Jaguars have beaten other backup and rookie quarterbacks in that span, defeating Jacoby Brissett, Cam Ward (twice), Brady Cook, Riley Leonard, and for some reason, Philip Rivers last season. This season, they have gotten wins against a few guys who have played in the Super Bowl in Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow, and Drake Maye. Add in wins against Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy and Stroud last year, and the argument thatg the Jaguars have beaten up on bad quarterbacks doesn't make much sense.
The Jaguars are a good team, and I expect Anthony Campanile's defense to get after the Ravens' young passer. Campanile likes to blitz and pressure quarterbacks into intentionally throwing the ball quickly, which helps the defense dictate where the ball will go in coverage. When you know where the ball is going, you can make plays on it or tackle and rally and make stops like the Jaguars have done for two years.
According to NextGenStats, Jacksonville has generated a 39.6% pressure rate this season (8th-highest), and its pressures have arrived in 2.43 seconds on average, the quickest in the NFL. Seven of Jacksonville's pressures have resulted in turnovers, tied for the most in the league, and the Jaguars have generated 31 unblocked pressures, tied for second-most.
This means the Jaguars' pressures are leading to big plays on the back end, and they force the issue with opposing quarterbacks. Against a young quarterback and a running game that has lesser numbers without Lamar Jackson, I think the Jaguars win this game with field position and red-zone stops. Jaguars 30, Ravens 13.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Ravens: Trevor Lawrence's MVP Showcase
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are ready for primetime.
The Jaguars are set to visit the Baltimore Ravens for a key Week 9 Thursday Night Football matchup, and a win would put the Jaguars at 6-2 and in a great spot in a bad AFC South moving into the final few months of the season.
So, how do we see Thursday Night Football play out? We break it down below with this week's bold predictions.
Simply put, Trevor Lawrence has been on a tear this season. There is a strong case to make he has been the best quarterback in football in 2026, with Lawrence noting earlier this week that he believes this is the most consistent stretch of play he has ever had in his career. He has had high peaks before, but it has now become the norm for him to heat up week in and week out and give the Jaguars a chance to win.
I think Lawrence has another hyper-efficient, MVP-caliber game on Thursday, and I will go as far as to say he has another game with a passer rating of 150+ after having one last week against the Colts. Lawrence's two games with a passer rating of 150+ in 2026 are more than the rest of the NFL combined (one). Lawrence leads the NFL with a 112.6 passer rating in 2026, which would be more than 10 points above the best single-season passer rating in Jaguars history (102.2 by David Garrard in 2007), according to NextGenStats.
How rare would this be? There were only seven such games by quarterbacks in all of 2025, with Jalen Hurts, Drake Maye, and Jared Goff doing it twice while Sam Darnold did it once. The last quarterbacks to do it three times in a season were Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in 2024. Liam Coen offenses have been terrific against Jesse Minter defenses in the past, and I think it happens again.
Ronnie Stanley has been a terrific left tackle throughout his career, but he has had a bit of a down season. According to NextGenStats, he has allowed a 11.5% pressure rate this year, 10th highest amongst all qualified left tackles. He will likely matchup with Josh Hines-Allen, who has aligned over the left tackle on almost 80% of his snaps. And according to NGS, Hines-Allen has generated five pressures across 17 career pass rushes against Stanley, generating a 29.4% pressure rate that is the second-highest Stanley has allowed to an individual defender in his career (min. 15 matchups).
The Jaguars' scheme asks its edge defenders to wear a lot of different hats, and Hines-Allen has played well this season in doing so. The Jaguars need defensive line help, but not because of their starting defensive ends. He has produced a few turnovers this season via pressures, and I think he gets home on Thursday night and gets a forced fumble on an undrafted rookie quarterback while doing so.
It remains to be seen if Bhayshul Tuten plays on Thursday after missing each practice this week and being listed as questionable. The fact that he is questionable, and not out, does at least give a chance to play. But regardless of whether he plays, I think the Jaguars' running back room plays well against a Baltimore Ravens front that ranks No. 18 in the NFL in EPA/Rush. Jaguars running back Chris Rodriguez has played well in his role this season, and Ameer Abdullah has some juice as the No. 3 running back.
The Ravens do have some strong players up front such as Travis Jones, Calais Campbell, and Nnamdi Madubuike, but I think we see another productive day from the Jaguars' running back room. The running game has been rolling despite not having an overly dominant offensive line, and that has a lot to do with how their running game is built, regardless of who is taking the bulk of the carries.
Derrick Henry is the thing Jaguars nightmares were made of once upon a time. Henry dominated the Jaguars for years during his Tennessee Titans tenure, with his last year of playing the Jaguars twice resulting in 191 rushing yards and 6.6 yards per carry. He has found paydirt against the Jaguars time and time again, and he is off to another good season in 2026. Add in the season-ending injury to star nose tackle Davon Hamilton, and this is a tough matchup for the Jaguars' top-ranked run defense.
With that said, I think the Jaguars manage to bottle Henry up. No running back with a minimum of five carries has averaged more than 4.0 yards per carry against the Jaguars this season, with Jonah Coleman leading the way at 3.9 yards per carry. Chase Brown had 1.1, TreVeyon Henderson had 2.9, and Jonathan Taylor had 2.9 as well. I think the Jaguars repeat against the Ravens, especially with no Lamar Jackson in the lineup.
Keep this in mind: according to NextGenStats, "Henry is averaging 3.5 yards per carry without Lamar Jackson on the field this season, a full yard less than with
 Jackson on the field (4.5). Henry has also been stuffed more often without Jackson (22.9%) than with him (16.0%), and he 
has been less efficient at keeping drives on schedule, posting a 33.7% success rate without Jackson compared to 49.3%
 with him."
A big reason the Jaguars' offense is so successful each week is the scheme. Trevor Lawrence calls multiple plays in the huddle and changes a ton of plays at the line of scrimmage depending on the look from the defense. This has, at times, gotten the Jaguars into some issues in terms of delay of games and illegal motions/formations, but it has also helped them become an offensive juggernaut.
According to NGS, the Jaguars have snapped the ball with just 7.0 seconds left on the play clock on average this season, second-slowest ahead of only the Pittsburgh Steelers (6.8). The Jaguars have used no huddle just 3.4% of the time (4th-lowest), while their motion rate sits at 74.1% (4th-highest). This all points to a team potentially having more issues on the road than at home, at least in terms of their operation. I think the Jaguars look crisp and like a contender on a short week, though, and avoid any such penalties vs. the Ravens.

title: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars may have to enter Thursday Night Football without one of their top weapons.
The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker.
There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten.
Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity.
“We'll see. I think he'll do something. Yeah, he'll do something," Coen said before practice. "But I would expect... I talked to him today; he said he feels better. I would think it's probably going to go up to game time.”
Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week.
The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played.
The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen.
Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say.
"I would imagine the way he would play football against Cleveland is if he practices the week of Cleveland. If he's able to practice the week of Cleveland and be able to actually feel comfortable, and feel fast and feel firm, then I'd be totally fine. But he's going to have to practice to play, absolutely.”
If that is the Jaguars' stance on injuries and playing, then history might be working against Tuten. The one thing working in his favor is that this is a short week that the Coen-led Jaguars haven't experienced before. Perhaps the wackiness of a Thursday Night Football is the X-Factor here. If not, then expect a decent amount of Chris Rodriguez Jr.

title: Jaguars Stock Report Entering TNF vs. Ravens: Changing Roles in Secondary Take Priority
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are coming off a big win from this past Sunday, but they have also been dealt a few losses since with season-ending injuries to key veterans.
As a result, Week 9 is about to be a test of the Jaguars' depth and their resolve after losing Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray.
"You got four starters get hurt in one game. How do you supplement that? Well, it's through the building. It's through the entire group," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday.
"It's not just, all right, the defensive captains or the offensive captains that need to feel the weight of that. It's the entire building. It's every single one of us, players, coaches, and staff included, to help pick that up.”
So with the Jaguars banged up entering a Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, whose stocks are rising and whose are falling?
The AFC Defensive player of the week. Rayuan Lane had a career performance against the Colts on Sunday, and he is now expected to step into the starting lineup against the Ravens and for likely the rest of the season unless the Jaguars make a move at safety. Lane was stellar in Week 8 and has made plays for the Jaguars in big spots before, giving their staff confidence in his abilities.
Lane is mostly known as a special teams ace, but he has been ready each time his number has been called in 2026. He will now need to be ready for the long haul, with all signs pointing to him as the full-time Eric Murray replacement for the rest of the 2026 season, and potentially even beyond then depending on his performances.
When asked Wednesday about the options on hand at safety, Coen noted three names right off the bat: Antonio Johnson, Rayuan Lane, and Kaevon Merriweather. He did eventually get to talk about third-round rookie Jalen Huskey, but it was very clear that when it comes to the safety spot after Murray's injury, he is fourth in the pecking order.
This, of course, could have already been easily guessed since the Jaguars have rarely deployed Huskey on defense during the first seven games of his NFL career. But if there was any wonder whether an injury to Murray would mean more snaps for Huskey moving forward, it is clear what the answer is now.
Jaguars running back Chris Rodriguez is set to have a large role on Thursday depending on the status of starting running back Bhayshul Tuten. Tuten will be a game-time decision according to Coen, which would obviously put the onus on Rodriguez in the Jaguars' backfield if their leading rusher is not able to push past his foot/ankle injury.
Rodriguez has gotten better and better as the season has gone on, and he has some of the best efficiency numbers of any running back in the NFL. Getting a larger workload is something that he has had to do as a backup running back in his career before, too, so there should be no doubt as to whether he would be up for the challenge.
Perhaps the Jaguars didn't deploy Jarrian Jones completely on Sunday due to injury, with the Jaguars' third-year versatile cornerback only playing 12 snaps in the blowout win. Jones has been limited this week in practice with an ankle injury, which makes this a plausible scenario. But with Montaric Brown completely healthy and playing well against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8, it begs to question just how large of a role Jones will have week-to-week other than spelling Jourdan Lewis.
Jones was playing much better than he has been given credit for during his few weeks starting opposite of Travis Hunter on the outside, with his only real down performance coming against the Houston Texans in Week 6. But for now, Jones is a player with a role worth watching moving forward into Thursday. It feels like this is injury-related, but Thursday will tell us.
The Jaguars saw some real positive signs from Branson Combs in coverage against the Indianapolis Colts. Combs has been their coverage linebacker since the offseason program, and on Sunday he showed the strides the Jaguars have been excited for since seeing him take genuine steps toward improvement after his rookie season.
"To have your third linebacker that we know that we had a lot of faith in come in and make an impact on special teams the way he did with the two big hits on our sideline and to get the interception, we've seen that kind of play from him out here in training camp," Coen said Wednesday. "Going up, climbing the ladder and making a great catch on an interception this training camp. He's got good ball skills and the more he can do for our team, the better we'll be.”
With Eric Murray out for the year , perhaps Combs is someone the Jaguars look to more in obvious passing situations in the middle of the field. He and Murray play very, very different roles and positions, but it could be a way to get the Jaguars' best athletes on the field.

title: The Jaguars’ Most Likely Trade Deadline Move: Finding Reinforcements for Davon Hamilton
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars should have one clear focus when it comes to the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline: replacing Davon Hamilton.
There might be no true replacement for the heart and soul of the Jaguars' run defense in Hamilton, who sustained a season-ending injury in Week 8 against the Indianapolis Colts. The Jaguars already likely wanted to swing for defensive tackle help before Hamilton's injury, but they are now forced into a significantly higher place of anxiety and urgency with the deadline approaching.
Consider this from NFL's NextGenStats: The Jaguars have allowed 6.9 yards per play without DaVon Hamilton on the field this season, over 3.0 yards more than their average with him on it (3.8). They’ve specifically allowed 3.8 yards per carry and 8.8 yards per attempt without Hamilton (3.1 and 5.3 with, respectively). The Jaguars have also allowed an 18.8% explosive play rate without Hamilton, which would be the highest by any defense since at least 2016. Their 6.2% explosive play rate allowed with Hamilton would be the lowest.
In short, Hamilton is arguably the most important player to their success this year who isn't named Trevor Lawrence. With Hamilton out and the Jaguars needing reinforcements, it is clear where their trade deadline focus is set to be. That is why addressing the position is the team's most likely move going forward.
All reports indicate the Jaguars are looking seriously at adding some defensive tackle help. The Jaguars reportedly were interested in Jeffery Simmons despite knowing that the Titans would not send him to another team in the AFC South. This means the Jaguars will have to look to other defensive tackles throughout the league to bolster their front, which adds an interesting question.
Do the Jaguars try to swing back and land a pass-rushing three-technique like Moro Ojomo, and then opt to let a platoon handle the loss of Hamilton? The committee option is how the Jaguars are entering Week 9 against the Baltimore Ravens, though that is much more out of necessity than anything else. Still, the Jaguars will get a chance on Thursday night to see what that kind of strategy may look like in terms of results with Arik Armstead, Ruke Orhorhoro, Austin Johnson, Matt Dickerson, and Albert Regis.
"On a short week, we got to have those guys step up to play. Regis has gotten better and better over the last few weeks, specifically giving us fits on the show team, has made our offensive line better over the last few weeks on the show team, and now it’s going to be a great opportunity for him to step up and give us some quality snaps," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday.
"Dickie's [Dickerson] been playing well. Ruke's been playing well. Arik had a really good game yesterday. It's going to be by committee. Those guys are all going to have to play meaningful snaps for us and help us stop a darn good run game and running back in [Ravens RB] Derrick Henry.”
So, let's say the Jaguars are able to patch together a rotation to replace Hamilton in the aggregate instead of just with one player. Finding a replacement nose tackle is easier said than done when it comes to finding one like Hamilton. There are options such as Los Angeles Chargers defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson, but this isn't where a big swing would likely come from.
Instead, it feels like that swing is more likely than not going to come from a pass-rusher inside, whether that be Ojomo, Zach Sieler, Christian Barmore, or a lesser-known player like Roy Lopez. The Jaguars were already clearly making this a focus before anything happened to Hamilton, and they have no reason to change course now.
John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. Previously, he covered UCF's undefeated season as a beat reporter for NSM.Today, covered high school prep sports in Central Florida, and covered local sports and news for the Palatka Daily News.
