title: Rams Midweek Report: A Concerning Trend on Offense, Matthew Stafford's Elbow, and Trade Buzz
full_text:
Through the first eight weeks of the NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams’ offense has been productive but inconsistent, to say the least. The Rams rank fourth in yards per game and third in offensive success rate. However, after failing to score 20 points against the Arizona Cardinals before scoring 35 against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams went three-and-out on their first five possessions last week against the Los Angeles Chargers. That was something that a Rams offense hadn’t done this century.
The Rams’ offense has had its games in which it has looked like a top-5 unit. However, they have struggled to find consistency. For an offense that made things look easy at times in 2025, the Rams have looked condensed and lacked the same level of explosiveness.
There is certainly some context to that as Davante Adams and Puka Nacua have each missed games. Terrance Ferguson has also been out since Week 3. At the same time, the Rams haven’t pushed the ball down the field very often.
Through eight weeks this season, the Rams’ passing game has an explosive play rate of just 4.1 percent. At this point last year, the passing game had an explosive play rate of 17.5 percent and it was 18.2 percent for the season.
The passing game is less than one-fourth as explosive as it was last year. That lack of explosiveness certainly helps explain some of the Rams’ troubles scoring consistently. Picking up yards hasn’t been an issue. The Rams also rank sixth in touchdown rate once they get into the red zone.
However, the Rams rank just 16th in points per play and have the seventh most plays per drive. The Rams are having to work extremely hard for their points because they have struggled to generate explosive plays.
Since Davante Adams went down with an injury, the Rams have just one passing play over 20 yards, and it was the 40-yard pass to Tutu Atwell last week. They have an overall explosive play rate of 5.8 percent, which ranks 27th.
The Rams have found success out of 13 personnel, but at some point the Rams need to be able to throw the ball. It’s easy to run against inferior teams when the game script is in your favor. However, when that goes south against a true contender, they need to be able to have confidence in their passing game. The eventual return of Ferguson and Adams will help, but is it enough?
Two of Matthew Stafford’s 10 lowest single-game averages in intended air yards per attempt have come this season. He has had four straight games averaging under six intended air yards per pass attempt. Over the last four weeks, Stafford has an average depth of target of 5.5 yards, ranking 25 out of 27 quarterbacks.
That’s simply not a world the Rams can live in consistently. When the quarterback isn’t pushing the ball down the field, there’s more pressure on the skill players to create after the catch.. Outside of Puka Nacua, there isn’t anybody the Rams trust to do that.
The Rams may be able to manage the situation until their bye week. However, it’s also a reason why adding a third wide receiver is so imperative to their success over the second half of the year.
One of the big stories coming out of Sunday’s game was Matthew Stafford being seen leaving the locker room with a bag of ice around his arm. Coincidentally, after not showing up on the injury report all season, Stafford was listed with a right elbow injury this week.
Despite Stafford saying he’s fine, this isn’t something to completely sweep under the rug either. It’s well known that Stafford is one of the toughest quarterbacks in the NFL. It will take more than an elbow injury to keep him out.
“Listen, I'm 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks,” said Stafford on Wednesday. “A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year. Again, I haven’t missed a rep at practice. I haven’t missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I'm not too worried about it.”
That’s what anybody would expect Stafford to say. He’s not going to let on that he’s in more pain than he’s actually in or dealing with something that would be considered concerning. Here’s what I will say, and it has since been confirmed to me by multiple sources.
According to Doug McCain of 97.1 The Fan LA, who is highly connected in LA Sports, Stafford suffered an elbow injury against the Denver Broncos, specifically when trying to tackle Talanoa Hufanga on the pick-6. It reportedly got to a point where the team was considering surgery. However, Stafford has opted to play through it and try to get right.
The Rams have a history of downplaying injuries. Look no further than this season with Myles Garrett. You can also point to Stafford’s back injury prior to last season and his elbow injury in 2022. Again, Stafford is going to try and play through it, which he has done successfully up to this point. At the same time, it is a situation worth monitoring.
This week, the Rams opened up Myles Garrett’s practice window . The Rams will now have 21 days to opt to take Garrett off of injured reserve and put him on the active roster. It’s important to clarify that just because the Rams activated Garrett’s practice window, it does not mean he will play on Sunday. His return could still happen after the bye week, as that would be when his 21-day practice window expires.
With that said, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier this week that when Garrett gets on the field for practice, it should all happen quickly. The expectation is for Garrett to play this week, but the Rams have prioritized a return to performance, not just a return to play.
“It's about that return to performance and a lot of it's going to be predicated on his communication and feedback to us,” McVay said. “Ultimately, being able to see that hopefully the expectation is he's ready to rock this week.”
Garrett practicing this week is certainly a positive. If he does play, it seems unlikely that he would play every snap on defense. The Rams have a strong rotation with Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey. They will likely lean on that. The important thing is for Garrett to get on the field and feel like himself.
Things have remained quiet on the trade front for the Rams . However, that doesn’t mean they haven’t made calls or been monitoring certain situations. The Rams may not be players at the deadline, but they have at least done their due diligence.
What I will say is that they have called on wide receivers, specifically Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. However, if a move does get done, it won’t happen until next week. According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz , the Colts are trying to maximize draft capital out of their roster and believe teams could up their offers after Sunday as the trade deadline gets closer.
Schultz named Downs as one of the players to monitor who could be on the move. However, after willingly giving up Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, the Colts are holding out on players like Downs and Jonathan Taylor. Right now, it appears the Pittsburgh Steelers and Kansas City Chiefs are the main players on Downs, but the Rams have called.
Earlier this week, the Rams cut wide receiver and returner Alex Bachman before re-signing him to their practice squad. As of now, it appears the Rams may be handing return duties over to Kyren Williams or Tutu Atwell. With that said, Williams is unlikely to offer more as a returner than Bachman and risks getting hurt. Atwell hasn’t returned punts since his rookie season, when he got hurt doing so.
Brennan Presley earned Second-Team All-Big 12 honors as a returner in 2022. He’s performed well in his preseason opportunities. Presley is exactly the type of player who should be a primary special teams contributor. It seems worth at least bringing him up to see what he can do.

title: Rams' Trade Deadline Priorities Shouldn't Change Despite Jaylen Watson Injury
full_text:
With less than a week to go before the NFL trade deadline, it remains unclear whether the Los Angeles Rams will be active. On Wednesday, the Rams announced that cornerback Jaylen Watson would undergo shoulder surgery and be done for the season. With needs at wide receiver and defensive line, it’s fair to wonder if cornerback is now added to the list as well.
Over the last two weeks, head coach Sean McVay has talked a lot about opportunity cost and how the price of acquiring a player could prevent the Rams from making a move.
“I would never rule out opportunities to get better, but at what opportunity cost?” McVay said on Monday. “You have to be able to figure out what does that look like for the long and the short.”
As it stands, it seems unlikely that the Rams will be active at the trade deadline, but the injury to Watson certainly adds a wrinkle. While the Rams may have a need at cornerback with Watson out, the needs at wide receiver and even defensive line remain far greater.
For the most part, the Rams should be able to manage at cornerback without Watson . Defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake has done a great job with the depth of that group, specifically with Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes.
According to Pro Football Focus, Wallace and Forbes both rank among the top 12 cornerbacks in the NFL. Forbes has a coverage grade of 79.9, which ranks seventh, and Wallace ranks 12 with a coverage grade of 76.4.
Additionally, Wallace ranks sixth in yards per coverage snap in 2026, and Forbes’ 0.49 yards per coverage snap ranks seventh. Forbes has been in more of a rotational role, but through eight weeks Wallace has the second-most snaps at cornerback on the roster behind Jaylen Watson.
“Josh has played a lot of snaps,” said McVay. “They both have played a bunch of meaningful snaps and they've earned the confidence of their teammates, their coaches, and I'm excited for them.”
Without Watson in Week 4 and McDuffie in Weeks 6 and 7, Wallace has played a large role on defense and stepped in nicely. It’s certainly different having to do that over the course of a season rather than filling in for a week or two here and there. At the same time, Wallace has done well in those opportunities. Wallace doesn’t give the Rams the same length as they would have with Watson, but he still brings decent size and has tackled well.
Despite the opening at cornerback, the Rams' priorities at the trade deadline should remain adding a wide receiver and a defensive lineman. The Rams aren’t going to be able to replace Davante Adams, but adding a third wide receiver who can play alongside him and Puka Nacua would make sense.
This season, Konata Mumpfield has remained extremely inefficient. Mumpfield has caught just 9-of-21 targets and has a -0.32 EPA per target. Tutu Atwell remains a limited receiver and Jordan Whittington is simply a special teams player.
It’s true that the Rams operate a lot of their offense out of 13 personnel, but that only works in a neutral-to-positive game script. In situations when the Rams have to throw the ball or are trailing, they have to be able to have three wide receivers on the field. Right now, even when Adams comes back, it’s hard to feel confident in them doing that. The Rams rank tied for 15th in EPA per pass out of 11 personnel.
At some point, it’s fair to say that the Rams will miss Poona Ford’s presence in the middle of the defensive line. The Las Vegas Raiders don’t have a strong rushing attack, and the same can be said about the Los Angeles Chargers. Ford played a big role in the Rams’ defense performing well against the run last season. Without Ford, the Rams are asking a lot of Ty Davis and Ty Hamilton to fill that void.
The Rams aren’t going to be able to address every need at the trade deadline if they opt to make a move. They will have to prioritize which positions make the most sense to address and whether adding a player at those positions would help close the gap as they push for a playoff spot in the second half of the season. While the Rams have a need at cornerback with Watson’s season coming to an end, the needs at wide receiver and defensive line remain much greater.

title: Rams vs. Commanders Prediction: Preview, Key Matchups, and What to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams finally won back-to-back games for the first time this season last week, beating the Los Angeles Chargers. Now, the Rams will head on the road to take on the Washington Commanders as they look to carry that momentum.
Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams have been inconsistent, but over the last two weeks, they’ve seemingly found their identity . The Rams have leaned into 13 personnel and the run game, making things easier on offense. They arguably had their best offensive performance two weeks ago against the Las Vegas Raiders and then were able to turn things around in the second half last week with a similar approach.
This season, the Commanders have been up-and-down as well, as they’ve managed an elbow injury to Jayden Daniels. However, despite being 2-4-1, they’ve played the NFC West tough. The Commanders beat the Seattle Seahawks back in Week 3 and then lost to the San Francisco 49ers by six.
After having a pass rate over expected of +4.9 in the first six weeks of the season, that has dropped to +0.6 over the last two games. The Rams have been much more balanced on offense and will look to continue that against the Commanders. This season, the Commanders rank 30th in EPA per rush allowed and 31st in defensive rushing success rate.
One of the best rookies this season has been linebacker Sonny Styles. It wouldn’t be surprising to see Sean McVay test Styles’ eye discipline, but his athleticism has been special to watch. Styles has had a Fred Warner-esque effect on the Commanders defense in coverage because of his range. The Rams have relied on their running backs in the passing game more often, and Styles will match up against them well. Styles also ran through Saquon Barkley in Week 1 on a blitz. The Rams’ running backs are going to have their hands full with Styles.
"That's not normal." DQ on Sonny Styles in coverage. #Commanders HC Dan Quinn and @LoganPaulsenNFL went to the 49ers tape for three Sonny plays: a square tackle in space, a third-down breakup on Mike Evans that had DQ comparing his range to Fred Warner's, and Sonny dropping into… pic.twitter.com/M6Td3iVtwc
This could be the first game back for Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett. That will certainly provide a boost for the Rams’ pass rush. Through Week 8, quarterback Jayden Daniels has yet to throw an interception, but with a new offensive coordinator, Daniels ranks 14th in EPA per play, and when he’s forced to throw, he ranks 19th. The Rams have struggled at times with running quarterbacks, notably Josh Allen in Week 5. Meanwhile, the Commanders have a scramble rate of 9.5 percent, which is the fourth-highest in the NFL. Having Garrett back could help with that, but the Rams’ linebackers will need to be on their game.
The Commanders have been steady at right tackle with Josh Conerly Jr. However, Brandon Coleman is susceptible to allowing pressure on the left side. Coleman has allowed 23 pressures this season, which is the seventh-most in the NFL. His 60.5 pass-blocking grade via PFF also ranks 49th out of 60 qualifying tackles. That should provide an opportunity for Josaiah Stewart to generate pressure and for Garrett to make an impact if he does play.
For a second time this season, the Rams will be playing an early game on the east coast. The last time was back in Week 4, when it took a 10-point fourth-quarter comeback for the Rams to win. If the Rams lean on 13 personnel and the run game, they should win this game. The Commanders don’t have Terry McLaurin and could struggle on offense. The Rams can’t get pass-happy in this game and risk falling behind. They need Kyren Williams and Blake Corum to combine for 25-30 carries, and that will put the offense in a good spot. Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 23

title: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
full_text:
While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury.
The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers.
“The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.”
McDuffie was also a non-participant in practice with a back injury that he suffered at the end of Sunday’s game against the Chargers. He’ll be a player to monitor throughout the week. Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), and safety Kam Curl (foot) also didn’t participate in practice. Parkinson missed last week’s game and he’ll be one to watch as well.
While the Rams got bad news with Watson, Wednesday marked the first time since Week 1 that Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald were on the practice field together . Garrett opened his 21-day practice window on Wednesday, leaving open the possibility that he could play against the Commanders.
“It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.”
The Rams are taking it day-by-day with Garrett. McVay made comparisons to the 2022 season with the number of injuries that the Rams have dealt with. They have erred on the side of caution with Garrett since training camp and that will likely continue.
In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams.  Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back).
Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury.
“It feels good. Full practice as I have been all year and hope to continue to be that way,” said Stafford. “Listen, I'm 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks. A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year. Again, I haven’t missed a rep at practice. I haven’t missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I'm not too worried about it.”
On the Washington Commanders’ side, quarterback Jayden Daniels was listed as a full participant with a left elbow injury that he’s managed most of the season. Wide receiver Treylon Burks and Stefon Diggs didn’t practice. However, Diggs missed practice for rest purposes.
For every step forward that the Rams seem to take on the injury front, they continue to take another step back. Garrett and Ferguson returning to practice are certainly encouraging developments, but losing Watson for the season is a significant blow. With McDuffie now dealing with a back injury, the Rams will need to hope that their improving health along the defensive front can help offset some of the concerns in the secondary.

title: Why the Rams' 2026 Bye Week Is Causing Controversy
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are quickly approaching their bye week, which is set to take place in Week 11. However, it won’t be a typical bye week that most teams get. While most teams get a full week off, making it 14 days between games, the Rams are only getting 10 days . Essentially, the Rams’ bye week has been negated with a mini-bye.
On Tuesday, Kelly Stafford posted a story on Instagram, criticizing the NFL for its scheduling choice.
Kelly Stafford, wife of #Rams QB Matthew Stafford, calls out the NFL for the team's bye being only 10 days. Because the Rams host the Packers on Wednesday night (Thanksgiving Eve), their Week 11 bye is only 10 days between games instead of the usual 14. pic.twitter.com/jdrdjispll
“Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week,” wrote Stafford. “Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season and I have never played a single snap. I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel.”
Instead of a typical bye week, the Rams will have a shortened break because of their upcoming Wednesday matchup against the Green Bay Packers. Stafford mentioned that the Rams are the only team to have a shortened bye week, but it’s worth mentioning that the Packers will be in the same situation.
The NFL did the right thing by putting the Rams and Packers in the same situation with both teams playing on a Wednesday. At the same time, the Rams were just one of three teams with a negated bye week in 2026.
With that said, the Rams got more rest after Week 1 coming back from Australia. They’ll get 10 days off for their actual bye and then eight days off before playing the Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams will then get a third-mini-bye before they play the San Francisco 49ers in Week 14.
When the NFL released its schedule, the Rams were a team with a significant rest disadvantage. The Rams were set to play five games with less rest than their opponen t. According to Warren Sharp ’s schedule analysis, the Rams were tied for 24th in net rest in 2026.
There is certainly reason for criticism for how the NFL came up with the Rams’ schedule. The lack of a true bye week is one of them.With that said, the Packers will be in the same situation.
That doesn’t mean that the NFL shouldn’t be criticized. Just because another team is in the same situation doesn’t make it right. Teams are given one bye week per season and the NFL has taken that away from two teams. With the NFL scheduling games on Thanksgiving Eve , it wouldn’t be surprising if two more teams faced the same situation next year.
Given that Kelly Stafford spoke out about the Rams’ lack of a true bye week, it’s fair to wonder if the players, especially Matthew Stafford, feel the same way. With the number of injuries that the Rams have had to manage this season, the extra four days would likely have been beneficial.

title: Rams May Be Better Equipped to Overcome Jaylen Watson Injury Than Expected
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams got more bad injury news on Wednesday when it was reported that cornerback Jaylen Watson would undergo shoulder surgery , ending his 2026 season. It has been a consistent theme for the Rams in 2026, and just as they were set to get Myles Garrett back, Watson is now out for the year.
There’s no doubt that losing Watson will be a huge blow to the secondary. The Rams made Watson their top free agent target in the spring after trading for his teammate Trent McDuffie. After giving up 346 yards passing and three touchdowns to Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams made it a point to rebuild their cornerback room and Watson was a big part of that.
Among qualifying cornerbacks, Watson’s 0.71 yards per coverage snap ranked 10th in the NFL. His 4.87 yards per target ranked sixth. The Rams signed Watson to give them a lengthy, physical outside cornerback to play on the boundary and he’s been able to provide that. Watson has nine pass breakups, which ranks fifth this season.
With Watson out, the Rams will be relying on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in his spot. While there is certainly a difference in being a rotational player and playing full time, the Rams have gotten good production out of Wallace and Forbes this season.
“I think those guys have done really well," said head coach Sean McVay. "Jimmy Lake has done such a great job really with those corners as a whole group. Josh has played a lot of snaps. I thought 'E-Forbes' really played well last week. Both of those guys have been tapped in. They've been ready to step up and it seems like there have been a lot of games that we've had our top corners get banged up and they've played a lot more."
Wallace ranks sixth in yards per coverage snap in 2026 and he’s played often. When Watson was hurt in Week 4, Wallace played 100 percent of the defensive snaps. He also played all of the defensive snaps in Weeks 6 and 7 with McDuffie out due to injury. Wallace may be a rotational player, but he’s played just five snaps fewer than Watson this season on defense and more snaps than McDuffie.
Additionally, Emmanuel Forbes has played well in 2026. Using Forbes less in a smaller, rotational role has benefited both the team and the player. The Rams have been able to be more selective about the situations he plays in.
Forbes’ 0.49 yards per coverage snap ranks seventh in the NFL and his 3.13 yards per target ranks fourth. Despite playing just 25 percent of the defensive snaps this season, Forbes has been credited with seven impact plays via Sumer Sports.
According to Pro Football Focus, Wallace and Forbes both rank among the top 12 cornerbacks in coverage grade. Forbes has a coverage grade of 79.9, which ranks seventh, and Wallace ranks 12 with a coverage grade of 76.4.
While it may have been disappointing when the Rams lost Aubrey Pleasant in the offseason, the impact that defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake has had on the cornerback room can’t go unnoticed. Under Lake, Wallace and Forbes have developed into reliable depth cornerbacks who have held their own when called upon. The Rams also signed Cam Lampkin to the active roster on Tuesday, who was a preseason and training camp standout.
Given that Wallace has played in a full-time role for much of the season, the moment shouldn’t be too big for him. Wallace has gotten grabby at times as he’s been called for three defensive pass interference penalties. However, for the most part, he’s exceeded expectations.
Again, losing Watson for the season is a significant blow to the defense. However, Wallace has stepped in well when his number has been called and Forbes has also played well. The Rams have spent much of the season overcoming injuries, and Watson's absence presents another challenge. With Watson out, the Rams’ depth will certainly be tested, but based on what Wallace and Forbes have shown, there’s reason for optimism.

title: Rams Suffer Another Major Injury Blow as Jaylen Watson Ruled Out for Season
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without cornerback Jaylen Watson for the rest of the season . After re-injuring his shoulder, Watson will undergo surgery, ending his 2026.
Rams CB Jaylen Watson is getting shoulder surgery and is out for the season.
Watson left in the third quarter of Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers after aggravating a shoulder injury. He had previously dislocated his shoulder in Week 3 and was forced to miss one game. Watson had played the next two games without issues, but re-injured his shoulder on Sunday.
Head coach Sean McVay discussed Watson’s shoulder injury during his media availability on Monday and expressed optimism about his status. However, after further evaluation, it was decided that surgery was the best option.
“We'll see what his status looks like as the week progresses,” McVay said on Monday. “Came in, had some good strength, feeling good and optimistic. We'll take his status a day at a time and see where he's at by the time the game rolls around.”
Watson now heads on injured reserve and is set to miss the rest of the year. In Watson’s place, the Rams will likely rely on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes. Wallace has filled in for both Trent McDuffie and Watson this season. He has quietly developed into a reliable depth cornerback. Wallace has allowed 0.71 yards per coverage snap in 2026, ranking 20th in the NFL among qualifying cornerbacks. Forbes has also played well in a smaller role and will be relied on going forward as well.
Coming into the season, Watson was one of the Rams’ big offseason additions. After allowing Sam Darnold to throw for 346 yards and three touchdowns in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams made it a point to rebuild their cornerback room.Watson was the team’s big free-agent signing following its trade for McDuffie.
The Rams simply can’t seem to shake the injury bug this season. It has been one injury after another all year. Two weeks ago, the Rams had to place Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, and Davante Adams on injured reserve. Just when it seemed like they were going to get healthy and get Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson back , the Rams had to place Watson on injured reserve.
Losing Watson is another blow to the defense that the Rams will have to manage over the second half of the season. Wallace and Forbes have shown that they can step up when needed, but Watson being out for the year is still a significant loss for a secondary that had finally started to find its footing.

title: Rams Could Find Low-Cost, High-Reward Wide Receiver Solution in Brandon Aiyuk (But It's Complicated)
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams approach the NFL trade deadline, there’s no doubt that they are in need of a wide receiver . Without Davante Adams, the Rams have struggled with their receiver depth options outside of Puka Nacua.
It’s possible that the Rams could look into making a trade for a player like Josh Downs or Brian Thomas Jr. However, with the market as competitive as it is at wide receiver, Downs and Thomas may require more draft capital than the Rams would want to give up.
On Tuesday, another option potentially became available as San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk requested reinstatement from the NFL . Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus to be his agent, who said that the wide receiver is healthy and ready to get back on the field.
According to reports, Aiyuk is prepared to report to the team’s facility on Friday. Once he does, the 49ers can’t turn him away and the options would be to cut him or find a trade. With that said, it’s unlikely that a team would give up any draft capital for Aiyuk given the 49ers’ situation. If the 49ers are set on trading him,  it’s hard to see him getting  moved inside the division.
The move Brandon Aiyuk could’ve made months ago to force the #49ers ’ hand. Now finally headed to the facility. Kyle Shanahan was asked in September if Aiyuk was an option and he said no. So this will seemingly result in Aiyuk’s release. https://t.co/269oQTmYqd
On Wednesday, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan reiterated that he doesn’t have any expectations for Aiyuk and that he’s moved on from the situation mentally. As Shanahan noted in September, he said that Aiyuk is not an option for the team anymore.
After signing a four-year, $120 million extension, Aiyuk tore his ACL, MCL and meniscus and stopped showing up to the team facility. The 49ers voided $27 million in future guarantees owed to Aiyuk and placed him on the Reserve/Left Squad list last December.
Over the summer, Aiyuk went on social media, calling out Shanahan and general manager John Lynch, effectively burning that bridge. Despite some interest from the Washington Commanders in the offseason, Aiyuk’s actions turned off Washington’s front office.
It seems unlikely that the Rams would go after Aiyuk, but it may be something worth at least exploring, especially considering their current wide receiver situation. Aiyuk hasn’t played since 2024, but he would still be an upgrade over Konata Mumpfield. If the 49ers released him, the Rams would not be responsible for the remainder of his $120 million contract that he signed in 2024. If Aiyuk is cut, he enters the open market as a free agent.
The situation could be similar to how the Rams handled Odell Beckham Jr. in 2021. In 2021, Beckham signed with the Rams on a one-year contract with a base salary of the league minimum, which was $750,000 at the time. The Rams then added up to $4.25 million in performance and postseason incentives.
There is certainly some risk with Aiyuk considering his injury history and that he hasn’t played in two years. Given that he’s burned several bridges with his social media outbursts, that may be a distraction that a team doesn't want to take on midseason.
Still, when Aiyuk was healthy, he was a borderline top-10 wide receiver. He had 1,300 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023. Aiyuk had eight touchdowns the season prior. Until 2024, he had five or more touchdowns in each of his first four seasons.
In 2023, Aiyuk’s 3.02 yards per route run ranked third behind Tyreek Hill and Nico Collins. His 0.73 EPA per target also ranked second in the NFL.
The off-field stuff is certainly concerning. However, McVay and the Rams have dealt with that before. Jalen Ramsey was considered a locker room cancer before the Rams traded for him. Ramsey became one of the best leaders on defense. When the Rams added Odell Beckham Jr., he had the locker room cancer stigma as well. Beckham played a big role in the Rams’ Super Bowl run as Robert Woods got hurt.
McVay has managed big personalities in the past. Ndamukong Suh was another player that fit that description as well as Baker Mayfield in 2022. If Aiyuk is serious about getting back on the field and returning to play at a high level, it may be a situation to look into.
One of the biggest issues for the Rams at the trade deadline is weighing the potential reward against the cost. When McVay has talked about the possibility of a trade , he’s brought up the team’s lack of draft capital.
“Sometimes you have to really ask yourself what kind of resources are you willing to give up?” McVay said on Monday. “I would never rule out opportunities to get better, but at what opportunity cost? You have to have another person that's willing to do it and you have to have somebody that you feel like would add a lot of value to your roster, and then what are the resources that you would be willing to give up when you're looking at it as a whole?”
If the 49ers were to simply release Aiyuk, the Rams wouldn’t have to give up anything draft capital-wise. He’s a player that fills a need, wouldn’t cost a lot, and has experience in the system. It doesn’t hurt that he’d also get the opportunity to face the 49ers twice a year, especially if there is still animosity between the two sides.
Again, this isn’t to say that the Rams need to sign Aiyuk, but just that it’s something they should explore if he becomes available. Aiyuk comes with obvious baggage, but he also brings a level of talent that rarely becomes available at this point in the season. The Rams benefitted from a similar situation in 2021 with Beckham. If the Rams can add an upgrade at a position of need without sacrificing draft capital, it's an opportunity worth considering. Aiyuk could be a low-risk, high-reward opportunity that Les Snead and McVay can't afford to overlook.

title: Rams May Have Answer to Return Game Struggles in Preseason Standout
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams released punt returner and wide receiver Alex Bachman on Tuesday, leaving a need at the position. Since making the move, there has been a lot of uncertainty about who will take over the role.
Releasing Bachman was certainly needed as it was time for the Rams to raise the bar from “just catch the punt.” Bachman averaged 5.2 yards per punt return and 22.9 yards per kick return. Bachman offered more reliability than Xavier Smith, but it still wasn’t good enough.
While Konata Mumpfield is listed as the backup punt returner, it’s unlikely that he’ll take that role. Some have brought up Tutu Atwell, but that’s not something that he’s done throughout his career. Atwell returned 10 punts as a rookie in 2021 before getting hurt and then returned just four punts in three years at Louisville.
It’s certainly possible that the Rams could look into trading for Josh Downs or even Chimere Dike if he’s available. At the same time, Downs may cost draft capital that the Rams don’t want to part with and Dike hasn’t offered a lot as a receiver in his career.
Before the Rams make a move, they will likely move forward with players already in the building. One who makes the most sense is wide receiver Brennan Presley.
Presley was signed as an undrafted free agent last year and has had impressive moments in the preseason . Presley had 14 receptions for 125 yards in the preseason with a touchdown this year. During the 2025 preseason, Presley’s 164 receiving yards ranked fourth.
What a catch from Brennan Presley in the endzone! 🤲 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/8zZMy6r9Sa
However, where the Rams will likely utilize Presley is on special teams as a returner. At Oklahoma State, he earned second-team All-Big 12 honors as a kick returner in 2021 and was twice named the Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Week. In 2024, he became the only Power Conference player to record at least 760 receiving yards, 200 kickoff return yards, and 50 rushing yards in a season.
In five years at Oklahoma State , Presley returned 51 punts and 61 kickoffs. However, most of his impact was felt as a returner on kickoffs. His 100-yard kickoff return against Oklahoma in 2021 helped lead the Cowboys to a 37-33 win.
We got Brennan Presley just chillen on the practice squad btw pic.twitter.com/N25BAk2dcr
Presley has had limited return opportunities in the preseason with the Rams. During the 2025 preseason, he had a 38-yard return on a kickoff and then averaged 29.5 yards per kickoff return during the preseason this year. As a punt returner, Presley has just two punt returns the last two years, averaging 5.5 yards per return. It is worth noting that Presley had seven muffed punts at Oklahoma State.
While Presley hasn’t been on the active roster, he has spent the last two years on the practice squad. As the Rams continue to look to improve their special teams, Presley might be exactly what they need. The Rams are currently averaging just 23.5 yards per kickoff return, which ranks 29th in the NFL. While it’s been better over the last four weeks, there is still room for improvement.
The Rams have spent much of the season trying to find answers on special teams. After adding Joshua Karty to help the kickoff coverage last week, they are focusing on the return game this week. Releasing Bachman was another step in working to improve in that facet. Presley’s upside is certainly intriguing, and his experience and speed make him an option worth exploring. His performance in the preseason has at least earned him that opportunity.

title: Myles Garrett's Return to Practice Could Change Everything for Rams
full_text:
For much of the season, the Los Angeles Rams have been waiting to reap the rewards of the big trade they made this offseason when they acquired edge rusher Myles Garrett. After managing knee swelling in training camp and then not playing at 100 percent in Week 1, Garrett has been on injured reserve since. However, Garrett is finally set to return to practice this week .
To be clear, that doesn’t necessarily mean that Garrett will play on Sunday against the Washington Commanders, but it’s also the first good news that the Rams have gotten on him in two months. With that said, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported that when Garrett gets on the field for practice, it should all happen quickly, leaving this week in play.
“I want to be careful to even set any sort of expectations. I think taking it a day at a time is going to be the best way that we can approach it,” said head coach Sean McVay on Monday. “That's the right thing for him and to see how he responds. I think it's a real positive that we're starting his clock.”
This is the moment that the Rams have been waiting for. During the offseason, Aaron Donald came out of retirement in large part because he wanted to play alongside Garrett. Those two have yet to play a snap together as Donald didn’t make the trip in Week 1 and Garrett was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 2.
Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams have been managing injuries to key players, Garrett being the first among them. The Rams have simply been trying to get by as they begin to get healthy and that is finally starting to happen.
Overall, the Rams’ depth has done well, all things considered. Josaiah Stewart was only expected to be a rotational player and has played 67.3 percent of the defensive snaps this season. Wesley Bailey was signed to the roster as an undrafted free agent and has played 30 percent of the defensive snaps, becoming a key part of the pass rush rotation.
Both players have two sacks on the year and Bailey forced a fumble last week against the los Angeles Chargers. However, Stewart’s 11.6 percent pressure rate ranks 70th out of 116 edge rushers. Bailey’s 8.5 percent pressure rate ranks 99th. Stewart and Bailey rank 61st and 78th in pass rush win rate.
The Rams have lacked consistent pressure off of the edge, and Garrett will certainly provide a huge boost to the defense and pass rush in that aspect if he’s healthy. While Jared Verse doesn’t have a sack this season for the Cleveland Browns, it’s fair to wonder what impact a healthy Verse could have had on the Rams’ defense.
Without Garrett, the Rams currently rank 21st in pressure rate, compared to second last year and 14th in 2024. The Rams were ninth in sack rate last year and 19th in 2024 and have dropped down to 27th this season. That’s despite going from the least-blitzing team to 16th. Chris Shula’s blitz rate has increased by nearly 10 percent to help the defense generate pressure on the quarterback.
Shula’s increased blitz rate has been a positive while Garrett has been out, and it will be interesting to see if that continues or if the defense goes back to what it has been the last few years when they’ve been comfortable getting pressure with four.
The Rams traded for Garrett in the offseason with the hope that he could take their defense and pass rush to the next level. Without Garrett, the Rams’ defense ranks sixth in EPA per play and their -0.15 EPA per pass ranks fourth. Garrett will be entering an already good situation without the pressure of having to do everything himself.
Still, this is what the Rams have been waiting for. The Super Bowl team that the Rams built this offseason is finally starting to come together as it gets healthy. They’ll still await the return of Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, and Terrance Ferguson, but having Garrett back in the lineup is a huge first step.
Without Garrett, the Rams have shown that they can play at a high level defensively. However, the Rams traded for Garrett so that the defense could take over games in JanuaryIf he returns healthy and can provide the consistent pressure that the Rams have been missing, this defense could become one of the NFL's most dangerous as they fight for a playoff spot. The Rams can finally start to look like the team they envisioned during the offseason. With Garrett set to return to practice, the Rams are one step closer to seeing that all come together.

title: Raiders' Primary Focus Clear Heading Into Week 9 Against 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders defense came up big when it mattered most in Week 8 against the New York Jets. However, almost everything else about last Sunday's game raised red flags for a Raiders defense that is still in transition in its first year under Rob Leonard.
The Raiders are only in the first season of their actual rebuild. Las Vegas' front office addressed multiple positions as much as it reasonably could, with what they hoped would be serviceable options. This was especially the case in the defensive backfield.
Las Vegas drafted several young defensive backs and planned to develop them throughout this season and beyond. The Raiders' defensive backfield is filled with several first- and second-year players they expect to contribute early in their careers.
However, few positions go through the rites of passage that young cornerbacks and safeties do, which is where the Raiders find themselves halfway through their first season under Klint Kubiak, and second under general manager John Spytek.
Week 8 proved that rebuilds take time, and that a team can win and walk away with some of the same feelings as a loss. Still, the Raiders didn't lose, which is both a win in the record books and a moral victory for Las Vegas' defense and defensive backfield, which made enough stops to seal the win.
“It was tough sledding. We need to be better, and we talked about some things. It’s hard to comment on what their mindset was, but we tried to fix some things and adjust," Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard said following practice on Thursday.
“ It wasn’t pretty. There’s a lot we have to fix, but I’ve been here a couple years, and not many times we come out finding a way to win. I was proud of the resilience of getting hit in the mouth the first three plays, and we have a red-area stop on the three-yard line. So, there’s a lot of points on the little things that helped us win that game and how they rallied in the fourth quarter. It was really fun to see.”
The 49ers are tough to play. Their 6-0 start to the season firmly established them as one of the league's best teams. This season, Las Vegas has struggled against teams that are considered such. Leonard knows his unit, specifically, the defensive backfield, will have their work cut out.
“They’re fundamentally sound, man. They’re a clean operation, and they got some good players. Quarterback’s playing at a high level, good tight end, running backs, and the offensive line is really good. So, that’s what jumps out to me, how fundamentally sound they are, and they’re able to put a lot of pressure on you,” Leonard said.
San Francisco presents Las Vegas with no shortage of issues, as the 49ers excel at many of the things the Raiders do not. This is true on both sides of the ball. Few teams on the Raiders' schedule will pose as many problems specific to Las Vegas' remaining roster issues as the 49ers will.
Given how injured the New England Patriots were when Las Vegas faced them earlier this season, Week 9 is arguably the toughest test to date for Klint Kubiak's Raiders. The game itself will be enough. It will be the first taste many of the 2026 Raiders get of a long-running rivalry, which will only add to it.
“If you respect the game and understand how this thing really went down and what it was when they were there, it means a lot to a lot of people. I think it’s awesome to be a part of. It’s very humbling, and we want to go and put on a performance that everybody’s proud of as a team,” Leonard said.
At 4-4, Sunday is a chance for Las Vegas to gain ground in the playoff hunt. It is also the start of another brutal three-game stretch for a Raiders team still processing the last five games, four of which they lost. The Raiders must take things one game at a time.
As they do, they must improve significantly upon the past month. The Raiders have a chance at a statement victory.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: These Raiders Need Standout Performances Against 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders had a nice bounce-back win last week against the New York Jets. However, this week is a completely different animal, as the team travels to Santa Clara to take on the San Francisco 49ers.
Following a strong start to the season - winning the first three games - the Raiders lost four consecutive games, stirring the conversation around potentially trading veteran pieces and looking forward to the 2027 season. Last week's win changed the narrative and validated the front office's decision to stand pat with the current roster. With that in mind, here are several Raiders who need a strong outing against the 49ers on Sunday.
The second-year running back has been disappointing since Las Vegas selected him with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. His struggles aren't solely on his shoulders, as the Raiders' offensive line has been lackluster during that span. However, Jeanty was viewed as a generational talent, which is why he went inside the top 10 in his draft class.
Jeanty was given a mulligan for last season because the offensive line play was so putrid. He ran for 975 yards and five touchdowns on 266 carries (3.7 yards per attempt), not a bad output for his rookie season.
It's been a tumultuous season so far for Jeanty, who has been battling adversity since the offseason. The Boise State product has battled injuries for the majority of the season. It can be assumed that he hasn't been 100 percent all season, averaging 3.1 yards per carry and rushing for one touchdown. He's been a tremendous pass catcher out of the backfield, but he's judged on how effective he is between the tackles as a runner.
Mike Washington Jr. outcarried Jeanty 25-2 last week, as the two running backs essentially flipped roles. If Jeanty struggles again on Sunday, last week's backfield distribution could look the same moving forward.
Nailor was the Raiders' most notable wide receiver addition this offseason, signing a three-year, $35 million contract in free agency. The former Vikings wideout hasn't lived up to the billing, catching 12 passes for 113 yards and one touchdown in seven appearances.
Luckily for Nailor, Las Vegas doesn't possess many weapons that could threaten his spot in the pecking order. That said, we've seen head coach Klint Kubiak limit Jeanty. Nailor needs to start producing at some point for the Raiders' offense to take flight. Additionally, general manager John Spytek could explore acquiring a wide receiver at the trade deadline.

title: 3 Areas Where Raiders Must Excel Sunday Against 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders will once again face one of the league's best teams this Sunday as they travel back to their old stomping grounds to face the San Francisco 49ers. One of the most historic rivalries in league history will add a new chapter in Week 9.
Both teams are on opposite ends, as the 49ers are a much more established team than Las Vegas. San Francisco is another team the Raiders will face this season that will likely make for an uphill battle on game day, as Las Vegas has one of the toughest schedules.
Las Vegas has gone toe-to-toe with some of the league's best teams, including the Kansas City Chiefs. Yet they have also come out flat in several of their losses. It will be interesting to see which Raiders team shows up on Sunday against the 49ers.
Below are a few of the matchups I believe will play a vital role in Sunday's results.
Las Vegas has struggled to stop the run this season, against teams with running backs who are not nearly as good as McCaffrey. The Raiders allowed 140 rushing yards in the first half of their Week 8 win over the Jets. They held New York to 26 rushing yards in the second half.
The Raiders cannot afford to let McCaffrey get going, which is easier said than done. Still, the Raiders must approach Week 9 as they did in the second half of Week 8. Las Vegas must focus on stopping the opponent in one area or another, instead of letting the opponent decide.
Las Vegas' issues stopping the run and the pass in recent weeks have been noticeable. Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard recently explained that several factors have contributed the unit's struggles this season.
“When you have multiple errors, which we did, it’s a combination of both [mental and physical errors], and making sure the guys are in the right spots or attacking certain things, or there’s some guys playing some different spots, so just being clear on all those things,” Leonard said earlier this week.
Las Vegas drafted Zuhn in the offseason to bolster the offensive line, but his ability to play all five positions forced the coaching staff to find the best fit. He spent most of training camp developing at essentially every position except for center. In Week 8, they finally put that hard work to use.
After struggling to find stability at the position, Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers earned their starts and playing time at the position. However, Las Vegas' offensive line looked relatively good against the Jets.
It will be interesting to see if Las Vegas starts Zuhn at right guard again. If they do, it will also be interesting to see how he fares against a better defense. Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko shared his thoughts on the rookie offensive lineman.
“I think he came out, competed, did a lot of good things, did a lot of things to build on. It was great that there’s some things that he’ll learn from and grow. And just being out there competing and helping us get a win was huge, huge for his confidence and huge for us going forward as an offense,” Janocko said on Thursday.
The Raiders' defensive backfield will be tested by one of the best all-around operations in the league.  Shanahan is an expert play-caller and is all but certain to capitalize on Las Vegas' defensive issues, especially against a young defensive backfield that has struggled over the last month.
Las Vegas' young defensive backfield can only do so much. As the coaching staff has often done, Leonard hopes the staff's development and preparation will pay off on game day. It is unlikely that any additional players will be added to the unit. They must step up.
“Stack plays. Really focusing on us, our alignment, our assignment, key technique, fundamentals, and it’s especially that time of the year where it’s hard to really out-scheme people. Everybody knows who they are, so you have to go out and execute,” Leonard said.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face.
The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season.
It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets.
In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense.
“I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week.
“If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.”
Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter.
On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets.
On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well.
Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers.
The Raiders will likely give rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses a bigger role than he has had in recent weeks. Masses has started multiple games for Las Vegas this season and played well overall.
However, like all rookie cornerbacks, Masses has also displayed a need for improvement in several games. Sunday will be another opportunity for Masses and the rest of the defensive backfield to bounce back after a disappointing past few weeks.
Las Vegas' young defensive backfield has long been the Raiders' primary issue. They are currently going through the expected growing pains that come with starting so many first-and second-year players in their defensive backfield. Not to mention all of the coaching changes.
Still, it's the National Football League, and these are the world's best football players. Las Vegas needs more from all of its defensive backs. After the unit's last two games, San Francisco will target Las Vegas' vulnerable secondary.
It is cliche, but it is true. The most important game is the next one, and Las Vegas is .500 headed into their next game. Their next three games will be tough, but stealing a win in Week 9 would be huge for Kubiak's Raiders.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Hondo's Raiders Musings: Silver and Black Locked in and Focused
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—With the overachieving Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) headed to California this weekend to take on the San Francisco 49ers (6-1), many storylines surround the Silver and Black.
The franchise is ahead of schedule on the rebuild, and first-year head coach Klint Kubiak has done nothing short of amazing. This franchise is following his example, and they are locked in.
The fast-approaching NFL trade deadline has the football world’s attention, and Klint Kubiak didn’t hide that he has the Raiders, and that he and GM John Spytek stay in constant communication on how to improve the team.
“They’re ongoing. Yeah, they’re constant at all hours of the day, whether it’s up against a trade deadline or not. So, we’re always talking.”
Klint Kubiak said the team is in the proverbial playoff hunt, with the 49ers and the Seattle Seahawks on the schedule over the next two weeks.
“I think every week’s that way. If you treat it that way, then you’ll have success throughout the season. So, we just keep our blinders on and focus on one opponent at a time.”
Kubiak has harped on the Silver and Black's struggles in the second half, which improved markedly versus the Jets last week.
“Yes, players executed. There’s things you focus on every week and sometimes you hit them, and sometimes you don’t. But I thought our guys were very intentional about that phase of the game, and obviously it has to continue.”
With the rise of Mike Washington Jr. and the struggles in the running game by Ashton Jeanty, Kubiak addressed his faith and confidence in Jeanty's future.
“Oh, absolutely! Yeah, Ashton’s a young player and has a really bright future ahead, and I’m so glad that we have him and all these young players on our roster that are continuing to grow, and it’s our job as coaches to develop them.”
The Raiders RB room includes the aforementioned Jeanty and Washington Jr., and don’t forget the unexpected dog in Dylan Laube, who is fierce. Add to it Roman Hemby on the practice squad, and the Raiders' future is bright at RB, and Kubiak knows it is fueled by great competition.
“Yeah, it’s always the best motivator. Coaching takes you so far, but when you’re competing for reps, it definitely adds a new gear to your giddy up in practice.”
Kubiak was raised by his father, Gary, who has a long and distinguished legacy in Denver. Kubiak was well acquainted with the Raiders through their fellow AFC West ties, and he shared his impressions of the team before he arrived.
“Yes, I remember definitely just overall with the Raiders, every time, being in Denver, everybody’s walking around with Raider Hater shirts on, and the town has a buzz to it. And I remember one specific game. I think it was in the snow, but Jerry Rice and Tim Brown, and just as a young kid, getting to watch on the sideline, those are your heroes."
"I just kind of remember the snow falling down in the stadium and watching those guys run on the field. And Tim Brown's got his finger tape rolled up, and then that week in my game, I’m rolling up my fingers. Tim Brown doesn’t need any gloves, neither do I. So, that really stands out, and I don’t remember your other question.”
For Kubiak, who is new to Raider Nation, he understands the enormity of this rivalry for the fan base, even though both teams have vacated the bay.
“Yeah, it’s a huge rivalry. I know both organizations for a long time have gone against each other. Times change, and they’re in Santa Clara, and we’re here in Vegas, and it’s just a blessing to be a part of that rivalry moving forward.”
Kubiak, because of his relationship with the Shanahan family and his brother Klay being the offensive coordinator, is well aware of the thinking behind the way the 49ers play. He discussed whether that can help the Silver and Black on Sunday.
“Yeah, you always have familiarity, but it’s the players’ game on Sunday, so we’ve got to get our players ready to do what they do best, so they can play at a high level on Sunday.”
Raiders rookie CB Jermod McCoy was the man many believed to be the best CB in the 2026 NFL Draft, but his injury issues in college set him back. He is healthy now, and with Darien Porter injured on Sunday, he got meaningful reps.
With an impressive 2026 NFL Draft class heavy at defensive back, Kubiak addressed his growth and what he is looking for.
“I think the focus hasn’t changed. Whether he was getting no reps or now getting more, it’s just getting better at your position and being really intentional about your individual and being a factor on special teams, being great with your eyes and your keys and your technique, and those are things that make Joe Woods such a special coach, and we’re so happy to have Joe. And those DBs are so happy to have him as a mentor and as a coach. A guy with so much experience that helps him play.”
Kubiak believes in his DC. He is a first-time DC, and just like Kubiak is a first-time HC, that comes with a learning curve. Add to it, the team knew Leonard has a thin DL and a very young DB crew; some of the criticism is ridiculous.
Leonard said he tells his players every day that they’re working and playing for their jobs. Kubiak was asked about his thoughts on Leonard’s comments.
“Well, I think if you’ve worked in the NFL long enough, then that’s the reality of our business. It’s a production business. It’s the most competitive industry that I know of, and any time that you start to feel comfortable, then you will be quickly humbled."
"And so, whether you’re having success or you’re working to get better, if your mindset stays the same and you continue to push and push through the hard times, you come out on the other end. So, that’s the NFL. The NFL brings adversity and makes you answer to it every day.”
Fernando Mendoza, the young man whom NFL executives ranked as the No. 1 quarterback prospect of the last four NFL drafts, looks better than ever. He is improving and learning every day, and Kubiak gave an update on his growth.
“I think when you are the backup quarterback and you don’t get a ton of reps, I think we all find out together on Sunday how ready he is. So, we put him through as much stress as we can. Coach [Mike] Sullivan does a phenomenal job, Coach Andrew [Janocko], and when his time’s called, whether he gets three more years of reps or he gets one more day of reps, he has to be ready.”
Jackson Powers-Johnson (JPJ) has struggled to stay healthy and has struggled at RG. Still, Kubiak loves versatility, and he talked about the potential for him to work at different positions on the OL.
“Yeah, this time of year, not everybody takes every rep, and that’s part of the development plan for everybody. We’ve got a lot of veteran guys with lots of snaps on their bodies, and the young guys and the guys behind him, they get opportunities to get more reps, so it’s good.”
So does he see JPJ drifting to the other side of the line?
“He can play both sides. He can play center. He has a ton of value to us, and probably the greatest value is him as a teammate. The energy that he brings, the genuine love that he has for his teammates and the game, really elevates the whole offense.”
Dylan Laube is an unexpected dog for the Silver and Black, and he is the reigning AFC Special Teams Player of the Week. Kubiak is happy to see his progress.
“Yeah, well, I think that he earned it. He earned his opportunities. He made the most of his opportunities, and like I said the other day, okay, now the expectations are that, and they’re higher, and now you’ve got to work twice as hard to exceed expectations.”
Kubiak has noticed that Laube doesn’t just return kicks; he makes plays on all of the special teams unit, and that his big-impact contributions have earned him his coaches' admiration and appreciation.
“Yeah, he made a huge tackle in the game. Very coachable. Again, Coach Joe D [Joe DeCamillis] and Marquice [Williams] and Tim [McConnell], those guys do a phenomenal job with our special teams, and Dylan [Laube]’s one guy that has really benefited…

title: What Raiders Would Prove With Week 9 Win Over 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders finally returned to the win column last week, defeating the New York Jets 38-33.
They hope to remain there as they travel to Santa Clara to take on the San Francisco 49ers, who are coming off a bye. It'll certainly be a tall task for the Raiders to defeat the 49ers, who also improved by acquiring defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts. Las Vegas is 4-4, and with the trade deadline looming on Nov. 10, this game has high stakes. With that in mind, here's what a win would prove for Las Vegas.
When the Raiders won their first three games of the season, they became legitimate playoff contenders. However, Las Vegas then lost four consecutive games, flipping that narrative on its head. Suddenly, there were completely shifted expectations for Las Vegas.
Las Vegas silenced that noise, for the time being, ending their four-game losing streak last week with a win over the Jets. While the victory was necessary, it can still be viewed as a fluke result, as New York had just lost to the Dolphins the week before.
San Francisco is a completely different animal, especially when head coach Kyle Shanahan has had a full week off to prepare for this matchup. It would be a statement win for the Raiders and likely re-establish them as legitimate playoff contenders.
As mentioned, when Las Vegas went through the recent four-game skid, the idea that the Raiders should take calls on multiple players, including Maxx Crosby , and turn the page to 2027 grew a bit louder. However, general manager John Spytek didn't budge and refused to make a knee-jerk reaction move. Now, Las Vegas can still end up being sellers at the deadline, but that probably won't be the case if it defeats the 49ers on Sunday.
In fact, if the Raiders depart on Sunday with a 5-4 record, we could see Spytek strike a deal for a position of need. Wide receiver is the top area on the roster that comes to mind in this discussion. Nevertheless, Las Vegas would make a major statement with a win in Week 9. Although the 49ers have dealt with a slew of injuries, they are 6-1 and atop the NFC West, which was evaluated as a two-horse race between the Seahawks and Rams before the season.

title: With Porter Injury, Raiders Could Get Extra Look at Promising Rookie
full_text:
This weekend, the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders travel back to the Bay Area to face the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers. It will be an emotional weekend for Raider Nation, especially those remaining in Oakland, as the team returns for the first time since their final game there nearly seven years ago.
As the Raiders prepare to face one of the best teams in the NFL after a bye week, they could be without No. 2 cornerback Darien Porter, who injured his groin early in their win over the New York Jets.
Porter did not practice on Wednesday, as head coach Klint Kubiak called him “day-to-day.”
“I think it's just we’re just taking it day to day, and he’s making progress,” Kubiak told reporters.
With Porter absent from practice and the possibility of him missing Sunday’s game, two rookie cornerbacks could get more opportunities to play opposite Eric Stokes.
Fifth-round rookie Hezekiah Masses has had an up-and-down rookie season, but the flashes have been encouraging when he has seen the field. It is hard to imagine him not having a major role in the defense in 2027. However, the Raiders need to begin viewing what they have in fourth-round selection Jermod McCoy as a unique case in these circumstances.
The former Tennessee Volunteer standout was once considered a top-15 prospect from this past spring’s NFL Draft. However, red flags around his major injury last January led to a shocking fall out of the first 100 picks, and the Raiders took an opportunity to bolster their defensive back room with a terrific talent who would need patience to get his feet under him.
McCoy played roughly 30 snaps against the Jets after Porter went down, and Kubiak said on Monday that it's all about getting better for McCoy, and I couldn’t agree more based on what I observed from Sunday’s game. However, there’s a sense that McCoy’s opportunity for more playing time could come this weekend at Levi’s Stadium.
While McCoy may get an extended look on Sunday, the focus for the rookie and the Raiders has not changed. Kubiak said as much on Wednesday, crediting defensive backs coach Joe Woods for being key in the growth of the young secondary pieces, including McCoy.
“Whether he was getting no reps or now getting more, it’s getting better at your position and being really intentional about your individual and being a factor on special teams, being great with your eyes and your keys and your technique, and those are things that make Joe Woods such a special coach, and we’re so happy to have Joe,” Kubiak said.
“And those DBs are so happy to have him as a mentor and as a coach. A guy with so much experience that helps him play.”
McCoy won’t yet be the star-studded talent he was as a sophomore in Knoxville, Tennessee. He is basically learning how to get comfortable on an active gridiron against live fire for the first time in almost two years. These things take time, but having a coaching staff that is disciplined in making sure young players have all the resources available to them is a key step in their development next week, the rest of the season, and the coming years.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: Raiders' Week 9 Depth Chart Presents Shakeups on Both Sides
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are slated for their second road game in a row, facing the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
The Raiders will have their work cut out for them. Below is our analysis of their Week 9 depth chart.

Analysis: Laube may be the answer at punt returner, too.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Raiders' Matchup vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 8 win over the New York Jets was just what they needed in between multiple games against the league's best teams. They are back to the grind as they prepare for another road challenge this week.
Las Vegas has already surpassed its win total from last season, but faces a three-game stretch that will leave little doubt about the direction of the season. Sunday's slate against San Francisco will be followed by games against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos.
The Raiders sit at 4-4, their best record this deep into the regular season in years. They look to build on their strong start by upsetting the 49ers this Sunday. Las Vegas will face a much more talented team this Sunday than they did last Sunday.
Still, if they perform well enough, there is always a chance the Raiders can leave San Francisco with a win. On the other hand, beating a team like the 49ers may take more than the Raiders currently have on their roster.
Sunday will be one of the Raiders' toughest games this season. However, not knowing which Raiders team will show up makes it a more interesting matchup than it may seem.
Below are the storylines I am watching the most in Las Vegas' Week 9 matchup against the 49ers.
The Raiders' defensive backfield has struggled over the past two weeks. After Matthew Stafford picked the unit apart, Geno Smith and the Jets' wide receivers did too. Las Vegas played man defense most of Sunday, which left veteran cornerback Eric Stokes on an island with the Jets' best receivers.
The Jets made the Raiders pay, targeting Stokes early and often. The veteran made several plays that helped the Raiders win, but his overall performance raised questions heading into Week 9. Stokes is the team's best cornerback. They need him to figure it out soon.
The Raiders may be without Darien Porter, which would add more to all of the defense's plate. Still, Stokes' performance will be the unit's most important on Sunday. Las Vegas will need all hands on deck against Brock Purdy and a well-coached 49ers team.
Against the Jets, Las Vegas largely used Washington to run the ball and Ashton Jeanty as the team's pass-catching option out of the backfield. It will be interesting to see if the Raiders take a similar approach to how they use their running backs on Sunday against San Francisco.
Washington's second half changed the game's trajectory for the Raiders, who trailed by almost double digits at halftime. One storyline I'll watch most closely is the Raiders' usage of Washington and Jeanty. How often Las Vegas hands off to Jeanty will be interesting to watch.
The Raiders may have made strides toward figuring out how to fix their ground game. However, their Week 9 game against the 49ers will give a better idea of whether or not that is the case. Las Vegas has yet to beat a team with a winning record. That could change this Sunday on the road.
Another storyline I will be watching is simply the fact that both teams have so much history individually and together, as the rivalry goes back decades. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak shared his memories of the Raiders from childhood, when his dad coached.
"I remember definitely just overall with the Raiders, every time, being in Denver, everybody’s walking around with Raider Hater shirts on, and the town has a buzz to it. And I remember one specific game. I think it was in the snow, but Jerry Rice and Tim Brown, and just as a young kid, getting to watch on the sideline, those are your heroes," Kubiak said on Wednesday.
"I just kind of remember the snow falling down in the stadium and watching those guys run on the field. And Tim Brown's got his finger tape rolled up, and then that week in my game, I’m rolling up my fingers. Tim Brown doesn’t need any gloves, neither do I. So, that really stands out, and I don’t remember your other question.”
Las Vegas looks to make it two in a row.
