title: Vikings' Biggest Defensive Concern Can Be Solved by a Trade Call With Eagles
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings may have a lot of bodies available on the defensive line, but many of them are struggling to be effective or are young players who need time to develop before they can become major contributors.
Minnesota should be in the market to trade for players to help stay on top of the NFC North and prepare for a hopeful playoff berth. One player who may be available in trade talks is Philadelphia Eagles defensive lineman Moro Ojomo.
Philadelphia selected Ojomo in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft, and he has played 335 defensive snaps for the Eagles this season. Through eight games, he has 21 tackles, four quarterback hits and three tackles for a loss.
The Vikings' defensive line has some solid play this season. Jalen Redmond is ranked tenth among all defensive linemen with a 78 overall Pro Football Focus grade and should be a priority for Minnesota to re-sign. However, other big men in the trenches haven't fared as well as Redmond.
Here are other Vikings' defensive linemen's PFF grades and rankings through eight weeks:
Ojomo has a 57.6 PFF grade, which would give him the third-highest grade on Minnesota's roster. This season, he has generated 18 quarterback pressures and 14 hurries while earning a 57.1 run defense grade.
Standing 6-foot-3 and weighing 292 pounds, Ojomo is a versatile defender in the trenches who could help give the Vikings more time to develop Banks and Orange slowly, and not rush their development, while still being competitive.
Minnesota has struggled to slow down the run lately and has given up long rushing touchdowns in each of its last two games. According to a clip from The Aftermath shared on X by ESPN senior reporter Jeremy Fowler, Ojomo is a player that Minnesota could show interest in acquiring .
Right now, Vikings fans are waiting for Minnesota to make a move. Trading for a quality player right now would prove that the franchise believes that a deep playoff run is possible. Hopefully, the Purple and Gold can get a deal done before the Nov. 10 trade deadline to make the team as competitive as possible for the remainder of the season.

title: Vikings Make Major Blunder With New FA Signing as Trade Deadline Approaches
full_text:
Vikings fans closely monitoring social media for possible trade deadline news may have gotten a bit of a jump scare Wednesday.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Vikings signed offensive lineman Corey Robinson II after he worked out with them, a report later confirmed by the team . The move came one day after the team released backup guard Trevor Keegan.
The #Vikings are signing OL Corey Robinson II after having him in for a workout. Robinson is an undrafted free agent out of Arkansas who was with the Bengals after the draft. https://t.co/4rXR0b61yP pic.twitter.com/5yGs6MNGyQ
Naturally, the move sparked questions and reopened conversations about the need for the team to make serious moves as the trade deadline approaches. Does the move actually make the 2026 Vikings any better?
We’ll have to see, but the timing was certainly odd for several reasons.
Robinson is, for the most part, a complete unknown in the NFL.
The former Arkansas Razorback signed with the Cincinnati Bengals as an undrafted free agent this past April, after starting 12 games at left tackle in 2025. It remains to be seen if the Vikings plan to use him at tackle or on their interior, but is betting on him really the right move after Trevor Keegan’s release on Tuesday left the Vikings without a true backup guard?
It was theorized that Keegan might re-sign with the practice squad, but ESPN ’s Mike Garafolo reported Wednesday afternoon that the Buccaneers claimed him off waivers.
The Vikings may make additional corresponding moves, but this one seems odd in a vacuum.
The #Buccaneers claimed G Trevor Keegan off waivers from the #Vikings .
Left guard Joe Huber is already starting in relief of an injured Donovan Jackson, and Will Fries has been shaky at right guard to start 2026. If either is injured, the Vikings may need to get creative given their lack of depth. An undrafted rookie tackle with no NFL experience does not exactly seem like the ideal backup plan. In the meantime, it’s clear Vikings fans were hoping for much bigger news.
The Vikings are 6-1 with an all-world defense and currently hold the NFC’s second seed. Seems like a perfect time to make a massive move, and in previous years, they probably would. But the long-term cap and roster situation makes things incredibly complicated . Still, most fans naturally want to see the team go all in, especially since so many key veterans may not be around after this season.
For those constantly checking their phones for news, signing a backup offensive lineman likely wasn’t what they hoped to see.
With the Nov. 10 deadline quickly approaching, it seems we’ll all have to wait on the edge of our seats a little longer as we wait for the “big” news to drop… if it ever does.

title: Vikings are Making an Ivan Pace Jr. Mistake as Trade Deadline Looms
full_text:
The Vikings have played seven games this season, and it has become abundantly clear that 25-year-old linebacker Ivan Pace Jr. hasn't been and won't be a major contributor in defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit.
Through those seven games, Pace played a total of 59 defensive snaps, an average of 8.4 defensive snaps per game. Even though he is a regular contributor on special teams and played 152 snaps there (83.5%), it is disappointing not to see him more involved on defense.
For comparison, this is what Pace's defensive snap count looked like in his first three seasons with the Vikings:
Despite the shrinking role, it'd be wise for the Vikings to give Pace some more snaps against the Bills in Week 9. The reason isn't to give Blake Cashman or Eric Wilson time on the sidelines, but to increase his visibility if Minnesota looks to put him on the trade block this year.
With Cashman and Wilson cemented into the Vikings' starting interior linebacker positions and rookie Jake Golday developing to be a future contributor at the position, Pace is struggling to get defensive snaps this year.
Pace could be a trade asset for Minnesota, but the Purple and Gold aren't going to raise his value by sitting him on the sideline. He used to be a starter for the Vikings (27 times in 52 appearances, to be exact. As an undrafted free agent in 2023, he recorded 102 tackles and 2.5 sacks,
Since that rookie year, his playing time and his stats have decreased with each passing season. Last year, he started only six games, but still had 62 tackles, two tackles for a loss, and one sack. His recent play has proven that he can be productive in a limited role.
However, now is not the time to let Pace spend so much time on the bench. Getting him some defensive action over the next few games could go a long way toward increasing his trade value, potentially allowing Minnesota to get an asset for him instead of allowing him to leave as a free agent after this season.
Pace is currently on a one-year, $3.52 million contract with the Vikings, but is unlikely to re-sign the former Miami (OH) and Cincinnati defender as long as the team has Cahman, Wilson and Golday on the roster. Another team could view his expiring deal as a chance to take a swing on a low-risk yet experienced rental.
There are defensive-needy teams out there that could use a young linebacker like Pace to hold down the middle of their defense. His age, history of production, and potential say a lot about what he has to offer, but the NFL is a league that is based on what a player has done recently.
Sadly, he hasn't been asked to do much in the Vikings' defense lately, giving the Purple and Gold all the reason to display him to potential suitors this weekend.

title: DeeJay Dallas Decision Leaves Vikings With an Obvious Roster Cut to Make in Week 9
full_text:
The Vikings were in an interesting position when it comes to a player who has been a contributor at running back. DeeJay Dallas has been bounced around between the practice squad and the active roster since signing a one-year, $411,300 contract for the 2026 NFL season.
Dallas signed to the 53-man roster two weeks after joining the practice squad, but was surprisingly released in October and signed back to the practice squad. Since then, he has been elevated to the main roster every week .
However, the Vikings can no longer elevate him after doing so three times before Week 9. Minnesota needed to decide whether to leave him on the practice squad or sign him to the 53-man roster to continue using him on game day. On Wednesday, they made their decision by officially signing him to the main roster.
The #Vikings have signed RB DeeJay Dallas ( @DallasDeejay ) to the 53-man roster and T Corey Robinson II ( @coreyrobinson76 ) to the practice squad. pic.twitter.com/z340dwDyb5
After the Purple and Gold signed him to the 53-man roster, another player needs to be released, with one name standing out above the rest in Week 9: rookie RB Demond Claiborne.
Dallas has played in every Vikings game this season, so it would've been surprising if he wasn't signed to the 53-man roster at some point. He has played 63 offensive snaps and 123 special teams snaps, showing his value to the team in more ways than one.
There are some candidates to be let go now that Dallas's spot is secure. Players like safety Jakobe Thomas and defensive lineman Elijah Williams have been inactive all season , meaning they wouldn't change what has been happening on the field.
Still, neither as big a cut candidate as Claiborne, who has been inactive and has been losing offensive snaps to Dallas. That said, Minnesota is potentially worried he will be signed by another team before he can join the practice squad.
Nevertheless, Claiborne has six rushing attempts for 13 yards this season. He hasn't played since Week 5 and has played 18 offensive and four special teams snaps this season. He has not been a player who offers a lot of value on the 53-man roster, and the Vikings shouldn't be worried about losing him.
Holding on to Claiborne out of fear of losing him would be keeping a roster spot hostage. If he is signed to the practice squad, he could be elevated up to three times this season before he would need to be signed back to the 53.
Right now, the Vikings have several players who are regulars on the inactive list, but only Claiborne makes the most sense. He and Dallas play the same position, and Minnesota has already shown its preference between the two running backs this season.

title: Vikings' Uphill Battle for a Potential Kyler Murray Trade Solution Officially Steepens
full_text:
As Week 9 of the NFL season begins, Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray continues to deal with a hamstring issue that could prevent him from suiting up against the Bills on Monday Night Football. But even if he can play, Murray has struggled as a quarterback this season, completing 64.9% of his passes while averaging only 170.3 passing yards per game. He has thrown five touchdowns to three interceptions while being sacked 15 times in six games played.
Whether it's due to his injury or inconsistent play, Murray has given the Vikings reason to consider outside arms.
If the Vikings are in the QB trade market, though, their lack of urgency could force the team to redirect their search after the news that the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens on Wednesday.
Trade: The #Ravens are finalizing a trade for former #AZCardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, per me and @AdamSchefter , filling the void left by the injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler “Snoop” Huntley. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend. pic.twitter.com/RWhT1LQ2fc
The Vikings probably don't feel bad about starting veteran backup Carson Wentz, but he isn't a quarterback who will provide a spark for Minnesota's offense. He may complete only 59% of his passes this year, but he has yet to throw an interception while throwing three touchdowns.
Wentz has a 3-3 record as a starter since joining the Vikings, but Minnesota could prove they are all-in on this season by making a trade for a quarterback who can ignite the offense and help put points on the scoreboard.
Brissett being off the market isn't a big deal, but it makes competing for other quarterbacks more challenging, whether that's Kirk Cousins, Justin Herbert or someone else. Now, the next wave of signal-callers to be traded will command a higher value based on how many teams need help at that position.
If nothing, the Vikings could use some help until Murray is ready to return to the field. If Minnesota doesn't acquire a quarterback soon, they could have to roll with Wentz as the starter and Max Brosmer as his backup, with no emergency third passer on the 53-man roster or practice squad.
The Vikings are 6-1 this season and on top of the NFC North. Every team in the division this year is playing good football and has a winning record heading into Week 9. The Purple and Gold need to give themselves the best chance to win every week, and that includes Monday night's game against the Bills.
If the Vikings are interested in acquiring a quarterback before the trade deadline, the team needs to act quickly and with purpose. The longer Minnesota waits, the more likely it becomes that it will overpay for a player who wasn't among its top options.

title: Looking Back at the 5 Best Rob Gronkowski Moments with Patriots
full_text:
Rob Gronkowski was a football unicorn, a man amongst boys, a one-man wrecking crew. Whatever analogy you prefer, they all tell the same story; Gronk was truly one of a kind. His otherworldly athletic ability and Adonis-like stature, paired with his carefree, childlike personality, made him a Hall of Fame talent who captured the hearts of fans across New England. With his Patriots Hall of Fame induction set for Saturday, Nov. 7, l et's take a look back at some of his greatest moments in a Patriots uniform .
Late in the fourth quarter of the Patriots' 42-20 dismantling of the Indianapolis Colts in 2014, Gronkowski delivered one of his most memorable moments in a New England uniform. However, it wasn't a touchdown. He didn't even have the ball. As Patriots running back Jonas Gray scored his fourth touchdown of the day (yes, four), Gronkowski was nearly 10 yards out of bounds, still executing his block on Colts safety Sergio Brown.
When Rob Gronkowski threw Sergio Brown “Out Of The Club.” pic.twitter.com/zp1BRCMGRs
The two former teammates (Brown played for New England from 2010-11) had some history before that moment. Brown was the player who broke Gronkowski's arm during an extra-point attempt in 2012. According to Gronkowski, he had also spent much of their 2014 matchup talking trash. "He was just yappin' at me the whole time," Gronkowski said at the time. "So I took him and threw him out of the club." Gronkowski's postgame comments perfectly captured his hard-nosed play style and instantly became a fan-favorite moment.
In their 2011 bout against Washington, Gronkowski delivered one of the most incredible individual efforts seen on the gridiron. After a diving below-the-knee catch, Gronkowski rolled back to his feet and carried two Washington defenders another five yards toward the sideline. At this point, nearly everyone in the stadium assumed the play was over, including the players on the field. Everyone except Gronkowski. He somehow shook off both defenders, stayed in bounds, broke another tackle, and gained a substantial chunk of yards in the process. "He almost had no room to work with on the sidelines," Bill Belichick said after the game. "He is a tough guy to cover, a tough guy to match up on. We don't tackle him every day in practice, but we have seen plenty of people try to do it." The incredible 49-yard reception set up an even bigger moment. On the very next play, Gronkowski hauled in an 11-yard touchdown, recording his 14th receiving score of the season and breaking the NFL record for most touchdown receptions by a tight end in a single season.
Following New England's 13-3 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Super Bowl LIII, the Patriots traveled to Fenway Park to participate in the Boston Red Sox's home opener, where several players were set to throw out the ceremonial first pitch. Before the festivities got underway, a handful of Patriots players took some time to practice their throws. That's when Gronkowski had an idea. What if he stepped into the makeshift batter's box against Julian Edelman, using the Lombardi Trophy as his bat? And so it was. Edelman wound up, ready to deliver the pitch, while Gronkowski stood with the Lombardi Trophy in hand. "We're all under the impression, 'No way is he going to swing the Lombardi Trophy,'" safety Devin McCourty said. As Edelman released the pitch, Gronkowski lifted the trophy off his shoulder and positioned it in front of him in a bunt stance. The ball collided with the trophy, leaving a baseball-sized imprint in the team's crowning achievement. "Gronkowski's parting gift," McCourty said. The dented trophy is still on display in the Patriots Hall of Fame.
One of the things that made Gronkowski so feared by opposing defenses was how fluid an athlete he was for his size. Standing 6-foot-6-inches and weighing roughly 265 lbs., you usually aren't supposed to make the acrobatic plays Gronkowski did. Especially the one he made against the Buffalo Bills in Week 16 of  the 2017 season.
Inside the Buffalo 20-yard line, down 10-3 in the second quarter, Tom Brady fired a back-shoulder pass to Gronkowski, who was blanketed by a Bills defender. Despite this, Gronkowski adjusted to the throw, extending his right arm out to haul in the pass before turning his body to get both feet in. Touchdown. Plays like these made Gronkowski a nightmare to cover.
With less than a minute remaining in the first half of Super Bowl XLIX , a game that would ultimately be decided by the thinnest of margins, Gronkowski hauled in a 22-yard touchdown pass from Brady over Seahawks linebacker K.J. Wright . Arguably the most important of Gronkowski's five Super Bowl touchdowns, the score helped give New England a 14-7 lead heading into halftime. Gronkowski finished the night with six catches for 68 yards and a touchdown, earning another championship ring in the process.
At this point in his career, Gronkowski wasn't quite the same player. Injuries had taken their toll, limiting both his availability and effectiveness throughout the season. But when New England needed him most, he came through. With the game tied 3-3 and just under eight minutes remaining, Brady found Gronkowski down the seam for a 29-yard completion, with the tight end making a diving catch to bring New England to the 2-yard line. This catch led to the eventual winning score, as Sony Michel punched it in on the very next play for the game's only touchdown. Gronkowski finished the night with six catches for 87 yards. A fitting stat line for No. 87 in what would be his final game as a Patriot.

title: Rob Gronkowski Tells Hysterical Patriots Practice Story Involving TD Prop
full_text:
FOXBORO — Nobody can spin a tale like Rob Gronkowski .
The legendary New England Patriots tight end , speaking to reporters Thursday, is set to be inducted into the team's Hall of Fame this weekend. His speech is certainly going to be filled with plenty of anecdotes from his nine-year career with the Patriots and his usual jokes.
He gave a little preview on Thursday speaking to a group of reporters virtually, remembering a story from his second season back in 2011. In typical Gronkowski fashion, it was as bizarre as you might expect.
It involved a Staples "That Was Easy" button that was gifted to him through the mail.
"I opened it up Friday before red zone practice and I look at Wes Welker and I go, 'Yo Wes, You that Terrell Owens celebration where he hid the ... marker or the sharpie behind the field goal post and he whipped it out and had the signature?'" said Gronkowski, the 38th inductee into the Patriots Hall of Fame.
That Owens celebration was when the wide receiver hid a Sharpie in his sock, and pulled it out to sign the football in 2002. Gronkowski made it his own, hiding that Staples button behind the goal post during the team's final practice of the week. Welker dared him to do it and hit it after scoring a touchdown.
In Gronkowski fashion, he was up for it.
"All of a sudden, boom! Another red zone play call. I run an in cut back of the end zone, catch it like two feet in front of the goal post," Gronkowski said. "I go, 'Yeah baby, this is it!' ... (I) grab the Staples button and started hitting it. That was easy. That was easy. Coach (Bill) Belichick starts shaking his head getting all pissed off and no one knew what to do because no one's ever seen that (sic) antics before.
"But no one could also say a word because I was absolutely balling that practice and balling in games too. That was one of the best moments, and Wes couldn't believe I pulled it off either. That story lives forever."
Gronkowski was right. He was balling — that year and the ones that would follow. The legendary tight end scored a franchise-record 79 touchdowns and ended his time in New England being on teams that went to the Super Bowl five times, winning three of them.
His induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame was without a doubt happening . He had embedded himself into the fabric of both the team and region, and it was because of stories like that.
"It was the right fit for me, the right people, the right organization, and now I call New England a place for me as home. It really is a home for me. It will always be a home for me for the rest of my life," Gronkowski said. "It’s somewhere where I’ll feel safe. I’ll feel secure, I’ll always feel loved here and that’s what it’s all about and vice versa. I’ll always love New England. I’ll always love the city of Boston, always love the New England Patriots fans, and it’ll be forever with me."
His Patriots career was legendary. So legendary that it oftentimes felt ... easy.

title: Making A Case for Rob Gronkowski as the Greatest Tight End in Patriots, NFL History
full_text:
On Saturday, the "Gronk Spike" will officially be immortalized as star tight end Rob Gronkowski is inducted into the New England Patriots Hall of Fame.
Gronkowski will become the 38th member of the Patriots organization to be inducted into the team's Hall of Fame , and the latest second dynasty player (following Vince Wilfork, Julian Edelman and Tom Brady) to wear the red jacket.
Gronkowski has more receiving touchdowns than any other Patriots player (79), and ranks second in receiving yards (7,861) and fifth in receptions (521). The dominant tight end played nine seasons in New England, and joined Brady in Tampa Bay for two more, acheiving a total of four Super Bowl victories in his career (XLIX, LI, LIII, LV).
The words " greatest tight end of all time " often describe the menacing 6-foot-6, 265-pound force, but people continue debate the accolades of Gronkowski with recent successes like Travis Kelce and previous players like Tony Gonzalez who made the tight end position unique.
However, when comparing Gronkowski, or "Robby G," or "Gronk" with other tight ends, it's clear that no one played the game like New England's No. 87.
Gronk has some of the clutchest plays of any tight end for any organization ever. He's a defining point of the 2010's Patriots dynasty, serving as one of the three figureheads with Brady and Edelman, who each carried a load in winning three Super Bowls in five years.
In Super Bowl XLIX, the tight end made an empowering catch over the Seahawks' K.J. Wright for a touchdown to give New England the lead before halftime in what would be their first title in a decade.
Brady also relied on Gronk for big third and fourth down conversions, in the 2015 AFC Championship, Gronkowski kept the Patriots in the game, catching a 40-yard reception and following it with a four-yard touchdown (New England would go on to lose to that year's Super Bowl champion Denver Broncos).
Perhaps one of his most notorious plays as a Patriot came in his final reception with a flying Elvis sticker attached to his helmet, as the veteran tight end hauled in a 29-yard seam route reception to put the Patriots within scoring position, and open up Super Bowl LIII in an effort to beat the Los Angeles Rams.
Even in Tampa Bay, Gronk still showed flashes of dominance, especially in his sixth Super Bowl appearance against the Kansas City Chiefs, where he was the Buccaneers leading receiver and acquired two touchdowns of his own.
Watching Kelce nowadays reminds me of how impressive it was that when Gronk was done physically he still made the biggest catch to win a Super Bowl. pic.twitter.com/iZlq7NK1LZ https://t.co/fC4SVladlg
The remarkability of Gronkowski's tenure is brought into higher status when considering the injuries he suffered during his 11-season career. He missed half of the 2016 season, including Super Bowl LI, where the Patriots overcame a 28-3 defecit to defeat the Atlanta Falcons.
Early in his career, Gronk sustained multiple back injuries, including a herniated disc that occured during his time at the University of Arizona. In 2013, he tore his ACL and MCL in his right knee, and also suffered a broken arm, playing with an implant in his forearm for most of his career.
He also sustained multiple rib and lung injuries, often taking big hits to the chest in an effort to bring down the towering pass catcher. Worse than the hits to his chest, were the hits to his head, which resulted in an unknown number of concussions that Gronkowski has openly estimated to be in double digits range.
Though he wasn't the most available tight end of all time, there's a case to be made that he was the toughest. Remarkably, his play never faltered from injury, despite the toll football put on his body.
There's no encapsulation of Robby G's NFL career without summarizing his escentric personality and the entertainment value he brought to football.
Picked in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft, Gronkowski famously huddled with his family before walking on stage to shake the commissioner's hand, and put a Patriots helmet on as soon as he exited the stage.
His irresistable and humorous identity as a not-so intelligent figure and a party lunatic allowed him to coin the phrase, "Yo soy fiesta," which translates from Spanish with plenty of grammatical errors to ,"I am party." After his NFL career he held parties during the Super Bowl titled, "Gronk Beach," and awkwardly, yet hilariously, made Robert Kraft and Bill Belichick take shots on stage during the Roast of Tom Brady, just four months after Belichick's tenure as New England's head coach ended.
Draft Day. 2010. Gronk! #NFLDraft #tbt pic.twitter.com/GBx3nOVGRj
More so than his off the field antics, Gronkowski brought his rambunctious behavior to the grid iron, too. His "Gronk Spike" was a generational touchdown celebration replicated by football fans and players across the world, each one more powerful and just as demeaning to New England's opponents.
When asked on Thursday about one moment in his career that stood out to him, Gronkowski couldn't define a singular play, but rather a trend.
"The 'Gronk Spike!' [It] was lethal, it was legendary," he exclaimed. "[The Gronk Spike] kind of defines my career, as well — powerful."
So many TDs, so many Gronk spikes 💪 Celebrating #NationalTightEndsDay with some of the best @RobGronkowski touchdowns. pic.twitter.com/qzeBnLPvD3
He laughed in the faces of defenders who failed to prevent him from scoring, used his massive arms to drive tacklers into the ground, and finished blocks by creating pancakes into the field, and at times, the stands (just ask the former Colt Sergio Brown who was on the receiving end of a block).
His competitive attitude was most evidently seen in his playstyle. While his receiving accolades were some of the best ever at his position, he was well-known for being one of the best run-blocking tight ends to ever play football. This allowed him to dominate in a Patriots offense that ran almost more play-action than any other team.
"That's why I love blocking" said Gronkowski. "That's what got my foot into the door with the Patriots. That's what got my respect from my teammates. I was a blocker first."
While Gronkowski's statistics aren't exactly better than any other players at his position, he still ranks top-six in yards, top-three in touchdowns, and had a much shorter career than the other players ahead of him (such as Gonzalez, Jason Witten, Antonio Gates, Kelce, and others).
The argument surrounding Gronkowski as the greatest tight end to ever play football comes from how transformational he was at the position, his two-way ability as a blocker and receiever, and his ball carrying skills to extend plays.
What Gronkowski did that other tight ends hadn't yet, was line up as both a receiver and a true tight end/extra offensive linemen. He excelled in a two-tight end offense — the first of its kind — and had the ability to be on the field for every offensive snap, unless he was dealing with injuries.
His four Super Bowls are more than any other player at his position, and to do it with two different teams and the same quarterback adds to how impressive that feat is.
"I know I gave it my all, I really really did," exclaimed Gronkowski. "I held on the last couple of years, I basically would've been carried off the field if I played one more year."
"To be recognized with [Patriots legends] is an absolute honor, an absolute thrill, it means everything."
Rob Gronkowski once played through a regular season game with a herniated disc and a punctured lung that was causing him to spit up blood… There will never be another Gronk. The #Patriots Hall of Fame just got a one-of-a-kind addition! (🎥 @Patriots ) pic.twitter.com/BssPWHE3CC
For New England fans, Gronkowski is a centerpiece of what it means to be a Patriot. He still resides in Foxboro and is a major advocate of the new era Patriots. On Saturday, Gronkowski will add to his abundant resume of accomplishments that make him…

title: Patriots QB Drake Maye Named October's AFC Offensive Player of the Month
full_text:
For the first time in his young NFL career, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has been named the AFC's Offensive Player of the Month.
Maye wins the award for October after leading the Patriots to a 3-1 record over four weeks of play, and turning around a slow start, following last year's Super Bowl LX appearance.
From Oct. 1 to Nov. 1, Maye threw for 1,398 passing yards, had 17 total touchdowns, and an average passer rating of 122.2. His 67.4% completion rate contributes to his nomination as player of the month.
October belongs to @DrakeMaye2 🤩 pic.twitter.com/VDlWFOadC0
Maye earns the nod as AFC Offensive Player of the Month in a competitive decision that saw the likes of Josh Allen, Jaylen Warren, and Kenneth Walker IV — September's AFC Offensive Player of the Month.
Maye turned around his season after putting up a 1-2 record in September , which saw the third-year player turn the ball over seven times and throw just one touchdown.
After a remarkable month of October, Maye becomes the first Patriot to win AFC Offensive Player of the Month since Tom Brady did so in November of 2017.
In the last 5 weeks… Drake Maye is #1 among all QBs in: 🏅 Total yards 🏅 Total TDs 🏅 EPA 🏅 Passer Rating Despite the following… ⚠️ Injuries to his WR1, WR2, WR3, TE1, RB2, LG and RG ⚠️ Pressured at the 4th highest rate in the NFL ⚠️ Playing with one of the league's… pic.twitter.com/xAeJX1jkP4
Over the course of the past five weeks, Maye has led the NFL in total yards, passing touchdowns, EPA (expected points added), and passer rating.
Maye is currently sixth in passing yards on the season (1,983) and tied for fifth in touchdown passes (15). Over the past two seasons, Maye holds the lead for touchdown passes of 30-plus yards, including two that he threw to Kyle Williams and DeMario Douglas in Week 8's win against the Miami Dolphins.
What makes Maye's recent success even more impressive is his ability to dominate with a weakened supporting cast. Maye has had his top-three receivers miss a combined six games due to injury, leaving last year's MVP runner-up to spread the ball around to other skill position players.
Earlier in October, Maye was asked if he's had to intentionally spread the ball around to build the confidence of his teammates.
"I try not to have that in the back of my mind," Maye said. "I was like that a little bit in high school, to be honest with you, of wanting – especially when we would run it up on teams in high school – to try to spread it around and get guys touches."
He's also used his legs to give the Patriots an advantage, running for 129 yards and two touchdowns throughout the October window of play.
On Thursday, Maye appeared on Rob Gronkowski and Julian Edelman's show on Fox, Gronk and Jules. He reflected on the turnaround this season, saying,"you got to realize that turning over the football is not going to help us win games."
"Realizing that the work you put in week-in and week-out is going to end up paying off, and not losing sight of trying to change things up."
Maye's October success has paid off for the Patriots, who now hold a 5-3 record as the calendar turns to November. Now they have the AFC Offensive Player of the Month leading their team.

title: Mike Vrabel Says Former Patriots Captain is 'Working Really Hard' to Return
full_text:
The New England Patriots got really good snaps out of Harold Landry to begin last season. This year? Different story.
The veteran edge rusher hasn't made his season (or practice) debut yet as he continues to work his way back from the Physically Unable to Perform list. He suffered a knee injury last year he played though.
Ahead of the team's Wednesday practice, Mike Vrabel was asked if Landry is trending to return in some capacity this season.
"I would say that anybody that's still here and that's getting treatment is tracking (to return)," Vrabel said. "How quickly they track or what that pace is, I don't know. I just know that he's working extremely hard. Like I've said a few times before, whenever he's ready, he'll start to return to play or he'll start that process. He's doing some things on the side and he's doing some things with the strength coaches and the trainers. I know he's working hard."
After signing a free agent contract ahead of last season, Landry was voted a captain by his teammates and recorded 8.5 sacks and 10 tackles for loss. He got banged up in the team's Week 6 win over the New Orleans Saints, but remained on the active roster for the rest of the year. He'd suit up in the Super Bowl in February and then reportedly got surgery in the offseason.
Since then, he hasn't participated in a single practice — missing all of the summer after being put on the PUP list. He also hasn't been spotted in the locker room while reporters are present, though that's not a true indication about anyone's status.
If you had told me in the summer that Landry would still be absent in Week 9, that would have sounded concerning. Considering the pre-season worries that people had about New England's edge rushers, having the veteran Landry back would have been nice to ease in some of the younger players asked to step into larger roles (Gabe Jacas, Elijah Ponder, Quintayvious Hutchins).
But the Patriots have gotten really good production out of Ponder and free agent Dre'Mont Jones. Both those players have combined for seven sacks through the first eight weeks and you haven't really felt the loss of Landry on the field.
Now, considering the fact that the Patriots have Landry on the books for $16.3 million this year and he's still not practicing, that's a little off-putting ahead of the trade deadline where the team could use as much cap space to bring in some fresh talent.
Landry's three-year contract is up at the end of the 2027 season, but considering how long it's taken him to get back into the fold, I wouldn't be surprised if he ends up retiring ahead of next season. Until then, like Vrabel said, he's working hard to get back in pads and help his teammates get back to the Super Bowl.

title: Patriots Know They'll Need to Slow Down Packers QB Jordan Love
full_text:
It's a premier deep-ball matchup this week between the New England Patriots and Green Bay Packers. Drake Maye and Jordan Love are some of the best at launching it down the field this year and have combined for 4,229 passing yards through seven weeks.
It should be a fun game to watch — and the Patriots defense knows that they'll need to be ready for the passing attack.
"Jordan Love's ability to get the ball out fast," edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones said about challenges they'll face. "We'll see how it plays out."
The Patriots, coming off a win against the lowly Dolphins, will be able to use this week against a 5-3 Packers team as a good measuring stick. They're currently winless in two attempts against NFC teams this season and could use a good win against an opponent gunning for the postseason.
Part of what's made this Green Bay team good (they're averaging 21.7 points per game) is the growth of Love under center.
"Nobody's had more 20-yard pass plays. A quarterback that's wildly efficient. He has a few off days, but they're few and far between. They throw shots," Mike Vrabel said. "I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that's an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he's able to find (Matthew) Golden, (Christian) Watson or Tucker Kraft."
Love, a first round pick by Green Bay back in 2020, had the time to learn under Aaron Rodgers during his first few years in the NFL. Once the reigns were officially passed, he hit the ground running. A playoff team a year ago, the Packers have surrounded Love with plenty of talent on the offensive of the ball. He's taken advantage.
One area where he's shined is making adjustments at the line of scrimmage, something that's stood out to Vrabel.
"Whether he's sight adjusting and the ball's coming out quick, or he's changing the protection and making a call, communicating, I think I've seen that growth over the last couple years," Vrabel said. "Certainly, give him a lot of credit for the way that his career started: watching. I think that that's hard. It's hard to develop when you're not playing. But he certainly did. He probably learned a lot from what Aaron was doing and how Matt (LaFleur) was doing it with him."
This Patriots defense has had up-and-down performances against some of the NFL's top offenses. They limited the Seahawks in Week 1 (albeit down their starting quarterback in Sam Darnold) and beat Josh Allen and the Bills three weeks later. But they also gave up 30 points to Caleb Williams and the Bears, and trailed to the Miami Dolphins for most of the first half of an eventual win.
They'll need to be on their Ps and Qs against a Packers team hungry to get back into the mix of things in the NFC North.
"He's a talented player. He does a good job of finding his guys," Jones said. "The more comfortable he is in the pocket, the more accurate the ball is going to be. He's another prototypical quarterback, 6-(foot)-6, fast, can make any throw, so we got to do a good job of being smart."
"We all know he throws one of the prettiest deep balls in the league outside of Drake Maye, those moon balls that he throws up there," safety Kevin Byard said. "I think he's one of the most underrated quarterbacks in this league."

title: Patriots to Travel More That Almost Any Other Team Over Next 4 Games
full_text:
The New England Patriots enter the third quarter(ish) of their season on Sunday, as they take on the Green Bay Packers at home for their ninth contest of 2026.
After starting 2-2 in their first four games, which was the toughest start to a season in over 30 years, New England righted the ship and went 3-1 over the next four they played.
Now sitting at 5-3, the Patriots will be challenged with immense travel, a pair of playoff teams from a season ago, and some of the best teamms in the NFC. Here's what's on the Patriots plate from Weeks 9 through 13:
Sunday's 4:25 p.m. game against Green Bay could have momentum shifting effects on the next few games. While the Packers have been a powerhouse, winning four of their last five, traveling to Foxboro to face one of the best defenses in the league will be a challenge for coach Matt LaFleur and quarterback Jordan Love.
The Packers may potentially be without Micah Parsons, as he continues to rehab an ACL tear from last season — though he practiced for the first time all season on Wednesday. Green Bay has blocking miscues up front, which doesn't bode well for a team going against one of the top-ranked interior defensive lines in the NFL in Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, and Cory Durden.
Green Bay's 5-3 record is impressive, but they've yet to have an impressive win — notching victories over the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield, the Bears without Caleb Williams, and the Cowboys, Jets, and Panthers (those three teams have an 8-15 combined record). Green Bay is entering Sunday's match looking for a legitimacy proving win over the defending AFC Champions.
Following Sunday's game against Green Bay, the Patriots attend their first long road trip of the third quarter of their schedule, heading to Germany to take on the Detroit Lions.
The Lions, currently coming off a victory against the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings, have provided one of the most efficient and high-powered offenses in the league. With a defense that's sturggled heavily this season, the Lions completely contrast to the Patriots, who have been leveraged by their defense to create opportunities for their offense.
It'll be interesting to see how this game plays out for both sides, that match up fairly well to one another, and how the international status of this game will effect the outcoming.
The good news is, regardless of if the Patriots escape Munich with a win, they'll have plenty of time to work towards one, as they enter their bye week in Week 11.
After a restful Thanksgiving break, New England will board for another lengthy trip, heading to Los Angeles to face the Chargers.
Los Angeles is currently a staggering 0-7 and are driving like a truck without its brakes, wheels, or gas pedal. However, this AFC Wild Card round matchup from 2025 could be sneaky for the Patriots on Sunday Night Football. While this game is often forgotten when reliving New England's playoff run earlier this year, the Chargers kept this game close until Hunter Henry broke free for a touchdown in the fourth quarter.
The Chargers defense has been efficient this year and the real issues in Los Angeles lay with the offensive liabilities. Mike Vrabel took his first regular season loss after a bye last year, which will be something to watch this year as New England enters their Week 12 match for a potential trap game.
New England closes this five-week stretch of action and rest in a major way, facing the Buffalo Bills at home on the first Sunday of December.
In Week 4, the Patriots gave the Bills their first and only loss of the season. Since then Buffalo has been a wagon, toppling the Rams in overtime, outlasting the Raiders, and cruising past the Ravens.
Buffalo will visit New England one week after facing the Kansas City Chiefs, which could be advantageous for the Pats that would be looking to dominate game two of Buffalo's back-to-back matchup against recent AFC Champions.
However, if the Bills lose to Kansas City on Sunday Night Football in Week 12, Buffalo could also be looking at the Patriots game as an opportunity to get back in the win column. For New England, they have a massive opportunity to potenitally hand Buffalo their third loss of the season, sweep both games against the Bills, and put themselves in the drivers seat for the race to the AFC East title.
Another exciting feature of Week 13's game against the Bills is the storm blue rivalry uniforms returning to Gillette Stadium for the second time since their debut in 2025.

title: Patriots Week 9 Injury Report: Injured Vets Return, Offensive Stars Sit
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots got some good news and some bad news as they headed out to practice on Wednesday to prepare for the Green Bay Packers.
Speaking to reporters, head coach Mike Vrabel shared that wide receiver A.J. Brown, running back TreVeyon Henderson and defensive tackle Christian Barmore will all miss the session. But two players currently working their way back from injured reserve — wide receiver Mack Hollins and offensive guard Greg Van Roten — would begin their 21-day clocks to be activated .
Even with the trade deadline approaching , the Patriots aren't worried about any extracurriculars.
"We're focused on trying to prepare for Green Bay and make the corrections from the game," Vrabel said. "This is business as normal here."
Both Hollins and Van Roten were spotted during the media portion of the day and a few hours later, here's how the Patriots' first injury report looked:
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (illness)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle/knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (foot)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (illness)
And in Wisconsin, the Packers announced their injury report, which included one of the NFL's best defensive players back in the fold:
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (concussion)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (shin)
Both Brown and Henderson missed last week's win in Miami with ailments. For Brown, he's been nursing an ankle injury suffered in Week 1 and a knee injury that's plagued him for years.
"My concern is about trying to prepare for the Packers," Vrabel said when asked about if he's concerned about Brown's knee. "That's really my only concern. ... Certainly the health of the team is critical, but we have to make sure that the guys that are practicing are preparing for Green Bay."
Henderson , on the other hand, has missed several days with an illness. This comes as the trade deadline looms and Henderson, who hasn't had that strong of a start to the season, has had his name thrown around in rumors. How serious is this illness?
"It's serious (enough) that he won't be available today," Vrabel said bluntly.
With Henderson sidelined, the Patriots relied on Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner, Lan Larison (who signed to the 53-man roster on Saturday) and Terrell Jennings ( who re-signed to the practice squad on Monday ).
The Patriots were also without starting tight end Hunter Henry, who suffered a foot injury against the Dolphins.
Each team is allowed to have eight players return off of IR during the regular season. Before Wednesday, the Patriots had only used a pair on Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant . Both Hollins and Van Roten were the next two designations and could come back as early as this week.
They both won't count towards the 53-man roster, but the Patriots have three weeks to fully activate them to the roster. If not, their seasons will be over. Right now, Vrabel is focused on getting them ready to go.
"We just want to get guys out there to practice," he said. "There's only so much that the trainers and strength coaches can do with them. So hopefully we can work those guys back in and see where they are here as we work through the week."
Hollins will be an easy fit into an offense that's had a number of wideouts banged up to this point . Last week in Miami, the Patriots had just four active wide receivers (and one of them was Ryan Miller, a temporary practice squad call-up). He'll become a starter the moment he gets back on the field.
"He's smart and ... he's easy to throw to and does a lot of things the right way," Drake Maye said of Hollins' return. "It's comforting, definitely, having 13 out there and looking forward to seeing whenever he gets a chance."
For Van Roten, his path is a bit cloudier. The Patriots have gotten good guard play out of Ben Brown and Matt Pryor, who both had to step up after Van Roten's injury in Week 3. If Van Roten comes back, he may push one of those guys back into a reserve role.

title: Patriots' Robert Kraft Among 5 HOF Contributor Candidates for 2027
full_text:
FOXBORO — Could this be the year that Robert Kraft finally gets inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame?
On Wednesday, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced that the New England Patriots owner is one of five finalists for the Class of 2027 contributor category. Kraft was named alongside Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten. These names were narrowed down from a larger group of 42 nominees by the contributor subcommittee.
Kraft, who bought the Patriots in 1994 and has helped usher in a new era of dynastic football, advanced in this process last year. Kraft was first nominated in 2013 and has eligible ever since. He wouldn't get inducted into Canton, along with former Patriots head coach Bill Belichick — who was the coaching nominee in 2026.
"I would just say that's unfortunate," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said last February after Kraft didn't earn induction . "In my experiences with Robert, he's more than deserving. He'll be in the Hall of Fame. I'm not in charge of deciding when that happens."
The Patriots have became a force in the NFL since Kr aft took over. During his time as owner, the Patriots have won 11 AFC titles and six Super Bowls. He also became the fastest NFL owner to reach 300 wins and has been a key member of several NFL ownership committees. In 2011, he was instrumental in helping to end the lockout ahead of that season.
It's a crowded group as it stands right now . Hay, who also reached this point a year ago, owned the Canton Bulldogs from 1918 to 1922 and was a key factor when it came to forming the NFL.
The late McCaskey was the principal owner of the Chicago Bears since 1983, and owned the team during their first Super Bowl over the Patriots in 1985. She was the daughter of Bears founder George Halas.
Williams played nine seasons in the NFL, winning Super Bowl MVP in 1987 and has spent the last 13 years in the Washington Commanders front office. He's also been a scout or front office executive in other years.
Wooten played offensive line for a decade before transitioning into scouting roles off the field. In 2003, he became chair of the Fritz Pollard Alliance, a group that hepps create opportunities for minorities in coaching and front office roles.
The Patriots have historically not been inducted into the Hall of Fame in recent years, despite having several people deserving of the honor. Last year, former kicker Adam Vinatieri was inducted as the first Patriots specialist to ever enter the halls of Canton.
The contributor category "recognizes individuals whose impact on professional football came through leadership, innovation and service to the game rather than on-field performance," according to the Hall of Fame. The voting committee will hold a meeting on Nov. 17 to narrow the group of five down to one.

title: Mack Hollins' Return Revitalizes a Broken Patriots WR Room
full_text:
On Wednesday, NFL Nework's Ian Rapaport reported that New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins would be returning to practice , beginning his 21-day window to be activated off the injured reserve.
In his second year with the Patriots, Hollins landed on injured reserve after sustaining a calf injury in the second half of New England's win over Buffalo in Week 4.
A big one for the #Patriots : WR Mack Hollins is set to return to practice today, sources say. Hollins, a glue guy for NE, has been on Injured Reserve with a calf injury and would help immensely vs the #Packers . pic.twitter.com/8uhIzxvxZ8
Through the first four weeks of the season, Hollins was the Patriots' leading receiver in yards and receptions, making his injury a major loss for the offense. Despite Hollins' absence, New England's passing game has been able to deliver, putting up 282.3 receiving yards per game from Weeks 5 to 8.
At the time of his injury, Hollins was the second Patriots receiver to land on IR this season, following A.J. Brown — who was injured in Week 1. Two weeks after Hollins came up gimpy on his right leg, Romeo Doubs was sidelined and sent to the injured reserve with a shoulder injury.
Brown returned in Week 6 and played only two games, missing Week 8's contest against Miami with a knee problem that arrived during last week's practice. Doubs isn't eligible to return off the injured reserve until Week 12. Drake Maye was left with just three receivers signed to the 53-man roster last Sunday against the Dolphins.
While New England's been able to make-do with the weakened wide recievers by utilizing tight ends and running backs in the passing game, those positions aren't exactly healthy either. TreVeyon Henderson didn't play in Week 8 due to an illness and is also still recovering a high ankle sprain sustained a couple games prior.
In the second half against Miami, tight end Hunter Henry injured his foot, leaving his status for Week 9's game against the Green Bay Packers up in the air. These considerations provide more value to Hollins' activation, who is looking to make an immediate impact in his return to play.
Hollins has played a major role in big situations for New England's passing attack. Maye often finds the 6-foot-4 receiver on third and fourth down plays. Since his injury, Henry has assumed that role, but with the tight end potentially missing some time, having Hollins back in the fold brings a much needed security blanket to last year's runner-up for MVP.
Part of the struggle for New England's wide receivers this year has been finding consistency, and the player that's been hurt the most by this is Brown. The superstar wide receiver has hauled in just nine of 20 passes thrown to him and has struggled to find meaningful production on offense.
Adding another perimeter threat in Hollins creates opportunities for Brown that he hasn't had due to defensive gameplans taking him out of the game (as well as uncharacteristically unreliable pass catching abilities). In the three quarters they played together in Week 1, Hollins' separation caused Seattle's defense to not overcommit on Brown. Maye took advantage of this adjustment, placing a deep pass to Brown that slipped off his fingers.
The Hollins effect can be seen through the sample size of games he missed last year with an abdomen injury. The wide receiver landed on injured reserve late last season, missing the final two weeks of the regular season and two playoff games. In those games, Maye threw for an average of 35 yards less than his season average passing yards per game. Returning to action in the AFC Championship game and the Super Bowl, Hollins was the leading receiver for New England in both contests.
The 33-year-old Hollins is in his 10th NFL season and is the most veteran receiver residing in Foxboro. While he's never been known to be a top wideout option, his voice and demeanor had a huge impact on a receiver room that many defenses looked past last season.
Hollins has extended his interest in this Patriots team far beyond the field. In both weeks the Patriots traveled while he was injured, Hollins made the trip with the players to Chicago and Miami — something that isn't required of players on IR.
Last week, New England's receivers had an average of 2.75 years of experience in the NFL. Activating the veteran Hollins and hopefully seeing Brown return to play on Sunday will bring a transformational impact to New England's offense and its high-caliber quarterback.

title: Saints Get Major Injury Boost as Browns Face Quarterback Uncertainty
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints received encouraging injury updates Wednesday as left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. and rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
Meanwhile, Cleveland could be without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , who entered the NFL's concussion protocol Wednesday after reporting symptoms following Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Watson initially passed concussion evaluations and finished the game but reported symptoms Monday night, putting his availability against New Orleans in question.
If Watson cannot play, second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his first start of the season.
Sanders started seven games as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. However, he has seen limited action this season, completing just three passes for 2 yards.
Watson has started all eight games for Cleveland this season, completing 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions.
Despite his efficiency, the Browns have struggled offensively, ranking 29th in the NFL with just 17.4 points per game.
For New Orleans, Wednesday's biggest development was the return of Banks, who practiced for the first time since undergoing ankle surgery in September .
The second-year left tackle has progressed considerably faster than initially expected, returning more than a month ahead of schedule.
The Saints now have a two-week window to activate Banks from injured reserve, potentially providing a significant boost to an offensive line that has struggled in his absence.
Backup left tackle Asim Richards has experienced difficulties adjusting to coach Kellen Moore's offensive scheme while filling in for Banks.
Initially expected to return in mid-December, Banks could reclaim his starting role once medically cleared, giving the Saints additional protection up front.
New Orleans also welcomed back Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State.
The rookie wide receiver participated on a limited basis Wednesday after missing the entire season to this point with a hamstring injury suffered during training camp .
Although his availability for Sunday's matchup remains uncertain, Tyson's return represents another encouraging development for a Saints offense looking to improve its passing attack.
With Banks and Tyson progressing toward their respective returns and Cleveland potentially facing a quarterback change, Sunday's matchup could feature a considerably different outlook for both teams than initially anticipated.

title: Saints Make Coaching Staff Changes, but Mickey Loomis Shouldn't Escape Blame
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints have fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti following their Week 8 bye, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football.
The decision comes as head coach Kellen Moore attempts to fix one of the NFL's least productive rushing attacks, with New Orleans sitting at 2-5 through seven games.
The Saints have parted ways with run game coordinator TJ Paganetti, according to sources. Paganetti came from Philadelphia, where he helped architect the run game and was part of developing one of the league’s best offensive lines
The Saints are averaging just 86 rushing yards per game and 3.5 yards per carry, with their struggles reaching a low point in a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Oct. 25.
New Orleans had one of the most embarrassing rushing performances in franchise history, managing only 18 rushing yards on 17 attempts and averaging a dismal 1.1 yards per carry.
Paganetti joined Moore's staff in 2025 after spending 10 seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles , where he helped develop one of the NFL's most dominant rushing attacks.
During Philadelphia's Super Bowl-winning 2024 season, the Eagles rushed for a franchise-record 3,048 yards and averaged 179.3 yards per game, ranking second in the NFL.
However, that success never consistently translated to New Orleans.
While Paganetti deserves some responsibility, the Saints' problems extend beyond coaching.
While Moore is getting heat for the Saints’ offensive struggles, ultimately the biggest issue with the New Orleans Saints is the person who hired him: general manager Mickey Loomis .
Loomis is responsible for building the roster, including the backfield and the offensive line, the two weakest links on the Saints.
The running back room, featuring Alvin Kamara , Travis Etienne , Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson , hasn't delivered consistent production.
Etienne's placement on injured reserve has further complicated matters, especially when the Saints signed him on a four-year, $52 million deal.  Kamara, by contrast, hasn't shown the same explosiveness that made him one of the NFL's most dynamic playmakers.
The offensive line also remains a concern despite significant investments, including first-round selections Kelvin Banks Jr. , Taliese Fuaga and Cesar Ruiz along with the free agent signing of David Edwards for $76 million
New Orleans has struggled to consistently create running lanes, particularly along the interior, leaving its running backs with limited opportunities.
Paganetti arrived in 2025 after spending 10 seasons with Philadelphia, where he helped develop one of the NFL's most productive rushing attacks. However, the Eagles also had considerably better offensive line personnel.
Moore and Loomis must now share responsibility for determining whether the Saints' struggles stem from their offensive philosophy, player development or questionable roster construction.
Firing Paganetti sends a message that the current production is unacceptable, but changing coordinators won't automatically solve personnel deficiencies.

title: Saints Midseason Stock Report: 4 Bright Spots Amid a Disappointing Start
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints enter their bye week with a disappointing 2-5 record despite the hype around the Saints being contenders to possibly win the NFC South.
While the season has been anything but positive, the team still has bright spots on both offense and defense.
Here's a look at four players who have performed above and beyond as we reach the midseason point.
Tyler Shough hasn't been perfect, but the second-year quarterback continues to show encouraging signs of development under coach Kellen Moore .
Through seven games, Shough has completed 67% of his passes for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's also contributed 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
His pass yardage and touchdown totals are both in the top 10 as he is tied for seventh in passing touchdowns and ninth in passing yards, but for a majority of the season he was either No. 1 or No. 2 in passing yards.
Those numbers are impressive considering New Orleans' struggles establishing a consistent rushing attack and protecting its quarterback.
Despite occasional mistakes, Shough has demonstrated improved accuracy, pocket presence and command of Moore's offense.
If he continues developing and limits turnovers, the Saints should feel increasingly confident about their quarterback situation.
Wide receiver Chris Olave has shown why the Saints gave him a 4-year, $132 million extension.
Through seven games, the former first-round pick has caught 49 passes (fourth in the NFL) for 636 yards (third in the NFL) and two touchdowns, averaging 90.9 receiving yards per game.
He opened the season with four 100-yard performances in his first four games, including a dominant 182-yard outing against Detroit .
Chase Young has arguably been New Orleans' most impressive player on defense through seven games.
The former No. 2 overall pick has recorded seven sacks, establishing himself as one of the NFL's most productive pass rushers.
Out of 50 edge rushers with at least 125 pass rushes, Young ranked second with a 90.0 Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade.
Young is on pace to record over 15 sacks, potentially putting him in the conversation for Pro Bowl recognition.
Though Young draws much of the spotlight, Carl Granderson is quietly putting together a standout year as well.
Across seven contests, the experienced defensive end has registered 25 tackles alongside 5.5 sacks, highlighted by a 1.5-sack effort versus Pittsburgh .
Granderson's current trajectory puts him on track for roughly 13 sacks, setting up a potential career mark.
Combined, Granderson and Young have racked up 12.5 sacks, forming one of the few reliable highlights for New Orleans' defense.
Even with the unit's broader difficulties, his growth paired with Young gives the Saints a high-caliber pass-rush duo for the future.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Saints' 16-10 Loss to Steelers in Paris
full_text:
Hoping to build momentum ahead of their upcoming bye week after a major victory last week, the New Orleans Saints instead fell 16-10 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday in Paris, exposing several recurring issues under coach Kellen Moore .
New Orleans' offensive struggles continued as missed scoring opportunities proved costly as the Saints fell to 2-5.
From an emerging young playmaker to a disastrous rushing performance, here is a look at the good, the bad and the ugly from the Saints' disappointing loss to Pittsburgh .
One of the few bright spots in New Orleans' disappointing loss was rookie wide receiver Barion Brown's emergence.
The sixth-round pick got a chance to show his explosiveness, finishing with three receptions for 57 yards and adding another 97 yards on four kickoff returns.
His biggest offensive play came in the first half when he caught a 49-yard pass from Tyler Shough , setting up Daniel Carlson 's 38-yard field goal.
Brown also returned a kickoff 42 yards in the second quarter, setting up a possession that ended with Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele .
Despite those contributions, Brown received just three targets.
That limited involvement raises questions about whether coach Kellen Moore is maximizing one of the offense's most explosive young playmakers.
With rookie Jordyn Tyson still sidelined by a hamstring injury, Brown has a chance to become a more consistent contributor alongside Chris Olave and Vele.
New Orleans gets a vital jolt on offense from Brown's explosive speed and big-play dynamism.
Following a sluggish 281-yard performance against Pittsburgh, integrating him must become a top priority for the Saints. To fully leverage the rookie's skill set, Moore ought to scheme designed touches, vertical routes and run-after-catch opportunities for him. Given how much he has delivered on minimal opportunities, Brown has earned a larger role.
In a narrow 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh, kicker Daniel Carlson missed a crucial 52-yard field goal in the fourth quarter — his fourth failure in 11 attempts this season. This ongoing volatility in special teams poses a critical problem for the 2-5 Saints.
The fourth-quarter miss was particularly damaging because New Orleans had already wasted a promising red-zone opportunity earlier in the second half. Rather than positioning themselves to tie or take the lead with a field goal late in the game, the Saints remained trapped in a six-point deficit.
Carlson's 63.6% conversion rate stands in sharp contrast to Steelers kicker Chris Boswell , who accounted for nine points by flawlessly making all three of his field goals (from 28, 47 and 39 yards).
With three one-score defeats recorded this year, New Orleans simply lacks the margin for error to withstand repeated scoring blunders in tight contests. Carlson's continuous field goal woes add to head coach Kellen Moore's list of bye-week priorities, as unreliable special teams only exacerbate the team's offensive stalls, defensive breakdowns and turnovers.
While much of the focus has centered on Tyler Shough's growth, an inept rushing attack still severely limits the Saints' offensive ceiling.
Sunday's outing represented a new low point for the ground game.
New Orleans generated a paltry 18 rushing yards across 17 carries, resulting in an abysmal 1.1 yards per carry.
The stat line is even more damning because Shough — a quarterback whose primary role isn't to lead the run game — was the team's top rusher with just 7 yards on three carries.
It is downright appalling that primary backs Alvin Kamara (six carries, five yards) and Kendre Miller (eight carries, six yards) both logged more rush attempts than total yards gained.
This embarrassing output highlights a backfield without a true lead option, further compounded by an offensive line that failed to establish leverage up front.
Such complete non-production is intolerable at any level of football—especially when relying on a developing quarterback to sustain drive after drive.
By stifling the run, Pittsburgh's defense put the burden entirely on Shough's shoulders.
Even with Shough connecting on nearly 79% of his passes, New Orleans repeatedly stalled because it lacked offensive balance.
Unfortunately, this isn't merely a single bad afternoon.
The Saints' season-long inability to establish the run has made the offense predictable and easy for physical front sevens to counter.

title: 3 Takeaways From Saints' Loss to Steelers: Same Problems, Different Country
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints traveled across the Atlantic Ocean hoping to build momentum heading into their bye week and salvage their season. Instead, they returned home with its fourth loss in five games and it just seems like another repeating nightmare for Who Dat Nation.
New Orleans fell 16-10 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in Paris, dropping to 2-5 through seven games under second-year coach Kellen Moore . It was the NFL's first regular-season game in France.
Despite another efficient passing performance from quarterback Tyler Shough , the Saints struggled to establish their rushing attack, failed to capitalize on scoring opportunities and couldn't get off the field defensively when it mattered most.
The loss marked New Orleans' third one-possession defeat this season, reinforcing concerns about the team's ability to execute in critical situations.
Here are three takeaways from another disappointing performance from the Saints performance.
For all the attention surrounding Shough's development, New Orleans' inability to run the football continues to undermine its offense.
Sunday's performance might have been its most concerning yet.
The Saints finished with just 18 rushing yards on 17 attempts, averaging a dismal 1.1 yards per carry.
Even more alarming, Shough led the team with 7 rushing yards on three attempts. However, he is a quarterback and that is not his job.
But for Alvin Kamara (six carries for five yards) and Kendre Miller (eight carries for six yards) to have more carries than rushing yards is disgusting.
It shows the lack of life in a running back room without a primary option, compounded by an offensive line struggling to create leverage.
That level of production is unacceptable for any offense regardless of the level of play, especially one relying on a young quarterback to consistently move the ball.
Pittsburgh's defense shut down the run, forcing Shough to carry nearly the entire offensive load.
Although Shough completed nearly 79% of his passes, New Orleans could not consistently finish drives because it lacked balance.
The problems extend beyond one disappointing performance.
New Orleans has struggled to generate consistent production on the ground throughout the season, making the offense increasingly predictable against physical defensive fronts.
Because of the rushing problems, the Saints had to rely on Shough again.
Shough did everything you could ask of him, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards and a touchdown. However, one costly mistake ultimately changed the game's complexion.
Trailing 13-10 at the start of the second half, New Orleans put together a 13-play drive that moved the offense inside Pittsburgh's 10-yard line as the Saints appeared positioned to take their first lead of the afternoon.
Instead, Shough threw a pass intended for Chris Olave , which Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson intercepted at the Pittsburgh 11-yard line.
The turnover erased a scoring opportunity and let Pittsburgh respond with a field goal, extending its lead to 16-10.
The interception proved costly, but it also highlighted the impossible position Shough has found himself in because of New Orleans' offensive struggles.
Despite completing nearly 79% of his passes, the quarterback could not afford even one mistake because the Saints had virtually no rushing attack to complement him.
That is an unrealistic expectation for any quarterback, much less one still developing at the NFL level.
Shough showed he could move the football against a Pittsburgh defense, distributing the ball effectively and keeping New Orleans competitive despite a one-dimensional offensive approach.
However, his play reinforced a troubling reality: when Shough plays well, the Saints can win; when he makes one mistake, the operation unravels.
Until Moore builds a credible run game and finishes drives, Shough bears an unreasonable load and New Orleans must create an offense where its quarterback does not need to be perfect to win.
Unless the Saints give Shough a credible rushing attack and adequate protection, they risk repeating a familiar chapter in franchise history: asking a talented young quarterback to overcome problems far beyond his control, much like Archie Manning decades ago.
Daniel Carlson 's fourth missed field goal in 11 attempts this season — a 52-yarder in the fourth quarter — kept New Orleans trailing in a 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh, highlighting a critical special teams weakness for the 2-5 Saints.
The missed 52-yard attempt came while the Saints trailed 16-10 in the fourth quarter, keeping Pittsburgh's lead at six points. Carlson's 63.6% success rate contrasts with Steelers kicker Chris Boswell , who converted all three attempts (28, 47 and 39 yards) for nine points.
The fourth-quarter miss was especially costly as New Orleans had already squandered a promising red-zone drive earlier in the second half. Instead of entering the final minutes needing only a field goal to tie or lead, the Saints remained six points behind.
Carlson's kicking struggles add to head coach Kellen Moore's bye-week concerns. For a team hampered by offensive inefficiency, defensive lapses and turnovers, unreliable special teams further shrink a narrow margin for error.
With three one-score losses this season, New Orleans cannot afford missed points. Sunday's loss highlights that the Saints lack the margin for error to overcome recurring scoring mistakes in tight games.

title: Saints vs. Steelers: Full Injury Report, Statistical Comparison and Game Details
full_text:
Heading overseas this Sunday, the New Orleans Saints seek to gather momentum and rectify their ongoing defensive issues as they prepare to battle the Pittsburgh Steelers at Saint-Denis's Stade de France.
Coming off a victory over the New York Giants , New Orleans meets a formidable challenge against a Pittsburgh squad anchored by veteran passer Aaron Rodgers and a tough defensive unit.
In their second season under head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints feature an 11th-ranked scoring attack that posts 25.3 points per contest. Conversely, the defense continues to lag, surrendering 29.7 points (near the bottom of the league) and 377.7 total yards per game.
These defensive shortcomings prompted owner Gayle Benson to issue a public call for better results on the field .
The Saints now line up against a stout Pittsburgh defense that sits 9th in total yards allowed per game (307.5), 8th in pass defense (204.3 YPG), and 6th in third-down conversions allowed (32.5%).
This international contest offers New Orleans a prime stage to demonstrate growth as both franchises fight to stay in the postseason race.

title: Why Giants Special Teams Coach Still Believes in Kicker Dominic Zvada
full_text:
New York Giants assistant head coach/special teams coordinator Chris Horton still believes in kicker Dominic Zvada.
Despite the rookie’s recent struggles, Horton remains confident that Zvada has the physical talent and mental fortitude to be New York’s long-term investment at the position. To ensure that happens, one of his most important post-bye duties will be keeping the kicker’s confidence high.
“I’ve said this before: Just continue to believe in the kid,” Horton said. “Just help him understand some of those misses; a lot of those things are fundamental things that I know we can get fixed, we can take care of.
“We spend a lot of time on the bye week, just diving into it and just thinking about what we can do on these kicks,” he added.
“We just watch those kicks over and over and over again, and he will be consistent, and those are the things that we are expecting of him, and he’s expecting of himself.”
After starting his rookie season a perfect 9-for-9 on field goals, including three makes from 50-plus yards, Zvada’s fortunes have reversed sharply in recent weeks.
The undrafted rookie out of Michigan missed three field-goal attempts in New York’s Week 5 tie with the Washington Commanders, followed by 44- and 56-yard misses in Week 7 against the Texans.
In total, Zvada has connected on 13 of 18 field-goal attempts while going 12-for-12 on extra points.
Though some have begun to question whether Zvada’s difficulties may be a harbinger of things to come, Horton made it clear that the Giants are not yet ready to declare them a worrisome problem.
“I don’t think that’s something that we think about,” Horton said. “I think we think about the process of now, where are we now? And so far, you think about the kicks that he has missed, the five kicks that he’s missed, again, to me, those are all fundamental things that we can work on. I don’t think you go into it and say, ‘hey, alright, we need to be worried about this, we need to be worried about that.’”
Head coach John Harbaugh has also said the Giants have no current plans to make a change at kicker. After all, Zvada is still in the midst of an impressive season.
His 51 points not only put him on track to lead all rookies in scoring in 2026 (Ali Haji-Sheikh had 127 in 1983), but also put him just two points behind Washington Commanders kicker Drew Stevens.
Therefore, they remain hopeful that helping Zvada with his plant-foot placement and other fixable mechanics will be enough to get him back on track. While the talent is clearly there, New York cannot afford for its kicking game to become a liability in a postseason bid, a point Horton knows all too well.
“We just let him go out there, and we perform, and we believe in him, let him know we believe in him, and then, yes, we expect kicks to go in,” Horton said. “That’s a requirement. Those are the things that we are asking of him, and he’s asking of himself, and we put him out there, and he’ll go get it done.”
Zvada and the Giants will return from their bye with a Week 9 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.
