title: Giants Injury Report: Skattebo Out Again, Nabers Added With Knee Issue
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo missed his second straight day of practice with a hamstring strain, further putting his status for Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles in doubt.
Skattebo was seen on the sideline with a trainer during the media viewing portion of practice. It’s probably safe to say that if he doesn’t get at least some practice in on Friday, he’s likely to be scratched for Sunday, with the team instead eyeing the second-year running back for its Thursday night game against the Washington Commanders four days later.
Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers are the healthy running backs on the roster, with Tyrone Tracy on injured reserve. The team also has Eric Gray and Phil Mafah on the practice squad.
Receiver Malik Nabers, the newly minted NFC Offensive Player of the Month for October 2026, is now on the team’s injury report after missing Thursday’s practice.
Nabers, who appears to have put the ACL injury that ended his 2025 season firmly in the rearview mirror, was listed with a knee injury and did not participate Thursday.
Nabers last appeared on the injury report in Week 5 with a knee ailment, missing Wednesday’s practice, being limited Thursday and returning to full participation Friday.
Nabers assured reporters that he’d “be good” for Sunday’s game against the Eagles.
In other injury developments, receiver/return specialist Charlie Jones (hand), wearing a red non-contact jersey, was seen with a cast on his hand while trying, unsuccessfully, to field punts during the media portion of Thursday’s practice.
Jones also participated in a limited capacity Wednesday.
The Giants’ unofficial depth chart lists safety Jevon Holland as the backup punt returner, but it’s unlikely they would go in that direction since Holland is a starter.
On kickoff returns, assistant head coach/special teams coordinator Chris Horton didn’t rule out using starting cornerback Deonte Banks alongside Singletary, who is expected to have a bigger role on offense if Skattebo can’t play.
“I don’t think anything’s off the shelf,” Horton said. “We talk about trying to win football games. And if that gives us the best opportunity to win a football game. We’re talking about one rep. We’re talking about one rep where we can go out there and have the most success. So I don’t think anything’s off the table in that regard.”
The most likely scenario is that running back Eric Gray gets the call-up from the practice squad, since he has experience on punt and kickoff returns. Gray would also give the Giants additional depth at running back if Skattebo can’t play Sunday.
Outside linebacker Abdul Carter (illness) returned to practice on a limited basis after being sent home Wednesday to rest.
In addition to Nabers, four other Giants were added to the injury report: defensive lineman Darius Alexander (foot), tight end Thomas Fidone II (thumb), outside linebacker Trace Ford (knee) and inside linebacker Micah McFadden (foot). All four were full participants.
As anticipated, quarterback Jake Haener was waived from the 53-man roster. The Giants will look to add him back to the practice squad, but they will need an extra roster spot to accommodate the injury-related additions.
The Giants had four players in for a tryout Thursday: receivers Maurice Alexander, River Cracraft and Steven Sims, and punter Wes Pahl.

title: Malik Nabers Named NFC Offensive Player of the Month for October
full_text:
The New York Giants have finally seen the best of wide receiver Malik Nabers since his return from an ACL injury in 2025, and the rest of the league is taking notice.
The NFL named Nabers NFC Offensive Player of the Month after a highly productive October for the third-year pass catcher. The recognition is Nabers’ first since the Giants drafted him with the No. 6 pick in the 2024 draft, and it makes him the first wide receiver to bring it home to East Rutherford.
The other six award winners for Big Blue are Tiki Barber (three-time winner), Kerry Collins (December 2002), Brandon Jacobs (October 2007), Eli Manning (November 2008), David Meggett (September 1994) and Phil Simms (December 1986).
Nabers joined the Giants carrying immense expectations for a high first-round selection and another talented receiver from the LSU pipeline, where he authored back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons in 2022 and 2023 and finished his career with 189 catches, 3,003 yards and 21 touchdowns.
It looked like Nabers, now 23, was on the fast track to becoming one of the best pass catchers in Giants history after his rookie season, when he amassed 109 receptions for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns. His reception total was the most among all first-year players in his class.
The next season, Nabers’ promising start was cut short by a torn ACL in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers, in rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart’s first NFL start, leaving the young signal caller without his trusty No. 1 target to ease the transition.
There was concern about how quickly Nabers would return in his first year under head coach John Harbaugh, and what his abilities would look like coming off a significant injury and long rehab.
No. 1 made it back to the field in time for the Giants’ season opener against the Dallas Cowboys, announcing his return with six catches for 69 yards and flashing his vertical skills with a long of 16 yards to help New York defeat its division rival 28-20 in front of the blue faithful.
Despite losing the long-awaited chance to pair with Dart when the quarterback went down for the season in Week 2, and having to find chemistry with two other quarterbacks in Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy, Nabers has been stellar in reminding everyone why he was the most coveted receiver in his class.
With October in the books, he finished atop the league with 36 catches for 509 yards and the two aforementioned scores. His 36 receptions were second-most in the same span and helped the Giants go 2-1-1 to establish a strong grip on first place in the NFC East.
Nabers leads the Giants with 48 receptions on 70 targets for 605 yards (12.6 average) and two receiving touchdowns after seven starts this season.
He is also on a four-game streak of 100-plus receiving yards, including a season-high 165 yards on 12 catches against the Saints in Week 6. It is the longest active streak in the league and matches the franchise’s second-longest run, set by Odell Beckham Jr. in 2014.
The pairing of Nabers and McCarthy has gotten off to a solid start as the two playmakers have become familiar with each other and aim to push the Giants’ success into the second half of the year.
After Nabers vowed to get open for his new starting gunslinger and delivered in the team’s most recent victory over the Houston Texans, he’ll have another chance to dominate Sunday when the Giants travel to Philadelphia to face the Eagles in the first of two highly important divisional meetings.
One can’t deny he is making the Giants fan base excited for what the next couple of months could bring. He also shines a light on his alma mater with his award, becoming the third LSU product to earn it, joining quarterback Joe Burrow and wide receiver Justin Jefferson.

title: J.J. McCarthy Says Bye Week Left Him “Caught Up Completely” Before Eagles Test
full_text:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy is understandably eager to get back to work.
With a well-deserved Week 8 bye now firmly behind them, Big Blue’s starting quarterback is once again preparing to lead his team in pursuit of their first postseason appearance since 2022. Their first battle in that quest comes in Week 9 against the Philadelphia Eagles this Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field.
Despite the Eagles' 2-6 record and an avalanche of injuries, McCarthy knows that New York’s bitter rivals will pose a formidable challenge.
“It’s all about getting into the film room and just focusing on the things we can clean up, little things, little details,” McCarthy told reporters earlier this week. “And we’ve got a great team this week, going into their house. It’s going to be a hostile environment, a great defense. We’re looking forward to the challenge.”
Since being acquired by the Giants via trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28, the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft has quickly grasped the playbook and shown comfort in coordinator Matt Nagy’s offense.
McCarthy first took the Giants’ offensive reins with 11 minutes remaining in the fourth quarter of the team’s Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints, after starter Jameis Winston’s second interception of the day.
The Michigan product finished the game having completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards and one touchdown.
After being named Big Blue’s new starter by coach John Harbaugh, McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes (71.4% completion) for 252 yards and a passer rating of 99.1 in New York’s 27-21 victory over the Houston Texans in Week 7.
While he has enjoyed notable success since his auspicious debut, McCarthy wisely used the bye week to improve his game for the Giants’ potential run to the playoffs.
“The bye week came at a great time,” McCarthy said. “I definitely feel caught up completely with our offense and the intent behind every single play. And that’s a credit to all the guys in the room with me, all the coaches, and everyone on this team.
“They’ve helped me out so much, and I’m extremely blessed to be able to take advantage of this downtime that we had and really work on the mental game and make sure we’re caught up and definitely feel like I’m in a really good spot in terms of operating this offense.”
McCarthy will need his best performance of the season to gain the upper hand on an Eagles defense that can still make life difficult for opposing offenses.
Led by defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, Philadelphia’s defense is at its best when playing downhill from a deep-safety shell, often using either split-field or pre-snap two-high safety looks.
In short, the Eagles’ defense is designed to prevent the big play, a point that McCarthy knows well.
“Yeah, I think he makes you earn it the long way and the hard way,” he said of Fangio’s defense.
“Just being able to keep everything in front of him, he gets pressure with four most of the time and tries to play deep to short. A lot of single high safety, and a bunch of simulated pressures, if you will, where it can confuse the protections, and if you can keep the back in, we only got four viable receivers out on routes, but (they’ve) got tremendous players.
“It’s an absolutely talented defense,” he continued. “I’ve got so much respect for every single one of those guys out there on that field, and tremendous respect for Coach Vic, for sure.”
With division wins at a premium, McCarthy knows the Giants must take full advantage of an Eagles team that has struggled to date.
If he delivers a performance equal to or better than his previous outings, the Giants will take a significant step toward entering the postseason as NFC East champions for the first time since 2011.
For McCarthy, the chance to lead the Giants is the blessing he has sought since joining the NFL.
“I think the way I would describe it is, I’m just so blessed. I’m so blessed to be a part of this team,” McCarthy said.
“So blessed to be a part of this historic organization and feeling the love on the outside, it just is so motivating to continue to do our job at a high level and keep doing whatever we can to win football games for this organization.
“I can’t thank everyone enough for making it feel like home for me,” he added. “It means the absolute world. But yeah, it feels absolutely amazing to put on that blue every single Sunday.”

title: Coughlin Makes Hall of Fame Cut, Joins Belichick and Three Others as Coaching Finalist
full_text:
Legendary New York Giants head coach Tom Coughlin, a two-time Super Bowl winner, is among the five nominees for the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Coaching category.
Coughlin made the cut from the original list of 14 nominees. On Nov. 17, the Hall of Fame subcommittee will meet virtually to narrow the five-member list to one candidate. That candidate’s name will be submitted to the full selection committee, which will vote on the Class of 2027 in early 2027.
Coughlin began his head coaching career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (1995-2002) before signing with the Giants (2004-2015) and ushering in a new and prosperous era of Big Blue football with Eli Manning as the team’s franchise quarterback.
Coughlin posted a 182-157 record (including playoffs). In addition to the two Super Bowl championships he won as head coach of the Giants, Coughlin was part of Hall of Fame head coach Bill Parcells’ assistant coaching staff when the franchise won its first Super Bowl championship in 1986.
In addition to Coughlin, two of the other four remaining coaching nominees have ties to the Giants organization.
Bill Belichick, like Coughlin, served as an assistant on Parcells’ staff, first as a special teams/defensive assistant in 1979, then as the special teams/linebackers coach from 1980 to 1984, and then as the defensive coordinator from 1985 to 1990.
Belichick’s candidacy, though, rests on his legacy as head coach of the New England Patriots, where he coached from 2000 to 2023 and won six Super Bowl titles.
Dan Reeves is the other candidate with ties to the Giants organization. Reeves served as the Giants’ head coach from 1993 to 1996 after spending most of his head coaching career with Denver.
His Broncos teams went to the Super Bowl three times, and he also led the Atlanta Falcons, whom he coached from 1997 to 2003, to a Super Bowl appearance. Unfortunately, he didn’t have that kind of luck with the Giants.
The other two head coaching finalists are Mike Shanahan, who coached the Raiders, Broncos and Commanders, and Mike Holmgren, who coached the Packers and Seahawks.

title: Harbaugh Says Giants Aren’t Looking Ahead, Even as They Lead the NFC East
full_text:
Every so often, New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh likes to dabble in history when he speaks to the media.
But when it comes to football, he’s less interested in the past than in the future.
That’s why Harbaugh, whose NFC East-leading Giants are getting ready for their first game after the bye, isn’t worried about his players becoming complacent about what they have accomplished so far.
“I do think that that’s definitely something to get locked in on, but I don’t believe it is this week,” he said on Wednesday as the team kicked off its preparation for Sunday’s NFC East showdown with a wounded Philadelphia Eagles team that, by the way, has beaten the Giants 13 straight times at Lincoln Financial Field.
“Although our players have mentioned it, our leaders have talked to the guys about that. We’re not really anywhere close to that yet. We’re fighting for our lives, too. We’ve got everything to gain, and we know how big this game is. We know who we’re going against. We’ll be ready.”
They need to be. Beyond the long, winless drought in the City of Brotherly Love, the Giants have a chance to keep putting space between themselves and the rest of the division, especially considering that each division game counts in the season-ending tiebreakers, the first of which is head-to-head.
And with a challenging slate of opponents coming up, starting in Week 11 when the Jacksonville Jaguars come to town, the Giants can ill afford to slip up this week or next week when they host the Washington Commanders on Thursday Night Football .
But while Harbaugh clearly knows where things stand in the division, the only thing driving him is making sure the team goes 1-0 every week.
“Yeah, we’ve got to win the game. The opportunity is the game, and within the game, the opportunity is the next play within the game, right? That’s the opportunity,” he said.
“This is the game, the game where everything is on the line. Once this game is done, it will be the next game where everything is on the line. That’s how our guys look at it, and that’s what that 1-0 T-shirt is all about.
“So, I know these guys think that way. That’s the way they think. That doesn’t guarantee you’re going to play great, but that’s their mindset going into the game.”

title: Why Tony Pollard Could Be the Giants’ Best Fallback if the Jonathan Taylor Bid Fails
full_text:
With less than a week until the NFL’s annual trade deadline on Nov. 10, the New York Giants are busy hunting for roster additions that could strengthen their chase for the NFC East crown.
One position New York has made clear it wants to address is running back, where head coach John Harbaugh wants a bell-cow option, and the team has reportedly been an aggressive suitor in the bidding war for Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor amid the franchise’s selloff of top talent.
However, the Giants’ chances of casting the winning bid for Taylor’s services feel extremely unlikely given the Colts’ reported asking price of a huge haul of draft capital. The Giants are already missing a couple of mid-round picks in 2027, and a slew of other reported suitors have more to offer.
The Giants may also have found new hope in their current backfield, led by Cam Skattebo, who answered their coach’s call to boost the run game with a 188-yard, three-touchdown performance in the Week 7 win over the Houston Texans.
Even with that stellar game for the group, Big Blue’s rushing attack still ranks 20th in the league in average yards per carry , meaning there is room to reach their ceiling with a solid addition that won’t break their bank or carry much risk.
If the Giants bow out of the bidding for Taylor or lose it, the next best option, assuming he’s available for a trade, is Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard.
The Giants are familiar with Pollard from his days facing them in the NFC East as a member of the Dallas Cowboys.
In his first five pro seasons with the Cowboys, Pollard started his career as the late-down back behind former All-Pro Ezekiel Elliott. As heavy usage and injuries ate into Elliott’s efficiency, the 2019 fourth-round pick out of Memphis earned his shot at more reps and a flashier rushing resume.
Since the start of the 2021 season, Pollard has topped 130 carries and 719 yards in every year while averaging 4.65 yards per carry.
That includes four consecutive 1,000-yard campaigns, two with the Cowboys and two more after joining the Titans in 2024. He also has 32 rushing touchdowns, which ranks 14th among active running backs since the 2021 season.
With eight games under his belt in 2026, Pollard has tallied 133 carries for 595 yards (4.5 average) and six touchdowns, making him the most productive weapon in Tennessee’s offense while creating a team-best 83.2 scrimmage yards per contest.
The intrigue around Pollard also comes from his reliability: he has missed only four of 125 games while starting 64 throughout his eight-year career, and he does a good job protecting the football, having fumbled more than twice in only one season.
For the Giants, adding a running back like Pollard would, most importantly, upgrade their backfield. Skattebo’s presence as an uber-physical rusher who fights for extra yards has been a big factor in New York’s top-15 status when running up the middle.
Running outside the tackles hasn’t been as efficient, and Skattebo’s physical style likely doesn’t translate to outside zone runs. The Giants have taken only 41 rushing plays beyond the B-gaps this season and averaged 2.2 yards per attempt , which lands them near the basement, per NFL GSIS.
Some might want to blame the offensive line’s suspect run blocking, but the key is that the Giants are missing an experienced running back with the intangibles to handle a larger load of outside zone rushing, and Pollard could fill that void.
Pollard’s best reps this season have come on the edges, where he earned 53 total carries for 261 yards and an average haul as high as 7.2 yards, per PFF advanced data. He has churned over 10 yards on six of those attempts and used his frame and shiftiness to produce 210 yards after contact and 13 of 23 missed tackles this year.
Inserting him into the top of the rushing rotation would give Harbaugh his three-down bell-cow while the Giants can mix in Skattebo’s power to help convert critical short-yardage downs that swing football games in their favor.
The Titans seem to love what Pollard has been bringing to their offense since he arrived in 2024. They’ve even suggested the veteran running back isn’t on the table ahead of the deadline.
The Titans are an extremely young team and far from the same level as the Giants, and they’ll have to address the lack of talent at several key positions this offseason and in the draft. Keeping pricier veterans like Pollard might not make sense when they can gain some extra capital for the next stage of their roster rebuild.
The Giants have been an aggressive suitor for a running back despite their arguably larger need at defensive tackle and their limited array of draft choices in 2027. Still, Harbaugh understands what making a big splash can do for his offense and the health of his roster.
The only issue is that Pollard will be a free agent at the end of the season, making him a rental who would require the Giants to give him a new contract if they want him as their bell-cow back beyond the final nine games.
If they were interested in such an arrangement, Pollard would likely replace Devin Singletary, who is also set to be an unrestricted free agent in the offseason. Singletary, nicknamed “Motor,” brings a special set of intangibles to the Giants’ ground game, but his days as a No. 1 back are long behind him.
Harbaugh could get his lead back in Pollard with Skattebo as the power back, and Tyrone Tracy sprinkled in as the pass-down back, leaving New York with a respectable trio in the backfield.
Aside from having to offer him a new deal at some point, the best projection of Pollard’s trade value is a Day 3 pick and, more specifically, a sixth-round selection based on the comparison of what the Bengals got from the Texans for Joe Mixon.
Again, the Giants face a bit of a dilemma in parting with any draft capital unless they are willing to dig into their 2028 picks. They already do not own a fourth- or fifth-round pick after the J.J. McCarthy deal with Minnesota, and losing a third pick would leave them with just three total picks this April.
A continued positive stretch for McCarthy could open the door for the Giants to trade him in the offseason and reclaim a pick or two, and it sounds like Harbaugh is already bold enough to sacrifice more draft assets to pry Jonathan Taylor from Indianapolis.
The difference is Taylor wouldn’t be a rental, since he is under contract through the 2027 season, and while a lack of assets is hurting the Giants’ chances of landing him, he has a much more accomplished resume that could make it worth it.

title: Greg Newsome II Bet on Himself, and It Paid Off With a $46 Million Extension
full_text:
There’s no safer bet in life than betting on yourself.
That’s exactly what New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II did. The 26-year-old signed a low-risk, high-reward one-year deal worth $8 million (including incentives) with Big Blue this offseason.
Seven games into that contract, Newsome has parlayed that “prove it” deal into a three-year, $46 million extension with $32 million guaranteed that he officially signed on Wednesday.
Not that Newsome ever doubted this was the direction things were heading.
“I knew the type of person I was, first and foremost. And I knew what type of player I was, and I knew that if I get to the right place, the money will take care of itself,” he said on Wednesday.
“I feel like when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted, you’re somewhere that you’re loved, everything else takes care of itself. So, I knew this would be the place.”
The Giants certainly wanted Newsome, a former first-round pick of the Browns whose up-and-down tenure in Cleveland ended when he was traded to Jacksonville midway through last season.
The trade proved a poor fit for Newsome’s strengths. He struggled in Jacksonville’s system, and the Jaguars showed little interest in bringing him back.
“Yeah, I definitely think it’s difficult. When you play in a primarily man-to-man, press scheme, getting traded midseason to a place where it’s a lot of zone, it’s a lot of reading different things and just learning your teammates, learning where you fit in that defense, learning everyone’s strengths, it’s definitely tough,” Newsome said.
“But God doesn’t make mistakes, and I feel like that helped me in the long run, just being able to adjust and get out of your comfort zone in a sense.”
With the Giants, Newsome has found that comfort zone. He has allowed a career-low 57% completion rate and has a 62.0 coverage rating.
Newsome has also not allowed a touchdown and has four pass breakups and one interception, matching what he did in 2023 with Cleveland, when he had his best season as a pro.
“(Defensive coordinator) Dennard (Wilson) has the perfect scheme for me,” he said. “Being able to challenge people, being aggressive and things like that. And just, man, just the ability to play with all 11 guys. We got some of the best players in the league, so they make my job a lot easier as well.”
Newsome is confident his best football is still ahead, but he recognized that the smart move was to strike while the financial iron was hot.
“You obviously could play it out, maybe make a few more millions, continue to play well. But for me, it’s not really about that,” he said.
“Once again, I chose (the Giants) because it just fits me. The coaches, my teammates — I love being around these guys.”
That love made accepting the Giants’ extension offer a no-brainer.
“It wasn’t, ‘how about I play it out and maybe make a few more millions?’ Obviously, it would be great to have a few more, but when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted and loved, the money, I’m getting good enough money that I’ll be secure for the rest of my life,” he said.
As the Giants prepare for their Week 9 showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles, Newsome will need to keep playing at a high level to help the team maintain its success. If New York hopes to earn its first trip to the playoffs since 2022, Newsome and the defense must meet the challenge every week.
The fans’ confidence and acceptance have not gone unnoticed by Newsome.
“Just seeing how passionate the fans are, just seeing how I come in and do the things that I want to do, and the fans are behind it,” Newsome said.
“They were behind me being here, and all that I can ask for is just to do my best for this fan base. And I’ll continue to see that as well. Obviously, they like winners. That’s what fans like, and we’re going to continue to do that.”

title: Giants Look to End 13-Game Losing Streak at Philadelphia
full_text:
The table has been set for the New York Giants — now all they have to do is cook the meal, and that means following a winning recipe one step at a time.
Head coach John Harbaugh has his team atop the NFC East at 4-2-1 as they come off their bye week with a visit to Philadelphia (2-6).
They have already beaten Dallas (3-5) and own a road tie against the Commanders (2-4-1). Yet he continues to tell his players to focus on the upcoming game, even though there’s little doubt they realize they’ve put themselves in good position to make a second-half run at the playoffs.
“I think they do keep it in mind,” Harbaugh said.
“It’s definitely always forefront because that’s the ultimate goal. We’ll bring it up every now and then, just answering the question in terms of how often, I don’t really know. Whenever it comes up or comes to mind, it probably gets mentioned. It’s more in context of what is the value of this game.
“What is the big picture value of this game? Why is this game so important? Why does this game matter? Why does this game require all of our attention? Because this game puts us in this position for what we’re trying to accomplish, ultimately. That’s really the context of it.”
The Giants have dropped 13 straight road games at Philadelphia since Josh Brown booted five field goals in a 15-7 victory on Oct. 27, 2013. Of course, none of their active players were on that roster, and that’s fine with Harbaugh, who knows you can only control the present.
“Our guys keep it in perspective, it really comes back to one play at a time. I know it’s a cliche, but it’s true,” he said.
“If you can do that and if you can lock in on one play, because it could be the play that makes a difference in the game, you have the best chance to be successful in that play. I think it all ties together, I guess is what I’m saying.”
Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen are always looking to improve the team, and the NFL’s trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.
It’s impossible to predict whether they will find the right price and the right trading partner to make a move. They have put themselves in a strong spot with the most difficult part of their schedule ahead.

title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) tops the team’s Week 9 injury report after missing Wednesday’s practice.
Skattebo was injured on his 42-yard run in overtime against the Houston Texans two weeks ago.
At the time, he tried to downplay the injury, but head coach John Harbaugh later characterized the running back as “day to day up to the game,” and said, “We’re just going to have to see where we’re at.”
Where things stand doesn’t look very promising, as hamstrings are tricky injuries and Skattebo’s absence from practice has raised concerns for the Giants, especially since Tyrone Tracy Jr. is currently on injured reserve with his own hamstring injury, also suffered in the game against the Texans.
Skattebo undoubtedly doesn’t want to miss any more time, especially after losing most of his rookie campaign last year to an ankle injury.
There’s obviously an extra motivating factor for Skattebo to be ready for Sunday’s game against Philadelphia because last year’s ankle injury happened on the Lincoln Financial Field turf, and for him to return to the scene of the crime and post another career day that matches or tops his Houston performance (17 carries, 124 yards, one touchdown) would bring his comeback full circle.
If Skattebo can’t go, the Giants will likely turn to Devin Singletary as their lead back. They also have Greg Desrosiers on the roster, whom they signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad last week, and they will likely elevate either Phil Mafaha or Eric Gray, the latter signed this week to the practice squad, for Sunday’s game.
"I feel very confident about the running back situation. I like the guys we've got," Harbaugh said. "Obviously, Motor (Devin Singletary) has been here. We've got some guys that have been here in the past, too, that we brought in, as you know, that were here, and we also brought in one, (running back) Eric (Gray).
"So, I feel good about it. We claimed a guy off the Chargers (Gregory Desrosiers). He's a very talented, young guy. So, those guys are in practice. They've got two practices now, and if they have to go, they'll definitely be ready to roll."
While it’s too soon to say for certain what Skattebo’s status will be for Sunday, keep in mind that the Giants have a short work week following their game against Philadelphia.
If Skattebo isn’t at least limited in the next day or two, it might make sense for him to sit out Sunday’s game so he’s ready for the clash against the Commanders on Thursday night.
Sitting Sunday would give him a few extra days to get right for that game, and a longer break afterward to make more progress on his hamstring.
Linebacker Abdul Carter, who missed Monday’s light practice due to illness, remained sidelined on Wednesday as he continues to recover.
Harbaugh, who said the lienbacker was home resting, "should be fine" for Sunday’s game against the Eagles.

title: Joseph Ossai Will Be on the Clock to Prove Himself to Jets Upon Returning From Injury
full_text:
As the Jets' Week 9 clash with the Chiefs nears, veteran pass rusherJoseph Ossai is back at practice after his ankle injury . The 26-year-old has missed five games this season and has not lived up to his $34.5 million price tag in the games he has played.
With the money he is promised, Ossai will already be under scrutiny when he takes the field Sunday.
Ossai is coming off a 2025 season in which he recorded five sacks and earned a 64.0 Pro Football Focus grade . This year, Ossai has yet to bring down the QB and has a 49.6 PFF grade. The former Bengal's time is running out to prove he was worth the price New York paid, especially if he can't make an immediate impact.
Ossai potentially returns to a Jets defense that got rang up for 38 points in Week 8. New York only sacked Kirk Cousins once and gave up 95 rushing yards to a Las Vegas team ranked 31st in the category in 2026. The bar is low for Ossai to show his value coming off a game like that.
Ossai must show up in some way on the stat sheet. He has 10 total tackles this season, with seven against the Bears. The real issue is the lack of pressure that Ossai has put on opposing quarterbacks. In 49 pass-rush snaps this season, Ossai has yet to record a single pressure. For comparison, he had 43 in 14 games with the Bengals last season—an average of 3.1 per outing.
The veteran disruptor has to find himself in the backfield soon.
New York may start to feel buyer's remorse if the fifth-year veteran does not start to impact games. Missing five games and not pressuring the quarterback won't keep Ossai employed; stats will. Whether it's in the running or passing game, Ossai must perform in his first game back to prove he is worth his contract.
Joseph Ossai doesn't need to sack Patrick Mahomes multiple times in Week 9 or become the Jets' sack leader to meet expectations. He just needs to be a legitimate option for the Jets' defensive line. If Ossai is to be back for the trip to Kansas City, he has a chance to stake his claim.
The Chiefs' offensive line has been less than stellar in pass protection this season. Kansas City allows a 37% pressure rate, ranking 19th in the NFL. This is the type of welcome back that Ossai should be clamoring for. If the veteran can get in the backfield and impact the passing game, questions about his contract will begin to dissipate.
Ossai can also help against Kenneth Walker and the run. The end had a 70.7 grade against the run in 2025; this year it's a measly 54.3. Ossai needs to return to form against the NFL's third-leading rusher. As a Bengal, Ossai showed he could impact the run, with 21 stops in 2025. He needs to show that he still has that skill set against Kansas City and for the rest of the season.
For the rest of 2026, the defensive end has to perform. Whether sacks or pressures, Ossai needs to start affecting the passer. He also needs to be the run-stopper the Jets know he can be. With zero sacks and only two run stops this season, the defensive end has been a far cry from his best.
Ossai will look to return and be the game-changer he and the organization know he can be.
He's yet to live up to his three-year, $34.5 million contract. Three games of subpar football are not what Ossai was paid to do. The clock is ticking for the 26-year-old, and every game he doesn't show up for gets him one step closer to midnight. A trade after June 1, 2027, would save the Jets $10.5 million in cap space while only taking on $1.75 million in dead money, per OverTheCap .
Ossai must return to form if his career as a Jet is to be anything but a mistake.

title: Forgotten Jets Rookie's Potential Return Could Signal the End of Andre Cisco in New York
full_text:
With another crushing loss behind them and a difficult road test ahead against the Chiefs in Week 9, the 2026 season continues to get away from the Jets as some coaching malpractice and struggles getting off the field defensively continue to plague them.
A double-digit lead was not even enough as the Jets orchestrated a second-half collapse and completely gave the game away at home. That said, injuries have also been a talking point all season, as multiple players have dealt with setbacks since the season began, and that has been no different for rookies VJ Payne and Anez Cooper, as they have still not played a single snap despite being eligible to return since they started the season on injured reserve.
That is about to change for Payne after ESPN 's Rich Cimini reported on Wednesday that "the Jets are opening the 21-day practice window" for him.
The Jets are opening the 21-day practice window for rookie S V.J. Payne, per source. They also signed rookie WR Joe Manjack (Broncos UDFA) to the practice squad. #Jets
That does not necessarily mean that Payne will play on Sunday, but it does suggest his return is on the table after remaining on the injury report coming out of the Week 8 loss .
That is not a good sign for safety Andre Cisco, who had a big role early in the season with at least 44 defensive snaps in the first three games before playing nine or fewer in each of the last five.
For someone who already needed to prove himself coming into the season after a torn pectoral muscle forced him to miss nearly half of his first season in Gang Green in 2025, a one-year, $2.5 million contract would make it easy for the Jets to turn the page on him either by cutting him or trading him by the Nov. 10 trade deadline .
While Cisco's lack of long-term stability is clear, and the questions surrounding his health coming into the season, his outlook grew even murkier after general manager Darren Mougey signed Dane Belton and acquired veteran Minkah Fitzpatrick from the Dolphins to bolster the secondary before the season even began.
Although he had an opportunity to change his Jets future when Fitzpatrick was sidelined by a groin injury earlier this season, Cisco did not exactly make the most of that opening. Even after playing 44 snaps in the Week 1 win over the Titans, he still finished with the third-worst Pro Football Focus grade (52.6) among defenders on the team in that game, which was a sign of what was to come from him in the ensuing weeks.
To be fair, we still have not seen Payne on an NFL field after he suffered a bone bruise in his knee during training camp. However, while he was the last player drafted in this rookie class, the seventh-rounder has the speed, versatility and overall intangibles to likely be able to contribute at some point.
If anything, the Jets may want to see what they have in Payne to see if he has a shot at competing for a role next season. After all, this season is all but lost for the Jets, especially if they lose the next two games to the Chiefs and Bills, as expected.
Even if the Jets don't get rid of Cisco this season and let him finish out the season, knowing that Payne can slot in could lead them to letting the former walk in free agency. With the 39th-ranked overall grade (63.2) and 60th-ranked coverage grade (54.1) out of 98 qualified safeties from PFF , Cisco clearly has some work to do to retain his spot on the roster, even if the Jets keep him around past the deadline.
Cisco may not officially be a lost cause heading into Week 9 like some players are, but he certainly has his work cut out for him with Payne's potential return and a cheap deal that is set to expire at the end of the season. His time in Gotham may not be over at the trade deadline, but if he is fortunate enough to make it past that, Payne could still get pushed out the door by season's end.

title: Frank Reich May Have Tipped the Jets’ Breece Hall Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The Jets are firmly in seller territory just days away from Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, with one name drawing more attention than others : star running back Breece Hall.
While Hall has missed the last four games due to a quad injury, backup Jets RB Braelon Allen has thrived in his spot . The former 2024 fourth-rounder has eclipsed 100 rushing yards in three of his last four games and has racked up 504 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 93 carries over five starts in Hall's absence.
With plenty of RB-needy teams around the NFL, it's not unfathomable to imagine New York being open to a trade—especially if it believes Allen is a legitimate RB1. That said, offensive coordinator Frank Reich's latest comments help shed light on what the Jets seemingly intend to do with their franchise rusher at the trade deadline.
On Thursday, offensive coordinator Frank Rank was asked about how the Jets will split the backfield workload between Allen and Hall when the latter returns. According to ESPN' s Rich Cimini, Frank said that the staff waits for head coach Aaron Glenn to figure out the " framework for what the vision is ," making it clear that it's a work in progress.
Additionally, Reich didn't sound like an OC who's preparing to see his RB1 traded in the coming days.
If the Jets were looking for potential trade partners, chances are that Reich would be doing everything to hype up Hall's eventual return. Whether that would've been talking about how good he's looked lately or the potential impact he brings to the field, Reich would've done something to boost Hall's trade value.
Instead, Reich made it abundantly clear that the Jets are legitimately trying to figure out how a Hall-Allen tandem could work . The offense has been a sore spot all season, but even though the playoffs are likely out of reach, figuring out how to weaponize the potentially two-headed beast could help Gang Green hit the ground running (no pun intended) in 2027.
The RB duo's contract situation also likely plays a role in why a trade likely isn't in the cards. Hall is still under contract with $14.5 million and $15.5 million cap hits in 2026 and 2027 , respectively, while Allen won't hit free agency until 2028 and carries an affordable $1.3 million cap hit next season.
Realistically, the Jets could take the rest of the 2026 campaign, the 2027 offseason and the first few games of next season to decide if they want to trade Hall. As mentioned above, he isn't a free agent until 2029, meaning they can still recoup some decent value since he'd be more than a rental. Besides, Hall likely needs to prove he can stay healthy and productive before any team is willing to pay the potential ransom New York might ask for.
Assuming his health continues to improve, Jets fans can expect to see Hall in Gang Green against the Chiefs in Week 9, as well as for the rest of the season beyond the trade deadline.

title: Kenyon Sadiq’s Quiet Stretch Raises a bigger Questions About the Jets
full_text:
Following his breakout in Week 3, it seemed like New York Jets first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq was on the precipice of stardom.
Seven catches, 105 yards and a touchdown had left the Detroit Lions flummoxed about how to defend him, and the Jets thrilled with what he could bring to the offense.
Since then, though, Sadiq has been quiet. Horrifically quiet. After his dominant performance in September, he has been targeted 13 times, has caught five passes, with just 43 yards to boot. All of the success found earlier in the season has seemed to go away.
It's left some Jets fans worried. What has caused Sadiq's quiet stat sheet over the last several weeks? Is he not as good as many fans may have hoped?
In reality, there should be no concern about Sadiq's standing. It just highlights the true failing of the team's coaching staff.
Rookie seasons for tight ends are always a crapshoot. Young players have to learn how to both block and operate the route tree for NFL offenses. There should be no fan that is concerned over what Sadiq can do on the field. The fact he had one breakout game is enough to show his upside.
The reason why he hasn't gotten the ball is the same reason Garrett Wilson and other top targets have had uneven target share seasons: there are so many weapons to get the ball to.
"It's only one ball, and Garrett [Wilson] has to get it, Braelon [Allen] has to get it, Sadiq has to get it, Mason [Taylor] has to get it," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said last week .
In fairness to the team, it's a great problem to have. With so many weapons, the offense can target specific matchups against their opponents to get the ball to their best players. There is a reason why the group has seemingly turned a corner as a collective group.
Sadiq will be a part of that. And his breakouts will come in time.
"He's uncoverable, the way I see it," Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson said after his breakout in Week 3. "You can put safeties on him and stuff, but he's just a tough cover. You got a guy that runs that well, that can catch the ball ... Not to mention he's confident. He's a great dude to be around. It's awesome to have him here."
Despite all the positive future thoughts, though, the reality is this coaching staff is unable to make the most of the unit they have.
The true reality of Sadiq's statistical fallout over the last month has only highlighted how much offensive coordinator Frank Reich has failed this group. When the team first drafted Sadiq, they understood they had to come up with a plan to find success with the rookie and second-year tight end Mason Taylor.
Reich pointed to his past experience with two tight ends, and the fact he had a plan to get Sadiq going as an offensive weapon.
Through eight games, it's clear there is no plan. The offensive game plan is not creative enough to scheme players open or have people stand out in matchups. New York runs its offense the exact way they always do.
They are unable and unwilling to adapt.

title: Projected Breece Hall-Broncos Trade Nets Jets Realistic Return as New Era Begins
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, playoff contenders are looking to strengthen their rosters for the postseason, whereas teams near the bottom of the standings are beginning to sell veteran players for future draft capital.
That’s been the Jets’ strategy for most of the last 15 years, and it’ll likely continue this year with Gang Green sitting at 2-6.
New York traded away cornerstone players Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams for multiple first-round selections last year, and while we shouldn’t expect New York to do another fire sale, the team could move on from star running back Breece Hall.
With Braelon Allen breaking out during Hall’s five-game absence , rushing for 504 yards and three touchdowns, a backfield controversy has emerged that could ultimately lead to the Jets trading Hall.
One team in desperate need of a running back is the Broncos, who placed Tyler Badie and R.J. Harvey on injured reserve over the last couple weeks. With Denver currently sitting second in the AFC standings at 6-2, the Broncos have plenty of incentive to pursue a trade for Hall as they look to strengthen their backfield for a playoff run.
A potential deal between the two teams could give New York more valuable draft capital while providing Denver with much-needed help in the backfield.
While head coach Aaron Glenn said that the five-year veteran isn’t going anywhere, per ESPN’s Rich Cimini , his word may not carry as much weight as it once did. Since Glenn took over coaching duties in 2025, the Jets have posted a 5-20 record and are 0-8 against the AFC East.
His tenure has been highlighted by poor coaching decisions and a lack of improvement despite a major overhaul to the roster this past offseason. It’s unlikely Glenn will keep his job beyond 2026, and the team’s best interest should be setting the next era of Gang Green football up for success.
Darren Mougey will play a large role in doing so.
Over his two seasons as New York’s general manager, he’s built a strong foundation of valuable draft capital by trading Gardner and Williams. He’s also had early success in his draft classes, with Armand Membou and David Bailey among his most notable selections.
Trading Hall would add to this.
Although a third-round pick isn’t the greatest asset, it’s a valuable return, and it would add to New York’s massive stockpile of draft capital.
The pick would put the Jets at 10 picks for the 2027 draft, six of them coming in the first three rounds. That would give the Jets plenty of flexibility to address multiple areas or trade for an immediate starter.
Running back trades are tricky.
Years ago, teams spent high-value draft picks on running backs, but since the Trent Richardson trade in 2013, the market for the position has changed significantly. The Christian McCaffrey trade in 2022 was by far the biggest one, as the 49ers gave up 2023 second-, third-, and fourth-round pick plus a 2024 fifth-round pick.
Remember, McCaffrey was a top-three player at the position who was just entering his prime years. While Hall isn’t on the level of McCaffrey, he’s coming off the best season of his career and is still just 25 years old.
The Jets reportedly turned down a fourth-round offer from the Chiefs for Hall last season, with Mougey insisting on receiving a third-round pick in return. With Hall’s best years ahead of him, a third-round pick is a reasonable deal for both sides.
With Hall under contract through 2028, Denver would strengthen its chances throughout the next several years of its Super Bowl window.
For New York, it provides more valuable draft capital to build their team for next season while allowing Allen to take over as the team’s starting running back.
We’ve seen that the Jets aren’t close to competing for a championship; however, they are a few pieces away from being a playoff-caliber team. Trading Hall to Denver for a third-round pick would be a step towards ending the 15-year playoff drought.

title: 3 Most Realistic Jets' Trade Candidates Entering Final Week Before Deadline
full_text:
We're under a week away from the NFL trade deadline and it appears the New York Jets are ready to be silent. Last season, they gave away Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams in mega-deals.
It's clear the team won't be dealing with something similar this year.
Still, there are three players who could find themselves in a new home away from Florham Park. Let's go through the three most likely candidates to be moved going into next week.
Early in the year, Brownlee was New York's best player in the secondary. A dip in production, coupled with an in-season benching and struggles in Week 8 has made Brownlee expendable. More importantly, the team has D'Angelo Ponds waiting in the wings to get reps across the board.
Brownlee may not get a lot on the market, but his role for the team simply doesn't match where the team is currently. New York would be best served moving on from him and allowing Ponds to play.
McDonald is a player that will arguably carry the most return for the franchise if they actually end up being sellers. He has three sacks this season, but over 21 in his first three years in the NFL. He's someone who can get to the quarterback in bunches.
There will be Super Bowl contenders who look at that skill as an absolute need. If the Jets can get an early Day Three pick (a fourth rounder) it may be enough to entice the team to restart the rebuild of their defensive line.
Wright has barely seen the field this year due to losing the cornerback position battle against AZ Thomas in training camp. The fact Wright is coming off a year where he led all cornerbacks in interceptions, and the Jets only have one recorded this season, is irrelevant to the coaching staff.
Wright isn't a fit for what the Jets want to do defensively at corner. Because of that, it makes more sense than anything to simply move on from Wright at this point for a late-round pick swap. Either that, or he'll be released for a chance to play with a contender.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has been clear: the team wants to keep Hall on the roster. Since he's missed the last five games, it's hard to envision a team giving New York a trade deal they are willing to listen to.
Remember, though, the team didn't have a dream in mind of moving on from Sauce Gardner from last season. Indianapolis simply gave them an offer they couldn't refuse.
Will another team do the same for Hall? Is a third-round pick something the team can't refuse? Most likely not. It seems Hall is here to stay at this point.

title: Garrett Wilson Injury Will Test if New Jets' Optimism is Deserved
full_text:
Garrett Wilson is the best player on the New York Jets. That has been the case over the last several years now.
Whenever the former Ohio State star is off the field, New York is worse for it. So when head coach Aaron Glenn announced Wilson entered concussion protocol before practice on Wednesday, most fans wouldn't be wrong to feel even worse going into Sunday's contest against the Kansas City Chiefs. New York is already 2-6 and needs everyone on deck to be able to thwart the playoff contender.
But what if I told you the Jets, for the first time since Wilson was brought to the team in 2022, aren't going to miss Wilson as much as before? What if the offense won't miss a beat?
And it has everything to do with the system and personnel at their disposal.
Sometimes, an injury to a WR1 doesn't have the kind of debilitating effect on an offense that you might expect. Part of that reason is due to the depth around the top receiver. If Wilson does not pass concussion protocol in time for Sunday's game, the Jets will be perfectly fine.
And it's due to the depth on the roster.
At receiver, Adonai Mitchell and rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. have shown their own breakout capabilities over the last few weeks. In Week 6 and 7, Cooper was the first rookie receiver with back-to-back 100-yard games since Al Toon in 1985. Just last week, Mitchell recorded a seven-catch, 142-yard game as the most productive player in the offense. Without Wilson, players like Cooper will be in the spotlight, and he appears ready for it.
“What he did is showcase who he is," Geno Smith said after Week 6 of Cooper.  "He’s a playmaker. He finds ways to make catches, the tough catches … he makes them look easy.”
And what about Smith himself? Many times a top receiver leaves a game, the quarterback normally struggles immediately after. Only true veterans with years of experience are able to keep an offense afloat. Smith is among the latter quarterbacks mentioned.
So far this season, he has recorded 1,913 yards passing with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions. He has been everything the team has hoped for at the position and more. It's another reason why the team should be perfectly fine without Wilson.
"He's really commanding that offense the way you want a quarterback to do that, so the drop back game he's doing a hell of a job," Glenn said of Smith.
Remember, we haven't even brought up the fact that Braelon Allen is on a historic five-game pace, and Breece Hall could be in line to return to the team after missing the last five contests. New York having a successful rushing attack changes the desperate need for a top receiver, especially with quality other wideouts on the roster.
Losing Wilson is never easy for the Jets offense. But unlike prior years, the team is better prepared for his absence. They might even remain a unit that's able to put up plenty of points without him.

title: 3 Logical Breece Hall Trade Destinations to Give Jets the Best Return
full_text:
Breece Hall's last snap for the Jets was on Sept. 27, and Gang Green has gone 1-4 since the injury. However, that has not been because of the running back room. Braelon Allen has taken over the backfield, leaving New York with an interesting conundrum.
In the five games Hall has missed, Allen has 504 rushing yards and is averaging 5.4 yards per carry. This has put Hall's future with the Jets in question.
Hall is no stranger to trade rumors. The running back was one of the names in rumor mills when the Jets were selling in 2025. Hall ultimately stayed with the Jets and signed a three-year, $45.75 million contract with New York. The former Iowa State Cyclone looks to be on the trading block again as the Jets look like sellers before the deadline.
So if Hall is on his way out, what teams would be willing to give New York the best return for the fifth-year veteran?
The Broncos' run game has been less than stellar in 2026. Denver has averaged just 92.6 rushing yards per game this season. Denver is in the conversation for teams looking for running back help at the trade deadline.
Denver holds nine draft picks for the 2027 draft. The Broncos have two fourth-round picks, which opens the door for negotiations. Breece Hall won't fetch as high a return as Jonathan Taylor, but the Jets can still get value from trading the running back.
The Jets could snag the Broncos' third-round pick as Denver has two in the fourth. If New York gets a third for Hall, that would give them six picks in the first three rounds. Denver needs help in the run game, and it may be a perfect trade for both teams.
The Packers are another team that could be a good trade partner for Hall.
Green Bay's rushing attack has been abysmal, ranking dead last in the NFL. Josh Jacobs has returned from his stint on the Commissioner's List to a paltry 2.3 yards per carry and may miss more games due to his ongoing investigations .
The Packers are 5-3 despite a poor rushing attack, so Green Bay may be willing to trade for a talent like Hall. The Packers don't have a first-round pick in 2027, but they hold two fourth-round picks. The Jets could benefit more from the Packers' draft capital if they trade Hall.
New York should look for the third-round pick from the Packers if Green Bay wants Hall. That doesn't mean the Jets can't snag a second-round pick for the running back. The Packers are desperate to contend, and an answer to their running-game woes might be worth a late second if Green Bay is to have two picks in the third.
The Bengals have had one of the league's worst rushing attacks throughout Joe Burrow's career. They have trusted Chase Brown, but the fourth-year RB has managed only 340 rushing yards in seven games in 2027. Hall could be the perfect replacement for a Bengals team that has struggled to establish the run.
Hall makes an impact in both the rushing and passing game. That is exactly what Cincinnati needs. They are almost too dedicated to the pass, having had a bottom-five rushing offense over the past five years. Hall's ability to shine in both aspects of the offense may matter more to a team like Cincy than some think .
Hall is in the first year of a three-year contract, so this is more than a rental. Hall could slot into the Bengals' offense and take over the backfield immediately. With the Ohio team holding all its 2027 draft picks, including an extra third-rounder, New York could push for the Bengals' second-round pick.
The Jets set a precedent that Hall will not go for less than a third-round pick during last year's trade deadline. With these teams, the Jets will have a chance to get that caliber of return and maybe more. If they want to move on from Hall, they should want, at least, Day 2 picks in return.

title: Jets Desperately Need Omar Cooper Jr. to Bounce Back Even More Amid Garrett Wilson Concussion Concerns
full_text:
Coming off a 38-33 loss to the Raiders last Sunday and falling to 2-6 on the season, the Jets are in deep trouble with a challenging road trip to Arrowhead Stadium to face the Chiefs in Week 9.
While Braelon Allen has been sensational on the ground and the offensive line continues to show some positive signs, it was a disaster for the special teams unit, the defense and a coaching staff that cannot seem to make the appropriate adjustments from week to week and over the course of a game.
For the last two weeks, though, the Jets have slowly started to get a little healthier, especially in the wide receiver room as rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (high ankle sprain) and Adonai Mitchell (finger) made their return from their respective injuries.
While that has given the Jets their top-three wideouts the last two weeks, that may not be the case on Sunday after ESPN 's Rich Cimini confirmed on Wednesday that WR1 Garrett Wilson "is in concussion protocol," per head coach Aaron Glenn.
WR Garrett Wilson is in concussion protocol, per Aaron Glenn. #Jets
That means he would have to pass the NFL's five-stage concussion protocol and could be unable to play on Sunday. If that is the case, that could present the opportunity Cooper needs to respond after receiving zero targets in the Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
Sure, Mitchell led the team with seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown, while Wilson was targeted a team-high 12 times against Las Vegas. That said, Cooper had back-to-back 100-yard receiving games prior to that dud last Sunday and could benefit the most if Wilson is unable to play as the Jets take a three-game losing streak into Kansas City .
Wilson may not have been on the injury report earlier this week , but the fact that his status is in doubt speaks to the potential opportunity that could exist for Cooper, who has already demonstrated first-round talent and shown why he is one of the top targets on this team.
If Wilson is not on the field or is limited in some capacity, the Jets need Cooper to take on a larger target share alongside Mitchell and create some consistent separation. It is no secret that the Jets will not be given much of a chance against the Chiefs, so it is crucial for Cooper to take advantage of slants and quick-hitting routes to rack up yards after the catch.
It might be easy to overreact to Cooper's lack of impact and usage in the Week 8 loss to the Raiders, but let's not forget how frustrated Wilson has been with his limited targets and the additional attention that Mitchell receives in the passing attack when he is healthy. It was also just one game and likely a small blip on the radar for Cooper if the two weeks beforehand were any indication.
With the attention mostly focused on Mitchell and tight end Mason Taylor, who broke out for two receiving TDs in Week 7, Cooper could be instrumental in keeping the chains moving and preventing the offense from stalling out, which has become an issue at times throughout the season.
Considering seven of Cooper's 12 catches this season have been over the middle of the field, everything could be lining up for him to bounce back in Week 9. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , the Chiefs gave up six completions on eight middle-of-the-field attempts against the Broncos in Week 8, so this could be a favorable opportunity for him against a formidable opponent.
Regardless of how Cooper performs on Sunday, though, his disappearing act against the Raiders should not be too concerning for the Jets . That said, even though his workload should see an increase, there is still a boom-or-bust nature when you consider the inconsistency from this coaching staff and the targets that were coming Mitchell's way last week.
If Cooper can break free and create an explosive play or two, it may not matter how many times quarterback Geno Smith looks his way. With that in mind, expect Cooper to have an expanded volume and usage as the uncertainty surrounding Wilson potentially leads to more opportunities for the rookie.

title: 3 Jets Face More Pressure After Garrett Wilson Concussion News Creates New Obstacle in Week 9
full_text:
The Jets will look to avoid a season-worst fourth consecutive loss when they visit the Chiefs for some Sunday afternoon action in Week 9 . Beating Patrick Mahomes & Co. was never going to be easy, especially with how inconsistent Gang Green's performances have been this season, but a potential upset in Kansas City will be even tougher to pull off if the Jets are without star wide receiver Garrett Wilson.
On Wednesday afternoon, New York head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that Wilson has been placed in concussion protocol and will be "day-to-day."
WR Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol Full injury update from Coach Glenn ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/la6Lq13a1G
Given that Wilson must clear the NFL's five-step protocol to get back into the lineup, there's a good chance that the Jets won't have him when they take on the Chiefs this weekend. As such, New York needs this trio to step up if it hopes to keep Sunday's clash competitive.
Alongside rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Mitchell is another Jets playmaker who needs to take things to another level if Wilson misses time. Fortunately, he proved he could do exactly that last week.
Even though his team didn't win, last week's loss to the Raiders was a career day for Mitchell, who converted nine targets into seven catches, 142 receiving yards and a touchdown. Considering how he had a 9-123-0 stat line in three games before that (mostly due to a nagging finger injury), it's safe to say that the former Georgia/Texas product is more than capable of being the Jets' lead pass-catcher.
An incredible 48-yard catch by Adonai Mitchell! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/a7pOlkJn27
The Chiefs have a fairly middle-of-the-road pass defense this season, ranking 18th in passing yards allowed per game (222.9) and T-16th when it comes to yards per completion (10.2). With a career-high average depth of target of 18.2 yards this season , per Pro Football Focus , Mitchell has what it takes to take advantage of any potential miscues in Kansas City's secondary.
The Jets' passing attack hasn't been consistent this season, but another huge performance from Mitchell (sans Wilson) would boost optimism about the unit's outlook.
It's safe to say that Kenyon Sadiq's big seven-catch, 105-yard performance in Week 3 is nothing but a distant memory at this point. The rookie tight end has been nearly invisible since then, catching just five balls on 13 targets (38.5%) for 43 receiving yards without a touchdown in the last five games. Even though it's only his rookie season, that's pretty disappointing for someone drafted 16th overall in April .
All slumps eventually end, though, especially when a player is as talented as Sadiq. Despite the Jets being underdogs this weekend ( by 10 points, per DraftKings Sportsbook ), a clash with the Chiefs might be exactly what the doctor ordered.
As previously mentioned, Kansas City's pass defense hasn't been great, and that's even truer when it comes to stopping tight ends. Heading into Week 9, when it comes to TEs, the Chiefs have allowed:
In other words, it's a great opportunity for Sadiq (and Mason Taylor) to step up if Wilson is stuck in concussion protocol.
With Wilson's immediate outlook uncertain, a potential Breece Hall return in Week 9 would be huge for the Jets. The stud running back hasn't played since Week 3 due to a quad injury, but head coach Aaron Glenn revealed on Wednesday that Hall's situation is "trending in the right direction," per ESPN 's Rich Cimini.
Breece Hall is "trending in the right direction," Glenn says. https://t.co/O4Rn1Q6iOy
Hall's job is to run the ball, but that doesn't take away from the fact that his presence is a key part of the Jets' passing game. The Iowa State product has amassed 198 catches for 1,744 receiving yards (8.8 yards per reception) and nine touchdowns in 59 career games, which includes catching all 10 of his targets for 102 yards this season.
For comparison, New York's other two running backs—Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis—have combined for just 149 yards on 22 receptions this season. That's just 6.8 yards per reception compared to Hall's 10.2.
Besides, having Hall available in pass-catching situations would allow the Jets to keep Allen on the field, looking to keep taking advantage of his ongoing breakout .
Assuming he can finally play for the first time since September, Hall's looming return certainly looks a lot more important for the Jets.

title: Landon Dickerson, Moro Ojomo Among Eagles Speaking Up About Trade Deadline Rumors
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Breaking news: The Eagles are trading the last two remaining players on their offensive line from the Super Bowl days of just two years ago, their alleged generational defensive tackle, and their best pass rusher, who still has a year left on his rookie contract at a relative discount.
It’s beyond silly. Sure, trade Jordan Mailata and Landon Dickerson. That opens two positions of major need in the draft. Go ahead and deal Jalen Carter; save some money, but then you need another defensive tackle. Nolan Smith? He’s a bargain next year at $13.7 million.
Landon Dickerson called it propaganda when asked where his head is, with the NFL trade deadline creeping closer. It's Tuesday at 4 p.m.
“It's really not up to me,” said the Eagles’ left guard. “I've said it a lot of times; I love this team. I love this city. This is my home right now. Really, all I care about is winning a championship.”
That’s not to say Eagles general manager Howie Roseman won’t be wheeling and dealing, and if the value is great, maybe he does part ways with one—and only one—of the aforementioned players. Nobody saw him dealing Cam Jurgens in early October, but a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-rounder next year was one of those Godfather deals—an offer he couldn’t refuse.
So, Jurgens is gone. To deal Mailata and Dickerson would be a clear white flag of surrender on 2026. Maybe 2027, too, depending on how and where they would find a new left tackle, a new left guard (okay, Willie Lampkin is okay, but is he really starter material?), and possibly a new right guard if Tyler Steen moves on in free agency.
Roseman doesn’t do surrender.
Maybe it will be Steen who goes. He is in the final year of his contract. That is the sweet spot, which puts players like Dallas Goedert, Riq Woolen, and Moro Ojomo in the crosshairs of a potential trade.
“I'm here right now, trying to go through practice, go through meetings, and prepare for this game,” said Goedert, referencing Sunday’s Week 9 home game against the New York Giants.
Then there’s Ojomo, who could possibly deliver the greatest return.
“Howie and [owner Jeffrey] Lurie mean so much to me for giving me this opportunity to play for this team,” said the seventh-round defensive tackle. “I think I was the 23rd DT picked up, so if we can make [a new contract] work,  I love playing for the city. I love working hard for the city. I wanna produce results for the city. I hate letting them down.”
It’s an unusual situation the Eagles are in—being potential sellers at the trade deadline, after making the playoffs in eight of the last nine seasons. But at 2-6, it doesn’t make sense to stand pat. Not since 2021, when Roseman dealt Zach Ertz, who was still in his prime, has he traded away a talent like Ertz.
The rumors of who could be going can be distracting for a player whose name is being bandied about in trade rumors. Nick Sirianni addressed it earlier in the week when asked if he talks to the team about them or the individuals involved.
“You're always in constant communication with your guys,” he said. “I think we have a good beat on what guys are going through, any situation that they're going through, what guys need to be talked to. Of course, you talk to all the guys about that. I'm not saying that necessarily is in front of the room, but maybe more one-on-one situations there.”
Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio was asked how he approaches the trade deadline with his players, and whether he talks to them about the rumors.
“No,” he said. “I mean, I would if I thought there was a rumor out there gaining steam that had no truth to it, but I don't see that at this point in time.”

title: Sean Mannion's Complicated Offense Is Becoming Another Eagles Concern
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ offense is too complicated for the current personnel, and the fourth-and-four sequence at Washington in Week 8 provided all the proof needed.
Trailing 16-10 with just over nine minutes left, the Eagles had driven into the red zone and faced a make-or-break situation from the Commanders’ 13-yard line.
Aggression was the correct decision by head coach Nick Sirianni . Everything unraveled, however. Rookie right tackle Markel Bell jumped offsides, and Jake Elliott’s subsequent field goal was wiped out by an illegal formation penalty on Jordan Mailata. Elliott then missed the longer kick.
From that point, the Commanders finished strongly and won going away, 27-10.
The cascade of self-inflicted damage turned a legitimate chance to cut into the deficit—or even take the lead—into another empty trip for the league’s worst offense.
It was a microcosm of the season for a unit that ranks among the worst in franchise history through eight games: dead last or near the bottom in yards, points, efficiency, and nearly every meaningful metric.
This week, embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was asked by Eagles on SI about the failed fourth-down attempt and the visibly late snap. His answer was revealing:
“I think any quarterback’s going to want to gather some degree of information at the line of scrimmage,” the first-year play-caller said. “Sometimes it’s because you may have a kill on the play; sometimes it’s not.”
The Eagles rarely discuss scheme specifics, but Mannion revealed just how many moving parts exist in his Shanahan/McVay-inspired offense .
“I’m not going to get into specifics of that call necessarily, but with anything, I try to get all these calls in as quickly as possible,” he said. “Some of them have motions; some of them demand a little bit more diagnosis at the line of scrimmage than others. So sometimes when you see the clock winding down, it can be a multitude of factors there.
“But we want to give [quarterback] Tanner [McKee] the opportunity to use his cadence, to use a motion to undress things that he may or may not need to see. Sometimes it might be a call-it-run-it play, but he just wants a little bit extra intel in terms of how to execute it.
“Obviously, that was unfortunate with us jumping offsides there. It was a critical moment in the game. We work that mechanic where, hey, if we’re up against the clock and we are on a silent count—so it’s something we work on—we just didn’t execute it at the level that we need to.”
Read that again. Motions. Diagnosis. Cadence. Silent counts. Kills. Extra intel.
Those are multiple variables that must be processed, communicated, and executed under pressure by a backup quarterback in his fifth career start, working without his top two receivers and with a patchwork offensive line featuring a rookie right tackle.
That is not a criticism of the desire for information. Every good quarterback wants it. The problem is that the system appears to require too much of it, too often, from a group that is not executing at a high level and that has been rebuilt on the fly around injuries and departures.
When the play clock is winding down on fourth down in a one-score game, the margin for “a multitude of factors” does not exist.
Bell’s jump is the visible failure; the late or overloaded processing that contributed to it is the structural one.
The Eagles installed the more complex, Shanahan/McVay-influenced offense built around under-center looks, wide zone, layered play-action, and pre-snap movement.
It was supposed to create an identity and force defenses to adjust. Instead, the under-center concepts have largely been inefficient; the run game has little push; protection has been porous, and the offense has somehow looked both predictable and overcomplicated at the same time.
Different quarterbacks have produced the same problems.
That said, Mannion is right that execution failed on that snap. However, he is also describing a system in which execution has become harder than it needs to be, especially for an inexperienced quarterback.
The Eagles are 2-6. The offense is historically bad. Sirianni has said he is not changing the play-caller. Fine.
Then the play-caller and the staff need to strip the offense down to what this personnel can actually execute cleanly and repeatedly—especially on the snaps that matter most.
McVay once described his scheme as “the illusion of complexity.” Right now, the Eagles’ version is a liability because it is too complex for the group currently on the field.
Perhaps Sirianni’s about-face and decision to start Joe Milton—who arrived only on Oct. 16—at quarterback for Sunday’s game against the NFC East-leading Giants is an effort to push his offensive coordinator to scale back his ambitions and better fit the players he has.

title: Joe Milton Is Already Winning Eagles Over Amid Surprise Quarterback Change
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — In the back of the Eagles locker room on Wednesday, offensive linemen Jordan Mailata and Landon Dickerson were selling their coach’s competitive advantage talking point, telling reporters that Joe Milton and Tanner McKee were splitting reps at practice.
In another area of the locker room, Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, and Darius Cooper were addressing what was reported by the national media : McKee will take a seat on Sunday against the Giants, and Milton will make the first start of his career in Week 9 .
Perhaps the two QBs are splitting reps, but when you are trying to give a crash course to a player like Milton, who was signed on Oct. 16, you would think he needs every first-team rep he can get to be ready to go.
“Definitely excited for his opportunity,” Cooper said, who was then asked about how McKee took the news that he was headed to the bench after going winless in three starts.
“I feel like Tanner actually handled it pretty well. Offense has been … we've been trying to get there. Tanner, I feel like he came in and did his best at the end of the day.”
Neither quarterback was made available to give their side of the story on Wednesday, but they are expected to talk after Thursday’s practice. Players in charge of catching the ball, like Cooper, Goedert and Eli Stowers, each talked about the zip Milton has on the ball.
“He can spin it, that's for sure,” Stowers said. “You feel it when he throws it to you. I mean, it hits your hands pretty quick. And then he can, when he lets it go downfield, it's pretty good.”
Added Goedert: “It's kind of perfect for a pass catcher. The balls that are in the air for a long time, when you can think, those ones are the scary ones. The ones that get on you, you just have to catch them. Those are the easy ones. He slings that thing. He throws it hard, but it’s really a catchable ball.”
Milton only arrived from the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16. He wasted little time trying to get to know his new teammates. Shortly after he arrived, he went up to Stowers and said, ‘What’s up 8-7?’ Stowers had his head down and looked up, startled. His expression said, ‘Who are you?’
Asked about that, Stowers laughed.
“No, no, he's a great guy,’ the rookie tight end said. “Since he's got here, he's made it a priority to talk to everybody, get to know everybody, so I appreciate that. He's been kind of a light in the locker room. … He's done a really good job of being relatable to everybody.”
