title: 3 Pending Eagles Free Agents Who Should Be Used as Trade Deadline Bait
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is now less than a week away, which means there could be some major moves coming for the Eagles in the very near future. The Eagles could look to recoup some value for several players prior to the deadline, especially players without a long-term future in Philadelphia.
Here's a look at three pending free agents who the Eagles should use as trade deadline bait.
A plethora of teams in the contender conversation could use some added depth at the linebacker position. Meanwhile, the Eagles aren't in the contender conversation, but they're deep enough at linebacker to get by if one is traded away.
So, the Eagles should do what they can to move on from veteran A.J. Epenesa. Not necessarily because he can't play, but because he doesn't appear to have a future with the franchise.
It seems unlikely that the Birds would bring him back in free agency over the offseason, so they should try to recoup some value while they can. Granted, they probably wouldn't get much more than a late-round pick in a potential deal, but something is better than nothing.
The Browns were interested in Epenesa over the offseason, and even signed him initially before opting out of the deal following concerns about his physical. Perhaps they'll revisit that interest now that he has shown that he's healthy enough to play. On the season, Epenesa has appeared in six games and tallied seven combined tackles and one pass defended.
This one is obvious. Brown has no future in Philly beyond the current campaign , but there are plenty of teams out there who would be interested in adding an extra weapon for a potential playoff push.
Just last season, Brown caught 49 passes for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Kansas City Chiefs. Perhaps a reunion with the Chiefs is in the cards? Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes certainly wouldn't be upset about the addition of another viable option to throw to.
If not the Chiefs, other contenders, including the Rams, Bills and 49ers, could possibly be interested in a veteran receiver like Brown. Given his lack of action with the Eagles (4 total receptions), Brown would likely welcome a change of scenery.
As a young defensive lineman with plenty of promise, there is ample interest around the NFL in Moro Ojomo, including from the Jaguars , according to a report from ESPN . As opposed to the first two players listed above, Ojomo would likely fetch a nice return for the Eagles in a potential trade if they use him as bait prior to the deadline , which they should.
The Eagles already have a ton of money tied up in the defensive line moving forward thanks to the massive contracts of Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, so there's a real chance that they won't be able to pay Ojomo market value over the offseason. It's also fair to wonder whether they'd want to pay him a ton, as opposed to allocating that money to a different position.
If the Eagles were contending this season, there would be a real argument for holding onto Ojomo, even without the uncertainty about his long-term future with the franchise. But since that isn't the case, they should try to recoup as much value as possible.

title: 3 Realistic Nolan Smith Trade Destinations for Eagles to Consider Before Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than a week away (Nov. 10). The Eagles are in the midst of a disastrous six-game losing streak and are expected to be at least mild sellers . Dealing expiring contracts is an easy choice for general manager Howie Roseman to make, but there are options beyond that as well .
Keep an eye on Nolan Smith. High-motor edge rushers are routine targets for teams in need of a boost. The fourth-year pro has tallied 15 tackles, four sacks, and one pass breakup through seven games. Smith racked up 10.5 sacks and two forced fumbles during his first three NFL seasons.
Roseman has a chance to be aggressive, considering Smith isn't just a rental for contenders. The Eagles picked up his fifth-year option last offseason. That means any team that acquires Smith would have him under contract for 2027, with a projected affordable cap hit of $2.8 million , per Spotrac .
Here's a look at three Smith trade destinations for the Eagles to consider before the trade deadline.
Quarterback Josh Allen steals the show in Buffalo, but defense wins championships. The Bills would benefit from improving their defensive line. They rank 26th in pass rush win rate and 19th in run-stop win rate, according to ESPN Analytics . That won't be good enough once the playoffs roll around.
Smith has shown he has the speed to get around the edge and crush quarterbacks. The Georgia product has also proven consistent in run defense, regularly shedding blocks to squeeze running lanes. Lining him up alongside game-breakers like Greg Rousseau and Ed Oliver would be scary.
Nolan Smith with the takedown! pic.twitter.com/hn8bPC0xAc
Bills general manager Brandon Beane has been fearless in trades before, knowing that Buffalo's championship window is wide open. He most recently dealt a second-round pick to acquire wide receiver DJ Moore in March. Making a similar offer for Smith could be enough to seal the deal.
It is no secret that the Jaguars are searching for defensive line help . That was the case even before nose tackle DaVon Hamilton suffered a season-ending quad injury in Week 8. Jacksonville could go the route of adding to the interior of its line, or shifting Travon Walker inside and adding to the edge.
Smith sticks out as a target in that second scenario. After all, he has recorded more sacks than any Jags player (four) and would be tied for the team lead in tackles for loss (five). Smith's 18 total pressures would trail only Walker (23) and Josh Hines-Allen (21). The production speaks for itself.
Acquiring Smith would improve the Jaguars' chances of securing an AFC South title, both in 2026 and 2027. It'd be a move that shows they are all in for a Lombardi Trophy. Jacksonville owns its pick in the first three rounds of the next three NFL drafts, so it can deal a Day 2 pick with little concern.
Smith's extra year of control expands his destinations beyond contenders. The Colts have already started selling , trading away offensive lineman Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. The added draft picks could put them in the market for a young pass rusher like Smith.
Indianapolis has posted the league's third-lowest pressure rate (18.5%) and ranks dead last in pass rush win rate (per ESPN Analytics ). Opposing quarterbacks have had all the time in the world to find the open man. As a result, the Colts are surrendering the second-highest yards per completion (12.0).
Not only would Smith serve as an instant upgrade on Indy's defensive line, but he would fit into a potential rebuild. There's still room for him to grow at 25 years old. The Colts are projected to have a combined 18 picks in the 2027 & 2028 NFL Drafts. Roseman could work his magic to maximize his return.

title: Eagles’ 48-Hour Flip From ‘Tanner’s Our Guy’ to Joe Milton Exposes a Bigger Problem
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — The Eagles spent Monday insisting stability mattered. By Wednesday afternoon, stability was out and a “spark” was in.
Forty-eight hours after Nick Sirianni declared , “Tanner’s our guy. We’re not making any changes there,” the organization reversed course and is ready to make Joe Milton the starting quarterback against the NFC East-leading Giants on Sunday.
The decision was first reported by NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Mike Garafolo, and tight end Dallas Goedert said it was announced at a team meeting Wednesday.
Other players who told reporters Tanner McKee and Milton split reps and had no idea who would play were likely protecting the Sirianni party line of competitive advantage.
Either way, the messaging was a disaster.
Milton has been in the building for less than three weeks. Signed off the Cowboys’ practice squad on October 16 after Jalen Hurts’ season-ending blood-clot issues were materializing, he quickly jumped developmental prospect Cole Payton for the backup job.
Now he has leapfrogged the man Sirianni publicly locked in as the starter. An NFL source framed the move as an attempt to inject energy into an offense that has produced almost none during a six-game losing streak. McKee had dropped three straight starts.
Something, anything, had to change.
That “something” is a quarterback who has barely practiced with the offense, has no established rapport with the skill players, and arrives with a resume built on arm talent and limited NFL snaps rather than sustained success.
The Eagles are not installing a new system; they are hoping Milton’s physical tools create explosives that McKee can not.
Sirianni’s Monday comments make the pivot look worse. He spoke about finding solutions through scheme, practice structure, and coaching adjustments while explicitly ruling out the change.
Two days later the change is the solution. Either the staff reached a sudden about-face, concluding that Milton gives them the best chance to win, or the public stance was never as firm as it was presented.
In a season already defined by injury chaos and offensive stagnation, the distinction matters less than the optics: a franchise that has looked reactive all year just became more so.
Teams hide injuries and rotate personnel in practice all the time. They do not usually have the head coach plant a flag on one quarterback and then pull it up two days later without a clear external explanation.
The Giants, already leading the division, will prepare for Milton’s skill set regardless. The real cost is internal: another message that the plan has no real conviction behind it and can change on a whim.
None of this guarantees Milton will fail. He is a big, athletic passer with the arm to stress defenses vertically. More importantly, this offense needs a mobility aspect behind a shaky offensive line  to succeed, something McKee doesn’t possess.
The process to get to Milton reveals the larger problem, however.
Elevating a recently acquired practice-squad quarterback over the player the coach had just endorsed is an admission that the previous plan has already run out of road.
Sunday will tell whether the Milton spark is real or just the latest dart throw. Right now, the Eagles’ clearest statement is that they no longer believe McKee is the answer.
Everything else is still being written.

title: Nick Sirianni's Job Is Seemingly Safe Despite Eagles' Ongoing Six-Game Slide
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. – For six years, Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has had head coach Nick Sirianni’s back. That hasn’t changed, even as the coach endures some of the toughest times of his coaching career, trying everything he can to end a six-game losing streak .
“I've always felt I have nothing but complete support from Mr. Lurie, in everything, through good times, through bad times,” Sirianni said before the Eagles hit the practice field on Wednesday. “That's huge, right? That's huge to be able to know that the owner has your back in all these situations.”
Sirianni is on the hot seat. Depending on where you get your betting odds, he is listed as the first head coach to get fired. It won’t happen—if it happens at all—until the end of the season. It’s not usually Lurie’s style to do that, though he cut bait with Chip Kelly before the final game of the 2015 season. That had become an intolerable situation, however.
Sirianni’s situation isn’t Kelly’s, even as the Eagles muddle along on a six-game losing streak to fall to 2-4 and get ready for a visit from the New York Giants on Sunday.
Remember when the Eagles suffered an embarrassing 32-9 loss in the wild-card round of the 2023 playoffs? Sirianni had his team 10-1 that year, and it looked like the Eagles would land back in the Super Bowl, a season after losing to the Chiefs in the final seconds.
There were issues, though, and Philly lost five of their last six to land second in the NFC East. Then came that playoff laydown in Tampa.
Sirianni’s seat was red-hot. Lurie didn’t think so, or at least he took some time to decompress from the disappointment of not making it back to the playoffs to try to make another run to the Super Bowl. The owner went yacht shopping at the conclusion of the season and decided to bring back his coach.
It was a good decision. Sirianni returned the following year and helped deliver the Eagles another Super Bowl title.
“We've been through high highs, we've been low,” the Eagles' coach said, “and I've felt nothing but support, and my communication remains the same with him as it has, whether we're on a winning streak or whether we're on a losing streak.
“I love that. I love that steadiness, and I'm trying to give that same thing to the guys—the consistency, the steadiness—because I know I'm receiving it from the very top.”
Perhaps that steadiness is revealing itself in ways unseen outside the team’s Jefferson Health Training Complex.
“I think the guys have been steady in how they come into work ready to go,” Sirianni said. “Obviously losing six in a row sucks, right? There's no doubt about it. But what I believe is, every time they come in here, they're ready to work, they're ready to get better, and it shows you the guys that we have in this building, that they're coming back every single day hungry to do everything we can do to turn it around.”

title: Kracz: Eagles' Transparency Is Wearing Thin After Naming Joe Milton QB1 in Week 9
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles started the season with four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Joe Milton wasn’t one of them, but he will make his first career start when the Giants visit on Sunday .
The about-face is in direct contrast to what head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters just 48 hours earlier: “Tanner's our guy. We're not making any changes there.”
Milton has been with the Eagles for 18 days since they signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad. The four QBs who began Week 1 were Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Andy Dalton and Cole Payton.
Dalton was released after throwing one pass—an end zone interception against the Bears in Week 3 loss—and reportedly turned an Eagles overture to return when the team tried to bring him back after Hurts got hurt .
McKee started three games after Hurts went on injured reserve with blood clots. He went 0-3, completing 63.2% of his passes with two touchdowns, two interceptions, and a lost fumble. McKee was sacked 10 times in those three games.
In the only extended action of his career , in Week 18 of 2024, when he played for the New England Patriots against the Buffalo Bills, the 6'5", 235-lb Milton completed 22 of 29 passes for 241 passing yards with two touchdowns—one by rushing, one by passing—with no interceptions and a 111.4 passer rating.
Milton will offer more mobility than McKee, but, oddly, the Eagles are pinning their hopes on someone who has been in town for less than three weeks.
Sirianni was asked about Milton on Wednesday afternoon. Given the opportunity to announce that Milton would be taking over for McKee, Sirianni didn’t.
“I think he's worked really hard,” was what the coach said. “Him and [Quarterbacks Coach] Parks [Frazier] have spent a ton of time together getting him caught up to speed. I know the developmental periods always help to be able to run our plays, but he works extremely hard. He's always in the building doing the extra things, and I like his progression.”
So, when was the decision made to remove McKee and replace him with Milton? Was it after Monday’s pronouncement that “Tanner’s our guy,” or was it in the two-hour window between Sirianni’s answer about Milton and when it was announced via a national media member that the Eagles were switching quarterbacks?
In the grand scheme of things, it probably doesn’t matter, but transparency is wearing thin with the organization.
It will now partially be up to Milton to help his really, really new team, at 2-6, end a six-game losing streak when the New York Giants visit for a Week 9 game on Sunday. He was at Wednesday’s practice taking first-team reps in individual drills. It appeared that Cole Payton was taking second-team reps, which would reduce McKee to the third-string, emergency QB on game day.

title: 2 Biggest Eagles Winners & 1 Loser After Joe Milton Being Named QB1 in Week 9
full_text:
As the late, great Owen Hart once said, "Enough is enough, and it's time for a change."
That appears to have been the Eagles' mindset on Wednesday afternoon, when NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Mike Garafolo reported that Joe Milton is officially replacing Tanner McKee as the starting quarterback ahead of Week 9's clash with the Giants.
A QB change in Philadelphia: the Eagles are naming Joe Milton their starting QB and benching Tanner McKee for Sunday’s game vs. the Giants, per @mikegarafolo and me. pic.twitter.com/kVkMqLmUb4
With Jalen Hurts's season likely over due to blood clots , McKee has started the Eagles' last three games, going 0-3 while completing 63.2% of passes for 638 yards, two touchdowns with as many interceptions and a 76.6 passer rating. His 67.1 passing grade on Pro Football Focus ranks 26th among 57 QBs who've thrown a pass this season .
Given the likelihood of being trade deadline sellers and having nothing left to lose from experimenting, Milton's promotion shouldn't be that surprising. The former Cowboys signal-caller has a huge arm and better mobility than McKee, which is the type of potential the Eagles should want to evaluate before planning what their QB room will look like in 2027 and beyond.
Not everyone will benefit from what Milton brings to the table, though. With that being said, here are two winners (and one loser) after the Eagles shook things up under center on Wednesday.
Remember Darius Cooper's terrific start to the 2026 season?
The former undrafted wideout instantly got on the same page as Hurts, connecting for seven receptions on 13 targets for 130 receiving yards and four touchdowns in the first five games. Sustainable all year? Maybe not, but it was exciting to see Cooper on pace for what would've been a 24-442-14 stat line in 17 games.
DARIUS COOPER, 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN EAGLES TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eKpCwhW8QZ
Since Hurts went down, though, it's been dead silence for Cooper. With McKee under center, the former Tarleton State playmaker has a quiet 4-45-0 stat line in the last three games, which includes a 36.4% catch rate—terrible, no matter how you slice it. A big part of that lackluster production is that McKee's arm simply isn't as reliable as Cooper— who carries a 12.4-yard average depth of target , per PFF —needs.
Having Milton around should help. A lot. To put things into perspective, McKee's ADOT when throwing is only 7.0 yards this season (down from 9.7 in 2025), whereas Milton's average was 10.1 last year.
With more downfield shots coming his way, Cooper is in a good spot to make noise this weekend.
Sometimes the biggest loser ends up being the most obvious one.
It's hard to imagine that McKee will have much of a future with Philadelphia after being benched before the 2026 campaign's halfway point. The 26-year-old QB was named the de facto starter as soon as Hurts went down, and only needed to do a serviceable job to show general manager Howie Roseman & Co. that he deserves to be re-signed when he becomes an unrestricted free agent in March.
Well, going winless in three straight starts is a pretty effective way to evaporate any goodwill that was there. A chunk of Eagles fans thought McKee would at least get to face the Giants before head coach Nick Sirianni contemplated a change, given that the bye is in Week 10, but the team clearly didn't think there was anything to gain by going down that route.
If Milton locks a vise grip around the job, there's a good chance last week's game could've been McKee's last with Philly. The Eagles won't have a reason to go back to him if Milton keeps them looking competitive, and the fact that he's only 26 years old opens the door to a longer stay in Philadelphia—either as a backup or a potential starting option, depending on what happens with Hurts .
Not every quarterback is a loser as Milton ascends the depth chart. After all, McKee's time with the Eagles potentially ending could have a positive impact on rookie QB Cole Payton's outlook.
Drafted 178th overall out of North Dakota State in April, Payton began the 2026 season as Philadelphia's fourth QB behind Hurts, McKee and Andy Dalton. He was more of a project-type selection after only making 14 starts in 52 appearances at NDSU, meaning a lot of patience would be needed from both Payton and the fan base before he'd see any meaningful action.
But now that McKee's time is running out, Payton's future looks a bit different. Suddenly, the door could be open later in the year for him to see in-game action if the Eagles remain out of playoff contention and further embrace the lost season. It'd be a useful assessment opportunity before Roseman decides if the team should draft a quarterback .
There's also a chance Milton won't impress the Eagles in the second half, fuelling the reasons why they'd want to give Payton a look at some point. Like McKee, Milton will also hit free agency in the offseason, creating an opportunity for Payton to grab one of two potentially available QB jobs behind Hurts.
Again, a lot has to happen to get there, but it's clear that Payton's future with the Eagles could be a lot clearer now that change has hit the quarterback room.

title: McMullen: One Eagles Experiment Was a Major Mistake That Cost Their Identity
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Head coach Nick Sirianni’s latest comments about the Eagles offense should sound familiar to anyone who has watched the team spiral in 2026.
Asked by Eagles On SI whether the players have embraced Sean Mannion’s system and whether the growing pains have been harder than expected, Sirianni essentially described a coaching staff in the middle of a rescue operation: they have a preferred system, but they’re also doing things outside of it, adapting to what the players do well, and treating every week as a problem-solving exercise.
"You have a system of what you want to do and the things that you want to hang your hat on, but you also have to have the ability to adapt to what you do well and what your players do well," Sirianni said. "Again, we're doing some things within the system. We're doing some things outside the system. Again, our job is to be problem solvers and if things aren't working,  it's to figure out what gives our guys the best chance to go out there and succeed.
"That's what we're in the midst of. I don't think it's like, 'Hey, this is a scheme. This is the only thing we can do.' We're doing everything we can do to figure out what fits  us the best, and what we will execute at a high level and what our players do well. ... I think there's a lot of different things that we'll continue to try, and we'll keep fighting, and we'll keep  hammering at it."
That is not the confident description of a scheme that was carefully chosen for this roster. It is the sound of a staff that bet big on a trendy, copycat offense and is now quietly walking it back in the wake of disastrous results.
For how bad it’s been, I direct you to The Ringer ’s Sheil Kapadia:
If you look at all 27 Eagles teams that have played football this century, the 2026 offense ranks: 27th in points per game 27th in yards per game 27th in yards per play 27th in YPC 27th in 3-and-out percentage 27th in EPA per play 27th in success rate 27th in explosive play rate
The decision to install a Shanahan/McVay-influenced offense—more under-center snaps, heavy pre-snap motion, play-action layered off wide-zone runs—was framed as a necessary evolution after the 2025 stagnation under Kevin Patullo.
Teams in that offensive tree use those concepts at high rates; the Eagles ranked near the bottom in motion and under-center usage under Sirianni.
The hope was that marrying the run and pass this way would create an identity the unit lacked in 2025. Instead, the Eagles have produced one of the league’s least efficient offenses, ranking at or near the bottom in yards per game, points, and overall production through stretches of the season, with under-center looks often generating far worse results than shotgun.⁠
The copycat element is at the core of the problem. The league’s best versions of this style succeed with specific personnel traits, continuity up front, and quarterbacks comfortable working under center with defined play-action windows.
Philadelphia’s recent success was built differently: a physical, Jeff Stoutland-coached offensive line and a quarterback in Jalen Hurts who had been most effective operating from the shotgun with a relatively static pre-snap picture.
Forcing the square peg into the round hole produced the predictable early-season mess—missed assignments, protection issues, and an offense that still looks like it is searching for what it does well rather than executing what it was built to do.
Sirianni’s own words now concede the point.
If the staff is already mixing “within the system” and “outside the system” while insisting they are not locked into one scheme, the original bet looks like an unnecessary overhaul rather than a tailored solution.
The cost of that bet goes beyond the box score. Stoutland, the longtime offensive line coach and run-game coordinator who helped build two Super Bowl championship lines, left after 13 seasons.
Reports indicated he felt bypassed on run-game adjustments late in 2025 and that the impending scheme change under Mannion left little room for the approach he had refined in Philadelphia. He was offered a reduced role and declined. The relationship fractured not over a single play call but over the decision to prioritize a different philosophy without properly integrating the coach who had delivered the most consistent success in the trenches.⁠ All at the expense of the passing game, which is somehow getting even worse .
The results—sacks, negative plays, and an inability to sustain drives—have been visible even when accounting for injuries.
Sirianni has repeatedly said the staff’s job is to put players in the best position to succeed . The evidence so far suggests the opposite happened when the organization chased a successful schematic template for those who tailored to it at the expense of continuity and personnel fit.
There is still time to salvage pieces of the season, and Sirianni’s comments indicate the staff is willing to keep adjusting rather than die on the original hill.
But the adjustment itself is the indictment. If the scheme required this much midstream improvisation to fit the roster, the decision to install it as the foundation was the mistake.
The Eagles did not need to become a lesser version of the Rams or 49ers. They needed to keep maximizing what had already worked for their players.

title: Steelers' Mike McCarthy Forcing Doubters Into Believers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have surprised many in their first eight regular-season contests. The defense is a top-10 unit, led by new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham and multiple veterans playing at an elite level.
The offense is still searching for consistency, but that hasn't stopped the Steelers from jumping out to a 6-2 record.
With the week off, the Steelers get the chance to rest, recuperate and self-scout. It's much needed, but one thing must be said. Head coach Mike McCarthy is doing exactly what he set out to do in his first season with Pittsburgh, and he's forcing all of his critics to confront the possibility that they were wrong.
While the Steelers haven't cracked the code for explosive plays, they are succeeding in two key areas.
One of them is discipline. The offense has been penalized a total of 23 times so far, the ninth-fewest in the NFL. In Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns, the offense was flawless in that regard. The team was flagged five times, but none of them were against the offense.
The other area is mitigating turnovers. Most of that falls on Aaron Rodgers. Aside from multiple instances where the pass hit the receiver's hands and wound up in the defender's, Rodgers has made smart decisions with the football. He has 13 touchdowns compared to five interceptions as he leads this offense.
There have been some problems with keeping possession of the ball from snap to whistle; I grant that, but this team has not turned the ball over as much as they could have. SumerSports data shows that the Steelers' offense turned the ball over eight times in eight games. They've coughed the ball up six times, but they've only surrendered possession twice.
Maybe you believe all of that is outside McCarthy's impact, but the way he has gotten more and more out of the running backs and tight ends is one of his biggest victories as head coach.
The three players who look the most improved in this offense, Jaylen Warren , Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, have been with the organization for multiple seasons. They've always had recognizable talent and potential to be impact players, but McCarthy and his staff have unlocked something special.
Even as the wide receivers stumble, the other skill positions are flourishing. Running back Jaylen Warren has spent the entirety of his career splitting his time in the backfield, until this season.
Under the watchful eye of McCarthy, the offense has centered on Warren, and the results have been excellent. Through eight games, Warren has 704 rushing yards (sixth in the NFL), and his 5.92 yards per carry tops all running backs with at least 50 touches this season. Add in his 294 receiving yards, and he's pushing 1,000 all-purpose yards as the team recovers during the bye week.
The tight ends are also giving the Steelers valuable production. Both Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington rank among the top 25 tight ends in receiving yards. Washington is averaging 13.37 yards per reception, the 11th-best mark among tight ends.
They've also combined for seven receiving touchdowns, making them one of the most trusted targets on offense.
The Steelers are not a perfect product. They have flaws. Their lack of wide receiver depth is a concerning issue that must be addressed before the Steelers can be considered a frontrunner in the AFC.
But make no mistake, Mike McCarthy is transforming more doubters into believers by the day.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Insider Floats Steelers QB as Potential Trade Target
full_text:
Though the Pittsburgh Steelers are buyers, it's still possible that they could receive some interest in one of their backup quarterbacks ahead of the November 10 trade deadline .
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted that while the Steelers are "more likely" to add to their roster over the next few days while sitting at 6-2, Mason Rudolph is a player who could theoretically be moved if the right opportunity presented itself.
“The Steelers are more likely to bring in players at the deadline," Fowler wrote . "In fact, I don’t expect Pittsburgh to move anyone. But it has a surplus at quarterback, and should more quarterback injuries occur around the league, perhaps teams call on Rudolph with an attractive offer.”
In-season quarterback trades are typically a rarity across the NFL.
There have only been five since the start of 2020, but two of them have come during the 2026 campaign, as J.J. McCarthy was sent from the Minnesota Vikings to the New York Giants in late September, while Jacoby Brissett was just dealt to the Baltimore Ravens from the Arizona Cardinals on November 4, following what are likely season-ending injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.
Minnesota landed a 2027 fifth-round pick for McCarthy, and Arizona's return for Brissett isn't yet official.
There are a few teams out there, with the Minnesota Vikings being chief among them, who could use another quarterback before the deadline .
Rudolph presents an interesting case as a trade candidate, though, because of both his lack of true upside and recent starting experience.
For example, McCarthy was a first-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft and thus had value due to his untapped potential despite things not working out in Minnesota, while Brissett has started 20 games over the last two seasons for the Cardinals and had spurts where he's looked like a quality option behind center.
As for Rudolph, however, he's made just one start since returning to Pittsburgh in 2025 after a one-year stint with the Tennessee Titans.
The 31-year-old has played a fair amount throughout his NFL career, appearing in 37 games and making 19 starts, but his 53 passing attempts during his second go-around with the Steelers might not be all that alluring on the trade market.
If another team decides they need an upgrade  at backup quarterback or their starter goes down in Week 9, the chances of Rudolph being traded would jump.
Otherwise, it's hard to imagine him not sticking around with the black and gold for the remainder of the year before hitting free agency next offseason.
Equipped with 18 picks over the next two NFL Drafts, the Steelers aren't exactly hurting for extra assets.
At the same time, if they could acquire a mid-to-late Day 3 selection for a veteran on an expiring deal in Rudolph, perhaps it's something they'd consider.
The organization's willingness to move on from Rudolph, though, comes down to their confidence in Will Howard and/or Drew Allar to take another step and fill in as Aaron Rodgers' backup.
Sitting just a game outside of the No. 1 seed in the AFC, and in a tight division race in the AFC North as the first-place team, Pittsburgh can't really afford to slip up over the back-half of its schedule.
If Rodgers were to ever miss a game or two due to injury, Rudolph would likely present the Steelers their best odds of remaining competitive without the future Hall of Famer on the field.
Neither Howard or Allar has taken a regular season snap, though they both played a good amount during the preseason and have continued to grow while serving as the No. 3 and 4 quarterbacks, respectively, behind Rodgers and Rudolph so far this year.
Howard and Allar have higher ceilings than Rudolph and could be in the mix to serve as Pittsburgh's starting quarterback down the line, perhaps as early as 2027, but their collective readiness to play now is a question mark.
If the Steelers believe either could fill in for Rodgers if necessary and keep the offense afloat, than trading Rudolph could be on their radar. If not, holding onto Rudolph would be the right course of action.

title: Former Browns DB Calls Out Steelers' Mason McCormick
full_text:
A former Cleveland Browns defensive back took issue with Mason McCormick's hit on Jared Verse as the Pittsburgh Steelers blew out their division rivals 27-6 in Week 8 .
During a recent episode of the "Speakeasy" podcast, T.J. Ward shared his belief that McCormick proved Verse's prior claim that the Steelers are "dirty" right when the former threw the latter to the ground on an extra-point attempt.
“They proved his point right. That’s a dirty-a** play,” Ward said . “You can’t pick nobody up on field goal block and dump them on their head. You can’t do that. That’s illegal. Did he play well? No. Was his point proven? Yes. That’s a dirty-ass play, whether it was warranted or not.”
#Browns DE Jared Verse has been talking plenty of trash about the #Steelers .... Well, Steelers G Mason McCormick just did this to him.  😳😳 pic.twitter.com/OP1iknS4JP
McCormick was tagged with a 15-yard unnecessary roughness for his slam of Verse , which was tacked on during the ensuing kickoff.
After the game, Verse responded to the play by stating that he was, "very upset about it," and that, "to do something like that, I just can't have respect for that," (per ESPN's Kimberley A. Martin ).
McCormick told reporters that he had no clue that it was Verse whom he was taking down, and that he did so because players are taught to bring down the hands of jumpers.
“I really had no idea who it was,” McCormick said. “Just felt somebody jump, and we’re told to get jumpers’ hands down, and that’s really it.”
Verse then circled back to the topic this week, revealing that he talked with his Browns teammates about not defending him after the situation with McCormick while admitting that he put them in a disadvantageous position by not telling them that he'd be talking trash to the Steelers ahead of the matchup.
“I made my concerns known, I’ve made my issues known about the situation,” Verse said, per ESPN Cleveland . "I didn't put them in a position...I didn't let them know beforehand I was going to talk the way I talked to the Steelers and the Steeler Nation. I've got to be better in that aspect."
The Steelers were playing with a clear edge against the Browns, and it showed up in the results of the game.
Not that they needed extra motivation against a divisional opponent with whom they were tied for first place heading into the contest, but Verse's comments, which also included saying Cleveland was, "about to make Pittsburgh ours," definitely fanned the flames of the rivalry.
With eight sacks of Deshaun Watson while holding the Browns to 34 rushing yards on 15 carries and recovering two fumbles, the defense sent a rather strong message. On the offensive side of the ball, Pittsburgh ran for 200 yards and three touchdowns across 33 attempts while leaving a good amount of points on the field.
With their three-score victory over Cleveland, the Steelers are now in sole possession of first place in AFC North at 6-2 amidst their Week 9 bye.
Cam Heyward stated ahead of the game that Verse's comments "will be addressed" during an appearance on "The Rich Eisen Show" , and that certainly ended up being the case.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Trade Price for Josh Downs May Be Dropping
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are one of many teams circling a potential wide receiver trade. It's clear that the offense needs a bit of spark for the back half of the regular season, and general manager Omar Kham has his work cut out for him before this year's NFL Trade Deadline.
One of the names consistently linked to the Steelers is Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs. The 25-year-old is exactly the kind of speedy and productive pass-catcher who could make an impact in Pittsburgh, and with few star names available, he remains the top option on the block.
Reports around the league were that the Colts held firm on their asking price, needing a third-round pick to finalize a deal. But with just days before this year's deadline, insider Ian Rapoport shared that a slightly lower return could pry Downs out of Indianapolis.
"They'd like around a three or a four as far as pick compensation," he said on Good Morning Football. "There's several teams needing a receiver, (we) just don't know yet if they're going to meet the Colts' price."
From @GMFB : The #Colts are at a standstill with RB Jonathan Taylor and the rest of their trade candidates. pic.twitter.com/u7NkvO18rr
The Steelers' pursuit of help on offense may have gotten a lot easier. Admittedly, the third-round pick asking price is reasonable. It's an asset that the organization can afford to part with, especially for the right player in return.
But a third-round pick is also a bit too rich for the Steelers to pay when you compare it to the recent trade market for receivers. Pittsburgh sent George Pickens to the Dallas Cowboys ahead of the 2025 season in exchange for a third-round pick, so there is likely to be a sour taste if they acquired a far less productive receiver for the same price less than two years later.
A fourth-round pick, by contrast, is an easy price to pay for a contending team looking to upgrade.
There's only one problem for Pittsburgh.
The Steelers don't own a fourth-round draft pick in 2027. That pick was traded away to the Cowboys, along with offensive lineman Broderick Jones , in exchange for a 2027 third-round and sixth-round pick.
They do own a 2028 fourth-round draft pick. That is likely to be less enticing for the actively rebuilding Colts, but it's an excellent starting point.
The Steelers have to work with what they have. If the Colts were interested in making a deal, the Steelers would have to add a bit of a sweetener to finalize this trade. One idea would be to include a pick swap in 2027 in addition to that 2028 fourth-round pick.
It's not a sure thing, but what is becoming clear is the asking price for Downs is dropping. And that might benefit the Steelers ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Should Bring in Former WR After Raiders Release
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need wide receiver help at the NFL trade deadline , and while this suggestion won't fix their problem, it does offer added security with a player who has had a pretty decent season operating in a smaller role.
The Las Vegas Raiders released veteran wide receiver Cody White before Week 9, making a surprising roster move after their win over the New York Jets. White, 27, was the team's sixth-leading receiver with eight receptions for 112 yards and three touchdowns on the year.
It's not the most impressive stat line, but White was finding his groove in Las Vegas before the release. As a special teamer and reliable pass-catcher, the veteran has played 38 games throughout his NFL career, but this season, he reached career highs in all categories.
And maybe the Steelers should see if his production can continue.
Now, the Steelers need a little more than the help of White. While a reliable player, Pittsburgh is in need of a starter-level wideout who can come into their locker room and make an immediate impact, and a pretty big one.
Names like Garrett Wilson, Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. are who they should be targeting. But White is a great addition for their practice squad who they should be considering.
First off, White played for the Steelers before and was beloved during his time with the team. As a special teamer, he's physical and a player you don't need to worry about when putting him out there. Instead, he usually adds to the production of the special teams unit.
Pittsburgh knows that well as White played 16 games during his time with the team, mostly as a special teams contributor.
His dad, Sheldon White, is the senior personnel executive for the team as well, adding a family connection to a potential reunion.
The Steelers have already used their three call-ups on Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson. They signed Smith to their 53-man roster and must do the same with Johnson if they want to bring him up for game day again.
So, chances are they move on to another option on their practice squad. Marques Valdes-Scantling and Isaiah Hodgins are the two options they have.
White could probably replace either of them. And with a productive season already underway, why not take the risk on a player who's been putting up decent numbers on the field and is a known special teams player?
It makes sense for Pittsburgh to consider it. And while it's not a home run addition to their wide receiver options, it's probably better than the two they're going to turn to next.
So, if this team is ready to make a trade at the deadline for wide receiver help, why not sign someone to their practice squad as well?
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: 2 Steelers Veterans Who Could Be Traded Before Deadline - And One Who Won't
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are caught in a tough situation. The team has an impressive 6-2 record through eight games, and it's clear that they are lacking in one key area on offense.
The Steelers have to improve the wide receiver group before this year's NFL Trade Deadline. Otherwise, they run the risk of having an offense that can't compete come the postseason.
Taking care of the wide receiver problem should be priority number one for the Steelers, but that might not be the only move the organization makes. If the right team comes calling with the right price, these two Steelers are possible trade candidates
The inside linebacker group has gone from the biggest worry on defense to one of the most impressive positions recently.
As Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson keep ascending, there are two veterans in the background. Elandon Roberts remains on the practice squad, and it's possible he doesn't ever see the field this season.
Cole Holcomb, who has given the team backup inside linebacker reps and special teams snaps, may be on the trade market. There is nothing to indicate the team is trying to move him, but for the right price, why not? The Steelers have four other inside linebackers they can rely on, especially when you factor in Roberts and second-year special teamer Carson Bruener.
The intention was sound when the Steelers claimed cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers practice squad. The team needed help in the secondary with injuries mounting.
The problem is that he's barely cracked the lineup, and when he has, it's only been in a special teams role. But after he's worked his way back from a massive injury, maybe another franchise views him as a piece that could step onto the field and make an impact.
It's clear that won't happen in Pittsburgh, unfortunately.
The most notable player on the roster with trade questions ahead of the deadline is linebacker Patrick Queen. In the final year of his current contract, trade talks are a natural part of the conversation. Complicating the matter is Queen's up-and-down performance over his tenure in Pittsburgh.
The only problem with any possible trade talks involving Queen is that he's playing too well to move. In eight games, he's been a defensive force. He's recorded 60 total tackles, four passes defended, 2.5 sacks and a forced fumble. He hasn't been perfect, but he's brought stability to the middle of what's become a top NFL defense this season.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers' Perfect Trade Deadline Outcome
full_text:
At 6-2 and atop the AFC North as they enjoy their Week 9 bye, the Pittsburgh Steelers are well-positioned to make a splash at the trade deadline .
The Steelers have made a habit of getting out to strong starts over the past few seasons, which includes being 7-4 in 2023, 8-2 in 2024 and 4-1 in 2025. They finished 10-7 all three of those years, though they bowed out in the Wild Card round of the playoffs in each instance.
Something about the 2026 campaign feels different for Pittsburgh, though. Its defense is arguably a top-five unit in the league under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, while the offense is being fueled by an All-Pro-esque year from Jaylen Warren as the offensive line has really kicked into gear and has also helped protect Aaron Rodgers, who looks the best he has in several years.
This Steelers team is certainly capable of going on a bit of a run and snapping their seven-game postseason losing streak in the process. That doesn't mean they don't have any roster holes, though.
In order for Pittsburgh to achieve what could feasibly be deemed a "perfect trade deadline", here's what the organization has to accomplish over the next handful of days.
The Steelers, particularly during the prior two seasons, went into the trade deadline with an obvious need at receiver.
In 2024, they sent a 2025 fifth-round pick to the New York Jets for Mike Williams, which didn't prove to be worthwhile considering he logged just 132 yards and a touchdown over nine games.
Pittsburgh didn't address the position at all at the 2025 deadline, and that decision came back to haunt it, considering the team was relying heavily on Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Adam Thielen down the stretch as a free agent signing and waiver claim, respectively.
One could make a strong argument that the Steelers' current receiver room, assuming Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) return from the reserve/injured list in the not-too-distant future, is the franchise's best in a decent amount of time. It's still not good enough, however, if Pittsburgh wants to be taken seriously as a legitimate contender to come out of the AFC.
DK Metcalf continues to underperform, particularly with drops while struggling to separate, and Germie Bernard is an incredibly promising rookie who's shown flashes of becoming a star, but it's unfair to count on him as the top option at the position.
Having Warren and Rico Dowdle in the backfield as well as Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth at tight end does help disguise Pittsburgh's opening at receiver to a certain extent, though it's bound to become more of an issue once the playoffs roll around.
The likes of Garrett Wilson (New York Jets) and DeVonta Smith (Philadelphia Eagles) are pipe dream targets for the Steelers as clear No. 1 receiver-types who will cost a first-round pick and then some to acquire.
Because neither Wilson nor Smith is guaranteed to stick with their current teams, Pittsburgh has to lower its sights just a bit while understanding there are several other potential targets at the position who could make a real difference moving forward.
Whether it's moving a 2028 fourth-rounder or a 2027 third-rounder for Josh Downs and a mid-to-late Day 3 pick, the fourth-year Indianapolis Colts receiver is a perfect fit in the Steelers' offense as a smaller player who's at his best from the slot as a speedy separator with good route-running and is a threat with the ball in his hands.
Landing Ladd McConkey from the Los Angeles Chargers would probably take parting ways with a second-round pick if he is made available, but he's another intriguing option for Pittsburgh given that he's under control through the 2027 season (while Downs is a rental) and is also a strong route-runner with impressive quickness while having a rather high ceiling.
Brian Thomas Jr. is another name to watch, as he's been connected to the Steelers and is a theoretical high-reward target after posting 1,282 yards as a rookie in 2024, even if he's completely trailed off for the Jacksonville Jaguars ever since.
Pittsburgh's passing offense simply needs to become more explosive, and splurging for one of the top wide receivers on the trade market is almost a necessity for the organization.
As stated before, the Steelers' defense has excelled under Graham.
Allowing the sixth-fewest yards (305.6) and third-fewest points (18.0) per game while having the most sacks as a team with 26, there isn't much more you could ask for from the group as a whole.
Still, if there is a potential problem area, it's at outside cornerback.
Jamel Dean has held up well as the No. 1 cornerback amidst Joey Porter Jr.'s initial absence and eventual departure via trade to the Dallas Cowboys.
He does have some durability concerns, though, as evidenced by the fact that he missed Pittsburgh's Week 5 game vs. the Indianapolis Colts with an ankle injury and missed 12 total games from 2023 to 2025 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Asante Samuel Jr.'s been solid for the Steelers, though he's definitely had his ups and downs, and third-round rookie Daylen Everette has logged just 12 defensive snaps over the team's last two contests despite showing some real promise.
Jalen Ramsey is entrenched as the starting slot corner, meaning the likes of Brandin Echols, Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith all have minimal to nonexistent defensive roles for Pittsburgh as its backups at the position.
Considering the Steelers' coverage has been spotty at times, adding a proven No. 2 corner could do wonders for the team and help elevate the defense even further.
While there aren't quite as many eye-opening names available at the position as there are at receiver, Donte Jackson (Los Angeles Chargers), Riq Woolen (Philadelphia Eagles), Nahshon Wright (New York Jets), Alontae Taylor (Tennessee Titans) and Mike Sainristil (Washington Commanders) are all possible targets who could potentially help Pittsburgh out and raise both its floor and ceiling.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Ranking Steelers' Remaining 2026 Regular Season Opponents
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are having one of their better starts to a season in recent history, and can really build towards another AFC North Title.
The Steelers are 6-2 at the bye week and have won their past four games to take control of the AFC North.
The winning streak includes home wins over the Indianapolis Colts, 34-22 in Week 5, and 26-7 against the Cleveland Browns in Week 8, plus road victories over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 26-19 at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6, and against the New Orleans Saints, 16-10 in Paris, France in Week 7.
Pittsburgh is in a great spot with the bye week, but they'll face some good competition over their final nine games.
No surprise here for the worst team the Steelers face the rest of the way, as the Tennessee Titans are one of the worst teams in the NFL.
The Steelers face the Titans at Nissan Stadium in Week 17, so it's not a contest that happens anytime soon, and not one they will worry about anytime soon.
The Titans are 1-7, last in the AFC South Division, the second-worst record in football ahead of the 0-7 Los Angeles Chargers and have lost all four games at home.
Tennessee has put up strong performances against the Browns and the Cincinnati Bengals in the past two weeks, but lost both games late.
The Titans give up the second-most total yards (382.4) and passing yards (258.3) per game, while amassing the second-least total yards (272.5), fourth-least passing yards (173.0), fifth-least points (18.0) and 10th-least passing yards (99.5) per game.
Tennessee is a young team, led by second-year quarterback Cam Ward, who is growing and trying to figure out how to be competitive in the NFL.
Pittsburgh may face a strong challenge from Tennessee, but they should win this contest.
The Titans may have the worst record, but there's a real argument that the Philadelphia Eagles may be a worse team.
It's been an awful season for the Eagles, who have lost six straight games and are 2-6, last in the NFC East.
Philadelphia lost star quarterback Jalen Hurts to a blood clot after Week 5 and he is out for the rest of the season.
The Eagles went with Tanner McKee at quarterback, but after his struggles, they are now rolling with Joe Milton.
Philadelphia is terrible offensively, with the least total yards (265.3), third-least points (17.1), sixth-least passing yards (177.1) and rushing yards (88.1) per game.
The Eagles have also struggled defensively, with the fifth-most rushing yards (131.9), the sixth-most total yards (367.3) and the eighth-most passing yards (235.4) per game.
Pittsburgh hasn't won in Philadelphia since 1965, but their Week 11 matchup at Lincoln Financial Field might be their best chance to do it.
It'll be almost a year between the Houston Texans coming to Acrisure Stadium for the AFC Wild Card Round and their Week 13 matchup.
Houston dominated Pittsburgh last postseason 30-6, scoring 23 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, with two defensive touchdowns.
The Texans are a much different team from the one they were last season, starting the season 0-4 and are now 2-5, third in the AFC South.
Houston hasn't been anywhere near as effective defensively, where they gave up the fewest yards per game (277.2), to now allowing the 14th-most (342.0).
Four of their five defeats have come within one possession, and they've had struggles closing out games when they should've won them.
The Texans have also not been effective on the ground, with the fourth-least rushing yards per game (84.7).
Pittsburgh will get a chance to enact revenge on Houston and if they can hold them in the passing game, with quarterback C.J. Stroud having a solid year, they can earn a big victory.
The Carolina Panthers are first in the NFC North Division, which normally wouldn't be a bad thing, but they are also just 3-4 this year.
Carolina has had a wild season, with some poor losses, 59-37 to the Chicago Bears in Week 1 and 43-13 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, but some solid victories too, 34-3 over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2 and 32-26 against the Detroit Lions in Week 4.
The Panthers have a terrible run defense, giving up the third-most yards (140.7) per game, while also giving up the fifth-most points per game (27.6), which resulted in them firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero.
Carolina is much better on offense, with Bryce Young having a solid season, and he has a few weapons at his disposal.
The Panthers have the fifth-best passing attack (261.7 yards per game), but don't have as potent of a rushing attack, 11th-least rushing yards per game (102.0).
Pittsburgh hosts Carolina in Week 16, and it could be a battle of two division leaders, which would make for a great late-season matchup.
The Steelers' biggest rival in the 21st century has been the Baltimore Ravens, and that won't stop anytime soon.
Pittsburgh and Baltimore face off twice this season, Week 15 at Acrisure Stadium and Week 18 at M&T Bank Stadium, both within a month's span.
The Ravens are in a difficult spot right now, 4-4 and lost their past three games, going from AFC North favorites to likely missing the postseason.
Baltimore lost both quarterbacks, Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, to injury in their 36-10 blowout defeat to the Buffalo Bills in Week 8.
The Ravens recently traded for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, a veteran who could help get them back on track and stay competitive in the tough AFC North.
Baltimore's biggest concern is their second-half play, as they have the worst second-half point differential, -87, and they've blown games they shouldn't have this season.
The Ravens will still give the Steelers a tough time in both games, with the rivalry and postseason hopes still in the balance.
Pittsburgh is the better team, but they need to be ready for this rivalry once again.
Perhaps the biggest game for the Steelers this season is their first one back, as they face the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium in Week 10.
The Bengals have won their past three games, are 5-2, and can take the AFC North lead if they beat the Steelers at home.
Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow has his flaws, but he's still one of the best in the game.
Pair that up with star wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and they have a fantastic offense that is scoring the second-most points per game (29.4).
The Bengals lead the NFL with 288.4 passing yards per game, but don't really run the ball, with just 80.3 yards per game, the third-lowest.
Pittsburgh came away victorious in the first meeting, 30-27 at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3, but this road matchup is a massive one that they have to be extremely prepared for out of the by week.
This will be a tough matchup for both offenses, as they each have great defenses that can stop the run.
It's a Week 14 matchup between the Steelers and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Everbank Stadium, pitting the AFC North and AFC South leaders against each other.
Both teams are great against the run, with the Steelers ranking third (83.9 yards per game) and the Jaguars ranking first (77.4 yards per game).
The Jaguars allow the second-least points per game (15.9) and the Steelers the third-least (18.0).
Both offenses are best on the ground, while having moderate success in the passing game, so this should be a defensive slugfest.
Jacksonville's weakness is their pass defense, giving up the third-most yards per game (254.7).
The Steelers need to take advantage of that, getting quarterback Aaron Rodgers going and attacking early on.
Both teams should make the postseason and could even meet then, too, as they each look to hoist the Vince Lombardi trophy at its conclusion.
One team that was close to winning the Super Bowl last season was the Denver Broncos, who fell to the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game.
The Broncos are a strong team this season as well, 6-2 with five wins in their last six games, four straight wins and coming off a 28-24 comeback win over the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8 to take the AFC…

title: Steelers Should Have Defensive Player of the Year Favorite
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers served up a platter of revenge to their divisional rivals. After they lost the first regular-season meeting against the Cleveland Browns, the Steelers emerged from their Week 8 contest with a commanding victory.
The run game led the way for the Steelers, but Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson will be reliving the nightmare of being sacked eight times for years to come.
Superstar EDGE rusher T.J. Watt was the main defender inflicting said nightmare on Watson. This season continues to be a redemption tour for Watt, erasing any doubt about his place as a premier defensive player in the NFL. After posting 2.0 sacks against the Browns, Watt is now tied for the league lead with 7.5 as Week 8 closes. After a few weeks of quiet performances, Watt has reinserted himself as a top candidate for the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year Award.
After eight games, Watt is at or near the top of multiple individual statistical categories. As previously noted, he is tied with Houston Texans EDGE Will Anderson Jr. for the league lead in sacks. Both superstars have posted 7.5 sacks, giving them a slight edge over players like New Orleans Saints EDGE Chase Young and Buffalo Bills linebacker Greg Rousseau.
Fifteen players have recorded at least 5.0 sacks through Week 8 of the regular season, but what makes Watt's different is how quickly he gets to the quarterback and creates pressure. SumerSports data shows that Watt's average time to pressure is 2.46 seconds. That's the same time as Anderson Jr. and just a few milliseconds behind Minnesota Vikings linebacker Dallas Turner, who averages 2.4 seconds to pressure.
So, what does this actually mean? For pass rushers like Watt, the number to beat is 2.5 seconds. If you can get to the quarterback or ball carrier in that time, you significantly increase your chances of making a tackle for loss or better. For reference, quarterback Aaron Rodgers averages 2.57 seconds to throw the ball in 2026. Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence is taking 2.61 seconds to get the ball out so far. Put that average against Watt's time to create pressure, and that tells you Watt is excellent at imposing his will before a quarterback has the chance to make a play.
Sacks aren't the only category demonstrating Watt's dominance this season. His 10 tackles for loss are the third-most amongst NFL defenders. That statistic matters because it demonstrates how often Watt is blowing up plays in the backfield. It's not just a matter of attacking the quarterback in passing situations; he makes life hellish for any ball carrier around the line of scrimmage.
Watt is back, there's no doubt about it. He paces the NFL in sacks and is a top performer in multiple other categories. If he's not the favorite right now for
The battle for the NFL's sack leader is going to be one of the most exciting competitions of the regular season, and it also might be the determining factor when naming the 2026 DPOY. On an underachieving Texans team, Anderson Jr. has been elite every single snap. He's a destructive force, and he's one of two defenders with more tackles for loss than Watt. Anderson also has 33 total tackles, a pass defended, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery.
With his trade to the Chicago Bears, defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons could become the first interior defensive lineman since Aaron Donald to capture the award. He's been one of the most productive defenders in the NFL for the past few years, but now the spotlight is on him in the Windy City.
The 29-year-old had an outstanding debut with the Bears, carrying over a strong start he produced with the Tennessee Titans. He has 44 tackles, 5.0 sacks, 32 quarterback pressures, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery.
Buffalo Bills EDGE Greg Rousseau would like a word, as well. He has 7.0 sacks, nine tackles for loss, 24 total tackles and a whopping three forced fumbles. He's leading Buffalo's defense in multiple ways, and he's putting himself firmly in this award's conversation.
Maybe it's AFC North bias, but Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton and Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward have also warranted discussion for the award. They have each been absolutely dynamic at their positions, forcing turnovers and eliminating scoring opportunities single-handedly.
Meanwhile, other secondary players like Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake are playing out of their minds. Lake has 56 tackles, three interceptions and 11 passes defended through eight contests, making him one of the most productive playmakers in the NFL right now. Quarterbacks have completed just 67.4% of passing attempts when targeting him in coverage. He's far from a star name in Los Angeles, but he's playing like a DPOY regardless.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Jack Sawyer Shares Worrying News on Steelers' Sebastian Joseph-Day
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers EDGE rusher Jack Sawyer offered a worrying update about Sebastian Joseph-Day, who's currently on the reserve/injured list with a triceps injury.
Sawyer told Gerry Dulac on 102.5 WDVE's "Chalk Talk" that while the Steelers are "looking forward" to Derrick Harmon's eventual return from IR, there's a chance Joseph-Day misses the rest of the season.
"Obviously, we're looking forward to getting Derrick back. It sucks we're not gonna be able to get Sebastian back for- maybe at all," Sawyer said.
Head coach Mike McCarthy stated last week that he thought, "they'll all have a chance to come back," when referencing Pittsburgh's players who are on IR.
If Sawyer's comments are any indication, however, Joseph-Day's odds of a return in 2026 are up in the air.
Joseph-Day signed a two-year, $11 million deal as a free agent with the Steelers this past offseason.
He was a little banged up during training camp and did not play throughout the preseason, though he was back on the field and ready to go by the time Week 1 rolled around.
Joseph-Day was on the field for 111 defensive snaps through Week 6, which made up 29 percent of Pittsburgh's total reps on that side of the ball (per Pro Football Reference ), and he logged 10 tackles with a fumble recovery over that span.
The 31-year-old was later placed on IR ahead of the team's Week 7 matchup with the New Orleans Saints in Paris, however.
Joseph-Day will miss four games at the absolute minimum while on IR, meaning he isn't eligible to be activated until Week 12 regardless of his status.
Given Sawyer's comments, though, Joseph-Day's timeline for a return now appears to be stretched out.
The exact nature of his injury isn't yet known, but it seems like it's rather significant if there's even a chance that he won't play again this season.
As a key rotational piece, potentially losing Joseph-Day for the remainder of the campaign would deliver a blow to a Steelers' defense that's emerged as one of the league's elite units .
Pittsburgh has an impressive amount of talent and depth along the interior of its defensive line. While it's not ideal, it could likely withstand a long-term absence of Joseph-Day.
Cameron Heyward and Keeanu Benton have both played at a high level this season. The same could be said for Harmon before he went down with a foot injury in Week 4, and the hope is that he's back sooner rather than later now that he can technically be activated from IR after missing the minimum of four games.
Yahya Black has also excelled at nose tackle, and sixth-round rookie Gabriel Rubio has stepped up in a big way, playing 70 defensive snaps over the Steelers' last four games.
Even undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity Jr. has gotten into the mix since Joseph-Day landed on IR, garnering 25 defensive snaps over the past two weeks and recording his first sack in the team's Week 8 win over the Cleveland Browns.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: 17 Seahawks Appear on Second Week 9 Injury Report vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are banged up with a very long injury report as they complete their first official practice of the week.
After losing on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears, the Seahawks held a walk-through on Wednesday and the team released a projection for the injury report.
The Seahawks are getting ready for their Week 9 contest against the Arizona Cardinals, which should be a test, considering that it is difficult to sweep a divisional opponent in a season. Here's a look at the Seahawks' most recent injury report.
Apart from Sam Darnold , the most notable name on this list is new offensive lineman Quenton Nelson, who was a limited participant in Wednesday's report but did not practice today. It's not great that the team's top trade acquisition is already dealing with an injury, but there is still hope that he can play on Sunday against the Cardinals.
Uchenna Nwosu is on a similar trajectory as him, having been a limited participant on Wednesday but not participating in today's practice.
With Darnold not playing this weekend due to his quad and rib injuries, Drew Lock is expected to start. He's been dealing with an elbow injury over the last couple of weeks and has been the emergency third quarterback on multiple occasions. He spoke to reporters and claimed to be a lot better, even though he is still a limited participant in practice.
If Lock were to worsen or get injured during the game, second-year pro Jalen Milroe would be the team's quarterback.
The most notable player on this portion of the injury report is Anthony Bradford, who is now on the second unit after trading for Nelson. If Nelson is unable to go, Bradford can step in right back at right guard, where he played at the beginning of the season.

title: Jonathan Taylor Trade to Seahawks Will Be Based on Cardinals Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are less than a week away from the trade deadline.
Their Week 9 contest against the Arizona Cardinals will be the last one before Seahawks general manager John Schneider has to make his final decisions. The biggest debate the Seahawks have faced has surrounded Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and whether the team will trade for him or not.
The Seahawks will have Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet active for the second game since their return from injury against the Cardinals. Their performances will likely dictate what Seattle ends up doing for the trade deadline.
The Seahawks have been listed as a trade candidate for Taylor over the past couple of weeks, but things began to cool down once Seattle acquired Quenton Nelson in a deal just before Week 8 against the Chicago Bears. Charbonnet and Price struggled in their first game back, combining for 16 carries for 52 yards.
The Seahawks need them to perform well in order for them to feel confident about the direction and the offense moving forward. If not, an offer for Taylor could make sense considering the Seahawks and Colts recently negotiated.
Ultimately, the Seahawks are seeking a championship, and they realize that they aren't as good as they were a year ago, especially on offense. The trade for Nelson was a step in the right direction, but there's a need for more firepower.
The Seahawks hope that their growth can come from within, but they need to maximize this Super Bowl-contending window as much as possible. Trading for Taylor ensures an upgrade at the running back position, and there is little concern about how they will progress in the run game during the final half of the season.
Adding an elite running back will change the entire offense, as it will allow them to truly establish a presence running the football like they were able to do last season. That will open things up for Darnold, making him less prone to turning the ball over, and ultimately create a much more dynamic unit.
The Seahawks hope that Charbonnet and Price can fill that role, but if they have another dud performance against the Cardinals, it might be worth considering making the trade for Taylor.

title: It Might Be Jalen Milroe Time for the Seahawks
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Jalen Milroe is going into his second season with the team, and he could be in line to make his first career start in Week 9 against the Arizona Cardinals.
The team has already ruled Sam Darnold out due to a quad and rib injury, which will give Drew Lock a chance to make his second start of the year. He was limited in practice at the beginning of the week with a right elbow injury that has plagued him over the last couple of weeks. Therefore, the Seahawks could turn to Milroe to make his first career start.
Milroe came to the Seahawks with a lot of hype from his college days at Alabama. He was viewed as a potential franchise quarterback of the future in case Darnold didn't work out. Last season, Milroe never saw the field because Darnold was playing at a high level. Now that Darnold is dealing with injuries and inconsistent quarterback play, the team might need to call Milroe's number.
Milroe struggled in the preseason despite having some strong practices early in training camp, but it didn't translate to the games. In the team's preseason finale against the Kansas City Chiefs, Milroe was able to showcase why the team used a Day 2 pick on him last year.
"I thought there was a lot of good stuff," Macdonald said after the preseason in August.
"He made some really good throws on time, went through his progressions. We go back to the ball. I think that's pretty obvious leaving the field. I thought the guy made some really cool plays around the game. Stuff that we can build on moving forward. Of course there's things that we want to get better at and put up more points and all that type of stuff, but definitely a good foundation moving forward."
The Seahawks may not have been anticipating using Milroe as a starter at some point this season, but he has been staying loose and ready in case the team needs him. This week might be the chance.

title: New Seahawks Mock Draft Lands DeMarcus Lawrence Replacement
full_text:
This season hasn't gone according to plan for the Seattle Seahawks. After winning the Super Bowl last year, they went into 2026 ready to prove they're still the team to beat. They started off with a bang, handing a loss to the New England Patriots , the same team they beat in Super Bowl LX.
Since then, it's been a tough ride as they enter a Week 9 showdown with the Arizona Cardinals sitting at 4-4. The good news for the Seahawks is that they're still in second place in the NFC West and there's plenty of time for them to catch fire.
That said, it's obvious that they haven't completely replaced some of the players they lost this offseason in free agency. One of those is Boye Mafe, and that hole on the edge is only going to grow in 2027. Not only is Dante Fowler set for free agency, but DeMarcus Lawrence has already announced his plans to retire . That's why Justin Melo of NFL Draft on SI is targeting a pass-rusher for Seattle in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
Melo has Seattle selecting 17th overall, which is where they pick Alabama's Yhonzae Pierre. Listed at 6-foot-4 and 251 pounds, Pierre broke out in 2025 with eight sacks. He hasn't done much to set himself apart this season, but is still viewed as a first-round prospect and could help Seattle stay strong on the edge should he be their selection.
"Yhonzae Pierre entered the season as the clear-cut favorite for EDGE3, but has cooled a bit. The Alabama standout is still roughly on track to match or surpass his 8.0 sacks in 2025. The Seattle Seahawks haven't appropriately replaced Boye Mafe, and both DeMarcus Lawrence and Dante Fowler Jr. won't be around much longer," Melo wrote.
While adding Pierre would be a huge help for their defense, the Seahawks could decide to go with more help on offense. Their biggest concern right now has to be at wide receiver, where they have hardly anyone outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba making any noise this year.
In this mock, Jeremiah Smith and Charlie Becker were already off the board, but players such as Cam Coleman out of Texas and Nick Marsh from Indiana were still on the board. Unless Rashid Shaheed or Tory Horton finished the season significantly stronger than they have been during the first eight weeks, it would be tempting to select one of those wideouts over Pierre.
